instructions: You will analyze different sorting algorithms and participate in a structured discussion about their practical applications. PREPARATION (60 minutes): Research and analyze three sorting algorithms: Quick Sort, Merge Sort, and Heap Sort. For each algorithm, prepare a 200-word written analysis covering: (1) Time complexity for best, average, and worst cases with mathematical justification, (2) Space complexity and memory usage patterns, (3) One real-world scenario where this algorithm would be optimal. Include specific examples with data sizes (e.g., sorting 1 million customer records vs. sorting 50 student grades). DISCUSSION FORMAT (30 minutes): Present your findings in small groups of 4-5 students. Each student presents one algorithm (2 minutes), followed by group discussion comparing trade-offs (15 minutes), then groups report key insights to the class (10 minutes). During discussion, address: Which algorithm would you choose for sorting a large database with limited memory? How do these algorithms perform on nearly-sorted data? What factors beyond Big O notation matter in real implementations? SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Submit your written analysis before the discussion session. Include your analysis document, one slide summarizing your key points for presentation, and a brief reflection (100 words) on insights gained from peer discussions. All submissions must be in PDF format with your name and student ID clearly marked.
grading_notes: Evaluate complexity analysis for mathematical accuracy - watch for students who only memorize Big O without understanding derivation. Look for depth in comparisons beyond just stating time complexities; students should demonstrate understanding of when each algorithm excels. For real-world application, expect concrete examples with specific data sizes and constraints. During discussion, note active participation vs. passive listening - students should ask questions and build on others' ideas. Common issues: confusing time vs. space complexity, ignoring constant factors that matter in practice, not considering data characteristics (sorted, random, reverse-sorted). Grade distribution expectation: 20% A-range (exceptional analysis with novel insights), 60% B-range (solid understanding with minor gaps), 20% C-range or below (significant conceptual errors or minimal participation). Deduct points for late submission or failure to engage meaningfully in discussion component.

title: End-to-End Machine Learning Pipeline: Business Impact Analysis and Presentation
description: Students will design, implement, and present a complete machine learning solution for a real-world business problem, demonstrating technical proficiency, business acumen, and communication skills through a comprehensive presentation to stakeholders.
estimated_time: 4-6 weeks (80-100 hours total including research, implementation, analysis, and presentation preparation)
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced machine learning techniques to solve complex, real-world business problems
Demonstrate proficiency in data preprocessing, feature engineering, model selection, and hyperparameter optimization
Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics and statistical validation techniques
Communicate technical findings effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Assess business impact and provide actionable recommendations based on data science insights
Implement MLOps practices including model deployment, monitoring, and maintenance strategies
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation (25 points): Demonstrates advanced ML techniques, proper data preprocessing, feature engineering, model selection with justification, hyperparameter tuning, and code quality. Includes appropriate statistical validation and handles edge cases effectively.

Business Problem Framing & Impact Analysis (25 points): Clearly defines business problem with quantified objectives, identifies key stakeholders, establishes success metrics, calculates ROI/business impact, addresses ethical considerations, and provides actionable recommendations with implementation roadmap.

Presentation Quality & Communication (25 points): Delivers clear, engaging presentation adapted to audience, uses effective visualizations, manages time well, demonstrates deep understanding through Q&A responses, and presents complex concepts in accessible language.

Methodology & Experimental Rigor (25 points): Shows systematic approach to problem-solving, implements proper train/validation/test splits, compares multiple models with statistical significance testing, addresses bias and fairness concerns, and includes comprehensive error analysis with model limitations.
instructions: Select a real business problem from the provided dataset options (e-commerce, healthcare, finance, or supply chain) or propose your own with instructor approval. Your presentation must be 20-25 minutes with 10 minutes for Q&A. Deliver your solution as if presenting to C-level executives and technical teams simultaneously. Required deliverables: (1) Live presentation with slides (max 15 slides), (2) Jupyter notebook with complete implementation, (3) Executive summary (2-page PDF), (4) Model deployment demo. Your presentation must cover: problem definition with business context and success metrics; data exploration with key insights and quality assessment; methodology including algorithm selection rationale, feature engineering decisions, and validation strategy; results with performance metrics, statistical significance, and comparison to baselines; business impact analysis with ROI calculations and implementation timeline; deployment strategy with monitoring and maintenance plans; limitations, risks, and future improvements. Technical requirements: use at least two different ML algorithms, implement proper cross-validation, include feature importance analysis, address class imbalance if applicable, and demonstrate model interpretability. Prepare for technical questions about methodology, statistical assumptions, and alternative approaches. Submit all materials 24 hours before presentation via course portal.
grading_notes: Evaluate presentations using a holistic approach considering both technical depth and business communication effectiveness. Common issues to monitor: oversimplified problem framing (deduct 5-10 points), inadequate statistical validation (deduct 8-12 points), poor time management (deduct 3-5 points), inability to explain methodology during Q&A (deduct 5-15 points). Grade distribution expectation: 15% A+ (95-100), 25% A (90-94), 30% A-/B+ (80-89), 25% B/B- (70-79), 5% below 70. Award bonus points (up to 5) for exceptional innovation, addressing fairness/bias proactively, or demonstrating advanced techniques. Penalize heavily for data leakage, inappropriate metrics, or unrealistic business claims. Consider recording presentations for calibration and feedback purposes. Provide detailed written feedback within one week covering technical accuracy, presentation skills, and specific improvement recommendations.

title: My First Programming Project - Interactive Calculator Presentation
description: Students will create a simple calculator application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, then present their project to the class, explaining their code structure, design decisions, and demonstrating functionality.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate understanding of basic HTML structure and semantic elements
Apply fundamental CSS styling principles including layout and responsive design
Implement basic JavaScript functions for user interaction and mathematical operations
Communicate technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
Explain code logic and troubleshooting approaches used during development
rubric_criteria: Functionality (25 points): Calculator performs basic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) correctly, handles user input appropriately, displays results clearly, and includes basic error handling (division by zero)

Code Quality (25 points): HTML is semantically structured with proper tags, CSS is organized with clear selectors and properties, JavaScript uses meaningful variable names and includes comments explaining key functions

User Interface Design (25 points): Clean, intuitive layout that works on desktop browsers, consistent styling throughout, proper button sizing and spacing, clear display of numbers and results, basic responsive elements

Presentation Skills (25 points): Clear explanation of how the calculator works, demonstration of all features, discussion of at least one challenge faced and how it was resolved, answers questions confidently, stays within 5-7 minute time limit
instructions: Create a functional calculator web application and present it to the class. Your calculator must include: 1) HTML file with proper structure including number buttons (0-9), operation buttons (+, -, ×, ÷), equals button, and clear button; 2) CSS file that makes your calculator visually appealing with consistent colors, readable fonts, and organized layout; 3) JavaScript file with functions for each mathematical operation, input handling, and display updates. Requirements: Use separate files for HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; include comments explaining your code; test all functions before presentation; ensure calculator handles basic errors like division by zero. Submission: Upload all files to the course platform 24 hours before your presentation date. During your 5-7 minute presentation, demonstrate each calculator function, explain one interesting part of your code, share one challenge you overcame, and be prepared to answer questions about your design choices. Focus on explaining your thought process rather than just showing the final product.
grading_notes: Look for evidence of genuine understanding rather than copied code - ask follow-up questions during presentations if needed. Common issues include: missing error handling, poor variable naming, inline CSS/JavaScript instead of separate files, presentations that only show the final product without explaining the process. Expect 70-85% of students to score in the B range (80-89 points). Award full points for functionality even if code isn't perfect, as long as it works. Deduct points from presentation score if students can't explain their own code. Provide specific feedback on code organization and suggest resources for improvement.

title: Real-World Data Analysis Portfolio: Customer Churn Investigation
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive analysis of a customer churn dataset, demonstrating proficiency in data cleaning, exploratory data analysis, statistical testing, and business insights generation. The portfolio includes a technical report, code documentation, and executive summary with actionable recommendations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply data cleaning and preprocessing techniques to handle missing values, outliers, and data quality issues
Conduct exploratory data analysis using appropriate statistical and visualization methods
Perform hypothesis testing and interpret statistical significance in business context
Create compelling data visualizations that effectively communicate insights to stakeholders
Translate analytical findings into actionable business recommendations
rubric_criteria: Data Preprocessing and Quality (25 points): Systematic identification and appropriate handling of missing values, outliers, and data inconsistencies. Clear documentation of data cleaning decisions with justification. Proper data type conversions and feature engineering where applicable.

Exploratory Data Analysis and Visualization (25 points): Comprehensive exploration of variables and relationships using appropriate statistical summaries and visualizations. Clear, well-labeled charts with proper scaling and color choices. Evidence of pattern recognition and anomaly detection.

Statistical Analysis and Methodology (25 points): Correct application of statistical tests with proper assumptions checking. Appropriate interpretation of p-values, confidence intervals, and effect sizes. Valid conclusions drawn from statistical evidence with acknowledgment of limitations.

Business Communication and Insights (25 points): Clear executive summary written for non-technical stakeholders. Actionable recommendations supported by data evidence. Professional presentation of findings with logical flow and compelling narrative.
instructions: You will analyze a telecommunications customer churn dataset to identify factors contributing to customer attrition and provide strategic recommendations. Your portfolio must include: (1) Jupyter notebook with complete analysis code, comments, and markdown explanations; (2) Technical report (4-6 pages) detailing methodology, findings, and statistical results; (3) Executive summary (1-2 pages) with key insights and recommendations for business leadership. Begin by exploring the dataset structure, handling any data quality issues, and conducting univariate analysis of all variables. Investigate relationships between customer characteristics, service usage patterns, and churn behavior using appropriate visualizations and statistical tests. Test at least three specific hypotheses about churn drivers (e.g., contract type impact, service quality correlation, pricing sensitivity). Create publication-quality visualizations that tell a clear story about your findings. Conclude with specific, data-driven recommendations for reducing churn, including expected impact and implementation considerations. Submit all files in a organized folder structure with clear naming conventions. Code must be reproducible and well-documented. Use proper statistical terminology and cite any external sources or methodological references.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy first, then communication effectiveness. Look for evidence of analytical thinking beyond basic descriptive statistics - students should demonstrate understanding of correlation vs. causation, statistical significance interpretation, and business context application. Common issues include: inadequate data quality assessment, inappropriate statistical test selection, over-interpretation of results, and generic recommendations lacking specificity. Excellent portfolios will show creative insights, acknowledge limitations, and demonstrate sophisticated understanding of business implications. Grade distribution should follow: 90-100 (exceptional insight and execution), 80-89 (solid analysis with minor gaps), 70-79 (adequate technical work but limited business application), below 70 (significant methodological errors or incomplete analysis). Provide specific feedback on statistical interpretation and business reasoning quality.

title: Comprehensive Project Risk Management and Recovery Analysis Lab Report
description: Students will conduct an in-depth analysis of a real or simulated project that encountered significant risks and setbacks, developing comprehensive risk management strategies and recovery plans using advanced project management methodologies and tools.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced risk identification, assessment, and mitigation techniques in complex project scenarios
Develop comprehensive project recovery strategies using earned value management and critical path analysis
Evaluate stakeholder impact and communication strategies during project crisis situations
Integrate multiple project management frameworks (PMBOK, Agile, Lean) for optimal project outcomes
rubric_criteria: Risk Analysis and Quantification (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of risk identification methods, probability-impact matrices, Monte Carlo simulations, and quantitative risk analysis techniques with accurate calculations and realistic scenarios

Recovery Strategy Development (25 points): Presents comprehensive, feasible recovery plans including schedule compression techniques, resource reallocation, scope management, and cost-benefit analysis with clear implementation timelines and success metrics

Stakeholder Management and Communication (25 points): Develops detailed stakeholder analysis, communication matrices, conflict resolution strategies, and change management approaches with consideration of organizational dynamics and cultural factors

Technical Proficiency and Professional Presentation (25 points): Uses advanced project management software tools effectively, presents findings with professional-quality charts, graphs, and documentation following industry standards with clear executive summary and actionable recommendations
instructions: Select a project case study from the provided database or propose your own (subject to instructor approval) representing a project with budget >$500K and significant documented risks/failures. Your lab report must include: (1) Executive Summary (1 page) highlighting key findings and recommendations; (2) Project Background Analysis (2-3 pages) including original scope, timeline, budget, and stakeholder map; (3) Risk Assessment Section using at least three quantitative analysis methods (risk register, probability-impact matrix, expected monetary value calculations); (4) Recovery Strategy Development with detailed implementation plan, revised WBS, updated Gantt charts, and resource allocation matrices; (5) Stakeholder Communication Plan including crisis communication protocols, meeting schedules, and reporting mechanisms; (6) Lessons Learned and Best Practices section with recommendations for future projects. Use Microsoft Project or equivalent software for all scheduling and resource planning visualizations. Include minimum 10 credible sources (peer-reviewed articles, industry reports, PMI publications). Format: 12-point Times New Roman, double-spaced, APA citation style. Submit as single PDF with embedded charts/graphs. Maximum 15 pages excluding appendices. Due: End of Week 2, 11:59 PM via learning management system.
grading_notes: Focus evaluation on depth of analysis rather than project selection complexity. Watch for oversimplified risk assessments lacking quantitative support - students often rely too heavily on qualitative measures. Strong submissions will demonstrate integration of multiple PM methodologies rather than singular approach application. Deduct points for unrealistic recovery timelines or resource assumptions. Award bonus consideration for innovative solutions or creative use of emerging PM tools. Common weaknesses include insufficient stakeholder analysis and lack of consideration for organizational constraints. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 40% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. Provide detailed feedback on technical tool usage and professional presentation standards.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Simulation and Analysis
description: Students will navigate a complex multi-stakeholder organizational crisis scenario, make real-time leadership decisions, and provide comprehensive strategic analysis of their leadership approach, decision-making rationale, and organizational impact assessment.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate advanced crisis leadership competencies including rapid decision-making under uncertainty and stakeholder management
Analyze and synthesize complex organizational dynamics to formulate strategic leadership interventions
Evaluate the effectiveness of different leadership styles and approaches in high-pressure, multi-variable scenarios
Apply systems thinking to assess cascading effects of leadership decisions across organizational levels
rubric_criteria: Crisis Decision-Making Excellence (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated judgment in high-pressure decisions, shows clear strategic thinking, considers multiple stakeholder perspectives, and makes decisions that balance short-term stability with long-term organizational health

Stakeholder Communication and Influence (25 points): Exhibits masterful communication strategies tailored to different audiences, demonstrates emotional intelligence in managing resistance, builds coalitions effectively, and maintains transparency while managing sensitive information

Strategic Analysis and Systems Thinking (25 points): Provides comprehensive analysis of organizational dynamics, identifies root causes and systemic issues, anticipates second and third-order effects of decisions, and demonstrates understanding of organizational complexity

Leadership Philosophy Integration and Reflection (25 points): Articulates clear leadership philosophy, connects theoretical frameworks to practical applications, demonstrates self-awareness of leadership strengths and limitations, and shows evidence of adaptive leadership growth
instructions: You will participate in a 2-hour real-time crisis simulation where your organization faces a major product safety recall, potential lawsuit, media scrutiny, and employee morale crisis simultaneously. During the simulation, you'll receive information updates every 15 minutes and must make immediate leadership decisions via the online platform. Document all decisions with brief rationales. Following the simulation, prepare a comprehensive 2,500-word strategic analysis report addressing: (1) Decision-making framework and rationale for key choices, (2) Stakeholder management strategy and communication approach, (3) Analysis of organizational dynamics and systemic issues revealed, (4) Critical evaluation of your leadership effectiveness, including mistakes and learning points, (5) Alternative approaches and their potential outcomes, (6) Long-term strategic recommendations for organizational resilience. Your report must integrate at least 5 advanced leadership theories or frameworks, include specific examples from your simulation experience, and demonstrate metacognitive awareness of your leadership development. Submit your decision log and analysis report as separate PDF documents through the course portal within 48 hours of simulation completion. Use APA format for all citations and include a reflection on how this experience connects to your personal leadership development goals.
grading_notes: Evaluate decision quality based on information available at time of decision, not hindsight. Look for evidence of strategic thinking processes rather than 'perfect' outcomes. Strong submissions will show sophisticated understanding of leadership complexity and demonstrate growth mindset. Common weaknesses include: oversimplified analysis, failure to consider stakeholder perspectives, lack of theoretical integration, and insufficient self-reflection. Expect grade distribution: 90-100 (exceptional strategic insight and integration), 80-89 (solid analysis with minor gaps), 70-79 (adequate understanding with significant limitations), below 70 (insufficient depth or major conceptual errors). Pay special attention to authenticity of reflection and evidence of genuine leadership learning versus superficial responses.

title: Deploy and Configure a Static Website on AWS S3 with CloudFront
description: Students will create and deploy a multi-page static website using AWS S3, configure it for public access, implement CloudFront distribution for global content delivery, and demonstrate understanding of AWS core services through documentation and testing.
learning_objectives_assessed: Deploy and configure AWS S3 buckets for static website hosting
Implement AWS CloudFront distribution for content delivery optimization
Apply AWS security best practices for public web content
Navigate AWS Management Console and use core AWS services effectively
rubric_criteria: S3 Bucket Configuration (25 points): Correctly creates S3 bucket, enables static website hosting, configures proper permissions, uploads all required files with appropriate folder structure
CloudFront Distribution Setup (25 points): Successfully creates CloudFront distribution, configures origin settings, implements custom error pages, demonstrates understanding of CDN concepts

Website Functionality and Content (25 points): Website loads properly via both S3 endpoint and CloudFront URL, all navigation works, includes required pages (home, about, contact), responsive design implemented
Documentation and Best Practices (25 points): Provides comprehensive project documentation, demonstrates security considerations, includes cost analysis, follows AWS naming conventions and tagging
instructions:
Create a professional portfolio website and deploy it using AWS services. Your website must include: 1) Homepage with personal/professional introduction, 2) About page with background information, 3) Contact page with form (frontend only), and 4) CSS styling for professional appearance. 

Technical Requirements: Create an S3 bucket with static website hosting enabled, upload your website files maintaining proper folder structure, configure bucket policy for public read access, create CloudFront distribution pointing to your S3 bucket, and configure custom error page (404.html). 

Deliverables: Submit a PDF report including both S3 website URL and CloudFront distribution URL, screenshots of AWS console showing bucket configuration and CloudFront settings, brief explanation of how CloudFront improves website performance, estimated monthly cost breakdown for hosting this website, and reflection on challenges encountered and how you resolved them. 

Submission Guidelines: Ensure both URLs are accessible before submission, include all screenshots clearly showing your AWS account ID or username, write your reflection in 200-300 words, and submit PDF report via learning management system. Name your file: FirstName_LastName_AWS_Website_Project.pdf
grading_notes: Test both S3 and CloudFront URLs for accessibility - deduct points if either is broken or inaccessible. Verify bucket permissions are correctly configured for public read (not wide open). Check CloudFront propagation status - allow 15-30 minutes for full deployment. Common issues include: incorrect bucket policy syntax, missing index.html file, CloudFront caching delays, and broken internal links. Grade distribution expectations: 90-100 points (Excellent - all requirements met with professional quality), 80-89 points (Good - minor issues or missing minor components), 70-79 points (Satisfactory - functional but with notable issues), Below 70 (Needs improvement - major functionality problems). Pay attention to security practices - websites should not have overly permissive permissions beyond what's needed for static hosting.

title: Project Risk Management and Stakeholder Engagement Simulation Exam
description: Students will analyze a complex project scenario involving multiple stakeholder conflicts and emerging risks, then develop comprehensive risk response strategies and stakeholder engagement plans using PMP methodologies and frameworks.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply risk identification, analysis, and response planning techniques to complex project scenarios
Develop stakeholder engagement strategies using appropriate communication and influence techniques
Integrate multiple knowledge areas (Risk, Stakeholder, Communications, Quality) to solve project challenges
Demonstrate proficiency in PMP tools, techniques, and processes for intermediate-level project situations
rubric_criteria: Risk Management Application (25 points): Correctly identifies at least 8 risks using appropriate techniques, performs qualitative/quantitative analysis with proper risk register documentation, and develops specific response strategies (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept) with clear rationale

Stakeholder Engagement Strategy (25 points): Creates comprehensive stakeholder analysis matrix, identifies engagement strategies for each stakeholder group, addresses conflict resolution approaches, and demonstrates understanding of influence/interest grid application

PMP Process Integration (25 points): Shows clear understanding of process flow between knowledge areas, correctly applies PMP terminology and frameworks, demonstrates knowledge of inputs/outputs for key processes, and integrates quality management considerations

Professional Communication and Documentation (25 points): Presents solutions in professional project management format, uses clear and concise language appropriate for executive presentation, provides actionable recommendations with timelines, and demonstrates critical thinking in problem-solving approach
instructions:
You are the project manager for a $2.5M digital transformation project at a healthcare organization. The project is 40% complete when several issues emerge: the IT department raises security concerns about the proposed cloud solution, the clinical staff threatens to withdraw support due to inadequate training time, a key vendor announces a 6-week delay in critical software delivery, and the CFO questions the project's ROI given recent budget constraints. Additionally, the regulatory compliance team has identified potential HIPAA violations in the current implementation approach.

Your task: 1) Create a comprehensive risk register identifying and analyzing all project risks (minimum 8 risks with probability/impact ratings). 2) Develop specific risk response strategies for high and medium priority risks, including contingency plans. 3) Create a stakeholder engagement plan addressing each stakeholder group's concerns and required communication approach. 4) Prepare an executive summary (1 page) recommending immediate actions and project adjustments.

Format requirements: Submit as a professional project management document package including: Risk Register (Excel format acceptable), Stakeholder Analysis Matrix, written Risk Response Plan (2-3 pages), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (2 pages), and Executive Summary (1 page). Use standard PMP terminology throughout. All recommendations must be specific, actionable, and include proposed timelines. Reference appropriate PMP knowledge areas and processes in your analysis.
grading_notes: Evaluate students on both technical PMP knowledge application and practical project management judgment. Look for: proper use of risk probability/impact matrices with numerical ratings, stakeholder power/interest grid application, integration of multiple knowledge areas rather than siloed thinking, and realistic timeline considerations. Common issues include: generic risk responses without specific context, failure to address stakeholder emotional/political concerns, inadequate consideration of organizational change management, and unrealistic resource assumptions. Grade distribution expectation: 20% excellent (90-100), 60% proficient (75-89), 20% developing (60-74). Deduct points for missing required components, improper PMP terminology usage, or solutions that ignore stated constraints.

title: Strategic Google Analytics Implementation Case Study Analysis
description: Students will analyze a real-world e-commerce business scenario and develop a comprehensive Google Analytics measurement strategy, including advanced tracking implementation, custom reporting solutions, and data-driven optimization recommendations through collaborative discussion and peer review.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design and implement advanced Google Analytics tracking strategies for complex business requirements
Create custom reports and dashboards using GA4 reporting tools and Google Analytics Intelligence
Analyze multi-channel attribution and customer journey data to inform strategic business decisions
Evaluate and optimize conversion funnel performance using advanced segmentation and cohort analysis
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation Strategy (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of GA4 setup, custom events, enhanced ecommerce tracking, and cross-domain measurement for the given scenario

Advanced Analytics Application (25 points): Effectively utilizes advanced features including custom dimensions, calculated metrics, audience segmentation, and attribution modeling with clear business justification

Strategic Analysis and Insights (25 points): Provides data-driven recommendations based on thorough analysis of user behavior, conversion paths, and performance metrics with clear connection to business objectives

Discussion Engagement and Peer Review (25 points): Actively participates in discussions with substantive responses, provides constructive feedback on peer solutions, and incorporates feedback to refine their own analysis
instructions:
You are the digital analytics consultant for 'EcoTech Solutions,' a growing e-commerce company selling sustainable technology products across multiple channels (website, mobile app, Amazon marketplace, and physical pop-up stores). They currently have basic GA4 tracking but need a comprehensive analytics strategy to support their expansion goals.

Your task: Develop a complete Google Analytics implementation and analysis strategy. Create an initial discussion post (800-1000 words) addressing: (1) Detailed GA4 configuration plan including custom events, enhanced ecommerce setup, and cross-platform tracking architecture; (2) Custom reporting dashboard design with specific metrics, dimensions, and visualization recommendations aligned with business KPIs; (3) Advanced analysis approach using attribution modeling, cohort analysis, and funnel optimization to identify growth opportunities; (4) Data governance framework including data retention policies, user permissions, and compliance considerations.

Include specific GA4 features, configuration steps, and sample code where applicable. Support your recommendations with industry best practices and expected business impact.

Discussion Requirements: Post your initial analysis by Wednesday. Review and provide substantive feedback on at least three peer submissions by Friday, focusing on implementation feasibility and strategic alignment. Submit a revised final analysis by Sunday incorporating peer feedback and additional insights from class discussions. Use proper analytics terminology and cite relevant Google Analytics documentation or case studies.
grading_notes: Look for specific technical knowledge of GA4 features rather than general concepts. Strong submissions will include actual configuration examples, specific metric calculations, and realistic implementation timelines. Common issues: vague recommendations without technical specifics, failure to address cross-platform complexity, insufficient consideration of privacy regulations. Expect grade distribution: 15% exceptional (90-100), 60% proficient (80-89), 20% developing (70-79), 5% inadequate (below 70). Deduct points for late discussion participation as real-time collaboration is essential. Bonus consideration for students who identify emerging GA4 features or integration opportunities with other Google Marketing Platform tools.

title: Enterprise Network Design and Implementation Presentation
description: Students will design and present a comprehensive enterprise network solution incorporating advanced Cisco technologies including DMVPN, QoS implementation, network security protocols, and disaster recovery strategies. The presentation must demonstrate expert-level understanding of network architecture, protocol optimization, and enterprise-grade implementation considerations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design scalable enterprise networks using advanced Cisco routing and switching protocols
Implement and optimize Quality of Service (QoS) policies for enterprise traffic management
Configure advanced security features including VPNs, firewalls, and intrusion prevention systems
Evaluate and recommend network monitoring and management solutions
Analyze network performance bottlenecks and implement optimization strategies
rubric_criteria: Network Architecture Design (25 points): Comprehensive network topology with proper VLAN segmentation, routing protocols (OSPF, EIGRP, BGP), redundancy planning, and scalability considerations. Must include detailed network diagrams, IP addressing schemes, and hardware specifications.

Advanced Technology Implementation (25 points): Detailed configuration and justification of at least three advanced Cisco technologies (DMVPN, SD-WAN, HSRP/VRRP, EtherChannel, STP optimization, or advanced security features). Must include CLI configurations and implementation methodology.

Performance Optimization and Monitoring (25 points): QoS policy design with traffic classification, marking, and queuing strategies. Network monitoring solution with SNMP, NetFlow analysis, and performance baseline establishment. Troubleshooting methodology and documentation.

Professional Presentation and Technical Communication (25 points): Clear articulation of technical concepts, effective use of visual aids, confident handling of technical questions, adherence to time limits, and demonstration of expert-level knowledge through detailed responses to audience inquiries.
instructions: Prepare a 20-minute technical presentation proposing a complete enterprise network solution for a multi-site organization with 500-2000 employees. Your presentation must include: (1) Executive summary with business requirements analysis and proposed solution overview, (2) Detailed network architecture diagrams showing physical and logical topologies, including data center, campus, and WAN connectivity, (3) Complete IP addressing scheme with VLAN design and routing protocol selection with justification, (4) Implementation of three advanced Cisco technologies with actual CLI configurations and step-by-step deployment procedures, (5) Comprehensive QoS strategy addressing voice, video, and data traffic prioritization, (6) Security implementation including perimeter security, access control, and VPN solutions, (7) Network monitoring and management strategy with specific tools and methodologies, (8) Disaster recovery and business continuity planning, (9) Project timeline, budget estimates, and risk assessment, (10) Performance metrics and success criteria. Submit presentation slides and supporting documentation (network diagrams, configuration files, implementation guides) 24 hours before presentation. Be prepared for detailed technical questioning focusing on protocol behavior, troubleshooting scenarios, and alternative implementation approaches.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy of configurations using Cisco documentation standards. Look for proper use of networking terminology and protocols. Deduct points for unrealistic designs or missing redundancy. Excellent presentations (90-100) should demonstrate innovation and advanced optimization techniques. Good presentations (80-89) show solid technical competency with minor gaps. Satisfactory presentations (70-79) meet basic requirements but lack depth. Below 70 indicates significant technical errors or incomplete requirements. During Q&A, assess ability to explain protocol operations, defend design decisions, and adapt solutions to hypothetical scenarios. Common issues include oversimplified QoS policies, inadequate security considerations, unrealistic budget estimates, and inability to justify technology choices.

title: Electromagnetic Wave Propagation Analysis and Antenna Design Project
description: Students will design and analyze a dipole antenna system for a specific frequency application, including theoretical calculations, electromagnetic field modeling, and experimental validation of radiation patterns and impedance characteristics.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply Maxwell's equations to analyze electromagnetic wave propagation in different media
Design antenna systems using electromagnetic field theory and transmission line principles
Evaluate antenna performance parameters including gain, directivity, bandwidth, and impedance matching
Integrate theoretical predictions with experimental measurements and computational modeling
Communicate complex electromagnetic concepts through technical documentation and presentations
rubric_criteria: Theoretical Analysis (25 points): Correct application of Maxwell's equations, boundary conditions, and wave propagation theory. Accurate calculation of antenna parameters including radiation resistance, directivity, and near/far field distributions. Proper use of transmission line theory for impedance analysis.

Design Implementation (25 points): Appropriate antenna geometry selection for specified frequency and application. Detailed engineering drawings with dimensions and materials. Consideration of practical constraints including bandwidth, efficiency, and environmental factors. Innovation in design approach.

Computational Modeling (25 points): Accurate electromagnetic simulation using appropriate software (ANSYS HFSS, CST, or equivalent). Proper mesh refinement and boundary condition setup. Validation of simulation parameters against theoretical predictions. Clear presentation of field patterns, S-parameters, and radiation characteristics.

Experimental Validation and Analysis (25 points): Systematic experimental methodology for measuring antenna performance. Proper use of network analyzer, anechoic chamber, or alternative measurement setup. Statistical analysis of measurement uncertainty. Critical comparison between theory, simulation, and experiment with discussion of discrepancies.
instructions: Your project involves designing a half-wave dipole antenna for a specific electromagnetic application. Choose from: (1) 2.4 GHz WiFi communications, (2) 915 MHz IoT sensor network, or (3) 433 MHz remote sensing application. Your deliverables include: a comprehensive technical report (15-20 pages) containing theoretical analysis, design calculations, simulation results, and experimental validation; engineering drawings showing antenna geometry, dimensions, and feed structure; computational models with simulation files and post-processing scripts; experimental data with measurement setup photos and calibration procedures; and a 15-minute technical presentation. The theoretical section must derive antenna parameters from first principles using Maxwell's equations, including radiation pattern derivation, input impedance calculation, and efficiency analysis. Include boundary condition analysis for the antenna-air interface and near-field to far-field transformations. Your design must meet specified performance criteria: VSWR < 2:1 across the operating bandwidth, minimum 2 dBi gain, and appropriate polarization for the chosen application. Simulation work should demonstrate convergence studies, parameter sweeps for optimization, and sensitivity analysis. Experimental validation requires at least three independent measurement techniques (e.g., return loss, radiation pattern, gain measurement) with proper uncertainty quantification. Compare all results critically, explaining discrepancies and proposing design improvements. Submit all materials in a organized digital portfolio with clear file naming conventions and include a brief video demonstration of your experimental setup.
grading_notes: Assess theoretical rigor by checking derivations step-by-step, particularly Maxwell equation applications and boundary condition implementations. Look for proper handling of complex electromagnetic concepts and mathematical sophistication appropriate for expert level. In design evaluation, reward creative solutions and practical considerations beyond basic requirements. Check that simulation parameters are physically reasonable and that students demonstrate understanding of numerical methods limitations. For experimental work, evaluate measurement technique validity and statistical treatment of data - common issues include improper calibration, insufficient measurement points, and neglect of systematic errors. Expect 15% of students to achieve 90+ points, 50% in 75-89 range, with lower scores typically due to inadequate experimental validation or superficial theoretical analysis. Deduct points for missing uncertainty analysis, poor technical writing, or failure to address discrepancies between theory and experiment. Award bonus consideration for students who extend beyond minimum requirements with advanced topics like antenna arrays or novel feeding mechanisms.

title: Personal Portfolio Website Development Exam
description: Students will create a complete personal portfolio website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to demonstrate fundamental web development skills including semantic markup, responsive design, styling, and basic interactivity.
learning_objectives_assessed: Write semantic HTML markup with proper document structure and accessibility considerations
Apply CSS styling including layout techniques, typography, and responsive design principles
Implement basic JavaScript functionality for user interaction and dynamic content
Follow web development best practices including code organization, commenting, and file structure
rubric_criteria: HTML Structure & Semantics (25 points): Proper use of semantic HTML5 elements, valid markup, accessibility attributes, and logical document structure with head/body sections, meta tags, and appropriate nesting

CSS Styling & Layout (25 points): Professional visual design, proper CSS syntax, responsive layout using flexbox or grid, consistent typography, color scheme, and mobile-first approach with media queries
JavaScript Functionality (25 points): Working interactive features including form validation, dynamic content updates, event handlers, proper variable declarations, and error-free console output
Code Quality & Best Practices (25 points): Clean, well-commented code, logical file organization, consistent naming conventions, proper indentation, and adherence to web standards
instructions: Create a personal portfolio website consisting of at least 3 pages: Home, About, and Projects. Your submission must include: (1) index.html as the main page featuring your name, professional photo, brief introduction, and navigation menu; (2) about.html containing your background, skills, and career goals; (3) projects.html showcasing at least 2 sample projects with descriptions and images; (4) styles.css file with all styling, ensuring responsive design that works on desktop and mobile devices; (5) script.js file containing JavaScript for contact form validation, interactive navigation highlighting, and at least one dynamic feature like a image slider or collapsible sections. Technical requirements: Use semantic HTML5 elements (header, nav, main, section, footer), implement CSS Grid or Flexbox for layout, include hover effects and transitions, ensure all images have alt text, and validate your HTML and CSS. Submit all files in a single ZIP folder named 'lastname_firstname_portfolio.zip' with proper folder structure. Test your website in multiple browsers and screen sizes before submission. Include a brief README.txt file explaining your design choices and any special features implemented.
grading_notes: Evaluate HTML using W3C validator - deduct points for validation errors. Check responsiveness by resizing browser window and testing on mobile viewport. Verify JavaScript functionality works without console errors. Common issues to watch: missing alt attributes, inline styles instead of external CSS, non-semantic div overuse, broken responsive layout, JavaScript syntax errors. Grade distribution expectations: 90-100 (Excellent - professional quality, exceeds requirements), 80-89 (Good - meets all requirements with minor issues), 70-79 (Satisfactory - meets basic requirements but lacks polish), 60-69 (Needs improvement - missing key components or major functionality issues), Below 60 (Unsatisfactory - significant problems or incomplete work). Provide specific feedback on code quality and suggest improvements for professional development.

title: Complex Multi-Phase Project Recovery Case Study Presentation
description: Students will analyze a failing enterprise-level project, develop a comprehensive recovery strategy, and present their turnaround plan to stakeholders. This assessment evaluates advanced project management skills including risk analysis, stakeholder management, resource reallocation, and crisis leadership under realistic constraints.
learning_objectives_assessed: Analyze complex project failures using advanced diagnostic frameworks and root cause analysis techniques
Design comprehensive recovery strategies incorporating risk mitigation, resource optimization, and stakeholder alignment
Demonstrate executive-level communication skills when presenting critical project decisions to diverse stakeholder groups
Evaluate and justify trade-offs between scope, timeline, budget, and quality constraints in crisis situations
rubric_criteria: Problem Analysis & Diagnosis (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of project failure factors, uses multiple analytical frameworks (fishbone, 5-whys, SWOT), identifies both technical and organizational root causes, shows systems thinking in problem assessment

Recovery Strategy Development (25 points): Presents comprehensive, realistic turnaround plan with clear phases, addresses scope/schedule/budget trade-offs, includes detailed risk mitigation strategies, demonstrates understanding of change management principles

Stakeholder Communication & Presentation (25 points): Delivers executive-level presentation with clear recommendations, adapts messaging for different stakeholder groups, handles challenging questions professionally, uses data visualization effectively, maintains credibility under pressure

Implementation Planning & Risk Management (25 points): Provides detailed implementation roadmap with milestones, identifies potential obstacles and contingencies, demonstrates resource allocation expertise, shows understanding of organizational dynamics and politics
instructions: You are a senior project manager brought in to rescue a failing $2.5M enterprise software implementation that is 8 months behind schedule, 40% over budget, and facing potential cancellation. Choose from provided case studies or instructor-approved alternative. Your presentation must include: (1) Executive summary of current situation and key findings, (2) Root cause analysis using minimum two analytical frameworks, (3) Comprehensive recovery strategy with three scenario options (aggressive, moderate, conservative timelines), (4) Detailed 90-day action plan with specific deliverables and milestones, (5) Stakeholder communication plan and change management approach, (6) Updated project charter with revised success metrics. Present as if addressing the project steering committee including CEO, CFO, and key business stakeholders. Use professional slides (15-20 maximum), include appendices with supporting analysis. Submit presentation materials 24 hours prior to presentation date. Be prepared to defend your recommendations and respond to challenging questions about feasibility, costs, and risks. Time allocation: 15 minutes core presentation, 5 minutes for scenario comparison, 10 minutes Q&A session.
grading_notes: Look for sophisticated project management thinking beyond basic methodologies. Excellent presentations (90-100 points) demonstrate executive-level strategic thinking and realistic implementation planning. Good presentations (80-89) show solid analysis but may lack depth in stakeholder considerations or risk planning. Satisfactory work (70-79) addresses requirements but shows limited advanced project management concepts. Below 70 indicates fundamental gaps in crisis management understanding. Common issues: unrealistic timelines, insufficient stakeholder analysis, overemphasis on technical solutions versus organizational factors, poor risk quantification. Expect 20% A-level work, 40% B-level, 30% C-level, 10% below standard. Deduct points for exceeding time limits or inadequate Q&A responses.

title: Transformational Leadership Portfolio: Real-World Impact Documentation
description: Students compile a comprehensive portfolio documenting their leadership journey through three major components: a critical incident analysis of a complex leadership challenge they navigated, evidence of organizational change they initiated or led, and a 360-degree feedback synthesis with personal development plan. This expert-level assessment evaluates authentic leadership experiences and strategic thinking.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate advanced competency in transformational leadership practices through documented real-world application
Analyze complex organizational dynamics and stakeholder relationships using leadership theory frameworks
Evaluate personal leadership effectiveness through multiple feedback sources and create evidence-based development strategies
Synthesize leadership experiences into actionable insights for organizational change and team development
rubric_criteria: Critical Incident Analysis (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated analysis of a complex leadership challenge using multiple theoretical frameworks, shows clear cause-and-effect reasoning, includes stakeholder impact assessment, and provides evidence-based resolution strategies with measurable outcomes

Organizational Change Documentation (25 points): Provides comprehensive evidence of leading or co-leading significant organizational change, includes before/after metrics, stakeholder communication artifacts, resistance management strategies, and sustainability measures with clear attribution to student's leadership actions

360-Degree Feedback Integration (25 points): Synthesizes feedback from minimum 8 sources across hierarchical levels, identifies patterns and blind spots, connects feedback to specific leadership behaviors, and creates SMART development goals with implementation timeline and accountability measures

Strategic Leadership Reflection (25 points): Demonstrates executive-level thinking through synthesis of experiences, articulates personal leadership philosophy evolution, provides industry-specific leadership insights, and presents compelling vision for future leadership impact with concrete next steps
instructions: Create a professional portfolio containing four sections: (1) Critical Incident Analysis: Select a complex leadership challenge you faced involving multiple stakeholders and competing priorities. Analyze using minimum three leadership theories, include actual artifacts (emails, meeting notes, presentations), and document measurable outcomes. (2) Change Leadership Evidence: Document a significant organizational change you led or co-led. Include project scope, timeline, stakeholder analysis, communication plan, resistance encountered, and quantifiable results. Provide artifacts such as project plans, feedback surveys, or performance metrics. (3) 360-Feedback Synthesis: Collect structured feedback from 8+ individuals including supervisors, peers, direct reports, and external partners. Use provided feedback template or similar structured tool. Analyze themes, identify development areas, and create 12-month leadership development plan with specific milestones. (4) Strategic Leadership Reflection: Write executive summary connecting all experiences to your evolving leadership philosophy, industry leadership trends, and future impact vision. Portfolio should be professionally formatted, include executive summary, table of contents, and appendices with supporting artifacts. Submit as PDF with all sensitive information appropriately redacted. Length: 25-35 pages plus appendices.
grading_notes: Evaluate authenticity and complexity of experiences - reject superficial examples. Look for evidence of genuine leadership responsibility, not just participation. Strong submissions show clear ownership of outcomes, both positive and negative. Watch for theoretical name-dropping without genuine application. 360-feedback should show vulnerability and genuine self-awareness, not just positive comments. Grade distribution expectation: 15% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 40% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. Common issues: choosing incidents without sufficient complexity, lacking quantifiable outcomes, superficial theory application, insufficient artifact evidence. Exceptional portfolios demonstrate board-room level strategic thinking and measurable organizational impact.

title: AWS EC2 Instance Deployment and Configuration Lab Report
description: Students will deploy, configure, and document an EC2 instance with a web server, demonstrating fundamental AWS cloud computing skills including instance management, security groups, and basic monitoring.
learning_objectives_assessed: Deploy and configure AWS EC2 instances using the AWS Management Console
Implement basic security practices including security groups and key pairs
Install and configure web services on cloud instances
Monitor basic instance metrics and understand billing implications
Document cloud infrastructure decisions and configurations
rubric_criteria: EC2 Instance Deployment (25 points): Successful creation of t2.micro instance with appropriate AMI selection, correct region/availability zone choice, and proper instance naming convention
Security Configuration (25 points): Proper security group setup with correct inbound/outbound rules for HTTP/HTTPS and SSH access, successful key pair creation and secure storage practices
Web Server Installation (25 points): Successful installation and configuration of Apache/Nginx web server, custom HTML page deployment, and verification of public accessibility via browser
Documentation and Analysis (25 points): Complete lab report with screenshots, configuration details, cost analysis, lessons learned, and proper technical writing quality
instructions:
Complete the following AWS EC2 deployment lab and submit a comprehensive report documenting your process and findings.

Lab Tasks:
1. Launch an EC2 Instance: Create a new t2.micro EC2 instance using Amazon Linux 2 AMI in the us-east-1 region. Use descriptive naming (lastname-webserver-lab).

2. Configure Security: Create a new security group allowing HTTP (port 80), HTTPS (port 443), and SSH (port 22) access. Generate and download a new key pair for secure access.

3. Install Web Server: Connect to your instance via SSH and install Apache web server. Create a custom HTML page displaying your name, the current date, and instance metadata (instance ID, public IP).

4. Test and Verify: Ensure your web page is accessible via the public IP address from a web browser.

Submission Requirements:
Submit a PDF report (4-6 pages) including: executive summary, step-by-step process with screenshots, configuration details (security groups, instance specifications), cost breakdown from AWS billing dashboard, challenges encountered and solutions, and reflection on AWS cloud benefits vs. traditional hosting. Include all screenshots showing successful completion of each step. Ensure your custom web page is accessible for instructor verification during grading period.
grading_notes: Grade distribution should typically be 90% A/B grades for students who complete all technical requirements with adequate documentation. Deduct 5-10 points for missing screenshots, incomplete security configurations, or inaccessible web servers. Common issues include: students forgetting to configure security groups properly (resulting in connection timeouts), not preserving key pairs (preventing SSH access), and inadequate documentation of their process. Verify web page accessibility by visiting provided URLs. Students should demonstrate understanding of basic AWS concepts rather than advanced optimization. Accept both Apache and Nginx implementations. Ensure students terminate instances after grading to avoid unexpected charges.

title: Project Risk Management and Schedule Optimization Quiz
description: This intermediate-level quiz assesses students' understanding of PMP risk management processes, schedule analysis techniques, and critical path method application. Students will demonstrate their ability to identify risks, analyze project schedules, and make informed decisions about project control measures.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply risk identification and qualitative risk analysis techniques to project scenarios
Calculate critical path, float, and schedule compression using CPM and PERT methods
Evaluate earned value management metrics to assess project performance
Recommend appropriate risk response strategies and schedule optimization techniques
rubric_criteria: Risk Management Application (25 points): Correctly identifies project risks, applies appropriate risk analysis techniques, and selects suitable risk response strategies based on risk priority and project constraints

Schedule Analysis Accuracy (25 points): Demonstrates proficient use of CPM calculations, correctly identifies critical path and float values, and accurately applies schedule compression techniques (crashing/fast-tracking)
Earned Value Management (25 points): Properly calculates EVM metrics (CPI, SPI, EAC, ETC), interprets performance indicators correctly, and provides accurate project status assessments

Decision-Making and Recommendations (25 points): Provides well-reasoned recommendations for project control actions, justifies decisions with appropriate PMP methodologies, and considers stakeholder impact and project objectives
instructions: This quiz consists of 4 comprehensive scenario-based questions requiring both calculations and analytical reasoning. Read each scenario carefully and provide complete solutions showing your work. For calculation questions, round to two decimal places and include appropriate units. For recommendation questions, justify your answers using PMP best practices and explain the rationale behind your choices. You may use a basic calculator, but no reference materials or collaboration is permitted. Answer all parts of each question completely - partial responses will receive reduced credit. Submit your work in the provided answer booklet, writing legibly and organizing your responses clearly. If you need to make assumptions, state them explicitly. Time management is crucial - allocate approximately 18 minutes per question. Review your answers before submission, ensuring all calculations are shown and recommendations are supported with reasoning. Late submissions will be penalized 10% per day.
grading_notes: Instructors should award full credit for correct methodology even if minor calculation errors occur - deduct maximum 20% for computational mistakes while awarding full points for proper technique. Look for students demonstrating understanding of risk tolerance, stakeholder considerations, and project constraint impacts in their recommendations. Common issues include confusing forward/backward pass calculations, misinterpreting EVM variance indicators, and failing to consider secondary risks in response strategies. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 35% C-level (70-79), 15% below 70%. Provide specific feedback on calculation errors and highlight strong analytical reasoning to reinforce learning objectives.

title: E-commerce Website Analytics Implementation and Performance Optimization Project
description: Students will implement comprehensive Google Analytics tracking for a simulated e-commerce website, create custom reports and dashboards, analyze 3 months of provided data, and present actionable optimization recommendations based on user behavior insights and conversion funnel analysis.
learning_objectives_assessed: Configure advanced Google Analytics tracking including enhanced e-commerce, custom events, and goal setup
Create and interpret custom reports, segments, and dashboards for business decision-making
Analyze user behavior patterns, conversion funnels, and attribution models
Develop data-driven optimization strategies based on analytics insights
Present technical findings to non-technical stakeholders effectively
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation (25 points): Correct setup of GA4 property, enhanced e-commerce tracking, custom events, conversions, and audience segments. All tracking codes properly implemented with data layer configuration.

Data Analysis Quality (25 points): Thorough analysis of user behavior, traffic sources, conversion paths, and funnel performance. Proper use of advanced features like cohort analysis, attribution modeling, and custom metrics.

Custom Reporting & Visualization (25 points): Creation of meaningful custom reports, interactive dashboards, and data studio visualizations that clearly communicate key insights. Proper use of dimensions, metrics, and filters.

Strategic Recommendations (25 points): Evidence-based optimization recommendations with clear rationale, expected impact quantification, implementation timeline, and success measurement plan. Professional presentation quality.
instructions: You will work with a provided e-commerce website demo (fashion retailer) and 3 months of simulated traffic data. **Phase 1: Setup & Configuration (Week 1)** - Create new GA4 property and implement tracking code. Configure enhanced e-commerce events (purchase, add_to_cart, view_item, begin_checkout). Set up 5 custom events relevant to the business (newsletter signup, size guide usage, wishlist additions, etc.). Create 3 conversion goals and 2 custom audiences. **Phase 2: Analysis & Reporting (Weeks 2-3)** - Analyze provided dataset focusing on: user acquisition channels, product performance, checkout funnel conversion rates, and customer lifetime value patterns. Create 2 custom reports in GA4 and 1 comprehensive Looker Studio dashboard. Perform cohort analysis and attribution modeling comparison. **Phase 3: Presentation (Week 4)** - Prepare 15-minute presentation with executive summary, key findings, and 5 specific optimization recommendations. **Deliverables:** 1) GA4 property screenshots showing configuration, 2) Written analysis report (2000-2500 words), 3) Looker Studio dashboard (shareable link), 4) PowerPoint presentation, 5) Implementation checklist for recommendations. Submit all materials via learning management system with GA4 property sharing permissions granted to instructor.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy by checking GA4 configuration screenshots against provided checklist. Look for proper event parameter naming, correct goal setup, and meaningful audience definitions. In analysis section, assess depth of insights rather than just data description - students should identify patterns, correlations, and anomalies. Dashboard evaluation should focus on clarity, interactivity, and business relevance rather than visual design. For recommendations, ensure each suggestion includes supporting data, expected impact metrics, and realistic implementation steps. Common issues: incomplete e-commerce tracking setup, surface-level analysis without actionable insights, dashboards that don't match business needs, and recommendations without proper data justification. Grade distribution expectation: 15% A grades, 60% B grades, 20% C grades, 5% below C. Provide detailed feedback on technical implementation gaps and suggest specific GA4 resources for improvement.

title: Enterprise Network Design and Troubleshooting Comprehensive Exam
description: A comprehensive practical examination assessing advanced Cisco networking skills including OSPF/EIGRP implementation, VLAN segmentation, network security configuration, and systematic troubleshooting of complex multi-site enterprise networks.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design and implement scalable enterprise networks using advanced routing protocols (OSPF, EIGRP) with proper area/AS design
Configure and optimize VLAN segmentation, inter-VLAN routing, and spanning tree protocols for network efficiency
Implement comprehensive network security measures including ACLs, VPN tunnels, and firewall policies
Diagnose and resolve complex network issues using systematic troubleshooting methodologies and Cisco diagnostic tools
rubric_criteria: Network Design and Routing Implementation (25 points): Correct OSPF multi-area design with proper LSA types, area boundaries, and route summarization. EIGRP configuration with appropriate metric tuning and load balancing. Full connectivity between all sites with optimized routing tables.

VLAN and Switching Configuration (25 points): Proper VLAN segmentation aligned with business requirements, correct trunk/access port configurations, STP optimization with root bridge placement, and functional inter-VLAN routing with appropriate SVIs or routed interfaces.

Security Implementation (25 points): Comprehensive ACL design blocking unauthorized traffic while maintaining required connectivity, successful site-to-site VPN establishment with proper encryption, NAT configuration for internet access, and basic firewall policies implementation.

Network Troubleshooting and Documentation (25 points): Systematic identification and resolution of pre-configured network issues using show commands and debug tools, clear documentation of problem diagnosis process, verification of solutions, and comprehensive network topology documentation with IP addressing schemes.
instructions: You will receive a complex multi-site enterprise network scenario requiring complete configuration and troubleshooting. The exam consists of four main components: (1) Configure a three-site enterprise network with headquarters and two branch offices using OSPF areas 0, 10, and 20, implementing proper route summarization and ensuring full connectivity; (2) Implement VLAN segmentation for different departments (Sales, Engineering, Management) across all sites with appropriate inter-VLAN routing and optimized spanning tree configuration; (3) Secure the network by configuring ACLs to restrict interdepartmental access, establishing IPSec VPN tunnels between sites, and implementing NAT for internet connectivity; (4) Diagnose and resolve five pre-configured network issues including routing loops, VLAN misconfigurations, and connectivity problems. You must document all configurations, justify design decisions, and provide verification commands demonstrating proper functionality. Submit complete device configurations, network topology diagram with IP addressing, troubleshooting methodology documentation, and verification outputs. All work must be completed using Cisco CLI commands appropriate for enterprise-grade equipment (ISR 4000 series routers, Catalyst 9000 series switches). Partial credit awarded for correctly implemented components even if full connectivity is not achieved.
grading_notes: Grade holistically considering both technical accuracy and practical implementation. Award full points for criteria only when configurations are production-ready and fully functional. Common deductions: -5 points for missing route summarization, -10 points for STP suboptimal configuration, -15 points for ACLs that break required connectivity. Expect grade distribution: 90-100 (expert level, 15%), 80-89 (proficient, 40%), 70-79 (developing, 35%), below 70 (needs improvement, 10%). Verify all student solutions by testing connectivity, examining routing tables, and validating security policies. Pay special attention to troubleshooting methodology - students should demonstrate systematic approach using show commands, not random configuration changes. Document specific technical errors for feedback.

title: Programming Concepts Discussion: Variables, Data Types, and Basic Operations
description: Students will participate in a structured online discussion analyzing fundamental programming concepts including variables, data types, and basic operations. They will compare these concepts across different programming languages and discuss real-world applications through peer interaction and critical thinking.
estimated_time: 3-4 hours over one week (initial post: 1 hour, peer responses: 2-3 hours)
learning_objectives_assessed: Explain fundamental programming concepts including variables, data types, and basic operations
Compare and contrast programming language features and syntax
Apply programming concepts to solve real-world problems
Communicate technical concepts clearly using appropriate terminology
rubric_criteria: Initial Post Quality (25 points): Demonstrates clear understanding of variables, data types, and operations with accurate examples from at least two programming languages. Post is well-organized, uses proper technical terminology, and shows original thinking.

Real-World Application (25 points): Provides meaningful, specific examples of how these programming concepts apply to real-world scenarios. Examples are relevant, well-explained, and show practical understanding of concept implementation.

Peer Interaction (25 points): Responds thoughtfully to at least three classmates with substantive comments that extend discussion, ask clarifying questions, or provide additional insights. Responses demonstrate engagement and add value to the conversation.

Technical Communication (25 points): Uses appropriate computer science terminology consistently and accurately. Writing is clear, professional, and free of major grammatical errors. Code examples (if included) are properly formatted and syntactically correct.
instructions:
This discussion will help you explore fundamental programming concepts and their practical applications. Your participation should occur over one week to allow for meaningful peer interaction.

**Initial Post Requirements (due by Wednesday):**
Create a 300-400 word post addressing the following:
1. Define variables, data types, and basic operations in your own words
2. Compare how these concepts are implemented in at least two programming languages (e.g., Python vs. Java, C++ vs. JavaScript)
3. Provide one specific real-world example where understanding these concepts would be crucial (e.g., calculating student grades, managing inventory, processing user input)
4. Include a simple code snippet (3-5 lines) demonstrating one concept

**Response Requirements (due by Sunday):**
Respond to at least three classmates' posts with 100-150 word replies that:
- Ask thoughtful questions about their examples or explanations
- Share additional insights or alternative perspectives
- Relate their examples to your own experience or knowledge
- Suggest improvements or extensions to their code snippets

**Submission Format:**
Post directly to the course discussion forum. Use clear headings to organize your initial post. When responding to peers, reference specific parts of their posts. Include your name in responses to ensure proper attribution.

**Additional Guidelines:**
- Be respectful and constructive in all interactions
- Cite any external sources using proper format
- Proofread all posts before submission
- Engage authentically rather than posting generic responses
grading_notes: Evaluate initial posts for conceptual accuracy and depth of understanding rather than perfect technical implementation. Look for evidence that students can explain concepts in their own words and make meaningful connections. For peer responses, prioritize quality over quantity - three thoughtful responses score higher than five superficial ones. Common issues include: generic responses lacking specificity, incorrect technical terminology usage, and late posting that prevents meaningful peer interaction. Grade distribution should typically be: 90-100 points for exceptional work showing deep understanding and excellent communication; 80-89 for good work meeting most requirements; 70-79 for adequate work with some gaps; below 70 for incomplete or significantly flawed submissions. Provide specific feedback on technical accuracy and suggest resources for students showing misconceptions.

title: Data-Driven Business Insights: End-to-End Analytics Project Presentation
description: Students will conduct a complete data science project using a real-world dataset, performing exploratory data analysis, building predictive models, and presenting actionable business recommendations through a professional presentation.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply statistical analysis and visualization techniques to explore and interpret complex datasets
Design, implement, and evaluate machine learning models for predictive analytics
Communicate technical findings effectively to non-technical stakeholders through data storytelling
Demonstrate critical thinking in translating data insights into business recommendations
rubric_criteria: Data Exploration & Visualization (25 points): Thorough exploratory data analysis with appropriate statistical summaries, meaningful visualizations, identification of patterns/outliers, and clear data quality assessment

Model Development & Validation (25 points): Appropriate algorithm selection with justification, proper train/test/validation splits, hyperparameter tuning, performance metrics evaluation, and comparison of multiple approaches

Business Insights & Recommendations (25 points): Clear translation of technical findings into business context, actionable recommendations supported by data, consideration of limitations and risks, and demonstration of business value

Presentation Quality & Communication (25 points): Professional slide design, logical flow and storytelling, appropriate technical depth for audience, confident delivery, effective use of visuals, and ability to answer questions clearly
instructions: Select a business-relevant dataset (minimum 1000 rows, 10+ features) from approved sources (Kaggle, UCI Repository, or instructor-provided options). Your 15-minute presentation must include: (1) Business context and problem definition with clear success metrics, (2) Data exploration section showing key statistics, distributions, correlations, and data quality issues with 4-6 professional visualizations, (3) Model development process including algorithm selection rationale, feature engineering decisions, and performance comparison of at least 2 different approaches, (4) Results interpretation with model performance metrics, feature importance analysis, and validation of assumptions, (5) Business recommendations section with specific, actionable insights, implementation considerations, and ROI projections where applicable. Technical requirements: Use Python or R with appropriate libraries (pandas, scikit-learn, matplotlib/seaborn, etc.), include code snippets in appendix, and provide a 2-page executive summary. Submit presentation slides (PDF), executive summary, and complete code notebook 48 hours before presentation date. Be prepared for 5 minutes of questions focusing on methodology choices and business implications.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical rigor while emphasizing practical application and communication clarity. Look for evidence of iterative model improvement and thoughtful feature selection rather than just high accuracy scores. Deduct points for overfitting indicators (unrealistic performance claims, lack of validation strategy). Strong presentations will demonstrate understanding of model limitations and business constraints. Average scores should range 75-85; reserve 90+ for exceptional business insight integration. Common issues include: inadequate EDA depth, inappropriate model complexity for problem size, poor business context connection, and technical jargon overuse. Encourage peer feedback during Q&A sessions.

title: Advanced Electromagnetic Induction Lab Report: Design and Analysis of a Linear Generator
description: Students conduct an independent investigation designing and testing a linear generator, analyzing electromagnetic induction principles through quantitative measurements and theoretical modeling.
