Assessment evaluates experimental design, data analysis, theoretical understanding, and scientific communication at an advanced undergraduate/graduate level.
estimated_time: 6-8 hours (3-4 hours lab work, 3-4 hours report writing)
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply Faraday's law and Lenz's law to predict and calculate induced EMF in complex geometries
Design controlled experiments to investigate electromagnetic phenomena with appropriate variables and controls
Analyze experimental data using statistical methods and uncertainty propagation
Evaluate theoretical models against experimental results and identify sources of discrepancy
Communicate complex physics concepts through professional scientific writing and data visualization
rubric_criteria: Experimental Design and Methodology (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of electromagnetic principles in apparatus design, identifies and controls relevant variables, establishes appropriate measurement protocols, shows clear rationale for experimental choices

Data Collection and Analysis (25 points): Collects comprehensive, high-quality data with appropriate precision, applies advanced statistical analysis including uncertainty propagation, creates clear professional-quality graphs and tables, demonstrates quantitative reasoning

Theoretical Analysis and Modeling (25 points): Develops accurate theoretical models using electromagnetic theory, performs complex calculations correctly, compares theory to experiment quantitatively, identifies and explains discrepancies with physical reasoning

Scientific Communication and Conclusions (25 points): Writes in clear, professional scientific style, organizes report logically with proper structure, draws evidence-based conclusions, discusses limitations and future improvements, cites sources appropriately
instructions: Design and construct a linear generator using provided materials (copper coil, neodymium magnets, motion track, oscilloscope, multimeter). Your investigation must address: (1) How does induced EMF vary with magnet velocity through the coil? (2) How do coil parameters (turns, geometry) affect power output? (3) What factors limit efficiency? Begin by developing theoretical predictions using Faraday's law and electromagnetic theory. Design experiments to test at least three different configurations, collecting quantitative data on EMF, current, and power as functions of relevant parameters. Use statistical analysis to quantify uncertainties and relationships. Submit a formal lab report (8-12 pages) including: Executive Summary (200 words), Introduction with theoretical background, Experimental Methods with detailed apparatus description and procedures, Results with professional data presentation and statistical analysis, Discussion comparing theory to experiment with physical explanations of discrepancies, and Conclusions identifying key findings and limitations. Include all raw data, calculations, and uncertainty analyses in appendices. Reports must follow standard scientific format with proper citations, figure captions, and professional presentation. Submit via LMS as single PDF within 72 hours of lab session completion.
grading_notes: Focus evaluation on depth of physics understanding rather than perfect results. Excellent reports should show sophisticated experimental design with clear rationale, thorough uncertainty analysis, and insightful comparison between theory and experiment. Common issues: insufficient theoretical development, poor uncertainty analysis, inadequate discussion of discrepancies, unprofessional presentation. Grade distribution should reflect expert-level expectations: A-level work (90-100) demonstrates graduate-level analysis and communication; B-level (80-89) shows solid understanding with minor gaps; C-level (70-79) meets basic requirements but lacks depth. Below 70 indicates significant deficiencies in experimental design, analysis, or communication. Deduct points for late submission (5% per day). Provide specific feedback on physics concepts, experimental techniques, and scientific writing to promote learning.

title: Comprehensive Project Risk Management and Crisis Response Examination
description: Advanced examination assessing students' ability to identify, analyze, and develop comprehensive risk mitigation strategies for complex project scenarios, including crisis response planning and stakeholder communication during project disruptions.
learning_objectives_assessed: Analyze complex project scenarios to identify potential risks across multiple project dimensions (scope, schedule, budget, quality, resources)
Develop comprehensive risk response strategies using quantitative and qualitative risk assessment methodologies
Design crisis management protocols and stakeholder communication plans for high-impact project disruptions
Evaluate risk mitigation effectiveness and recommend adaptive project management approaches
rubric_criteria: Risk Identification and Analysis (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive identification of project risks across all knowledge areas, uses appropriate risk assessment tools (probability/impact matrix, Monte Carlo analysis), and provides quantitative risk analysis with supporting calculations

Risk Response Strategy Development (25 points): Develops detailed, feasible risk response plans for identified risks, appropriately categorizes responses (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept), includes contingency planning with trigger events, and considers resource allocation for risk responses

Crisis Management and Communication Planning (25 points): Creates comprehensive crisis response protocols with clear escalation procedures, develops stakeholder-specific communication templates, establishes decision-making frameworks for crisis situations, and includes post-crisis project recovery strategies

Integration and Professional Application (25 points): Demonstrates integration of risk management with overall project management processes, shows understanding of organizational and industry-specific risk contexts, uses professional project management terminology correctly, and provides realistic implementation timelines and resource requirements
instructions: This examination consists of a comprehensive case study requiring you to develop a complete risk management framework for a large-scale, multi-stakeholder project scenario. You will receive a detailed project brief including scope, timeline, budget, stakeholder information, and initial risk indicators. Your response must include: (1) A comprehensive risk register identifying minimum 15 potential risks across all project knowledge areas, with probability/impact assessments and risk scores; (2) Detailed risk response strategies for the top 8 highest-priority risks, including specific actions, responsible parties, timelines, and budget implications; (3) A crisis management protocol document outlining response procedures for three high-impact risk scenarios, including stakeholder communication templates and escalation matrices; (4) A risk monitoring and control plan with KPIs, reporting schedules, and adaptive management triggers. All deliverables must be presented in professional project management format using industry-standard templates. Include references to PMI standards and best practices. Calculations must show work, and all assumptions must be clearly stated. Submit as a single PDF document with clear section headers and page numbers. Late submissions will incur a 10% penalty per day.
grading_notes: Evaluate submissions using the four-level scale (Excellent: 90-100%, Proficient: 80-89%, Developing: 70-79%, Inadequate: Below 70%). Focus on depth of analysis rather than quantity - students should demonstrate critical thinking and practical application. Common issues to watch for: superficial risk identification without proper analysis, generic risk responses not tailored to the specific scenario, unrealistic timelines or resource allocations, poor integration between risk management and overall project strategy. Excellent responses will show innovative thinking, consideration of organizational culture and constraints, and sophisticated understanding of risk interdependencies. Expect grade distribution: 15% Excellent, 35% Proficient, 40% Developing, 10% Inadequate. Provide specific feedback on calculation errors, missed risk categories, and communication plan feasibility.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Simulation: Multi-Stakeholder Decision-Making Analysis
description: Students will participate in a complex organizational crisis simulation requiring them to demonstrate advanced leadership competencies including strategic decision-making under pressure, stakeholder management, ethical reasoning, and adaptive leadership while facilitating a structured discussion with peers representing different organizational roles.
estimated_time: 3 hours (2 hours preparation + 1 hour facilitated discussion)
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate advanced strategic thinking and decision-making under ambiguous, high-pressure conditions
Exhibit sophisticated stakeholder analysis and multi-perspective leadership approaches
Apply ethical leadership frameworks to complex organizational dilemmas
Facilitate collaborative problem-solving while maintaining leadership authority and vision
rubric_criteria: Strategic Analysis & Decision Quality (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive situational analysis, identifies critical success factors, weighs multiple strategic options, and articulates clear rationale for decisions with consideration of long-term implications

Stakeholder Leadership & Influence (25 points): Shows sophisticated understanding of diverse stakeholder needs, adapts communication and leadership style effectively, builds consensus while maintaining direction, and manages conflicting interests diplomatically

Ethical Reasoning & Values Integration (25 points): Consistently applies ethical frameworks to decision-making, addresses moral complexities explicitly, demonstrates integrity under pressure, and balances competing ethical demands with clear justification

Facilitation Excellence & Adaptive Leadership (25 points): Guides discussion productively while encouraging diverse viewpoints, adapts leadership approach based on group dynamics, maintains focus on objectives, and demonstrates emotional intelligence in managing group tensions
instructions: You will assume the role of CEO during a major organizational crisis involving a product safety issue, significant financial implications, and intense media scrutiny. Your task is to facilitate a 60-minute executive team discussion to develop a comprehensive response strategy. Prior to the discussion, spend 2 hours analyzing the provided case materials, including financial reports, legal briefings, customer complaints, and media coverage. Prepare a strategic framework for the discussion, but remain adaptive to input from your 'executive team' (fellow students assigned roles as CFO, COO, Legal Counsel, and PR Director). During the facilitated discussion, you must: (1) Present your initial situational analysis and strategic options, (2) Guide the team through systematic evaluation of alternatives, (3) Address ethical dilemmas explicitly, (4) Manage conflicting viewpoints and priorities, (5) Facilitate consensus-building toward actionable decisions, and (6) Conclude with a clear implementation timeline and communication strategy. Your performance will be evaluated based on both your strategic leadership decisions and your effectiveness in facilitating collaborative problem-solving. Submit a post-discussion reflection (500 words) analyzing your leadership approach, key decisions made, stakeholder considerations, and lessons learned. All team members will provide peer evaluations of your leadership effectiveness using provided feedback forms.
grading_notes: Evaluate students on leadership process as much as outcomes - look for sophisticated thinking rather than 'perfect' solutions. Watch for: authentic stakeholder perspective-taking (not superficial acknowledgment), ethical reasoning that goes beyond compliance to values-based decision-making, and facilitation skills that balance assertiveness with inclusivity. Common weaknesses include over-focusing on technical solutions while neglecting stakeholder dynamics, making decisions too quickly without adequate consultation, and failing to address ethical dimensions explicitly. Grade distribution should reflect expert-level expectations: 90-100 points for exceptional strategic leadership with sophisticated stakeholder management; 80-89 for strong leadership with minor gaps in facilitation or ethical reasoning; 70-79 for adequate leadership with notable weaknesses in strategic thinking or group management; below 70 for insufficient demonstration of advanced leadership competencies. Peer feedback should comprise 10% of final grade to encourage authentic engagement.

title: AWS Cloud Fundamentals: Core Services Presentation
description: Students will create and deliver a 10-minute presentation explaining AWS core services and demonstrating how they solve real-world business problems through a practical use case scenario.
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify and explain the purpose of AWS core services (EC2, S3, RDS, VPC)
Demonstrate understanding of cloud computing benefits and AWS pricing models
Apply AWS services to solve a realistic business scenario
Communicate technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
rubric_criteria: Technical Content (25 points): Accurately explains 3-4 AWS core services, their functions, and key features. Demonstrates clear understanding of cloud computing concepts and AWS fundamentals.

Business Application (25 points): Presents a realistic business scenario and effectively demonstrates how selected AWS services solve the problem. Shows understanding of cost benefits and scalability.
Presentation Quality (25 points): Clear verbal communication, logical flow, appropriate use of visual aids, stays within time limit (8-12 minutes), engages audience effectively.
Visual Design & Organization (25 points): Professional slide design, appropriate graphics/diagrams, minimal text per slide, consistent formatting, includes AWS architecture diagram.
instructions: Create a 10-minute presentation addressing the following scenario: 'A small e-commerce company is moving from on-premises infrastructure to AWS cloud.' Your presentation must include: (1) Introduction to AWS and cloud computing benefits (2 minutes), (2) Explanation of 3-4 core AWS services relevant to the scenario - choose from EC2, S3, RDS, VPC, CloudFront, or Lambda (5 minutes), (3) A simple AWS architecture diagram showing how these services work together for the e-commerce solution (2 minutes), (4) Cost comparison between on-premises vs. AWS, highlighting 2-3 specific cost benefits (1 minute). Use 8-12 slides maximum. Include at least one diagram or visual representation of AWS services. Avoid reading directly from slides - use them as visual support. Practice your timing and be prepared to answer 1-2 questions after your presentation. Submit your PowerPoint/Google Slides file 24 hours before your scheduled presentation slot. File naming convention: LastName_FirstName_AWS_Presentation.pptx
grading_notes: Grade presentations immediately after delivery while content is fresh. Look for conceptual understanding rather than memorized definitions. Common issues: students often exceed time limits or read directly from slides - deduct from presentation quality score. Technical content should be accurate but doesn't need to be overly detailed for beginner level. Architecture diagrams can be simple but should show logical connections between services. Expect 15% A grades (90-100), 60% B grades (80-89), 20% C grades (70-79), 5% below 70. Students struggling with technical concepts often excel in presentation delivery and vice versa.

title: Project Risk Management Portfolio: Risk Register Development and Mitigation Planning
description: Students will create a comprehensive risk management portfolio for a simulated IT infrastructure upgrade project, demonstrating proficiency in risk identification, analysis, response planning, and monitoring strategies aligned with PMI standards.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply PMI risk management processes to identify, analyze, and prioritize project risks
Develop comprehensive risk response strategies using appropriate risk treatment approaches
Create effective risk monitoring and control mechanisms with quantifiable metrics
Demonstrate understanding of qualitative and quantitative risk analysis techniques
rubric_criteria: Risk Identification and Documentation (25 points): Comprehensive risk register with minimum 15 risks across all knowledge areas, proper categorization using RBS, clear risk statements following cause-risk-effect format, appropriate risk owners assigned

Risk Analysis and Assessment (25 points): Accurate qualitative analysis using probability/impact matrix, quantitative analysis for top 5 risks including expected monetary value calculations, proper risk prioritization with supporting rationale, sensitivity analysis completion

Risk Response Planning (25 points): Appropriate response strategies (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept) for each high/medium risk, detailed action plans with timelines and resource requirements, secondary and residual risk identification, contingency plans for critical risks

Risk Monitoring Framework (25 points): Clear risk indicators and triggers, monitoring schedule and responsibilities, escalation procedures, risk reporting template, lessons learned integration process, portfolio presentation quality and professionalism
instructions: You are the project manager for a $2.5M enterprise IT infrastructure upgrade affecting 500+ users across multiple locations. Create a complete risk management portfolio containing: 1) Executive Summary (1 page) outlining risk management approach and key findings, 2) Risk Register spreadsheet with all identified risks, analysis scores, and response plans, 3) Risk Response Plan document (4-6 pages) detailing strategies for top 10 risks, 4) Risk Monitoring Dashboard showing KPIs and tracking mechanisms, 5) Presentation slides (10-12 slides) for stakeholder communication. Use provided project charter and scope statement as baseline. All documents must follow PMI terminology and processes from PMBOK Guide. Include realistic assumptions about organizational context, regulatory requirements, and resource constraints. Submit all components as a single PDF portfolio with clear section dividers and professional formatting. Cite relevant PMI standards and include a reference list. Portfolio should demonstrate practical application of risk management theory to real-world scenarios with implementable solutions.
grading_notes: Evaluate portfolios using a 4-point scale per criterion: Exemplary (23-25 pts), Proficient (20-22 pts), Developing (15-19 pts), Inadequate (0-14 pts). Look for PMI process adherence, realistic risk scenarios, appropriate mathematical calculations in quantitative analysis, and professional document quality. Common issues include: generic risk statements, incorrect probability/impact assessments, unrealistic response strategies, and poor integration between portfolio components. Expect 15% A-level work, 60% B-level, 20% C-level, 5% below standard. Provide specific feedback on PMI alignment and practical feasibility of proposed solutions.

title: Advanced Google Analytics Implementation and Optimization Lab Report
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive analysis of a real or simulated e-commerce website by implementing advanced Google Analytics tracking, creating custom reports, and providing data-driven optimization recommendations based on user behavior patterns and conversion funnel analysis.
learning_objectives_assessed: Configure advanced Google Analytics tracking including enhanced e-commerce, custom events, and goal conversions
Analyze user behavior data using segmentation, cohort analysis, and attribution modeling
Create custom reports and dashboards to measure KPIs and business objectives
Interpret analytics data to identify optimization opportunities and make data-driven recommendations
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation (25 points): Correct setup of GA4 property, enhanced e-commerce tracking, custom events, and goal configurations with proper data layer implementation
Data Analysis & Interpretation (25 points): Thorough analysis of user behavior, conversion funnels, traffic sources, and audience segments with accurate statistical interpretation
Custom Reporting & Visualization (25 points): Creation of meaningful custom reports, dashboards, and data visualizations that clearly communicate insights and trends
Strategic Recommendations (25 points): Evidence-based optimization recommendations with clear rationale, expected impact, and implementation priorities
instructions:
Select an e-commerce website (provided demo site or approved alternative) and complete the following deliverables in a comprehensive lab report: 

1. **Technical Setup Documentation** (2-3 pages): Configure GA4 property with enhanced e-commerce tracking, set up 3 custom events relevant to business goals, implement 2 conversion goals, and document your tracking code implementation with screenshots.

2. **Data Collection & Analysis** (4-5 pages): Collect data for minimum 7 days, analyze user acquisition channels, behavior flow, and conversion funnels. Create audience segments based on demographics and behavior patterns. Include cohort analysis for user retention and attribution model comparison.

3. **Custom Reporting Suite** (2-3 pages): Build 3 custom reports addressing specific business questions, create 1 comprehensive dashboard with key metrics, and export/visualize data using Google Analytics Intelligence or Data Studio integration.

4. **Optimization Recommendations** (3-4 pages): Provide 5 specific, prioritized recommendations based on your analysis. Include expected impact estimates, implementation difficulty, and success measurement criteria.

**Format Requirements**: Submit as PDF with numbered sections, include all screenshots/data exports as appendices, cite any external sources, and provide GA property access for verification. Total length: 12-15 pages excluding appendices.
grading_notes: Verify student GA implementations by accessing shared properties - check for proper event firing and goal setup. Look for depth of analysis beyond surface-level metrics; students should demonstrate understanding of statistical significance and data limitations. Common issues include: improper goal attribution, misinterpretation of bounce rate, ignoring mobile vs desktop differences, and recommendations not supported by data. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 35% C-level (70-79), 15% below 70%. Deduct points for late submissions, incomplete technical implementations, or recommendations lacking data support.

title: E-Commerce Customer Analytics: Predictive Modeling and Business Intelligence Exam
description: Students will analyze a real-world e-commerce dataset to perform exploratory data analysis, build predictive models for customer behavior, and present actionable business insights. This comprehensive assessment evaluates data preprocessing, statistical analysis, machine learning implementation, and communication of findings.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply appropriate data preprocessing techniques including handling missing values, outliers, and feature engineering
Conduct comprehensive exploratory data analysis using statistical methods and data visualization
Implement and evaluate machine learning models for classification/regression problems
Interpret model results and translate findings into actionable business recommendations
rubric_criteria: Data Preprocessing and EDA (25 points): Quality of data cleaning, missing value handling, outlier detection, meaningful visualizations, and statistical summaries that reveal key patterns
Machine Learning Implementation (25 points): Appropriate model selection, proper train/validation/test splits, hyperparameter tuning, and correct implementation of at least two different algorithms
Model Evaluation and Interpretation (25 points): Use of appropriate metrics, cross-validation, feature importance analysis, model comparison, and identification of limitations
Business Insights and Communication (25 points): Clear presentation of findings, actionable recommendations supported by data, professional visualizations, and effective written communication
instructions:
You are provided with an e-commerce dataset containing customer transactions, demographics, and behavior data spanning 18 months. Your task is to develop a predictive model and provide business insights.

Deliverables:
1. Jupyter notebook with complete analysis (code, outputs, and markdown explanations)
2. Executive summary (2-page PDF) for business stakeholders

Specific Requirements:
- Perform comprehensive EDA with at least 5 meaningful visualizations
- Address data quality issues (missing values, duplicates, outliers)
- Engineer at least 3 new features based on business logic
- Build and compare minimum 2 ML models (e.g., Random Forest, Logistic Regression, XGBoost)
- Predict customer churn OR customer lifetime value (choose one)
- Use appropriate evaluation metrics and cross-validation
- Include feature importance analysis
- Provide 3-5 specific business recommendations

Submission Format:
- Upload notebook (.ipynb) and executive summary (.pdf) to learning management system
- Ensure all code runs without errors
- Include requirements.txt file with package versions
- Name files: LastName_FirstName_DataScience_Exam

Dataset access and submission deadline will be provided separately. Late submissions penalized 10 points per day.
grading_notes: Grade holistically within each criterion. Excellent work (90-100): Shows creativity, deep insights, professional-quality analysis. Good work (80-89): Meets requirements with minor gaps. Satisfactory (70-79): Basic requirements met but lacks depth. Below expectations (<70): Missing key components or significant errors. Common issues: overfitting, data leakage, inappropriate metrics for imbalanced data, weak business conclusions. Expect grade distribution: 20% A, 40% B, 30% C, 10% D/F. Partial credit available for each criterion - document specific deductions.

title: Mathematical Proof Techniques and Problem-Solving Strategies Discussion
description: Students will engage in a structured discussion analyzing multiple approaches to advanced mathematical proofs, evaluate the effectiveness of different proof techniques, and collaborate to solve complex multi-step problems involving real analysis and abstract algebra concepts.
learning_objectives_assessed: Analyze and critique mathematical proofs using various techniques (direct, contradiction, induction, contrapositive)
Synthesize multiple mathematical concepts to solve complex, multi-domain problems
Communicate mathematical reasoning clearly and respond constructively to peer arguments
Evaluate the elegance, efficiency, and rigor of different mathematical approaches
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Accuracy and Rigor (25 points): Demonstrates precise use of mathematical language, correct logical reasoning, identifies gaps or errors in proofs, and provides mathematically sound solutions with proper justification

Proof Technique Analysis (25 points): Compares and contrasts different proof methods, explains why certain techniques are more suitable for specific problems, and demonstrates understanding of when to apply various approaches

Problem-Solving Synthesis (25 points): Successfully integrates concepts from multiple mathematical domains, shows creative problem-solving approaches, and provides complete solutions to complex multi-step problems

Discussion Engagement and Communication (25 points): Posts thoughtful initial responses, provides substantive feedback to peers, asks probing mathematical questions, and explains concepts clearly using appropriate mathematical notation
instructions: This discussion spans one week and requires three phases of participation. **Phase 1 (Days 1-3):** Choose one of the three provided proof problems involving epsilon-delta definitions, group theory, or topology. Present two different proof approaches for your chosen problem, explaining the advantages and limitations of each method. Your initial post should be 400-500 words with proper mathematical notation. **Phase 2 (Days 3-5):** Respond to at least three classmates who chose different problems than you. Analyze their proof techniques, identify any logical gaps, suggest improvements, or propose alternative approaches. Each response should be 200-300 words. **Phase 3 (Days 5-7):** Collaborate in assigned groups of 4 to solve the capstone integration problem that combines elements from all three domains. Post your group's solution methodology and individually reflect on how the different proof techniques discussed earlier could be applied. Submit all work using proper LaTeX formatting for mathematical expressions. Include citations for any theorems or lemmas referenced. Late submissions lose 10 points per day. All responses must demonstrate original thinking and mathematical rigor.
grading_notes: Focus on mathematical correctness over length - concise, rigorous arguments score higher than verbose explanations. Common issues include: incomplete proofs, misuse of mathematical notation, and superficial peer responses. Expect grade distribution: 15% A+ (exceptional insight and rigor), 35% A/A- (solid mathematical reasoning), 40% B range (adequate with minor gaps), 10% C or below (significant mathematical errors). Pay special attention to proper use of quantifiers, logical connectives, and proof structure. Students should demonstrate understanding that different problems may require different proof strategies, and their peer interactions should focus on mathematical content rather than general encouragement.

title: Complex Project Crisis Management and Recovery Simulation
description: Students will analyze a multi-phase project crisis scenario involving scope creep, resource constraints, stakeholder conflicts, and external dependencies. They must develop a comprehensive recovery plan using advanced project management methodologies and demonstrate strategic decision-making under pressure.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced risk management and contingency planning techniques to resolve complex project crises
Synthesize multiple project management methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, Hybrid) to optimize project recovery strategies
Evaluate stakeholder management approaches and communication strategies during high-stakes project situations
Demonstrate critical thinking in resource reallocation and schedule compression techniques while maintaining quality standards
rubric_criteria: Crisis Analysis and Root Cause Identification (25 points): Demonstrates thorough analysis of underlying issues, correctly identifies primary and secondary causes, shows understanding of interconnected project elements and their impact on overall project health

Recovery Strategy Development (25 points): Develops comprehensive, realistic recovery plan incorporating appropriate PM methodologies, demonstrates strategic thinking in prioritization, shows innovative problem-solving while maintaining feasibility constraints

Stakeholder Management and Communication Plan (25 points): Creates detailed stakeholder analysis with tailored communication strategies, demonstrates understanding of influence/interest matrix, proposes conflict resolution approaches with clear escalation procedures

Implementation Timeline and Resource Management (25 points): Develops realistic implementation schedule with clear milestones, demonstrates advanced scheduling techniques (fast-tracking, crashing), shows optimal resource allocation while considering constraints and dependencies
instructions: You are the newly assigned project manager for Phoenix Software's ERP implementation project, currently 18 months into a planned 24-month timeline. The project is 45% behind schedule, 30% over budget, and facing severe stakeholder resistance. Recent developments include: key technical architect resignation, client requesting major scope changes, vendor delivery delays, and executive pressure for immediate course correction. Your deliverable is a comprehensive crisis recovery document (2,500-3,000 words) containing: (1) Executive Summary with crisis assessment and recommended actions, (2) Detailed root cause analysis using fishbone diagram and supporting narrative, (3) Multi-phased recovery strategy incorporating at least two PM methodologies with clear rationale, (4) Stakeholder management matrix with individualized engagement strategies, (5) Revised project schedule using critical path method with risk mitigation buffers, (6) Resource reallocation plan addressing skill gaps and budget constraints, (7) Communication plan with templates for key stakeholder groups. Include realistic assumptions, cite specific PM frameworks (PMBOK, PRINCE2, SAFe, etc.), and provide quantitative justifications for all recommendations. Submit as PDF with clear section headers and supporting visual aids (Gantt charts, organizational charts, etc.). All recommendations must be implementable within stated constraints.
grading_notes: Evaluate depth of analysis over breadth - students should demonstrate mastery of advanced concepts rather than superficial coverage. Look for creative yet practical solutions that show real-world applicability. Deduct points for generic responses not tailored to the specific scenario. Expect students to make reasonable assumptions but these should be clearly stated. Strong responses will integrate multiple PM knowledge areas seamlessly and show understanding of organizational dynamics. Common weaknesses include: oversimplified solutions ignoring political realities, unrealistic timelines, inadequate consideration of change management, and failure to address root causes. Grade distribution expectation: 15% A grades (90-100), 35% B grades (80-89), 40% C grades (70-79), 10% below 70. Partial credit available for each criterion - award points for demonstration of relevant knowledge even if conclusions are flawed.

title: Organizational Crisis Leadership Simulation and Strategic Response Plan
description: Students will navigate a multi-phase organizational crisis simulation, demonstrating advanced leadership competencies including stakeholder management, ethical decision-making under pressure, team coordination, and strategic communication. This assessment evaluates ability to lead through ambiguity while maintaining organizational values and long-term vision.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate transformational leadership behaviors in high-stakes, ambiguous situations
Apply ethical decision-making frameworks when facing competing stakeholder interests
Execute effective crisis communication strategies across multiple organizational levels
Design and implement strategic recovery plans that align with organizational vision and values
rubric_criteria: Crisis Response Leadership (25 points): Demonstrates decisive action, maintains team morale, adapts leadership style to situational demands, shows emotional intelligence under pressure, and provides clear direction during uncertainty

Stakeholder Management & Communication (25 points): Develops targeted communication strategies for different audiences, manages conflicting interests diplomatically, maintains transparency while protecting sensitive information, and builds coalition support

Ethical Decision-Making & Judgment (25 points): Applies consistent ethical frameworks, balances short-term pressures with long-term consequences, demonstrates moral courage in difficult decisions, and maintains organizational integrity throughout crisis

Strategic Recovery Planning & Implementation (25 points): Creates comprehensive recovery roadmap, anticipates future challenges, aligns solutions with organizational capabilities and culture, establishes measurable outcomes and accountability structures
instructions: You are the newly appointed Chief Operating Officer of TechNova Industries, a 2,500-employee technology company. You will face a three-phase crisis simulation over 6 weeks. Phase 1 (Weeks 1-2): A data breach exposes customer information while your CEO is overseas. Lead the immediate response, coordinate with legal/IT teams, and manage media relations. Phase 2 (Weeks 3-4): Investigation reveals the breach resulted from an employee's negligent security practices. Several major clients threaten contract cancellation, and employee morale plummets. Navigate personnel decisions, client retention efforts, and internal communications. Phase 3 (Weeks 5-6): Develop a comprehensive 12-month recovery strategy addressing security improvements, client relationship rebuilding, and organizational culture strengthening. Deliverables include: 1) Real-time decision logs with rationale (submitted after each phase), 2) Stakeholder communication artifacts (emails, presentations, statements), 3) Final strategic recovery plan with implementation timeline, 4) Reflective leadership analysis examining your decision-making process, leadership style adaptation, and lessons learned. Each phase includes surprise elements requiring rapid response. You'll receive performance feedback from simulated stakeholders (instructor-provided) and must adapt accordingly. All work must demonstrate graduate-level strategic thinking and professional presentation standards.
grading_notes: Evaluate authenticity of leadership voice and decision-making rationale rather than 'correct' answers, as crisis leadership often involves choosing between imperfect options. Look for evidence of systematic thinking processes, not just outcomes. Phase 1 should show 20% of total grade weight (immediate response capability), Phase 2 should show 35% (complex stakeholder navigation), and Phase 3 should show 45% (strategic recovery and reflection). Common issues include: students making decisions too quickly without stakeholder consideration, focusing only on technical solutions while ignoring human elements, or providing generic responses without situation-specific adaptation. Exceptional work (A-level) demonstrates innovative problem-solving, proactive anticipation of cascading effects, and sophisticated understanding of organizational dynamics. Students should show growth across phases - early mistakes followed by learning and adaptation should be rewarded.

title: AWS Cloud Fundamentals Practical Exam
description: A comprehensive practical examination testing foundational AWS cloud computing concepts, core services identification, basic security practices, and cost management principles through scenario-based questions and hands-on configuration tasks.
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify and describe core AWS services (EC2, S3, RDS, VPC) and their primary use cases
Explain fundamental AWS security concepts including IAM, security groups, and data encryption
Demonstrate understanding of AWS pricing models and cost optimization strategies
Apply basic AWS architectural principles for designing simple cloud solutions
rubric_criteria: Core Services Knowledge (25 points): Correctly identifies AWS services, explains their functions, and matches appropriate services to given scenarios with 80%+ accuracy
Security Understanding (25 points): Demonstrates solid grasp of IAM roles/policies, security groups, and encryption concepts through accurate explanations and practical applications
Cost Management (25 points): Shows understanding of AWS pricing models, identifies cost optimization opportunities, and correctly calculates estimated costs for basic configurations
Architecture & Best Practices (25 points): Applies fundamental design principles including availability zones, scalability concepts, and demonstrates logical problem-solving in cloud scenarios
instructions: This exam consists of four sections testing your foundational AWS knowledge. You have 90 minutes to complete all sections. Section A contains 15 multiple-choice questions about core AWS services - select the best answer for each question. Section B requires short written responses (2-3 sentences each) explaining security concepts and best practices. Section C presents three cost scenarios where you must calculate pricing and suggest optimizations using provided AWS pricing sheets. Section D includes two architectural scenarios requiring you to design basic solutions and justify your service selections. All written responses should be clear and technically accurate. For calculation questions, show your work for partial credit. You may use AWS documentation and pricing calculator during the exam, but no collaboration is permitted. Submit your completed exam through the learning management system before the time expires. Ensure all sections are completed as partial submissions will not be accepted. Technical diagrams in Section D can be hand-drawn or created digitally - focus on clarity and logical component relationships rather than artistic quality.
grading_notes: Use a 4-point scale for each criterion: Exemplary (23-25 points), Proficient (20-22 points), Developing (15-19 points), Inadequate (0-14 points). Common issues to watch: students confusing similar services (EC2 vs Lambda), incomplete IAM policy explanations, calculation errors in cost sections, and oversimplified architectural diagrams. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 40% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. Provide specific feedback on incorrect service selections and suggest AWS documentation sections for review. Partial credit available for showing work in calculations even if final answers are incorrect.

title: Risk Management Strategy Discussion: Comparative Analysis of Quantitative vs. Qualitative Approaches
description: Students will engage in structured discussions analyzing the effectiveness of quantitative versus qualitative risk analysis methods in different project contexts, demonstrating understanding of risk management processes and their practical application in project scenarios.
estimated_time: 90 minutes (45 minutes preparation, 45 minutes discussion participation)
learning_objectives_assessed: Evaluate and apply appropriate risk analysis techniques (quantitative and qualitative) based on project characteristics and organizational context
Demonstrate critical thinking in risk identification, assessment, and response planning across diverse project scenarios
Articulate the relationship between risk tolerance, project constraints, and stakeholder expectations in risk management decisions
rubric_criteria: Risk Analysis Technique Knowledge (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of quantitative methods (Monte Carlo, decision trees, sensitivity analysis) and qualitative methods (probability/impact matrices, risk categorization), including when each is most appropriate

Scenario Application and Critical Analysis (25 points): Effectively applies risk analysis concepts to specific project scenarios, identifies key contextual factors influencing method selection, and provides well-reasoned justifications for recommendations

Discussion Engagement and Professional Communication (25 points): Actively participates in discussion with substantive contributions, responds thoughtfully to peers' posts, asks probing questions, and maintains professional tone throughout interactions

Integration of PMP Framework and Best Practices (25 points): Consistently references PMI risk management processes, demonstrates understanding of risk register components, and connects discussion points to broader project management principles and organizational considerations
instructions: You will participate in a structured discussion analyzing quantitative versus qualitative risk analysis approaches. First, review the three provided project scenarios (IT system implementation, construction project, and pharmaceutical product development). Choose one scenario and prepare your initial post (300-400 words) addressing: (1) Which risk analysis approach (quantitative, qualitative, or hybrid) you recommend and why, (2) Specific techniques you would employ and their expected outcomes, (3) How organizational risk tolerance and project constraints influence your recommendation, and (4) Potential limitations of your chosen approach and mitigation strategies. Post your initial response by Wednesday 11:59 PM. Then, engage with at least three classmates' posts by Sunday 11:59 PM, providing substantive feedback that challenges assumptions, offers alternative perspectives, or builds upon their analysis. Each response should be 150-200 words and reference specific PMP concepts. Use proper citation format for any external sources beyond course materials. All posts must demonstrate professional communication standards expected in project management environments.
grading_notes: Look for depth of understanding rather than memorization of techniques. Excellent posts (90-100 points) will demonstrate synthesis of concepts and real-world application insights. Good posts (80-89 points) show solid understanding with some application gaps. Satisfactory posts (70-79 points) meet basic requirements but lack depth or critical analysis. Watch for: superficial responses that don't address scenario specifics, lack of PMP terminology integration, poor peer engagement quality, and late submissions. Expect 20% of students to earn 90+ points, 60% to earn 80-89 points, and 20% to earn below 80 points. Provide specific feedback on risk technique selection rationale and encourage students to consider stakeholder perspectives in their analysis.

title: Strategic Google Analytics Implementation and Performance Analysis Presentation
description: Students will create a comprehensive presentation demonstrating advanced Google Analytics implementation, custom reporting, and strategic insights for a real or simulated business scenario. The presentation must showcase technical proficiency in GA4 configuration, advanced analysis techniques, and the ability to translate data into actionable business recommendations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Configure and implement advanced Google Analytics 4 tracking including custom events, conversions, and audiences
Create and interpret custom reports, segments, and attribution models to support business decision-making
Analyze user behavior, conversion funnels, and customer journey data to identify optimization opportunities
Communicate complex analytics insights effectively to stakeholders and provide data-driven recommendations
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation (25 points): Demonstrates proper GA4 setup including custom events, conversion tracking, enhanced ecommerce, custom dimensions/metrics, and audience configuration with clear explanations of technical choices

Advanced Analysis & Reporting (25 points): Creates meaningful custom reports, applies advanced segments, uses attribution modeling, demonstrates proficiency with Explorations, and shows understanding of statistical significance

Strategic Business Insights (25 points): Identifies actionable insights from data, connects analytics findings to business objectives, provides specific optimization recommendations, and demonstrates understanding of KPIs and business impact

Presentation Quality & Communication (25 points): Delivers clear, well-structured presentation with effective data visualizations, professional slides, confident delivery, and ability to answer technical questions during Q&A
instructions: Create a 12-15 minute presentation analyzing a website's performance using Google Analytics 4. Choose either your own website, a client project, or use the Google Merchandise Store demo account. Your presentation must include: (1) GA4 implementation overview showing your tracking setup, custom events, and conversion configuration; (2) Three custom reports addressing specific business questions with detailed methodology explanation; (3) User behavior analysis including audience insights, acquisition channels, and engagement metrics; (4) Conversion funnel analysis with identification of drop-off points and optimization opportunities; (5) Strategic recommendations with projected impact and implementation timeline. Include live GA4 demonstrations during your presentation. Submit your slide deck (PDF) and a one-page technical appendix documenting your GA4 configuration details 24 hours before presentation. Be prepared for 3-5 minutes of technical Q&A following your presentation. Use professional formatting and ensure all data visualizations are clearly labeled and interpretable.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy by checking GA4 configuration logic and implementation feasibility. Look for proper use of GA4 terminology and features (not Universal Analytics concepts). Award full points for technical implementation only when students can explain their setup choices and demonstrate understanding of data collection methods. For analysis criteria, assess whether insights are supported by actual data and methodology is sound. Deduct points for generic recommendations not tied to specific findings. Presentation delivery should be professional but focus more on technical competency than polish. Common issues include: confusing GA4 with Universal Analytics, creating reports without clear business purpose, making recommendations without supporting data, and inability to explain technical implementation during Q&A. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90+), 35% B-level (80-89), 40% C-level (70-79), 10% below proficient.

title: Basic Algorithm Implementation and Analysis Lab Report
description: Students will implement basic sorting algorithms (bubble sort and selection sort), analyze their performance with different data sets, and document their findings in a structured lab report format.
estimated_time: 4-6 hours (2-3 hours coding, 2-3 hours report writing)
learning_objectives_assessed: Implement basic sorting algorithms using proper programming constructs
Analyze algorithm performance through empirical testing and time complexity analysis
Document programming work clearly with appropriate technical writing skills
Compare and contrast different algorithmic approaches to solve the same problem
rubric_criteria: Code Implementation (25 points): Both algorithms correctly implemented with proper syntax, logic, and functionality. Code is well-commented and follows naming conventions.

Performance Analysis (25 points): Accurate timing measurements for different input sizes (100, 500, 1000 elements). Correct identification of time complexity patterns and comparison between algorithms.
Technical Documentation (25 points): Clear explanations of algorithm logic, well-formatted code snippets in report, proper use of technical terminology, and accurate description of methodology.

Results Discussion and Conclusions (25 points): Meaningful interpretation of performance data, logical conclusions about algorithm efficiency, identification of trade-offs, and suggestions for when to use each algorithm.
instructions: Complete this lab report by implementing two sorting algorithms and analyzing their performance. First, write programs in your chosen language (Python, Java, or C++) that implement bubble sort and selection sort. Your code must include proper comments explaining each step and use meaningful variable names. Test both algorithms with three different array sizes: 100, 500, and 1000 randomly generated integers. Record the execution time for each test run (perform 3 trials per size and calculate averages). Create your lab report using the provided template, including: (1) Introduction explaining the purpose and algorithms being tested, (2) Methodology section describing your implementation approach and testing procedure, (3) Results section with tables showing timing data and graphs comparing performance, (4) Discussion analyzing the results and explaining the theoretical time complexity of each algorithm, (5) Conclusion summarizing key findings and practical applications. Include your complete source code in an appendix. Submit your report as a PDF along with your source code files through the course management system. Reports should be 4-6 pages in length, double-spaced, with proper citations for any external resources used. Ensure all graphs and tables are clearly labeled and referenced in the text.
grading_notes: Look for working code that produces correct sorted output - partial credit available if logic is sound but minor syntax errors exist. Performance analysis should show bubble sort taking longer than selection sort, with both showing quadratic growth patterns. Students may struggle with accurate timing measurements; accept reasonable attempts at benchmarking even if methodology isn't perfect. Technical writing should be clear but don't penalize heavily for minor grammatical errors - focus on accurate technical content. Common issues include: forgetting to include time complexity analysis, insufficient testing with edge cases, and poorly formatted code in appendix. Grade distribution should typically be: 15% A's, 35% B's, 40% C's, 10% D/F. Provide specific feedback on code efficiency and suggest improvements for algorithm optimization.

title: Customer Churn Analysis: Feature Engineering and Model Evaluation Quiz
description: Students will analyze a customer churn dataset by performing feature engineering, implementing multiple machine learning algorithms, and conducting comprehensive model evaluation. This assessment tests practical data science skills including data preprocessing, feature selection, model comparison, and result interpretation.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply feature engineering techniques to improve model performance
Implement and compare multiple machine learning algorithms for classification
Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics and validation techniques
Interpret results and make data-driven recommendations for business decisions
rubric_criteria: Feature Engineering (25 points): Creates meaningful features, handles missing values appropriately, applies proper encoding for categorical variables, and demonstrates feature selection techniques

Model Implementation (25 points): Correctly implements at least 3 different classification algorithms (e.g., logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting), uses proper hyperparameter tuning, and follows best practices for model training

Model Evaluation (25 points): Uses appropriate evaluation metrics (precision, recall, F1-score, AUC-ROC), implements cross-validation, compares models effectively, and addresses class imbalance if present

Analysis and Interpretation (25 points): Provides clear interpretation of results, identifies most important features, makes actionable business recommendations, and demonstrates understanding of model limitations
instructions: You will work with a telecommunications customer churn dataset containing 20 features and 5,000 customer records. Complete all sections in a Jupyter notebook with clear markdown explanations for each step. **Section 1: Data Exploration and Preprocessing (20 minutes)** - Load the provided dataset and perform initial exploratory data analysis. Identify and handle missing values, outliers, and data quality issues. Create visualizations to understand feature distributions and relationships with the target variable. **Section 2: Feature Engineering (25 minutes)** - Create at least 3 new meaningful features based on existing data. Apply appropriate encoding techniques for categorical variables. Implement feature scaling where necessary and perform feature selection using statistical or model-based methods. **Section 3: Model Development (30 minutes)** - Split data into training and testing sets. Implement three different classification algorithms with hyperparameter tuning. Use cross-validation to ensure robust model evaluation. **Section 4: Model Evaluation and Comparison (15 minutes)** - Evaluate all models using multiple metrics appropriate for the business context. Create comparison visualizations and select the best performing model with justification. Submit your completed Jupyter notebook (.ipynb file) with all code executed and outputs visible. Include a brief executive summary (2-3 paragraphs) at the end highlighting key findings and recommendations.
grading_notes: Award full points for technically correct implementation with clear explanations. Deduct 5-10 points per criterion for minor errors (e.g., missing cross-validation, incomplete feature engineering). Deduct 15-20 points for major errors (e.g., data leakage, inappropriate metrics, incorrect model implementation). Look for evidence of critical thinking in feature creation and business interpretation. Expect 70-85% of students to score in the 75-90 point range. Common issues include: data leakage in feature engineering, using accuracy as the sole metric for imbalanced datasets, insufficient hyperparameter tuning, and weak business interpretations. Bonus points (up to 5) can be awarded for exceptional creativity in feature engineering or particularly insightful analysis.

title: Urban Transit Optimization: Mathematical Modeling and Analysis Project
description: Students will develop and analyze mathematical models to optimize public transit routes in a city, applying advanced calculus, linear programming, and statistical analysis to solve real-world transportation challenges.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply multivariable calculus and optimization techniques to solve complex real-world problems
Construct and analyze mathematical models using linear programming and constraint optimization
Interpret statistical data and perform regression analysis to support mathematical conclusions
Communicate mathematical reasoning clearly through written reports and visual presentations
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Model Development (25 points): Constructs appropriate mathematical models using advanced techniques (optimization functions, constraints, variables). Models demonstrate deep understanding of mathematical relationships and real-world applications.

Problem-Solving and Analysis (25 points): Applies correct mathematical procedures including calculus-based optimization, linear programming methods, and statistical analysis. Shows work clearly with proper mathematical notation and reasoning.

Data Interpretation and Validation (25 points): Effectively analyzes provided transit data, performs appropriate statistical tests, validates model assumptions, and draws meaningful conclusions supported by mathematical evidence.

Communication and Presentation (25 points): Produces professional report with clear mathematical explanations, appropriate graphs/visualizations, proper citations, and compelling presentation of findings to stakeholders.
instructions: You are a consultant hired by Metro City Transit to optimize their bus route system. Using the provided dataset containing ridership patterns, traffic data, and demographic information, complete the following deliverables: (1) Mathematical Model: Develop an optimization model to minimize total travel time while maximizing ridership coverage. Define objective functions, constraints, and decision variables using multivariable calculus and linear programming techniques. (2) Analysis Report: Apply your model to propose three alternative route configurations. Use statistical regression to analyze ridership patterns and validate your assumptions. Include sensitivity analysis showing how changes in key parameters affect optimal solutions. (3) Executive Summary: Prepare a 10-minute presentation for city officials explaining your methodology, findings, and recommendations. Include professional visualizations and cost-benefit analysis. Technical requirements: Use appropriate mathematical software (Excel, Python, R, or MATLAB), show all calculations and derivations, include confidence intervals for statistical estimates, and provide complete bibliography. Submit: Written report (15-20 pages), mathematical appendix with detailed calculations, presentation slides, and digital files containing your models and data analysis. All work must demonstrate advanced mathematical thinking and practical application to urban planning challenges.
grading_notes: Evaluate mathematical rigor and accuracy first - students should demonstrate mastery of optimization techniques and statistical methods. Look for creative problem-solving approaches while maintaining mathematical validity. Common issues include: insufficient constraint modeling, improper statistical assumptions, unclear mathematical notation. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 40% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70%. Partial credit should be awarded generously for correct methodology even with computational errors. Emphasize that real-world applicability and mathematical sophistication should be balanced - neither purely theoretical nor overly simplified approaches meet expectations.

title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics and Electromagnetic Field Theory Comprehensive Examination
description: A comprehensive expert-level physics examination testing advanced understanding of quantum mechanical principles, electromagnetic field theory, and their applications in modern physics. Students must demonstrate mastery of mathematical formalism, physical interpretation, and problem-solving in quantum systems and electromagnetic phenomena.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply Schrödinger equation solutions to complex quantum systems including multi-particle states and time evolution
Analyze electromagnetic field propagation using Maxwell's equations in various media and boundary conditions
Demonstrate understanding of quantum mechanical operators, commutation relations, and measurement theory
Solve advanced problems involving quantum tunneling, barrier penetration, and bound state systems
Apply electromagnetic theory to waveguide propagation, antenna radiation, and relativistic effects
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Rigor and Formalism (25 points): Correct application of quantum mechanical and electromagnetic mathematical frameworks, proper use of vector calculus, differential equations, and complex analysis. Full credit requires error-free mathematical derivations with appropriate approximations clearly stated.

Physical Interpretation and Conceptual Understanding (25 points): Accurate interpretation of quantum wavefunctions, probability amplitudes, electromagnetic field behavior, and physical meaning of mathematical results. Must demonstrate deep understanding of underlying physics principles rather than mere formula manipulation.

Problem-solving Strategy and Methodology (25 points): Systematic approach to complex problems, appropriate choice of coordinate systems, boundary conditions, and solution methods. Credit given for logical progression, identification of key physics principles, and efficient solution pathways.

Communication and Presentation (25 points): Clear mathematical notation, well-organized solutions with logical flow, appropriate diagrams and graphs where needed, and concise but complete explanations of reasoning. Professional presentation of results with proper units and significant figures.
instructions: This examination consists of six comprehensive problems spanning quantum mechanics and electromagnetic theory. You have 4 hours to complete all problems. Show all mathematical work clearly and provide physical interpretation of your results. Use proper mathematical notation and include appropriate diagrams where helpful. Problem 1 involves solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for a particle in a time-varying potential well. Problem 2 requires analysis of electromagnetic wave propagation in a rectangular waveguide with specific boundary conditions. Problem 3 addresses quantum tunneling through a double barrier system with calculations of transmission coefficients. Problem 4 involves electromagnetic radiation from an accelerated charged particle in the non-relativistic and relativistic limits. Problem 5 requires solution of the hydrogen atom problem including spin-orbit coupling corrections. Problem 6 addresses electromagnetic field energy and momentum in dispersive media. You may use standard reference tables for physical constants and mathematical identities, but all derivations must be shown. Partial credit will be awarded based on correct methodology even if final numerical answers are incorrect. Clearly state any assumptions made and justify approximations used. Organize your solutions clearly with problem numbers and parts labeled. Submit all work including scratch calculations as partial credit may be awarded for correct intermediate steps.
grading_notes: Grade holistically considering both technical accuracy and conceptual understanding. Award partial credit generously for correct approaches even with computational errors. Common issues to watch: incorrect boundary condition applications (deduct 5-10 points per occurrence), sign errors in quantum mechanical phases (minor deduction if physics understanding is correct), improper normalization of wavefunctions (significant conceptual error, deduct 10-15 points), confusion between electric and magnetic field units in Gaussian vs SI systems (minor if consistent). Expect grade distribution: A (90-100): 15-20% of students, B (80-89): 25-30%, C (70-79): 30-35%, D/F (<70): 15-25%. Students scoring above 95 demonstrate exceptional mastery suitable for graduate-level research. Flag solutions showing unusually sophisticated techniques for potential academic integrity review.

title: Introduction to Programming Languages and Development Tools Discussion
description: Students will engage in a structured discussion comparing different programming languages and development environments, demonstrating understanding of fundamental programming concepts and tool selection criteria for beginner-level software development projects.
estimated_time: 2-3 hours (including research, writing, and peer responses)
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify and compare basic features of popular programming languages (Python, JavaScript, Java)
Understand the role of development tools and environments in software development
Communicate technical concepts clearly using appropriate terminology
Evaluate trade-offs between different programming languages for simple projects
rubric_criteria: Language Comparison (25 points): Accurately describes syntax, ease of learning, and use cases for at least two programming languages with specific examples
Tool Understanding (25 points): Demonstrates knowledge of development environments, text editors/IDEs, and version control basics with clear explanations
Technical Communication (25 points): Uses proper programming terminology, writes clearly and coherently, provides concrete examples to support points
Peer Engagement (25 points): Provides thoughtful responses to at least two classmates, asks relevant follow-up questions, contributes meaningfully to discussion
instructions: This discussion has two parts: an initial post and peer responses. For your initial post (300-500 words), choose two programming languages from the following list: Python, JavaScript, Java, C++, or C#. Compare these languages by addressing: 1) Syntax complexity and beginner-friendliness (provide code examples showing how to print 'Hello World' and create a simple variable), 2) Common use cases and applications for each language, 3) Development tools typically used with each language (IDEs, text editors, frameworks). Then, imagine you're tasked with creating a simple calculator program. Which language would you choose and why? Support your choice with at least three specific reasons. Include one challenge you might face as a beginner using your chosen language. For peer responses (100-150 words each), respond to at least two classmates by: commenting on their language choice for the calculator project, sharing an additional use case or tool they didn't mention, or asking a thoughtful question about their reasoning. All posts must use proper programming terminology and include at least one specific example or code snippet. Submit your initial post by Wednesday 11:59 PM and complete peer responses by Friday 11:59 PM. Cite any external sources used and ensure all code examples are properly formatted.
grading_notes: Look for accurate technical information - verify that language descriptions and use cases are correct. Award full points for syntax examples only if they're properly formatted and functional. For tool understanding, students should mention at least one IDE/editor and show basic awareness of development workflow. Strong technical communication includes proper use of terms like 'syntax,' 'variable,' 'framework,' and 'IDE.' Peer responses should demonstrate engagement beyond simple agreement - look for questions, additional insights, or constructive discussion. Common issues: students confusing programming languages with markup languages, providing incorrect code examples, or making unsupported claims about language popularity. Grade distribution should typically follow: 90-100 points (exceeds expectations with exceptional detail and engagement), 80-89 points (meets all requirements adequately), 70-79 points (meets most requirements with minor gaps), below 70 points (significant missing elements or technical inaccuracies).

title: Customer Behavior Data Analysis Presentation
description: Students will analyze a real-world e-commerce customer dataset, identify key behavioral patterns and trends, and present actionable business insights through a structured presentation with visualizations and recommendations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply statistical analysis techniques to identify patterns and trends in customer behavior data
Create effective data visualizations that communicate findings to business stakeholders
Translate analytical findings into actionable business recommendations
Present data-driven insights clearly and persuasively to a non-technical audience
rubric_criteria: Data Analysis Quality (25 points): Demonstrates proper use of statistical methods, identifies meaningful patterns, shows understanding of data limitations, and draws valid conclusions from the analysis

Visualization Effectiveness (25 points): Creates clear, appropriate, and visually appealing charts/graphs that support the narrative, uses proper labeling and scaling, and follows data visualization best practices

Business Insights & Recommendations (25 points): Provides specific, actionable recommendations based on data findings, demonstrates understanding of business context, and quantifies potential impact where possible

Presentation Delivery & Structure (25 points): Maintains clear logical flow, communicates effectively to target audience, manages time well, and demonstrates confidence in presenting technical content
instructions:
You will receive a customer transaction dataset containing 12 months of e-commerce data including customer demographics, purchase history, product categories, and seasonal patterns. Your task is to conduct a comprehensive analysis and present findings in a 10-minute business presentation. 

Your presentation must include: (1) Executive summary of key findings (1-2 slides), (2) Analysis methodology and data overview (1-2 slides), (3) Three major insights with supporting visualizations (4-5 slides), (4) Business recommendations with expected outcomes (2-3 slides), and (5) Next steps and limitations (1 slide). 

Submit both your presentation file (PowerPoint/Google Slides) and a separate document containing your analysis code/calculations 24 hours before your scheduled presentation slot. Use professional formatting suitable for a business audience. Focus on storytelling with your data rather than technical details. Practice timing to ensure you can deliver within the 10-minute limit while allowing 2-3 minutes for questions. 

Your analysis should address customer segmentation, purchasing patterns, seasonal trends, and at least one predictive insight. All visualizations must include proper titles, axis labels, and data sources. Avoid technical jargon and explain statistical concepts in business terms.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy first - ensure statistical methods are appropriate and correctly applied. Look for creativity in uncovering non-obvious patterns beyond basic descriptive statistics. Assess whether visualizations enhance understanding rather than just displaying data. Strong presentations will connect multiple data points to tell a cohesive story. Grade harshly on time management - deduct points for presentations exceeding 12 minutes. Common issues include: over-reliance on correlation without considering causation, inappropriate chart types for data being presented, recommendations that don't logically follow from analysis, and failure to acknowledge data limitations. Expect grade distribution: 20% A-level (90-100), 40% B-level (80-89), 30% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. Provide specific feedback on both analytical approach and presentation skills.

title: Enterprise Digital Transformation Project Portfolio
description: Students will develop a comprehensive project management portfolio for a complex digital transformation initiative, demonstrating advanced project management competencies through real-world scenario application, stakeholder management, risk mitigation, and adaptive project governance across multiple project phases.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced project management methodologies (hybrid Agile-Waterfall) to complex organizational change initiatives
Develop comprehensive stakeholder engagement and communication strategies for enterprise-level projects
Design risk management frameworks and contingency planning for high-uncertainty project environments
Create adaptive project governance structures that balance control with organizational agility
Demonstrate proficiency in resource optimization and budget management for multi-million dollar initiatives
rubric_criteria: Project Charter & Scope Management (25 points): Comprehensive business case with quantified benefits, detailed scope statement with clear boundaries, stakeholder analysis matrix with influence-interest mapping, and well-defined success criteria with measurable KPIs. Exceptional work demonstrates strategic alignment and addresses organizational readiness.

Integrated Project Planning & Scheduling (25 points): Work breakdown structure with appropriate decomposition levels, realistic timeline using critical path method, resource allocation plan with capacity analysis, and hybrid methodology implementation strategy. Superior submissions show contingency planning and multiple scenario modeling.

Risk Management & Quality Assurance Framework (25 points): Comprehensive risk register with probability-impact analysis, detailed mitigation strategies with ownership assignment, quality management plan with defined standards and testing protocols, and change management process documentation. Excellence demonstrated through proactive risk identification and adaptive response strategies.

Stakeholder Communication & Project Governance (25 points): Multi-tiered communication plan with audience-specific messaging, project governance structure with clear decision-making authority, progress monitoring dashboard design with real-time metrics, and lessons learned documentation with improvement recommendations. Outstanding work shows evidence of stakeholder feedback integration and governance effectiveness.
instructions: Select a real or realistic digital transformation scenario (e.g., ERP implementation, cloud migration, digital customer experience overhaul) for a mid-to-large organization (1,000+ employees, $50M+ budget). Your portfolio must include: (1) Executive Project Charter (10-15 pages) with business case, stakeholder analysis, and success framework; (2) Integrated Project Plan with detailed WBS, Gantt chart, resource allocation, and hybrid Agile-Waterfall methodology implementation; (3) Risk & Quality Management Framework including risk register, mitigation strategies, and quality assurance protocols; (4) Communication & Governance Strategy with stakeholder communication matrix, escalation procedures, and project dashboard mockup; (5) Executive Summary presentation (15-20 slides) suitable for C-level audience. All documents must demonstrate professional quality suitable for actual organizational use. Include realistic budget figures, timelines, and organizational constraints. Submit as a compiled PDF portfolio with clearly labeled sections and a table of contents. Presentation slides should be submitted as a separate PowerPoint file. Cite relevant project management frameworks (PMI, PRINCE2, SAFe) and justify methodology choices. Portfolio should reflect 18-24 month project timeline with multiple phases and dependencies.
grading_notes: Evaluate portfolios based on professional presentation quality, realistic scenario development, and practical applicability. Look for evidence of critical thinking in risk assessment, stakeholder analysis depth, and methodology selection rationale. Common weaknesses include unrealistic timelines, insufficient stakeholder consideration, generic risk identification, and poor integration between portfolio components. Grade distribution expectation: 15% exceptional (90-100), 35% proficient (80-89), 35% developing (70-79), 15% inadequate (below 70). Pay particular attention to executive summary alignment with detailed documentation, evidence of iterative planning thinking, and demonstration of advanced PM concepts beyond basic tools. Deduct points for template-based approaches without customization to selected scenario.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Management Lab Report
description: Students conduct a comprehensive analysis of a real organizational crisis, evaluating leadership decisions, developing alternative strategies, and presenting evidence-based recommendations for crisis leadership improvement. This assessment integrates strategic thinking, stakeholder analysis, decision-making frameworks, and leadership theory application.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced leadership theories to analyze complex organizational challenges and crisis situations
Evaluate leadership decision-making processes using multiple analytical frameworks and stakeholder perspectives
Synthesize research evidence to develop strategic recommendations for leadership improvement in high-stakes situations
Demonstrate critical thinking skills in assessing leadership effectiveness during organizational transformations
rubric_criteria: Crisis Analysis & Context (25 points): Comprehensive examination of the crisis situation including timeline, stakeholders, environmental factors, and organizational context. Demonstrates deep understanding of complexity and systemic issues.

Leadership Theory Application (25 points): Sophisticated application of 3+ leadership theories/models to analyze decisions and behaviors. Shows clear connections between theoretical frameworks and real-world leadership actions with nuanced interpretation.
