Strategic Recommendations (25 points): Evidence-based, implementable recommendations supported by research and best practices. Includes risk assessment, resource considerations, and measurable outcomes. Addresses both immediate and long-term leadership strategies.

Research Quality & Professional Presentation (25 points): Minimum 15 credible sources including peer-reviewed articles, case studies, and expert interviews. Clear writing, proper APA formatting, executive summary, and professional report structure with visual aids.
instructions: Select a significant organizational crisis from the past 5 years (e.g., Wells Fargo account scandal, Boeing 737 MAX crisis, Equifax data breach). Your lab report must include: (1) Executive Summary (1 page), (2) Crisis Overview with timeline and stakeholder mapping (3-4 pages), (3) Leadership Analysis applying transformational, authentic, and adaptive leadership theories to evaluate key decisions (4-5 pages), (4) Alternative Strategy Development with scenario planning for different leadership approaches (3-4 pages), (5) Strategic Recommendations with implementation roadmap and success metrics (2-3 pages), and (6) Reflection on lessons learned for future leadership practice (1-2 pages). Total length: 15-20 pages plus appendices. Include at least one interview with a current leader or crisis management expert. Use APA format with minimum 15 scholarly sources. Submit electronic copy with presentation slides summarizing key findings. Due dates: Crisis selection approval (Week 1), progress check with preliminary analysis (Week 2), final submission (Week 3). Late submissions penalized 10% per day.
grading_notes: Expect grade distribution: A-level (90-100) for exceptional synthesis and original insights, B-level (80-89) for solid analysis with good theory application, C-level (70-79) for adequate work meeting basic requirements, below 70 for incomplete or superficial analysis. Watch for: oversimplified crisis explanations, weak theory-practice connections, unrealistic recommendations, insufficient research depth, and poor professional presentation. Strong submissions demonstrate systems thinking, acknowledge leadership complexity, and provide actionable insights. Deduct points for: missing components (5-10 points each), inadequate source quality, formatting issues, and failure to include expert interview. Encourage peer review sessions and office hours consultations.

title: AWS Core Services Knowledge Assessment Quiz
description: A comprehensive beginner-level quiz assessing foundational knowledge of AWS core services, basic architecture concepts, pricing models, and security fundamentals. Students will demonstrate understanding through multiple-choice questions, scenario-based problems, and short identification tasks.
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify and describe the primary functions of AWS core services (EC2, S3, RDS, VPC)
Explain basic AWS pricing models and cost optimization strategies
Demonstrate understanding of AWS security fundamentals and shared responsibility model
Apply knowledge of AWS services to simple real-world scenarios
rubric_criteria: AWS Core Services Knowledge (25 points): Correctly identifies service functions, use cases, and basic configurations for EC2, S3, RDS, and VPC services

Pricing and Cost Management Understanding (25 points): Demonstrates knowledge of AWS pricing models, cost factors, and basic optimization strategies including Reserved Instances and resource right-sizing
Security and Compliance Fundamentals (25 points): Shows understanding of AWS shared responsibility model, IAM basics, security groups, and fundamental security best practices
Scenario Application and Problem Solving (25 points): Successfully applies AWS knowledge to realistic business scenarios and selects appropriate services for given requirements
instructions:
This assessment consists of 40 questions divided into four sections, each worth 25 points. You have 45 minutes to complete the entire quiz. Read each question carefully before selecting your answer.

Section 1 (Questions 1-10): AWS Core Services - Multiple choice questions about EC2, S3, RDS, and VPC functionality, features, and use cases.

Section 2 (Questions 11-20): Pricing and Cost Management - Questions covering AWS pricing models, cost calculation scenarios, and optimization strategies.

Section 3 (Questions 21-30): Security Fundamentals - Multiple choice and true/false questions about AWS security model, IAM, and best practices.

Section 4 (Questions 31-40): Scenario-based Applications - Short scenarios requiring you to select appropriate AWS services or configurations.

Answering Guidelines: Select the BEST answer for multiple choice questions. For scenario questions, choose the most cost-effective and appropriate solution. No partial credit is given for individual questions, but partial credit may be awarded for multi-part questions. You may return to previous questions within each section before final submission. Ensure all questions are answered before submitting - unanswered questions receive zero points.
grading_notes: Grade distribution: 90-100 points = A (Excellent understanding of AWS fundamentals), 80-89 points = B (Good grasp with minor gaps), 70-79 points = C (Basic understanding, needs reinforcement), Below 70 = Needs significant review. Common issues to watch for: confusion between similar services (EBS vs EFS), misunderstanding of shared responsibility boundaries, incorrect pricing model applications. Most students should score 75-85 points. Flag scores below 60 for additional support. Pay attention to Section 4 performance as it indicates practical application ability. Provide feedback on specific weak areas based on section performance.

title: Advanced Google Analytics Implementation and Analysis Exam
description: Comprehensive assessment evaluating advanced Google Analytics skills including custom tracking implementation, complex data analysis, attribution modeling, and strategic insights development for e-commerce optimization.
learning_objectives_assessed: Implement advanced tracking configurations including enhanced e-commerce and custom dimensions
Perform complex data analysis using advanced segments, custom reports, and attribution modeling
Interpret cross-channel attribution data and make strategic recommendations
Design measurement frameworks aligned with business objectives
Troubleshoot tracking issues and validate data accuracy
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation (25 points): Accurately configures enhanced e-commerce tracking, custom dimensions, and event tracking with proper parameter setup and data layer implementation

Advanced Analysis & Reporting (25 points): Creates sophisticated custom reports using advanced segments, applies appropriate attribution models, and demonstrates proficiency with calculated metrics and cohort analysis

Strategic Insights & Recommendations (25 points): Provides actionable, data-driven recommendations based on comprehensive analysis, identifies optimization opportunities, and connects insights to business impact

Data Validation & Quality Assurance (25 points): Demonstrates systematic approach to data verification, identifies potential tracking issues, explains data discrepancies, and proposes solutions for measurement gaps
instructions:
You are the digital marketing analyst for TechGear Pro, an e-commerce company selling electronics. Using the provided Google Analytics demo account and scenario data, complete the following tasks within 3 hours:

**Part 1: Implementation Planning (45 minutes)**
Design a comprehensive tracking implementation for a new product line launch. Include: enhanced e-commerce setup, 3 custom dimensions for customer segmentation, goal configurations for micro and macro conversions, and event tracking for video engagement and newsletter signups. Document your implementation plan with specific parameter names and trigger conditions.

**Part 2: Advanced Analysis (90 minutes)**
Using the provided 6-month dataset, create a comprehensive performance analysis including: customer acquisition cost analysis by channel using attribution modeling, cohort analysis showing customer lifetime value trends, advanced segments comparing high-value vs. low-value customers, and identification of conversion funnel drop-off points with quantified impact.

**Part 3: Strategic Recommendations (45 minutes)**
Prepare an executive summary with 5 specific, data-driven recommendations for improving ROI. Each recommendation must include supporting metrics, expected impact quantification, implementation timeline, and success measurement criteria. Address attribution insights, audience optimization, and conversion rate improvement opportunities.

**Submission Requirements:**
Submit a PDF report (8-10 pages) including screenshots of your configurations, data visualizations, detailed analysis, and strategic recommendations. Include a separate Excel file with your raw data extractions and calculations. Ensure all work shows formulas and methodology for verification.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy by verifying tracking setup against Google Analytics best practices - deduct 5 points per implementation error. For analysis section, assess methodology rigor and statistical validity - students should demonstrate understanding of attribution model differences and segment logic. Strategic recommendations should be SMART (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound) - vague suggestions receive partial credit only. Common issues include: confusing correlation with causation, ignoring statistical significance, incomplete data validation steps. Grade distribution expectation: 15% A-level (90-100), 30% B-level (80-89), 40% C-level (70-79), 15% below C-level. Partial credit available for each rubric criterion - award points proportionally for incomplete but methodologically sound work.

title: Enterprise Network Convergence Strategy: Campus-to-WAN Integration Analysis
description: Students will analyze and propose solutions for integrating a multi-campus enterprise network with SD-WAN deployment, addressing routing protocols, QoS implementation, security policies, and network automation strategies. This expert-level discussion requires deep understanding of Cisco enterprise technologies and real-world implementation challenges.
estimated_time: 4-6 hours research and composition, plus 2-3 hours for peer responses
learning_objectives_assessed: Evaluate complex routing protocol interactions in enterprise environments (EIGRP, OSPF, BGP)
Design comprehensive QoS strategies for voice, video, and data convergence
Analyze SD-WAN integration with traditional campus infrastructure
Assess network security policy implementation across distributed environments
Demonstrate advanced troubleshooting methodologies for enterprise networks
rubric_criteria: Technical Architecture Analysis (25 points): Demonstrates expert understanding of routing protocols, network segmentation, and infrastructure design. Accurately identifies technical challenges and dependencies. Shows mastery of Cisco IOS-XE, SD-WAN, and campus switching technologies.

QoS and Traffic Engineering Strategy (25 points): Provides comprehensive QoS design including classification, marking, queuing, and shaping strategies. Addresses bandwidth allocation, traffic prioritization, and congestion management across campus and WAN segments.

Security and Policy Integration (25 points): Develops cohesive security framework incorporating ISE, firewall policies, VPN technologies, and network segmentation. Addresses compliance requirements and threat mitigation strategies.

Implementation Planning and Automation (25 points): Creates realistic migration plan with risk assessment, rollback procedures, and timeline. Incorporates network automation tools (DNA Center, Python, APIs) and demonstrates understanding of operational challenges.
instructions: You are the senior network architect for a Fortune 500 company planning to modernize their network infrastructure. The organization has three campus locations connected via MPLS, with plans to implement Cisco SD-WAN while maintaining campus LAN functionality. Your task is to create a comprehensive analysis and recommendation document (1500-2000 words) addressing the following components: 1) Current State Analysis: Examine the existing network topology, identifying routing protocols in use, current QoS implementations, and security policies. Discuss limitations and performance bottlenecks. 2) SD-WAN Integration Strategy: Design the integration approach for Cisco SD-WAN (vManage, vSmart, vEdge/cEdge). Address routing protocol redistribution, policy migration, and hybrid connectivity scenarios. 3) QoS Redesign: Develop a comprehensive QoS strategy supporting voice (20%), video (30%), and data (50%) traffic across the converged network. Include specific Cisco QoS mechanisms and configuration considerations. 4) Security Framework: Design security policies incorporating Cisco ISE, next-generation firewalls, and encrypted transport. Address microsegmentation and zero-trust principles. 5) Automation and Monitoring: Recommend network automation strategies using DNA Center, Python scripting, and API integration. Include monitoring and troubleshooting approaches. Support all recommendations with specific Cisco technologies, configuration examples, and industry best practices. After posting your initial analysis, provide substantive responses to two peers, focusing on alternative approaches or identifying potential implementation challenges they may have overlooked.
grading_notes: Look for expert-level technical depth rather than surface-level descriptions. Students should demonstrate hands-on experience with Cisco technologies through specific configuration examples and realistic implementation challenges. Deduct points for generic networking concepts without Cisco-specific implementation details. Exceptional responses will include actual CLI examples, specific feature references (like IWAN vs SD-WAN migration paths), and demonstrate understanding of enterprise-scale considerations. Peer responses should add technical value, not merely agree with original posts. Watch for unrealistic timelines or oversimplified security approaches. Grade distribution should reflect expert-level expectations: 90-100 (expert demonstration), 80-89 (proficient with minor gaps), 70-79 (adequate but missing depth), below 70 (insufficient technical expertise demonstrated).

title: Customer Churn Prediction: End-to-End Data Science Portfolio Project
description: Students will complete a comprehensive data science project analyzing customer churn for a telecommunications company, demonstrating proficiency in data exploration, preprocessing, modeling, and business communication through a complete analytical workflow and presentation.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply exploratory data analysis techniques to identify patterns and insights in real-world datasets
Implement appropriate data preprocessing and feature engineering strategies
Build, evaluate, and compare multiple machine learning models for classification problems
Communicate technical findings effectively to both technical and business audiences
rubric_criteria: Data Exploration & Visualization (25 points): Comprehensive EDA with meaningful visualizations, statistical summaries, identification of data quality issues, and clear documentation of findings and patterns

Data Preprocessing & Feature Engineering (25 points): Appropriate handling of missing values, outliers, and categorical variables; creation of relevant features; proper data splitting and scaling techniques with clear justification

Model Development & Evaluation (25 points): Implementation of at least 3 different algorithms, proper cross-validation, comprehensive performance metrics, hyperparameter tuning, and model comparison with business context

Communication & Documentation (25 points): Clear executive summary, well-structured Jupyter notebook with markdown explanations, professional presentation slides, and actionable business recommendations
instructions: Using the provided telecommunications customer dataset, create a complete portfolio project predicting customer churn. Your submission must include: 1) A Jupyter notebook containing your complete analysis workflow with proper markdown documentation explaining your methodology and findings at each step. 2) An executive summary (2-3 pages) written for business stakeholders, including problem context, key insights, model recommendations, and proposed retention strategies. 3) A presentation (10-12 slides) suitable for presenting to company leadership. Your analysis should demonstrate the full data science pipeline: start with comprehensive exploratory data analysis including univariate, bivariate, and multivariate analysis with appropriate visualizations. Address all data quality issues through appropriate preprocessing techniques. Engineer at least 3 meaningful features that could improve model performance. Implement and compare at least three different classification algorithms (suggested: logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting). Use proper evaluation metrics including precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC, considering the business impact of false positives vs false negatives. Provide feature importance analysis and model interpretability. Submit all files in a single ZIP folder named 'LastName_FirstName_ChurnProject' containing your notebook (.ipynb), executive summary (.pdf), presentation slides (.pdf), and any additional code files. Ensure your notebook runs completely from start to finish without errors.
grading_notes: Evaluate notebooks for code quality, proper use of libraries (pandas, scikit-learn, matplotlib/seaborn), and statistical rigor. Look for evidence of iterative improvement and testing of assumptions. Common issues include inadequate EDA depth, inappropriate handling of class imbalance, overfitting, and weak business context. Expect grade distribution: 15% A grades (90-100), 35% B grades (80-89), 40% C grades (70-79), 10% below 70%. Deduct points for notebooks that don't run, missing visualizations, or purely technical communication without business insight. Reward creativity in feature engineering and thorough model validation approaches.

title: Statistical Analysis and Probability Modeling Lab Report
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive statistical investigation using real-world data, applying advanced probability distributions, hypothesis testing, and regression analysis to solve a complex problem and communicate findings through a formal lab report.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced probability distributions (normal, binomial, Poisson) to model real-world phenomena
Conduct hypothesis testing using appropriate statistical methods and interpret results
Perform regression analysis and evaluate model validity
Communicate mathematical findings clearly through written reports with proper statistical notation
rubric_criteria: Data Analysis and Mathematical Methods (25 points): Correct application of statistical techniques, appropriate choice of probability distributions, accurate calculations, proper use of mathematical notation and formulas

Hypothesis Testing and Inference (25 points): Clear statement of null/alternative hypotheses, correct test selection, accurate p-value interpretation, valid conclusions with appropriate confidence levels
Model Development and Validation (25 points): Appropriate regression model construction, residual analysis, R-squared interpretation, assessment of model assumptions and limitations
Communication and Presentation (25 points): Clear problem statement, logical organization, proper graphs/tables with labels, professional formatting, correct grammar and mathematical notation
instructions: Select a dataset from the provided options (housing prices, sports statistics, or economic indicators) containing at least 100 observations and 5 variables. Your lab report must include: (1) Introduction identifying the research question and relevant variables, (2) Exploratory Data Analysis section with descriptive statistics, appropriate graphs, and identification of probability distributions that model your key variables, (3) Hypothesis Testing section where you formulate and test at least two hypotheses using t-tests, chi-square tests, or ANOVA as appropriate, (4) Regression Analysis section developing a multiple regression model to predict your dependent variable, including residual plots and model diagnostics, (5) Results and Conclusions section interpreting all findings in context with discussion of limitations. Use statistical software (R, Python, or Excel) for calculations but show key formulas and steps. Include all code in an appendix. Format as a professional report with title page, numbered sections, labeled figures/tables, and references. Submit as PDF with accompanying data file and code. Report should be 8-12 pages including graphs and tables. Due in two weeks with optional draft feedback available after one week.
grading_notes: Look for mathematical rigor in statistical method selection - students should justify why they chose specific tests and models. Common errors include: incorrect hypothesis formulations, misinterpreting p-values as probability of hypothesis being true, ignoring regression assumptions, and poor graph design. Expect 15% A grades for exceptional insight and methodology, 35% B grades for solid technical work with minor errors, 40% C grades for adequate completion with some conceptual mistakes, 10% below C for major methodological flaws. Partial credit available for each criterion - give credit for correct setup even if final calculations contain errors. Emphasize that statistical conclusions must relate back to real-world context.

title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics and Electrodynamics Comprehensive Quiz
description: Expert-level assessment covering quantum field theory fundamentals, relativistic quantum mechanics, advanced electromagnetic field interactions, and mathematical formalism applications. Students will demonstrate mastery of complex theoretical concepts and problem-solving techniques at graduate level.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply quantum field theory operators and commutation relations to solve multi-particle systems
Analyze relativistic quantum mechanical phenomena using Dirac equation and spinor formalism
Calculate electromagnetic field interactions in curved spacetime using tensor calculus
Evaluate symmetry principles and conservation laws in advanced quantum systems
Derive and interpret solutions to Klein-Gordon and Dirac equations in various potentials
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Rigor and Formalism (25 points): Correct application of advanced mathematical techniques including tensor notation, operator algebra, Green's functions, and perturbation theory. Proper use of units and dimensional analysis throughout solutions.

Physical Interpretation and Conceptual Understanding (25 points): Accurate explanation of quantum phenomena, field interactions, and relativistic effects. Clear connection between mathematical results and physical reality, including discussion of measurement implications and uncertainty principles.

Problem-Solving Methodology (25 points): Systematic approach to complex multi-step problems, appropriate approximation techniques, limiting case analysis, and verification of results through alternative methods or physical reasoning.

Communication and Presentation (25 points): Clear, logical organization of solutions with proper scientific notation, well-labeled diagrams where applicable, and concise yet complete explanations of reasoning. Professional presentation of mathematical derivations.
instructions: This comprehensive quiz consists of 8 problems covering quantum field theory, relativistic quantum mechanics, and advanced electrodynamics. You have 3 hours to complete all sections. Show all mathematical work including intermediate steps, clearly state assumptions, and provide physical interpretations for your results. Use proper scientific notation and include appropriate units in all final answers. For derivations, begin with fundamental principles and clearly indicate each mathematical manipulation. When making approximations, justify their validity and discuss limitations. Partial credit will be awarded based on methodology and understanding demonstrated, even if final numerical answers are incorrect. You may use standard reference materials including fundamental constants, but programmable calculators or computational software are prohibited. Organize your solutions clearly with problem numbers prominently displayed. If you cannot complete a particular step, state your approach and continue with assumed results to demonstrate understanding of subsequent concepts. Include brief physical interpretations explaining the significance of your mathematical results. Submit all work on provided answer sheets with your name and student ID clearly marked on each page.
grading_notes: Grade distribution should target: A (90-100): 15-20%, B (80-89): 25-30%, C (70-79): 30-35%, D (60-69): 15-20%, F (<60): 5-10%. Award partial credit generously for correct methodology even with computational errors. Look for proper use of quantum mechanical formalism, appropriate boundary conditions, and physically reasonable results. Common issues include: incorrect normalization of wavefunctions, sign errors in relativistic calculations, dimensional inconsistencies, and misapplication of perturbation theory. Students often struggle with proper tensor index notation and may confuse coordinate vs momentum space representations. Emphasize that physical interpretation carries significant weight - purely mathematical solutions without physics insight should receive reduced marks. Time management is crucial; students attempting all problems with reasonable approaches should score higher than those providing perfect solutions to only half the quiz.

title: Complex Stakeholder Crisis Management Discussion: Navigating Multi-Organizational Project Conflicts
description: Students will analyze and propose comprehensive solutions for a complex multi-stakeholder project crisis scenario involving conflicting organizational priorities, resource constraints, and regulatory pressures. This assessment evaluates advanced stakeholder management, risk mitigation, and strategic decision-making capabilities.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate advanced stakeholder analysis and engagement strategies in complex organizational environments
Apply sophisticated conflict resolution and negotiation techniques to multi-party project disputes
Synthesize risk management frameworks with change management principles under crisis conditions
Evaluate and recommend strategic project recovery options considering organizational, financial, and regulatory constraints
rubric_criteria: Stakeholder Analysis & Mapping (25 points): Comprehensive identification and categorization of all stakeholders, accurate assessment of their influence/interest matrix, clear analysis of power dynamics, coalitions, and hidden agendas. Demonstrates understanding of stakeholder interdependencies and secondary impacts.

Crisis Response Strategy (25 points): Develops a coherent, multi-phase crisis response plan with specific actions, timelines, and contingencies. Shows evidence of risk-based prioritization, resource optimization, and consideration of both immediate stabilization and long-term recovery objectives.

Conflict Resolution & Negotiation Approach (25 points): Proposes specific negotiation strategies tailored to different stakeholder groups, identifies win-win opportunities, addresses underlying interests beyond stated positions, and provides realistic compromise solutions that maintain project viability.

Implementation Feasibility & Change Management (25 points): Presents actionable implementation steps with consideration of organizational change impacts, communication strategies, resistance management, and success metrics. Demonstrates understanding of project governance and escalation procedures.
instructions: You are the newly appointed project manager for a $50M digital transformation initiative involving three organizations: a government agency, a private technology vendor, and a consulting firm. The project is 18 months into a 24-month timeline when multiple crises emerge simultaneously: the government agency faces budget cuts requiring 30% cost reduction, the technology vendor's key personnel have left mid-project creating knowledge gaps, and new regulatory requirements mandate additional security features not in the original scope. Additionally, the consulting firm is threatening contract termination due to unpaid invoices, and end-users are resisting the new system after pilot testing revealed usability issues. Your response must address: (1) Complete stakeholder analysis including influence/interest mapping and identification of potential allies and opponents, (2) Prioritized crisis response strategy with specific 30/60/90-day action plans, (3) Detailed conflict resolution approach for each major stakeholder dispute, including negotiation strategies and compromise positions, (4) Implementation roadmap for your recommended solutions, including change management tactics and communication plan. Format your response as a structured executive briefing (1,500-2,000 words) with clear sections, bullet points for key actions, and supporting rationale for each major recommendation. Include at least three alternative scenarios with different risk/benefit profiles. Submit as a single document with appendices for stakeholder matrices and timeline visualizations.
grading_notes: Evaluate responses for depth of systems thinking rather than simple problem-solving. Look for evidence of advanced project management frameworks (e.g., PRINCE2, PMBOK conflict resolution processes). Excellent responses will demonstrate understanding that this is fundamentally a stakeholder alignment challenge requiring political sensitivity. Common weaknesses include: oversimplified stakeholder analysis missing secondary stakeholders, crisis responses that don't address root causes, generic conflict resolution approaches not tailored to specific stakeholder types, and implementation plans lacking change management sophistication. Grade distribution expectation: 10-15% A-level responses showing exceptional strategic thinking and practical feasibility, 30-40% B-level responses with solid analysis but missing some nuances, remainder showing basic competency but lacking advanced integration of concepts.

title: Strategic Leadership Vision and Change Management Presentation
description: Students will deliver a comprehensive 20-minute presentation analyzing a real-world organizational challenge and proposing a strategic leadership solution, demonstrating advanced leadership theory application, change management expertise, and executive communication skills.
estimated_time: 40 hours preparation + 20 minutes presentation + 10 minutes Q&A
learning_objectives_assessed: Synthesize complex leadership theories to address multifaceted organizational challenges
Develop and articulate strategic vision with measurable outcomes and implementation roadmaps
Demonstrate executive-level communication and stakeholder engagement skills
Apply change management frameworks to lead organizational transformation initiatives
rubric_criteria: Strategic Analysis & Problem Definition (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of organizational context, stakeholder dynamics, and systemic challenges. Uses multiple analytical frameworks effectively. Clearly articulates root causes versus symptoms.

Leadership Solution Design (25 points): Proposes innovative, evidence-based leadership intervention with clear theoretical foundation. Addresses multiple organizational levels. Includes risk mitigation strategies and contingency planning.

Implementation Strategy & Change Management (25 points): Develops detailed implementation roadmap with specific timelines, resource requirements, and success metrics. Applies advanced change management models. Addresses resistance and cultural factors comprehensively.

Executive Presentation & Communication (25 points): Delivers compelling, boardroom-quality presentation with executive presence. Uses sophisticated visual aids effectively. Handles challenging questions with expertise. Demonstrates authentic leadership style.
instructions: Select a current organizational challenge from a Fortune 500 company, government agency, or major nonprofit (within last 3 years). Your presentation must include: (1) Comprehensive situational analysis using minimum three leadership frameworks (e.g., Kotter's 8-Step Process, ADKAR, Systems Theory); (2) Strategic leadership solution addressing vision, culture, and operational dimensions; (3) Detailed 18-month implementation plan with specific milestones, KPIs, and resource allocation; (4) Stakeholder communication strategy and change management approach; (5) Risk assessment and mitigation strategies. Format requirements: Professional slide deck (15-20 slides), executive summary handout (2 pages), and appendices with supporting data. Presentation style should mirror C-suite executive briefing. Dress professionally. Submit materials 48 hours prior to presentation date. Be prepared for rigorous Q&A from instructor and peer panel acting as board of directors. Sources must include peer-reviewed research, industry reports, and primary organizational data. Minimum 15 academic references required.
grading_notes: Evaluate presentations against executive-level standards, not typical academic presentations. Look for: sophisticated business acumen, ability to synthesize complex information quickly, authentic leadership presence, and practical implementability of solutions. Common weaknesses include: superficial analysis lacking systems thinking, generic solutions not tailored to specific context, unrealistic timelines or budgets, poor handling of challenging questions. Grade distribution typically: 15% A-level (exceptional executive potential), 35% B-level (strong leadership capability), 40% C-level (adequate but needs development), 10% below C (significant gaps). During Q&A, probe for depth of understanding beyond prepared content. Assess ability to think strategically under pressure and adapt communication style to audience concerns.

title: AWS Three-Tier Web Application Portfolio Project
description: Students will design, deploy, and document a complete three-tier web application on AWS using core services including EC2, RDS, S3, and VPC. This portfolio project demonstrates practical application of fundamental AWS cloud computing concepts through hands-on implementation and professional documentation.
learning_objectives_assessed: Deploy and configure AWS EC2 instances with proper security groups and networking
Implement AWS RDS database services with appropriate backup and security configurations
Utilize AWS S3 for static content hosting and storage management
Design and implement VPC networking with public and private subnets
Apply AWS security best practices including IAM roles and access management
Document cloud architecture decisions and demonstrate cost optimization awareness
rubric_criteria: Infrastructure Implementation (25 points): Successful deployment of all required AWS services (EC2 web server, RDS database, S3 bucket, VPC with subnets) with proper configuration and connectivity between tiers

Security Configuration (25 points): Proper implementation of security groups, IAM roles, database security, and network ACLs following AWS security best practices with no unnecessary open ports or permissions
Documentation Quality (25 points): Comprehensive architecture diagram, clear setup instructions, troubleshooting notes, and professional presentation of technical decisions and configurations

Cost Optimization & Analysis (25 points): Demonstrated use of AWS Free Tier resources, accurate cost estimation using AWS Calculator, and identification of at least three cost optimization strategies with justification
instructions: Create a three-tier web application portfolio demonstrating AWS fundamentals. Your submission must include: 1) A functional web application with presentation tier (EC2 instance running web server), application tier (EC2 instance for application logic), and data tier (RDS MySQL/PostgreSQL database). 2) Use S3 for static content storage (images, CSS, JS files). 3) Configure VPC with public subnet for web tier and private subnet for database tier. 4) Implement proper security groups allowing only necessary traffic between tiers. 5) Create IAM role for EC2 instances to access S3. Submit a portfolio document (PDF, 8-12 pages) containing: architecture diagram showing all AWS services and connections, step-by-step deployment guide with screenshots, security configuration details, AWS cost analysis with monthly estimates, reflection on challenges faced and solutions implemented, and cleanup procedures. Include links to your deployed application and provide AWS account screenshots showing active resources. Ensure all resources use AWS Free Tier eligible services. Applications can be simple (e.g., basic CRUD operations, contact form, or blog) but must demonstrate inter-tier communication. Document any deviations from requirements with justification.
grading_notes: Verify students can provide live demonstration or screenshots proving deployment success. Check that security groups follow principle of least privilege - deduct points for overly permissive rules like 0.0.0.0/0 on non-web ports. Architecture diagrams should show clear data flow and proper subnet isolation. Cost analysis should be realistic and show understanding of AWS pricing model. Common issues include: improper VPC configuration preventing internet access, database connectivity problems due to security group misconfigurations, and excessive costs from choosing non-Free-Tier resources. Grade distribution expectation: 20% excellent (90-100), 50% proficient (75-89), 25% developing (60-74), 5% inadequate (below 60). Provide partial credit for attempted implementations even if not fully functional, but require complete documentation regardless of technical success level.

title: Project Risk Management Lab: Risk Register Development and Monte Carlo Analysis
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive risk analysis for a provided project scenario, developing a complete risk register, performing qualitative and quantitative risk analysis, and creating risk response strategies with Monte Carlo simulation results.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply risk identification techniques to develop comprehensive risk registers
Perform qualitative and quantitative risk analysis using PMP methodologies
Design appropriate risk response strategies aligned with organizational risk tolerance
Utilize Monte Carlo simulation tools for schedule and cost risk analysis
rubric_criteria: Risk Identification and Register (25 points): Complete identification of minimum 15 risks across all knowledge areas, proper risk categorization using RBS, clear risk descriptions with triggers and causes

Qualitative Risk Analysis (25 points): Accurate probability and impact assessments, proper risk prioritization matrix, risk categorization by urgency and proximity, thorough risk data quality assessment

Quantitative Risk Analysis (25 points): Correct Monte Carlo simulation setup and execution, appropriate probability distributions applied, accurate interpretation of simulation results, confidence interval analysis
Risk Response Planning (25 points): Appropriate response strategies for high-priority risks, realistic contingency plans, clear assignment of risk owners, integration with project schedule and budget
instructions: You are the project manager for a 12-month software development project with a $2.5M budget. Using the provided project charter and WBS, complete the following deliverables: 1) Develop a comprehensive risk register identifying at least 15 risks across technical, schedule, cost, resource, and external categories. Include risk ID, description, category, triggers, probability (1-5 scale), impact (1-5 scale), and risk score. 2) Conduct qualitative analysis by creating a probability-impact matrix, prioritizing risks, and assessing data quality. Document your assessment methodology and assumptions. 3) Perform quantitative analysis on the top 5 risks using Monte Carlo simulation (minimum 1000 iterations). Analyze impact on schedule and budget, providing confidence intervals and recommendations. Use Excel, @RISK, or Crystal Ball. Include screenshots of your simulation setup and results. 4) Develop response strategies for all high-priority risks (risk score ≥15). Specify response type (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept), action plans, responsible parties, timeline, and budget impact. Submit a professional report (8-12 pages) with executive summary, methodology, findings, recommendations, and appendices containing your risk register and simulation outputs. Include references to PMBOK Guide processes and tools used.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy of risk analysis techniques and adherence to PMBOK standards. Common issues include: incomplete risk identification (missing obvious technical or stakeholder risks), incorrect probability/impact scaling, poorly configured Monte Carlo simulations, and unrealistic response strategies. Excellent submissions (90-100) demonstrate comprehensive risk thinking, sophisticated quantitative analysis, and practical response strategies. Good submissions (80-89) show solid technique with minor gaps. Average submissions (70-79) meet basic requirements but lack depth or contain technical errors. Below 70 indicates significant methodological problems or incomplete work. Expect 20% A-level, 50% B-level, 30% C-level distribution.

title: Enterprise Network Design and Implementation with OSPF and BGP Integration
description: Students will design, configure, and document a complete enterprise network infrastructure incorporating multi-area OSPF, eBGP peering, VLANs, redundancy protocols, and security policies. This capstone project demonstrates mastery of advanced routing protocols, network segmentation, and enterprise-grade network design principles.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design scalable enterprise network topologies with proper hierarchical structure and redundancy
Configure and optimize multi-area OSPF routing with area summarization and stub areas
Implement eBGP peering with ISPs including route filtering and path manipulation
Deploy advanced VLAN configurations with inter-VLAN routing and spanning tree protocols
Apply comprehensive security policies including ACLs, port security, and DHCP snooping
Create professional network documentation and disaster recovery procedures
rubric_criteria: Network Design and Architecture (25 points): Logical topology design with proper IP addressing scheme (VLSM), redundant paths, hierarchical structure (core/distribution/access), and scalability considerations. Must include network diagrams with all device interconnections and IP assignments.

Routing Protocol Implementation (25 points): Correct configuration of multi-area OSPF with at least 3 areas including backbone area, proper area types (stub/NSSA), route summarization, and eBGP configuration with two ISP connections including route filtering and local preference settings.

VLAN and Switching Configuration (25 points): Implementation of at least 6 VLANs with proper trunking, RSTP configuration, inter-VLAN routing via Layer 3 switches or router-on-a-stick, port security, and DHCP snooping across the switching infrastructure.

Security Implementation and Documentation (25 points): Comprehensive security policies including standard and extended ACLs, network device hardening, backup configurations, detailed network documentation with IP address tables, and disaster recovery procedures with step-by-step restoration processes.
instructions: Design and implement a complete enterprise network for a multi-building corporate campus supporting 500+ users. Your solution must include: (1) Core network with redundant Layer 3 switches using HSRP/VRRP, (2) Multi-area OSPF design with backbone area 0 and at least two additional areas, one configured as stub area, (3) Dual ISP connectivity using eBGP with route filtering and traffic engineering, (4) Six VLANs minimum (Management, Sales, Engineering, Guest, Servers, DMZ) with appropriate IP addressing using VLSM, (5) RSTP implementation across all switches with proper root bridge selection, (6) Security implementation including ACLs controlling inter-VLAN traffic, port security on access ports, and DHCP snooping. Deliverables: Complete Packet Tracer file (.pkt) demonstrating all functionality, detailed network documentation including topology diagrams, IP addressing tables, routing tables, and VLAN assignments, configuration files for all network devices with comments explaining critical configurations, security policy document outlining all implemented security measures, disaster recovery plan with step-by-step procedures for network restoration. Submit all files in a compressed folder named 'LastName_NetworkProject.zip'. All devices must be properly configured and functional - include screenshots proving connectivity between all VLANs and external connectivity through both ISP connections.
grading_notes: Evaluate using actual Packet Tracer simulation - test all connectivity paths and verify routing tables. Common issues include: improper OSPF area configurations leading to routing failures, incorrect BGP neighbor relationships, misconfigured VLAN trunking causing connectivity issues, and inadequate ACL implementation. Grade distribution expectation: 15% should receive 90+ points, 70% should receive 75-89 points, 15% below 75 points. Deduct points heavily for non-functional configurations. Award bonus points (up to 5) for advanced features like QoS implementation, IPv6 dual-stack, or network automation scripts. Documentation quality is critical - poorly documented networks should not exceed 80 points regardless of technical implementation. Verify all routing protocols are working correctly by checking routing tables and performing traceroutes between distant networks.

title: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Business Problem Solving
description: Students will engage in a structured discussion analyzing the appropriateness, trade-offs, and implementation considerations of different machine learning algorithms for specific business scenarios. This assessment evaluates critical thinking, technical understanding, and communication skills in data science contexts.
learning_objectives_assessed: Evaluate and compare different machine learning algorithms based on problem requirements and constraints
Analyze bias-variance trade-offs and model performance metrics in practical contexts
Communicate technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Apply ethical considerations and business constraints to model selection decisions
rubric_criteria: Technical Accuracy (25 points): Demonstrates correct understanding of algorithm characteristics, assumptions, strengths, and limitations. Uses appropriate technical terminology and shows clear comprehension of model mechanics.

Critical Analysis (25 points): Provides thoughtful comparison of alternatives, considers multiple evaluation criteria, addresses trade-offs, and demonstrates analytical depth beyond surface-level observations.

Business Application (25 points): Effectively connects technical concepts to real-world constraints, considers implementation challenges, addresses stakeholder needs, and incorporates practical considerations like interpretability and scalability.

Communication and Engagement (25 points): Presents ideas clearly and coherently, responds thoughtfully to peers' contributions, asks insightful questions, and maintains professional discussion standards throughout the assessment period.
instructions: You will participate in a moderated online discussion analyzing machine learning model selection for three distinct business scenarios: (1) fraud detection for a financial institution, (2) customer churn prediction for a subscription service, and (3) demand forecasting for a retail chain. For each scenario, you must: initially post a 300-400 word analysis recommending your preferred algorithm choice, justifying your selection based on technical requirements, business constraints, and ethical considerations. Include discussion of at least two alternative approaches and explain why you rejected them. Respond substantively to at least three peers' posts, engaging with their reasoning and providing constructive feedback or alternative perspectives. Your responses should be 150-200 words each and demonstrate critical engagement rather than simple agreement. Address practical implementation challenges such as data quality requirements, computational resources, interpretability needs, and potential biases. Consider business factors including time-to-deployment, maintenance requirements, regulatory compliance, and stakeholder buy-in. All posts must be supported by specific examples and demonstrate understanding of algorithm assumptions and limitations. Initial posts are due by Wednesday 11:59 PM, with peer responses required by Sunday 11:59 PM. Use proper citation format for any external resources referenced.
grading_notes: Evaluate initial posts for depth of technical understanding and quality of business reasoning - avoid penalizing creative approaches if well-justified. Look for evidence that students understand algorithm assumptions and can articulate why certain models fit specific contexts. In peer responses, assess whether students engage meaningfully with others' ideas rather than simply restating their own positions. Common issues include: oversimplifying algorithm selection, ignoring business constraints, failing to address ethical considerations, and providing superficial peer responses. Expect grade distribution around: 20% A-level (90-100), 50% B-level (80-89), 25% C-level (70-79), 5% below 70. Partial credit available for posts that show good technical understanding but lack business application, or vice versa.

title: Advanced Mathematical Modeling: Real-World Optimization Problem Presentation
description: Students will identify, analyze, and solve a complex real-world optimization problem using advanced mathematical techniques, then present their complete solution methodology and findings to demonstrate mastery of mathematical modeling, calculus-based optimization, and mathematical communication.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced calculus concepts (multivariable calculus, differential equations) to solve real-world problems
Construct and validate mathematical models for complex optimization scenarios
Demonstrate proficiency in constraint optimization using Lagrange multipliers or linear programming
Communicate mathematical reasoning and solutions clearly to both mathematical and non-mathematical audiences
Analyze the validity and limitations of mathematical models in practical applications
rubric_criteria: Problem Selection and Mathematical Modeling (25 points): Quality of real-world problem chosen, appropriateness of mathematical model developed, clear identification of variables, constraints, and objective function

Mathematical Solution and Techniques (25 points): Correct application of advanced mathematical methods, accurate calculations, appropriate use of calculus-based optimization techniques, mathematical rigor and notation
Analysis and Validation (25 points): Critical evaluation of solution reasonableness, sensitivity analysis, discussion of model limitations, consideration of alternative approaches or assumptions

Presentation and Communication (25 points): Clear verbal explanation of mathematical concepts, effective use of visual aids, ability to answer questions, appropriate pacing and organization, accessibility to audience
instructions: Select a real-world optimization problem from fields such as economics, engineering, environmental science, or business operations. Your problem must require advanced mathematical techniques beyond basic algebra. Develop a mathematical model with at least three variables and multiple constraints. Your 15-minute presentation must include: (1) Problem context and significance, (2) Mathematical model formulation with clearly defined variables, constraints, and objective function, (3) Solution methodology showing all mathematical work, (4) Numerical or analytical solution with complete calculations, (5) Interpretation of results in the original context, (6) Critical analysis of model assumptions and limitations. Prepare visual aids including graphs, equations, and solution summaries. Submit a 2-page written summary 24 hours before your presentation. Be prepared to answer mathematical questions about your approach and defend your modeling choices. Examples of suitable problems include: optimizing shipping routes with capacity constraints, maximizing profit with resource limitations, minimizing environmental impact while meeting production goals, or optimizing investment portfolios with risk constraints.
grading_notes: Expect wide variation in problem complexity - ensure mathematical rigor is maintained regardless of topic choice. Common weaknesses include: inadequate constraint identification, computational errors in optimization, failure to validate solutions, and inability to explain mathematical reasoning clearly. Strong presentations will demonstrate clear understanding of both mathematical theory and practical applications. Grade distribution should reflect: A-level work shows exceptional mathematical insight and communication; B-level demonstrates solid mathematical competency with minor gaps; C-level shows basic understanding but may have computational or conceptual errors; below C indicates insufficient mathematical rigor or major solution flaws. Pay particular attention to students' ability to handle questions about their mathematical choices and alternative solution methods.

title: Advanced Physics Research Portfolio: Quantum Mechanics Applications
description: Students will compile a comprehensive portfolio demonstrating mastery of quantum mechanics principles through original research, mathematical derivations, experimental design, and real-world applications. The portfolio showcases deep understanding of wave-particle duality, uncertainty principles, quantum tunneling, and modern quantum technologies.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply quantum mechanical principles to solve complex, multi-step problems involving wave functions, operators, and probability distributions
Analyze and interpret quantum phenomena using mathematical formalism and physical intuition
Design theoretical experiments to test quantum mechanical predictions and evaluate measurement limitations
Synthesize connections between quantum mechanics and cutting-edge technologies in computing, cryptography, and materials science
Communicate complex quantum concepts clearly through written analysis, mathematical derivations, and visual representations
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Rigor and Problem-Solving (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated use of quantum mechanical formalism, including accurate wave function calculations, eigenvalue problems, and uncertainty principle applications. Solutions show clear methodology, proper mathematical notation, and correct physical interpretations.

Experimental Design and Analysis (25 points): Proposes feasible quantum experiments with detailed methodology, identifies key variables and controls, addresses measurement challenges, and predicts realistic outcomes. Shows understanding of experimental limitations and quantum measurement theory.

Research Quality and Innovation (25 points): Incorporates current scientific literature, identifies novel connections between quantum principles and emerging technologies, demonstrates original thinking in problem approach, and shows evidence of independent investigation beyond course materials.

Communication and Presentation (25 points): Maintains consistent professional formatting, uses appropriate scientific language and notation, creates clear diagrams and visual aids, organizes content logically, and effectively explains complex concepts to target audience.
instructions: Your portfolio must contain four main components, each demonstrating different aspects of quantum mechanics mastery. First, complete three original problem sets involving: (1) particle-in-a-box systems with complex boundary conditions, (2) quantum harmonic oscillator applications to molecular vibrations, and (3) quantum tunneling calculations for realistic barrier potentials. Include complete mathematical derivations, numerical solutions where appropriate, and physical interpretation of results. Second, design a theoretical experiment to measure quantum entanglement or demonstrate quantum superposition. Provide detailed experimental setup, identify required equipment, discuss measurement techniques, predict outcomes, and address potential sources of error. Third, research a current quantum technology (quantum computing, quantum cryptography, quantum sensors, or quantum materials) and write a 1500-word analysis connecting the technology to fundamental quantum principles covered in class. Include at least 8 peer-reviewed sources from the last 5 years. Fourth, create a comprehensive concept map linking all major quantum mechanics topics from the course, with detailed explanations of connections and real-world examples. Submit your portfolio as a single PDF document with clear section headers, numbered pages, and a table of contents. All mathematical work must be either typed using equation editors or clearly hand-written and scanned at high resolution. Include a reference list in APA format and ensure all figures are properly captioned and referenced in text.
grading_notes: Expect most expert-level students to score 75-85 points, with exceptional work reaching 90-100 points. Focus evaluation on depth of understanding rather than breadth - look for evidence of genuine comprehension of quantum mechanical principles rather than surface-level memorization. Pay particular attention to mathematical accuracy in problem-solving sections; minor computational errors are acceptable if methodology is sound, but conceptual errors should result in significant point deductions. For experimental design, prioritize feasibility and theoretical soundness over elaborate setups. Research sections should demonstrate critical thinking and synthesis rather than simple summarization of sources. Common issues include: inadequate mathematical justification, unrealistic experimental proposals, failure to connect quantum principles to applications, and poor organization. Grade distribution should reflect that this is expert-level work - use full point range but maintain high standards. Provide specific feedback on mathematical errors and suggest resources for improvement in weaker areas.

title: Comprehensive Project Management Plan for Technology Implementation
description: Students will develop a complete project management plan for implementing a new Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system in a mid-sized organization. This assessment evaluates students' ability to apply advanced project management methodologies, risk management strategies, stakeholder analysis, and resource optimization techniques to a realistic business scenario.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design and develop comprehensive project management plans using industry-standard methodologies and tools
Conduct thorough stakeholder analysis and develop effective communication strategies for complex projects
Apply advanced risk management techniques including identification, assessment, and mitigation strategies
Demonstrate proficiency in resource allocation, scheduling, and budget management for large-scale initiatives
Evaluate project success metrics and develop sustainable change management approaches
rubric_criteria: Project Scope and Planning (25 points): Comprehensive project charter, detailed WBS with 3+ levels, realistic timeline using critical path method, clear deliverables and milestones, appropriate methodology selection (Agile/Waterfall/Hybrid)

Stakeholder Management and Communication (25 points): Thorough stakeholder analysis matrix, tailored communication plan with frequency and methods, change management strategy, conflict resolution procedures, executive reporting structure

Risk Management and Quality Assurance (25 points): Comprehensive risk register with probability/impact analysis, detailed mitigation strategies, contingency planning, quality management plan with specific metrics, compliance considerations

Resource Management and Financial Planning (25 points): Detailed project budget with cost breakdown, resource allocation matrix, team structure and RACI chart, procurement plan, ROI analysis and business case justification
instructions: Develop a comprehensive project management plan for implementing a CRM system in a 500-employee manufacturing company transitioning from legacy spreadsheet-based customer tracking. Your organization has a $2.5M budget, 18-month timeline, and must maintain operations during implementation. Submit a 25-30 page professional document including: Executive Summary (2 pages), Project Charter with scope statement and success criteria, Work Breakdown Structure with at least 50 tasks across 3 levels, Gantt chart showing critical path and dependencies, Stakeholder analysis matrix identifying 15+ stakeholders with engagement strategies, Risk register with minimum 20 risks including probability, impact, and mitigation plans, Resource allocation plan with team structure and skill requirements, Budget breakdown with contingency reserves, Communication plan specifying frequency and audiences, Quality management plan with testing protocols, Change management strategy addressing user adoption. Use Microsoft Project or equivalent for scheduling, include at least 5 industry-standard templates or frameworks, cite minimum 8 professional sources (PMI, industry reports, case studies). Format as professional business document with table of contents, appendices for detailed charts, and executive presentation summary. Demonstrate understanding of both technical implementation and organizational change aspects.
grading_notes: Evaluate projects holistically considering both technical competency and practical feasibility. Excellent work (90-100) shows sophisticated understanding of PM methodologies with innovative solutions and exceptional attention to stakeholder needs. Good work (80-89) demonstrates solid PM principles with minor gaps in integration or detail. Satisfactory work (70-79) covers basic requirements but lacks depth in analysis or shows unrealistic assumptions. Pay special attention to: realistic timeline and budget estimates, depth of stakeholder analysis beyond obvious participants, creativity in risk mitigation strategies, integration between different plan components, professional presentation quality. Common issues include: overly optimistic timelines, insufficient consideration of change management, weak risk probability/impact assessments, inadequate stakeholder engagement strategies. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level, 35% B-level, 40% C-level, 10% below C-level. Provide specific feedback on methodology application and suggest industry resources for improvement.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Simulation and Executive Analysis
description: Students will navigate a complex multi-stakeholder organizational crisis through real-time decision-making, followed by a comprehensive executive analysis of their leadership approach, strategic decisions, and organizational impact.
estimated_time: 4 hours (2.5 hours simulation + 1.5 hours written analysis)
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate advanced crisis leadership and decision-making under pressure with incomplete information
Apply strategic thinking to balance competing stakeholder interests while maintaining organizational vision
Evaluate and adapt leadership styles based on situational demands and team dynamics
Synthesize complex organizational data to develop actionable strategic recommendations
rubric_criteria: Crisis Decision-Making & Strategic Thinking (25 points): Quality of real-time decisions, consideration of long-term consequences, ability to prioritize competing demands, and demonstration of systems thinking

Stakeholder Management & Communication (25 points): Effectiveness in managing diverse stakeholder groups, clarity and persuasiveness of communications, cultural sensitivity, and ability to build consensus while maintaining authority

Leadership Adaptability & Self-Awareness (25 points): Demonstration of situational leadership, ability to pivot strategies based on new information, recognition of personal leadership strengths/limitations, and effective team mobilization

Executive Analysis & Reflection (25 points): Depth of post-simulation analysis, integration of leadership theory with practice, quality of lessons learned, and sophistication of future strategic recommendations
instructions: You will participate in a live 2.5-hour crisis simulation where you lead a mid-size technology company facing a data breach affecting 50,000 customers, concurrent with a potential acquisition offer and employee unionization efforts. You'll receive information packets every 30 minutes requiring immediate decisions via recorded video responses to your board, employees, media, and customers. All communications will be evaluated for leadership presence, strategic clarity, and stakeholder sensitivity. Following the simulation, prepare a 1,500-word executive analysis addressing: (1) Your leadership approach evolution throughout the crisis, (2) Critical decision points and rationale, (3) Stakeholder management strategy and effectiveness, (4) Integration of relevant leadership frameworks, and (5) Strategic recommendations for organizational resilience. Submit your analysis as a professional executive memo within 24 hours. Include specific examples from the simulation and cite at least three leadership theories. All simulation communications and written analysis must demonstrate executive-level professionalism and strategic sophistication.
grading_notes: Evaluate students' ability to think strategically under pressure rather than perfect outcomes. Look for evidence of systematic decision-making processes, stakeholder awareness, and leadership presence in video communications. Common weaknesses include: reactive rather than proactive thinking, failure to consider long-term implications, poor stakeholder prioritization, and superficial theoretical integration in written analysis. Expect grade distribution: 10% A+ (exceptional strategic insight), 25% A (strong performance across criteria), 35% A-/B+ (solid competency with minor gaps), 25% B/B- (adequate but lacks sophistication), 5% below B (significant deficiencies). Pay particular attention to authenticity in leadership voice and genuine reflection rather than textbook regurgitation.

title: AWS Cloud Migration Discussion: Small Business Case Study Analysis
description: Students will analyze a fictional small business scenario and participate in a structured discussion about migrating from on-premises infrastructure to AWS cloud services. This assessment evaluates understanding of AWS fundamentals, cost considerations, and migration planning through peer discussion and individual reflection.
estimated_time: 2-3 hours (including research, discussion participation, and reflection writing)
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify core AWS services and their business applications
Analyze cost benefits and considerations of cloud migration
Evaluate security and compliance factors in AWS adoption
Communicate technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
rubric_criteria: AWS Services Knowledge (25 points): Accurately identifies and explains relevant AWS services (EC2, S3, RDS, etc.) with appropriate use cases for the business scenario
Cost Analysis (25 points): Demonstrates understanding of AWS pricing models, compares on-premises vs. cloud costs, identifies cost optimization opportunities
Security and Compliance Discussion (25 points): Addresses data security, backup strategies, compliance requirements, and AWS shared responsibility model
Communication and Peer Engagement (25 points): Posts are clear, professional, and constructive; actively engages with peers through meaningful responses and questions
instructions: You will analyze the following scenario: 'TechStart Solutions' is a 50-employee software development company currently using on-premises servers for their development environment, customer database, file storage, and email system. They spend $8,000 monthly on hardware maintenance and are considering AWS migration. Your task includes three components: (1) Initial Analysis Post (300-400 words): Research and recommend specific AWS services for their needs, estimate potential cost savings, and identify 2-3 security considerations. Use AWS pricing calculator for cost estimates and cite specific AWS documentation. (2) Peer Discussion: Respond to at least two classmates' posts with substantive feedback, alternative suggestions, or thoughtful questions. Each response should be 150-200 words. (3) Reflection Summary (200-300 words): After reading peer discussions, write a final reflection on what you learned and how peer feedback influenced your original recommendations. Submit all components in a single document with clear section headers. Include a reference list with at least 3 credible AWS resources (documentation, whitepapers, or case studies). All posts must be original, professional, and demonstrate critical thinking rather than just summarizing AWS features.
grading_notes: Look for specific AWS service recommendations rather than generic cloud benefits. Students should demonstrate actual research using AWS pricing calculator and official documentation. Deduct points for vague statements like 'cloud is cheaper' without supporting data. Strong responses will include specific service names, estimated costs, and real-world implementation considerations. Common issues include: oversimplifying security concerns, not considering data migration challenges, and failing to address the company's specific size and needs. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level work (90-100), 60% B-level work (80-89), 20% C-level work (70-79), 5% below 70. A-level work shows deep research, creative problem-solving, and excellent peer engagement with industry best practices referenced.

title: Project Risk Management Strategy Presentation
description: Students will develop and present a comprehensive risk management strategy for a realistic project scenario, demonstrating their ability to identify, analyze, and plan responses to project risks using PMP methodologies.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply risk identification techniques to systematically discover project risks
Conduct qualitative and quantitative risk analysis using PMP tools and techniques
Develop appropriate risk response strategies aligned with project objectives
Create risk monitoring and control processes for ongoing project execution
rubric_criteria: Risk Identification and Analysis (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive risk identification using at least 3 PMP techniques, provides clear risk register with probability/impact ratings, and shows understanding of risk categories and sources

Risk Response Planning (25 points): Develops appropriate response strategies (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept) with clear rationale, assigns risk owners, estimates response costs, and creates contingency plans for high-priority risks

Presentation Quality and Professional Communication (25 points): Delivers clear, organized presentation within time limit, uses appropriate visual aids, demonstrates confident knowledge of content, and effectively responds to questions

PMP Framework Application and Documentation (25 points): Correctly applies PMP risk management processes, uses proper terminology and tools, provides realistic timeline and budget considerations, and includes monitoring/control mechanisms
instructions: You will receive a project scenario (construction, IT implementation, or product launch) and must develop a complete risk management strategy presentation. Your 12-15 minute presentation must include: (1) Executive summary of the project and key risk factors, (2) Risk identification process showing at least 15 identified risks using brainstorming, expert interviews, and SWOT analysis, (3) Risk register with probability/impact matrix and risk scoring, (4) Detailed response plans for top 5 risks including specific actions, owners, timelines, and budgets, (5) Risk monitoring dashboard proposal with KPIs and reporting frequency. Use PowerPoint with 10-12 slides maximum. Include speaker notes for each slide. Submit your presentation file 24 hours before your scheduled presentation date. Be prepared for 3-5 minutes of Q&A focusing on your decision-making rationale and alternative approaches. Your presentation should demonstrate real-world applicability and show integration with other project management knowledge areas such as schedule, budget, and quality management.
grading_notes: Evaluate presentations using a 4-point scale per criterion (Exemplary=23-25pts, Proficient=20-22pts, Developing=15-19pts, Inadequate=0-14pts). Look for practical application rather than theoretical recitation. Common issues include: insufficient risk detail, unrealistic response strategies, poor time management, and failure to connect risks to project objectives. Expect grade distribution of 15% A, 35% B+, 35% B, 15% below B. Deduct 5 points for exceeding time limits. Award bonus points (up to 5) for exceptional creativity or industry-specific insights. Require resubmission if fewer than 10 risks identified or no quantitative analysis provided.

title: Comprehensive E-commerce Analytics Strategy and Implementation Portfolio
description: Students will create a comprehensive Google Analytics portfolio demonstrating advanced implementation, analysis, and optimization strategies for a real or simulated e-commerce website. The portfolio must include technical setup documentation, custom reporting dashboards, conversion funnel analysis, and data-driven business recommendations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Configure advanced Google Analytics features including Enhanced E-commerce, custom dimensions, and goal tracking
Create and interpret complex custom reports and dashboards for business decision-making
Analyze user behavior patterns and conversion funnels to identify optimization opportunities
Integrate Google Analytics with other marketing tools and platforms for comprehensive attribution modeling
Present data-driven insights and actionable recommendations to stakeholders using professional reporting standards
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation (25 points): Proper GA4 setup with Enhanced E-commerce tracking, custom events, conversions, audiences, and at least 3 custom dimensions. Code snippets and configuration screenshots must be included with clear documentation.

Dashboard Creation and Data Visualization (25 points): Development of 2 professional dashboards using Google Analytics and Data Studio/Looker Studio with appropriate KPIs, visual hierarchy, and interactive elements. Must include audience segmentation and cohort analysis.

Analytical Insights and Business Intelligence (25 points): Comprehensive analysis of user behavior, conversion funnels, traffic sources, and customer journey mapping. Must identify 5+ specific optimization opportunities with supporting data and statistical significance testing where applicable.

Strategic Recommendations and Presentation (25 points): Professional presentation of findings with executive summary, actionable recommendations prioritized by impact/effort matrix, projected ROI calculations, and implementation timeline. Must include stakeholder-appropriate data storytelling.
instructions: Create a comprehensive Google Analytics portfolio for an e-commerce website (real business, personal project, or provided case study). Your submission must include: 1) Technical documentation showing GA4 implementation with Enhanced E-commerce tracking, custom events, and audience configurations; 2) Two interactive dashboards created in Data Studio/Looker Studio focusing on different stakeholder needs (executive overview and marketing operations); 3) A detailed analytical report (8-10 pages) examining user behavior, conversion optimization opportunities, and attribution analysis across multiple channels; 4) A strategic presentation (15-20 slides) suitable for C-level executives containing key insights, prioritized recommendations, and implementation roadmap. All work must demonstrate proficiency with advanced GA4 features including Exploration reports, predictive audiences, and cross-platform tracking. Include screenshots, code snippets, and data exports to validate your implementation. Submit all components as a single ZIP file with organized folders and a README file explaining your methodology and data sources.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy by checking GA4 configuration screenshots and implementation code. Look for proper event naming conventions, parameter setup, and conversion tracking. Assess dashboard quality based on design principles, data accuracy, and business relevance. For analytical insights, verify statistical reasoning and look for actionable findings beyond surface-level observations. Common issues include: insufficient custom tracking implementation, dashboards lacking business context, analysis without statistical significance consideration, and recommendations without clear success metrics. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level work (comprehensive, innovative approaches), 60% B-level work (competent execution with minor gaps), 20% C-level work (basic requirements met), 5% below standards (significant technical or analytical deficiencies).

title: Multivariable Calculus and Linear Algebra Applications Exam
description: Comprehensive assessment evaluating students' mastery of multivariable calculus concepts including partial derivatives, multiple integrals, vector calculus, and their applications to optimization problems and linear transformations in three-dimensional space.
learning_objectives_assessed: Compute and interpret partial derivatives and gradients for multivariable functions
Evaluate double and triple integrals using appropriate coordinate systems
Apply vector calculus theorems (Green's, Stokes', Divergence) to solve real-world problems
Solve constrained and unconstrained optimization problems using calculus techniques
Analyze linear transformations and their geometric interpretations in higher dimensions
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Computation and Accuracy (25 points): Correct application of calculus formulas, accurate arithmetic calculations, proper use of mathematical notation, and error-free algebraic manipulations
