Problem-Solving Strategy and Method Selection (25 points): Appropriate choice of solution techniques, logical progression through multi-step problems, effective use of coordinate transformations, and demonstration of strategic mathematical thinking

Conceptual Understanding and Interpretation (25 points): Clear explanation of mathematical concepts, correct interpretation of results in context, understanding of geometric and physical meanings, and ability to connect abstract mathematics to applications

Communication and Mathematical Reasoning (25 points): Clear presentation of solutions with justified steps, proper mathematical language and symbolism, logical flow of arguments, and complete explanations of reasoning processes
instructions:
This exam consists of 6 problems covering multivariable calculus and linear algebra applications. You have 3 hours to complete all problems. Show all work clearly and justify your reasoning for full credit. Partial credit will be awarded for correct methods even if final answers are incorrect.

Problem Format: Problems include computational exercises (finding partial derivatives, evaluating integrals), application problems (optimization of functions with constraints), and conceptual questions (interpreting gradients, explaining geometric transformations).

Required Materials: Bring a scientific calculator, ruler, and pencil. Graphing calculators are permitted but not required. No books, notes, or electronic devices other than approved calculators are allowed.

Answer Requirements: Write solutions in the provided blue books. Number each problem clearly and show all intermediate steps. For word problems, define variables, set up equations, solve systematically, and interpret results in context. Draw diagrams where helpful.

Submission: Submit your blue book(s) at the end of the exam period. Late submissions will not be accepted. If you finish early, use remaining time to check your work and ensure all problems are attempted.
grading_notes: Grade distribution expectation: A-range (85-100%), B-range (70-84%), C-range (55-69%), below 55% requires additional support. Common issues to watch: sign errors in partial derivatives, incorrect limits of integration, forgetting to check constraint conditions in optimization problems, and incomplete justification of vector calculus theorem applications. Award partial credit generously for correct setup and method, even with computational errors. Deduct points for lack of units in applied problems and unclear mathematical notation. Flag students scoring below 60% for additional review sessions.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Bell's Theorem: Implications for Local Realism
description: Students will engage in a structured discussion analyzing the experimental validation of Bell's theorem, its implications for Einstein's concept of local realism, and the fundamental nature of quantum mechanics. This assessment evaluates understanding of quantum entanglement principles, critical analysis of experimental evidence, and ability to articulate complex quantum mechanical concepts.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate mastery of quantum entanglement principles and mathematical formalism
Critically evaluate experimental evidence supporting Bell's theorem violations
Analyze the philosophical implications of quantum mechanics for our understanding of reality
Synthesize complex quantum mechanical concepts to form coherent arguments about fundamental physics
rubric_criteria: Conceptual Mastery (25 points): Demonstrates thorough understanding of quantum entanglement, Bell inequalities, and experimental setups. Uses appropriate mathematical notation and correctly explains quantum mechanical principles underlying the phenomena.

Critical Analysis (25 points): Provides sophisticated evaluation of experimental evidence, addresses potential loopholes in Bell test experiments, and demonstrates understanding of the significance of violation magnitudes in different experimental configurations.

Argumentation and Synthesis (25 points): Constructs well-reasoned arguments about the implications for local realism, effectively integrates multiple sources of evidence, and demonstrates ability to connect experimental results to broader theoretical frameworks.

Communication and Engagement (25 points): Writes clearly and precisely using appropriate scientific terminology, engages meaningfully with peers' contributions through substantive responses, and demonstrates professional scientific discourse.
instructions: Participate in a week-long structured discussion forum addressing quantum entanglement and Bell's theorem. Your participation must include: (1) An initial post (500-750 words) analyzing a specific Bell test experiment of your choice, explaining the experimental setup, results, and significance for our understanding of local realism. Include relevant mathematical expressions and cite at least three peer-reviewed sources. (2) Two substantive response posts (300-400 words each) to classmates' initial posts, providing constructive criticism, additional insights, or alternative interpretations. Focus on experimental methodology, theoretical implications, or connections to other quantum phenomena. (3) One synthesis post (400-500 words) reflecting on the discussion's key themes and your evolved understanding of the topic. All posts must demonstrate graduate-level physics knowledge and professional scientific communication. Use LaTeX formatting for mathematical expressions. Posts will be evaluated on accuracy, depth of analysis, quality of scientific reasoning, and constructive engagement with peers. Submit initial post by Day 3, response posts by Day 5, and synthesis post by Day 7.
grading_notes: Evaluate initial posts for accurate explanation of chosen experiment and clear connection to Bell's theorem. Look for proper use of mathematical notation and understanding of measurement correlations. In response posts, assess whether students identify strengths/weaknesses in others' analyses and provide meaningful scientific contributions. Common issues include oversimplification of experimental setups, confusion between correlation and causation, and inadequate discussion of detection loopholes. Expect 15-20% A grades for exceptional synthesis and original insights, 60-70% B grades for solid understanding with minor gaps, and remaining grades for incomplete analysis or conceptual errors. Deduct points for late submissions and inadequate peer engagement.

title: My First Web Application: Design and Development Presentation
description: Students will present a simple web application they designed, explaining their development process, technical choices, and lessons learned. This assessment evaluates their ability to communicate technical concepts, demonstrate basic web development knowledge, and reflect on their learning journey.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate understanding of basic web development technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)
Explain software development process and decision-making
Communicate technical concepts clearly to an audience
Reflect on challenges faced and problem-solving approaches used
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation (25 points): Application demonstrates correct use of HTML structure, CSS styling, and basic JavaScript functionality. Code is clean and well-organized with appropriate comments.
Development Process Explanation (25 points): Student clearly describes planning phase, development steps taken, tools used, and technical decisions made. Shows understanding of development workflow.
Presentation Skills (25 points): Clear verbal communication, appropriate use of visual aids, maintains audience engagement, stays within time limit (8-12 minutes), professional delivery.
Problem-Solving and Reflection (25 points): Identifies specific challenges encountered, explains solutions implemented, discusses what was learned, and suggests improvements for future projects.
instructions: Create a simple web application (3-5 pages) that demonstrates your understanding of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript basics. Your application should include: a homepage with navigation, at least two additional pages, interactive elements using JavaScript (e.g., form validation, button clicks, dynamic content), and responsive design elements. Prepare a 10-minute presentation covering: 1) Project overview and goals, 2) Technical implementation walkthrough with live demo, 3) Development process and tools used, 4) Challenges faced and how you solved them, 5) Key learnings and future improvements. Submit your code files in a ZIP folder 24 hours before presentation. Include a README file with setup instructions and brief project description. Use visual aids (slides, live demo) during presentation. Be prepared to answer 2-3 technical questions from instructor or peers. Focus on explaining your thought process rather than just showing features.
grading_notes: Look for evidence of genuine learning over perfect execution. Common issues: rushed explanations of technical concepts, lack of reflection on learning process, applications that are too simple or overly ambitious for beginner level. Excellent presentations (90-100) show clear understanding and good communication. Good presentations (80-89) demonstrate competency with minor gaps. Satisfactory (70-79) shows basic understanding but limited depth. Below 70 indicates significant gaps in technical knowledge or communication. Encourage students to focus on explaining 'why' behind their choices, not just 'what' they built. Deduct points for presentations significantly over/under time limits.

title: Retail Sales Performance Analytics Portfolio
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive analysis of retail sales data using multiple analytical techniques, including exploratory data analysis, statistical testing, predictive modeling, and data visualization. The portfolio demonstrates proficiency in the complete data analysis workflow from data cleaning to actionable business insights.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply data cleaning and preprocessing techniques to prepare datasets for analysis
Conduct exploratory data analysis using descriptive statistics and visualizations
Perform statistical hypothesis testing to validate business assumptions
Build and evaluate predictive models using appropriate algorithms
Create compelling data visualizations that communicate insights effectively
Translate analytical findings into actionable business recommendations
rubric_criteria: Data Preparation & Quality (25 points): Thorough data cleaning documentation, handling of missing values, outliers, and data inconsistencies. Clear explanation of preprocessing steps and rationale for decisions made.

Analysis Methodology (25 points): Appropriate selection and application of statistical methods, exploratory analysis techniques, and predictive modeling approaches. Proper validation of model assumptions and limitations.

Visualization & Communication (25 points): Professional, clear visualizations that effectively communicate key findings. Well-structured report with logical flow, proper interpretation of results, and appropriate use of technical terminology.
Business Impact & Recommendations (25 points): Actionable insights that address specific business questions, quantified impact where possible, and feasible recommendations supported by data evidence.
instructions: Using the provided retail sales dataset (available on course platform), create a comprehensive analytics portfolio consisting of: 1) Executive Summary (1 page): Key findings and recommendations for business stakeholders. 2) Technical Analysis Report (8-12 pages): Include data exploration with summary statistics and initial observations, data cleaning documentation with before/after comparisons, statistical analysis addressing at least two business hypotheses, predictive model comparing at least two algorithms with performance metrics, and minimum six professional visualizations (charts, graphs, dashboards). 3) Code Repository: Well-commented Python/R scripts organized in logical sections, reproducible analysis that runs without errors, and clear variable naming and documentation. 4) Presentation Slides (8-10 slides): Executive-level summary suitable for business presentation. Submission Requirements: Submit as ZIP file containing all components, ensure all code runs independently with provided dataset, include requirements.txt or environment file for dependencies, and use consistent formatting and professional presentation throughout. Focus on retail business questions such as seasonal trends, product performance, customer segmentation, and sales forecasting. Your analysis should demonstrate both technical proficiency and business acumen.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy first - ensure statistical methods are correctly applied and code executes properly. Look for evidence of critical thinking in methodology choices and interpretation of results. Common issues include: inadequate data cleaning documentation, choosing inappropriate statistical tests, over-interpreting correlation as causation, and vague or unrealistic business recommendations. Excellence indicators: creative insights beyond basic requirements, sophisticated handling of data quality issues, appropriate model selection with clear justification, and recommendations that demonstrate deep understanding of retail business context. Grade distribution expectation: 20% should receive 90+ points for exceptional work, 60% should fall in 75-89 range for solid competency, 20% below 75 indicating need for additional support. Provide specific feedback on each rubric criterion and highlight both strengths and improvement areas.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Management Simulation Assessment
description: Students will demonstrate expert-level leadership competencies by developing and presenting a comprehensive crisis management strategy for a complex organizational scenario, including stakeholder analysis, decision-making frameworks, and implementation plans with measurable outcomes.
estimated_time: 4-5 hours (3 hours preparation + 1-2 hours presentation and defense)
learning_objectives_assessed: Synthesize multiple leadership theories to develop situational leadership strategies for high-stakes organizational challenges
Demonstrate advanced stakeholder management and communication skills in crisis scenarios
Design and justify strategic decision-making frameworks that balance competing organizational priorities
Evaluate leadership effectiveness through measurable outcomes and continuous improvement methodologies
rubric_criteria: Strategic Analysis & Vision (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of crisis context, identifies all relevant stakeholders, presents clear strategic vision with supporting rationale, integrates multiple leadership theories appropriately

Decision-Making Framework (25 points): Develops sophisticated decision-making model, addresses ethical considerations, demonstrates risk assessment capabilities, provides contingency planning with clear decision trees

Implementation Strategy (25 points): Creates detailed action plan with timelines, assigns appropriate resources and responsibilities, establishes measurable KPIs, addresses potential obstacles with mitigation strategies

Communication & Leadership Presence (25 points): Delivers compelling presentation with executive-level presence, adapts communication style for different stakeholder groups, handles challenging questions with confidence, demonstrates authentic leadership voice
instructions: You are the newly appointed CEO of a Fortune 500 company facing a major crisis (scenario will be provided 48 hours before presentation). Develop a comprehensive leadership strategy addressing immediate response and long-term organizational recovery. Your assessment consists of two components: (1) A 15-minute executive presentation to the Board of Directors outlining your crisis management strategy, followed by (2) A 10-minute Q&A session where you'll defend your approach and handle challenging stakeholder questions. Your presentation must include: stakeholder impact analysis with prioritization matrix, evidence-based decision-making framework citing relevant leadership theories, detailed 90-day implementation roadmap with specific milestones, measurable success metrics and monitoring systems, and contingency plans for three potential complications. Prepare professional-grade slides (maximum 12 slides) and a one-page executive summary. You may use any resources during preparation but must present without notes. Dress professionally and be prepared for realistic pushback scenarios including budget constraints, regulatory challenges, and stakeholder resistance. Submit your executive summary 24 hours before presentation via LMS. Late submissions result in 10-point penalty.
grading_notes: Evaluate based on executive-level expectations - students should demonstrate readiness for senior leadership roles. Look for sophisticated thinking beyond textbook applications. Strategic Analysis: Expect multi-dimensional stakeholder mapping, not just identification. Vision should be inspiring yet realistic. Decision-Making: Framework should be original, not copied from existing models. Ethical reasoning must be explicit and nuanced. Implementation: Plans should show project management sophistication with realistic timelines. KPIs must be specific and measurable. Communication: Assess executive presence - confidence without arrogance, clear articulation under pressure. Grade distribution expectation: 15% receive 90-100 (exceptional strategic thinking), 35% receive 80-89 (strong competency), 40% receive 70-79 (meets standards), 10% below 70 (needs development). Common issues: over-reliance on single leadership theory, unrealistic timelines, vague success metrics, poor handling of Q&A pressure. Bonus consideration (+5 points) for innovative approaches that show original strategic thinking beyond course materials.

title: Project Integration Management Case Study Exam
description: Students will analyze a complex project scenario involving scope changes, resource conflicts, and stakeholder issues. They must demonstrate understanding of integration management processes by developing a comprehensive change management plan, updating project documents, and recommending corrective actions using PMP methodologies.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply project integration management processes to coordinate project activities and manage changes
Develop and execute change control procedures following PMI standards
Analyze project performance data to identify variances and recommend corrective actions
Demonstrate understanding of project charter, project management plan, and work performance reports integration
rubric_criteria: Change Request Analysis (25 points): Correctly identifies all change impacts, performs thorough impact analysis including scope, schedule, budget, quality, and risk implications, and follows proper change request documentation standards

Integration Management Application (25 points): Demonstrates proper use of integration management processes, shows understanding of how changes affect multiple project areas, and applies appropriate PMI tools and techniques

Stakeholder Communication Strategy (25 points): Develops comprehensive communication plan for change implementation, identifies all affected stakeholders, determines appropriate communication methods and timing, and addresses potential resistance

Documentation and Professional Presentation (25 points): Uses proper PMP terminology throughout, presents work in professional format with clear structure, provides complete and accurate project document updates, and demonstrates attention to detail
instructions: You will receive a detailed case study describing 'TechFlow Implementation Project' - a 12-month IT system integration project currently in execution phase. The case includes project charter, current project management plan excerpts, work performance reports, and three concurrent change requests from different stakeholders. Your task is to assume the role of project manager and provide a comprehensive response addressing all integration management challenges presented. Your submission must include: (1) Individual analysis of each change request with complete impact assessment covering scope, schedule, cost, quality, risk, and resource implications; (2) Integrated change management plan showing how all three requests will be processed through change control board, including prioritization rationale and implementation sequencing; (3) Updated project management plan sections affected by approved changes; (4) Stakeholder communication matrix detailing who needs what information, when, and through which channels; (5) Risk register updates identifying new risks introduced by changes and corresponding mitigation strategies. Format your response as a professional project management report with executive summary, detailed analysis sections, and supporting documentation. Use PMI terminology throughout and reference specific PMBOK processes where applicable. Submit as single PDF document with clear section headers and page numbers. All work must be original and demonstrate individual understanding of integration management principles.
grading_notes: Focus evaluation on student's ability to see interconnections between project elements rather than memorization of processes. Look for evidence of systems thinking - how changes ripple through multiple project areas. Common issues include: treating change requests in isolation without considering cumulative impact, weak stakeholder analysis missing key affected parties, unrealistic timelines for change implementation, and failure to update all relevant project documents. Excellent responses (90-100 points) will show sophisticated understanding of integration complexities and provide creative but practical solutions. Good responses (80-89 points) cover all requirements with minor gaps in analysis depth. Satisfactory responses (70-79 points) demonstrate basic understanding but may miss some integration points or stakeholder considerations. Below 70 points indicates fundamental gaps in integration management understanding requiring remedial work.

title: Google Analytics Implementation Strategy and ROI Analysis Discussion
description: Students will analyze a provided e-commerce case study and develop a comprehensive Google Analytics implementation strategy, then engage in peer discussions to evaluate different approaches and their potential return on investment. This assessment evaluates advanced GA4 configuration knowledge, measurement planning, and business impact analysis.
estimated_time: 4-5 hours (2 hours preparation, 2-3 hours discussion participation)
learning_objectives_assessed: Design and justify advanced Google Analytics 4 measurement frameworks for complex business scenarios
Evaluate the business impact and ROI of different analytics implementation strategies
Critically analyze and provide constructive feedback on peers' analytics approaches
Synthesize multiple data sources and measurement techniques to solve real-world business problems
rubric_criteria: Strategic Analysis (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of business context, identifies key performance indicators aligned with business goals, and justifies measurement priorities with clear reasoning

Technical Implementation Plan (25 points): Provides detailed, accurate GA4 setup recommendations including custom events, conversion tracking, audience configuration, and integration with other platforms

Discussion Engagement (25 points): Actively participates in peer discussions with substantive comments, asks insightful questions, provides constructive feedback, and responds thoughtfully to others' critiques

Business Impact Assessment (25 points): Clearly articulates expected outcomes, defines success metrics, estimates implementation costs and timeline, and presents realistic ROI projections with supporting rationale
instructions: You will receive a detailed case study of 'TechGear Pro,' a mid-size e-commerce company selling consumer electronics across multiple channels (website, mobile app, physical stores, marketplaces). Review the provided business context, current analytics setup, and strategic goals. Develop a comprehensive GA4 implementation strategy addressing: 1) Measurement plan with specific events, conversions, and custom dimensions, 2) Enhanced e-commerce tracking setup, 3) Attribution modeling recommendations, 4) Integration with Google Ads, social media platforms, and email marketing tools, 5) Custom reporting and dashboard requirements, 6) Implementation timeline and resource allocation. Present your analysis in a structured 800-1000 word post covering technical specifications, business justification, and expected outcomes. After posting your initial analysis, engage with at least three peers' proposals by providing detailed feedback on their technical approach, questioning assumptions, and suggesting improvements. Respond to feedback on your own post with clarifications or revisions. All posts and responses must demonstrate advanced GA4 knowledge and include specific examples. Submit your initial post by Wednesday 11:59 PM, complete peer interactions by Friday 11:59 PM, and provide final responses by Sunday 11:59 PM.
grading_notes: Evaluate initial posts for technical accuracy of GA4 features and realistic implementation timelines. Look for specific event naming conventions, proper use of parameters, and understanding of GA4's event-driven model. In discussion interactions, assess quality over quantity - substantive feedback that demonstrates critical thinking scores higher than multiple superficial comments. Watch for students who make unsupported claims about ROI or implementation complexity. Strong submissions will reference specific GA4 documentation, industry best practices, and include concrete examples with numbers/metrics. Grade distribution should reflect: 90-100 (exceptional technical depth with innovative solutions), 80-89 (solid technical knowledge with good business reasoning), 70-79 (adequate understanding but missing key technical details or business context), below 70 (incomplete analysis or fundamental technical errors). Provide specific feedback on technical inaccuracies and suggest resources for improvement.

title: Enterprise Network Architecture Design and Implementation Presentation
description: Students will design and present a comprehensive enterprise network solution for a multi-site organization, demonstrating advanced Cisco networking concepts including routing protocols, network security, QoS implementation, and disaster recovery strategies. The presentation must include detailed network diagrams, configuration snippets, and justification for all design decisions.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design scalable enterprise network architectures using advanced Cisco technologies
Implement and configure complex routing protocols (OSPF, BGP, EIGRP) for multi-site connectivity
Integrate comprehensive network security solutions including firewalls, VPNs, and access control
Configure and optimize Quality of Service (QoS) for voice, video, and data traffic
Develop network redundancy and disaster recovery strategies
Analyze network performance and troubleshoot complex connectivity issues
rubric_criteria: Network Design Architecture (25 points): Comprehensive topology design with proper hierarchical structure, VLAN segmentation, IP addressing scheme using VLSM/CIDR, scalability considerations, and detailed network diagrams using industry-standard symbols

Routing and Switching Implementation (25 points): Appropriate selection and configuration of routing protocols (OSPF areas, BGP AS design, EIGRP metrics), inter-VLAN routing, spanning tree optimization, and redundancy protocols (HSRP/VRRP/GLBP)

Security and QoS Integration (25 points): Implementation of security policies, firewall rules, VPN configurations, 802.1X authentication, QoS classification and marking, traffic shaping, and priority queuing mechanisms with specific configuration examples

Presentation Quality and Technical Justification (25 points): Clear communication of technical concepts, well-structured presentation flow, accurate use of networking terminology, thorough justification of design decisions, effective response to technical questions, and professional visual aids
instructions: You are tasked with designing a complete enterprise network solution for a fictional organization with headquarters, two branch offices, remote workers, and cloud integration requirements. Your presentation must be 25-30 minutes followed by a 15-minute technical Q&A session. Create a scenario-based organization (manufacturing, healthcare, financial services, etc.) and design accordingly. Include the following components: (1) Executive summary with business requirements and constraints, (2) Detailed network topology diagrams showing physical and logical layouts, (3) IP addressing scheme with VLSM calculations and subnet allocations, (4) Routing protocol selection and configuration with specific Cisco IOS commands, (5) VLAN design with inter-VLAN routing implementation, (6) Security architecture including firewall policies, VPN configurations, and access control lists, (7) QoS implementation strategy with traffic classification and bandwidth allocation, (8) Network redundancy and high availability solutions, (9) Disaster recovery and business continuity planning, (10) Performance monitoring and troubleshooting methodology. Submit your presentation slides (PowerPoint/PDF) and a technical documentation packet including all configuration files, network diagrams in Visio format, and a detailed implementation timeline 48 hours before your scheduled presentation. Be prepared to demonstrate specific configurations using packet tracer simulations and answer detailed technical questions about your design choices, alternative solutions, and troubleshooting scenarios.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy over presentation polish - look for deep understanding of Cisco technologies rather than superficial coverage. Common issues include: inadequate IP addressing schemes, inappropriate routing protocol selection, missing redundancy considerations, and unrealistic QoS policies. Expect 15% A grades (exceptional technical depth with innovative solutions), 35% B grades (solid technical implementation with minor gaps), 35% C grades (adequate coverage but missing advanced concepts), 15% D/F grades (fundamental technical errors or incomplete coverage). During Q&A, ask probing questions about scalability, security implications, troubleshooting methodologies, and alternative design approaches. Award bonus points for creative solutions that go beyond basic requirements, such as SD-WAN integration, network automation scripting, or advanced security implementations. Deduct points for inaccurate configurations that wouldn't function in production environments.

title: First Programming Projects Portfolio
description: A comprehensive portfolio showcasing fundamental programming skills through three small projects: a calculator program, a simple text-based game, and a data processing script. Students will demonstrate their understanding of basic programming concepts, problem-solving abilities, and code documentation practices.
learning_objectives_assessed: Write syntactically correct programs using variables, data types, and basic operations
Implement control structures including conditionals and loops effectively
Apply problem decomposition and algorithmic thinking to solve programming challenges
Create clear, readable code with appropriate comments and documentation
rubric_criteria: Code Functionality (25 points): All three programs run without errors, meet specified requirements, and handle basic edge cases appropriately
Programming Concepts (25 points): Correct use of variables, data types, conditionals, loops, and functions; demonstrates understanding of program flow and logic
Code Quality and Style (25 points): Clean, readable code with consistent indentation, meaningful variable names, and appropriate comments explaining complex logic
Documentation and Reflection (25 points): Complete README file for each project, portfolio summary explaining learning journey, and thoughtful reflection on challenges and solutions
instructions: Create a portfolio containing three programming projects using Python (or instructor-approved language). Project 1: Build a calculator that performs basic arithmetic operations (+, -, *, /) and handles invalid input gracefully. Project 2: Develop a number guessing game where the computer generates a random number and provides hints until the user guesses correctly. Project 3: Create a program that reads a text file containing student names and grades, then calculates and displays the average grade and highest/lowest scores. Each project must include: functional code with clear variable names and comments, a README file explaining how to run the program and what it does, and example input/output. Additionally, write a 500-word portfolio summary reflecting on your programming journey, biggest challenges faced, problem-solving strategies used, and key concepts learned. Organize all files in a clear folder structure: Project1_Calculator/, Project2_GuessingGame/, Project3_GradeProcessor/, and include a main Portfolio_Summary.md file. Submit as a single ZIP file named 'LastName_FirstName_Portfolio.zip'. Ensure all programs run successfully before submission and test with various inputs.
grading_notes: Focus on growth and learning over perfection. For Code Functionality: 90-100% = all programs work flawlessly, 80-89% = minor bugs or missing features, 70-79% = programs run with significant issues, below 70% = major functionality problems. For Programming Concepts: look for appropriate use of data structures, logical flow, and evidence of understanding. Code Quality should reward readability over complexity - beginners often over-complicate solutions. Documentation assessment should emphasize clarity and genuine reflection rather than length. Common issues include: hardcoded values instead of variables, missing input validation, unclear variable names, and superficial reflections. Expect 15% A grades, 40% B grades, 35% C grades, 10% D/F grades. Provide specific feedback on code improvements and encourage resubmission for major issues.

title: Advanced Calculus Problem-Solving Assessment: Optimization and Integration Applications
description: A comprehensive quiz evaluating students' ability to solve complex optimization problems, apply advanced integration techniques, and analyze real-world applications using multivariable calculus concepts including Lagrange multipliers, double integrals, and vector field analysis.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply Lagrange multipliers to solve constrained optimization problems in multivariable contexts
Evaluate double and triple integrals using appropriate coordinate systems and techniques
Analyze vector fields and compute line integrals and surface integrals
Model and solve real-world optimization problems using calculus methods
Demonstrate mathematical reasoning and provide complete, rigorous solutions
rubric_criteria: Problem Setup and Mathematical Modeling (25 points): Correctly identifies given information, establishes appropriate variables, formulates constraints and objective functions, and demonstrates clear understanding of the problem context

Mathematical Technique and Execution (25 points): Properly applies calculus methods (Lagrange multipliers, integration techniques, vector calculus), shows accurate calculations, uses appropriate coordinate systems, and demonstrates mastery of advanced techniques

Solution Analysis and Interpretation (25 points): Verifies solutions using second derivative tests or boundary analysis, checks reasonableness of answers, interprets results in context of original problem, and identifies maximum/minimum values correctly

Mathematical Communication and Rigor (25 points): Provides clear, logical progression of steps, uses proper mathematical notation, explains reasoning at key steps, presents work in organized manner, and includes appropriate units and conclusions
instructions: This assessment consists of 4 multi-part problems requiring advanced calculus techniques. You have 120 minutes to complete all problems. Show all work clearly and justify your reasoning at each step. Use proper mathematical notation throughout. For optimization problems, you must verify that your solutions are indeed maxima or minima using appropriate tests. For integration problems, state which technique you are using and show setup clearly. When solving real-world applications, define your variables explicitly and interpret your final answers in context. You may use a graphing calculator for numerical verification, but all analytical work must be shown by hand. Partial credit will be awarded based on correct setup, appropriate method selection, computational accuracy, and complete analysis. If you cannot complete a part, show your progress and explain your approach for potential partial credit. Round final numerical answers to three decimal places unless otherwise specified. For problems involving vector fields, include diagrams where appropriate to support your analysis. Each problem is worth 25 points and should receive roughly equal time allocation. Begin each problem on a new page and clearly label all parts.
grading_notes: Award partial credit generously for correct setup and method selection even if computational errors occur. Common issues include: forgetting to check second-derivative conditions for optimization, incorrect bounds setup for multiple integrals, sign errors in vector calculations, and failure to interpret answers in context. Grade distribution should target: 15% A-level (90-100), 25% B-level (80-89), 35% C-level (70-79), 20% D-level (60-69), 5% F-level (below 60). Deduct 2-3 points for minor computational errors, 5-8 points for method errors, and 10+ points for conceptual misunderstandings. Give full credit for alternative valid solution methods. Watch for students who show work but make systematic errors - provide substantial partial credit for correct reasoning.

title: Electromagnetic Induction Laboratory Investigation and Design Project
description: Students will design, conduct, and analyze a comprehensive investigation into electromagnetic induction phenomena, including experimental verification of Faraday's and Lenz's laws, quantitative analysis of induced EMF under various conditions, and design of a practical electromagnetic device with theoretical modeling and performance optimization.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply Faraday's law and Lenz's law to predict and calculate induced EMF in complex electromagnetic systems
Design and execute controlled experiments to investigate electromagnetic induction with proper uncertainty analysis
Analyze the relationship between magnetic flux, rate of change, and induced current in various geometric configurations
Synthesize theoretical knowledge to design and optimize a practical electromagnetic device
Communicate complex physics concepts and experimental results through technical writing and data visualization
rubric_criteria: Experimental Design and Execution (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated experimental methodology with proper controls, systematic variable manipulation, accurate data collection techniques, and appropriate use of measuring instruments with uncertainty quantification

Theoretical Analysis and Mathematical Modeling (25 points): Applies electromagnetic theory correctly to predict experimental outcomes, uses calculus-based physics to model complex induction scenarios, and demonstrates deep understanding of flux linkage, mutual inductance, and energy considerations

Device Design and Innovation (25 points): Creates an original electromagnetic device (transformer, generator, motor, or induction system) with detailed engineering specifications, optimization analysis, efficiency calculations, and practical feasibility assessment

Data Analysis and Scientific Communication (25 points): Presents results with professional-quality graphs, statistical analysis of uncertainties, clear discussion of sources of error, comparison between theoretical predictions and experimental results, and well-structured technical report following scientific conventions
instructions: This project consists of three interconnected phases completed over 4-6 weeks. Phase 1 (Week 1-2): Design and conduct at least three distinct experiments investigating electromagnetic induction. Examples include: varying coil geometry and measuring induced EMF, investigating eddy current damping, or exploring mutual inductance between coil pairs. Your experimental design must include proper controls, systematic parameter variation, and quantitative measurements with uncertainty analysis. Phase 2 (Week 3-4): Using your experimental insights, design an original electromagnetic device such as a variable transformer, AC generator, linear motor, or wireless charging system. Provide detailed technical specifications, theoretical performance predictions using electromagnetic principles, and efficiency analysis. Build a working prototype or detailed CAD model with justification if construction isn't feasible. Phase 3 (Week 5-6): Compile your work into a comprehensive technical report (15-20 pages) including: executive summary, theoretical background with relevant equations, experimental methodology and results, device design rationale and specifications, error analysis, conclusions, and references. Include high-quality data visualizations, circuit diagrams, and technical drawings. Submit all raw data, calculations, photos/videos of experiments, and device documentation. Present your findings in a 10-minute technical presentation with visual aids. All work must demonstrate expert-level understanding of electromagnetic theory, professional experimental techniques, and clear scientific communication suitable for peer review.
grading_notes: Evaluate experimental rigor by checking for systematic methodology, proper use of measurement tools, and realistic uncertainty estimates (typically 2-5% for well-designed experiments). Strong theoretical analysis should include calculus-based derivations and correct application of Maxwell's equations. Device designs should show innovation beyond textbook examples while remaining physically realistic. Common issues include insufficient controls in experiments, confusion between EMF and current measurements, and oversimplified theoretical models. Expect grade distribution: 85-100% for exceptional work showing research-level competency, 70-84% for solid understanding with minor gaps, 60-69% for adequate work meeting basic requirements, below 60% for incomplete or fundamentally flawed analysis. Bonus points (up to 5%) may be awarded for exceptional creativity, advanced mathematical analysis, or practical applications with broader impact.

title: Comparative Analysis Discussion: Statistical Methods for Business Decision-Making
description: Students will engage in a structured discussion analyzing the appropriateness and effectiveness of different statistical methods applied to real business scenarios, demonstrating their understanding of when and how to use various analytical approaches.
learning_objectives_assessed: Evaluate the appropriateness of different statistical methods for specific business problems
Analyze and interpret statistical results in business contexts
Communicate data analysis findings effectively to diverse audiences
Apply critical thinking to assess the validity and limitations of analytical approaches
rubric_criteria: Initial Analysis Post (25 points): Provides comprehensive comparison of at least 3 statistical methods for the given scenario, with clear justification for recommended approach including assumptions, limitations, and expected outcomes

Data Interpretation & Business Context (25 points): Demonstrates thorough understanding of how statistical results translate to actionable business insights, addresses potential risks and uncertainties, and considers stakeholder perspectives

Peer Responses & Critical Evaluation (25 points): Contributes 2+ substantive responses that challenge or extend peers' analyses, introduces additional considerations, provides constructive feedback with specific examples or alternative approaches

Communication & Professional Presentation (25 points): Uses appropriate statistical terminology accurately, presents arguments logically with supporting evidence, writes clearly for business audience, includes proper citations for any external sources
instructions:
You are a data analyst consulting for RetailMax, a mid-sized retail chain experiencing declining sales. Management has provided 2 years of sales data including: monthly revenue by store location, customer demographics, product categories, seasonal trends, and marketing spend. They want to identify factors driving the decline and develop a data-driven strategy for improvement.

For your initial post (300-400 words):
1. Compare at least three different analytical approaches you could use (e.g., regression analysis, time series analysis, cluster analysis, hypothesis testing)
2. Recommend ONE primary method and justify your choice
3. Explain what insights this method could provide and what limitations to expect
4. Describe how you would present findings to non-technical executives

For peer responses (150-200 words each, minimum 2 responses):
1. Evaluate a classmate's recommended approach - what are its strengths/weaknesses?
2. Suggest additional analytical techniques or considerations they might have missed
3. Challenge assumptions or offer alternative interpretations
4. Build on their ideas with your own insights or experiences

Submission requirements:
- Initial post due by Wednesday 11:59 PM
- Peer responses due by Sunday 11:59 PM
- Use discussion board reply feature
- Include at least one credible source (textbook, journal article, or industry report)
- Professional tone appropriate for business consulting context
grading_notes: Focus on depth of analytical thinking rather than perfect technical knowledge. Students should demonstrate understanding of when different methods are appropriate, not just how to execute them. Look for evidence of critical thinking in peer responses - simple agreement or praise doesn't meet criteria. Common issues: choosing overly complex methods without justification, ignoring business context, superficial peer responses that don't add value. Grade distribution typically: 20% earn 90-100 points (exceptional analysis and engagement), 50% earn 80-89 points (solid understanding with minor gaps), 25% earn 70-79 points (basic competency but limited depth), 5% below 70 points (significant gaps in understanding or minimal effort).

title: Complex Project Recovery and Stakeholder Management Presentation
description: Students will present a comprehensive project recovery strategy for a failing multi-million dollar project, demonstrating advanced project management competencies including risk mitigation, stakeholder management, resource reallocation, and change management while defending their approach to a simulated executive board.
learning_objectives_assessed: Analyze complex project failures and develop comprehensive recovery strategies using advanced PM methodologies
Demonstrate expert-level stakeholder management and communication skills in high-pressure scenarios
Apply integrated change management, risk assessment, and resource optimization techniques
Evaluate and justify strategic project decisions using data-driven approaches and PM best practices
rubric_criteria: Project Analysis & Recovery Strategy (25 points): Demonstrates thorough root cause analysis, realistic recovery timeline, comprehensive risk mitigation plan, and integration of appropriate PM frameworks (Agile, Waterfall, hybrid approaches)

Stakeholder Management & Communication (25 points): Identifies all stakeholder groups, develops targeted communication strategies, addresses resistance management, and demonstrates cultural sensitivity and conflict resolution approaches

Financial & Resource Management (25 points): Provides detailed budget recovery analysis, resource reallocation justification, ROI projections, and demonstrates understanding of portfolio management implications

Presentation Quality & Executive Engagement (25 points): Delivers professional executive-level presentation, handles challenging questions effectively, uses appropriate visual aids, maintains composure under pressure, and provides actionable recommendations
instructions: You are a senior project manager called to rescue a failing $50M technology implementation project that is 8 months behind schedule and 40% over budget. Choose from provided case studies or develop your own realistic scenario. Your presentation must include: (1) Executive summary with key metrics and recommendations, (2) Root cause analysis using fishbone diagrams and 5-whys methodology, (3) Detailed recovery plan with revised timeline, budget, and scope, (4) Stakeholder impact assessment and communication strategy, (5) Risk register with mitigation strategies, (6) Success metrics and monitoring plan. Format: 15-20 slides maximum, professional business presentation style. Include appendices with detailed project artifacts (Gantt charts, risk matrices, stakeholder maps). Submit presentation 24 hours before delivery. During presentation, you'll face challenging questions from 'executives' (instructor and guest evaluators) who may push back on recommendations. Be prepared to defend methodological choices, provide alternative scenarios, and demonstrate deep PM knowledge. Dress professionally as this simulates a real board presentation.
grading_notes: Look for integration of multiple PM methodologies rather than textbook regurgitation. Award higher points for realistic constraints acknowledgment and creative problem-solving. Deduct points for unrealistic timelines or budgets, failure to address stakeholder concerns, or inability to defend recommendations. Expect 15% A grades (exceptional strategic thinking), 25% B+ grades (solid competency), 45% B grades (meets expectations), 15% below B (requires improvement). Pay attention to how students handle pressure during Q&A - this differentiates advanced practitioners. Common issues: oversimplifying stakeholder dynamics, ignoring organizational politics, unrealistic recovery timelines, poor executive communication style. Bonus consideration for students who proactively address lessons learned and future project governance improvements.

title: Executive Leadership Portfolio: Strategic Transformation Initiative
description: Students demonstrate advanced leadership competencies by designing, implementing, and reflecting on a comprehensive organizational transformation initiative. This portfolio showcases strategic thinking, change management, stakeholder engagement, and adaptive leadership skills through real-world application and critical analysis.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design and execute complex organizational change strategies using evidence-based leadership frameworks
Demonstrate advanced stakeholder management and communication skills across diverse organizational levels
Apply systems thinking to analyze organizational dynamics and implement sustainable transformation initiatives
Exhibit adaptive leadership behaviors while managing ambiguity, resistance, and competing priorities
Critically evaluate leadership effectiveness through reflective practice and continuous improvement methodologies
rubric_criteria: Strategic Vision and Planning (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of organizational analysis, develops comprehensive transformation strategy with clear objectives, timeline, and success metrics. Shows integration of multiple leadership theories and frameworks.

Implementation and Change Management (25 points): Executes initiative with evidence of stakeholder engagement, communication planning, resistance management, and adaptive problem-solving. Documents decision-making processes and adjustments made during implementation.

Leadership Competency Demonstration (25 points): Provides concrete evidence of advanced leadership skills including influence, conflict resolution, team building, and cultural sensitivity. Shows ability to operate effectively across organizational hierarchy and functional boundaries.

Critical Reflection and Professional Development (25 points): Conducts thorough analysis of leadership effectiveness, identifies specific growth areas, demonstrates learning integration, and creates actionable development plan. Shows metacognitive awareness and commitment to continuous improvement.
instructions: Create a comprehensive portfolio documenting your leadership of a significant organizational transformation initiative (minimum 3-month duration). Your portfolio must include: (1) Executive Summary (2 pages) outlining the initiative scope, objectives, and outcomes; (2) Strategic Analysis (8-10 pages) including organizational assessment, stakeholder mapping, change strategy, and theoretical framework application; (3) Implementation Documentation (6-8 pages) with project timeline, communication artifacts, meeting minutes, and evidence of leadership interventions; (4) Stakeholder Feedback Collection including 360-degree evaluations, team surveys, or interview transcripts from at least 5 participants; (5) Critical Reflection Essay (4-5 pages) analyzing your leadership effectiveness, challenges encountered, lessons learned, and specific examples of adaptive leadership; (6) Professional Development Plan (2-3 pages) identifying growth areas and concrete action steps. All materials must be professionally presented with clear organization, proper citations, and appendices containing supporting documents. Submit as a single PDF with bookmarked sections for easy navigation.
grading_notes: Evaluate portfolios holistically, focusing on depth of analysis rather than initiative size. Look for evidence of genuine leadership challenge and growth, not just project management. Strong portfolios will show vulnerability in reflection, specific examples of leadership moments, and clear connection between theory and practice. Watch for generic reflections or initiatives where student had limited actual leadership authority. Expect 15% A-range (exceptional strategic thinking and self-awareness), 60% B-range (solid demonstration of competencies with good reflection), 20% C-range (adequate coverage but limited depth), 5% below C (insufficient evidence or superficial analysis). Provide detailed feedback on leadership development areas and commend specific examples of effective leadership behaviors demonstrated.

title: AWS EC2 Web Server Deployment and Security Configuration Lab Report
description: Students will deploy a web server on AWS EC2, implement basic security configurations, and document their process with screenshots and explanations. This assessment evaluates practical AWS skills including EC2 instance management, security groups, and basic web hosting.
learning_objectives_assessed: Deploy and configure AWS EC2 instances for web hosting
Implement AWS security best practices including security groups and key pairs
Document cloud infrastructure deployment processes effectively
Troubleshoot common AWS connectivity and configuration issues
rubric_criteria: EC2 Instance Deployment (25 points): Successfully launches EC2 instance with correct AMI, instance type, and configuration. Screenshots show proper instance details and running state.

Security Configuration (25 points): Correctly configures security groups with appropriate inbound/outbound rules for web traffic. Demonstrates understanding of SSH key pair authentication and principle of least privilege.

Web Server Implementation (25 points): Successfully installs and configures Apache/Nginx, deploys custom HTML page, and demonstrates web server is accessible via public IP. Shows understanding of Linux commands and web server basics.

Documentation Quality (25 points): Provides clear, step-by-step documentation with annotated screenshots, explains troubleshooting steps taken, includes cost analysis, and demonstrates reflection on security considerations.
instructions:
Complete the following AWS deployment task and submit a comprehensive lab report documenting your work:

**Task Overview:**
1. Launch an Amazon EC2 instance using Amazon Linux 2 AMI
2. Configure security groups for web traffic (HTTP/HTTPS)
3. Install and configure a web server (Apache or Nginx)
4. Create a custom HTML webpage displaying your name and current date
5. Ensure the webpage is accessible from the internet

**Required Deliverables:**
Submit a PDF report (8-12 pages) containing:
- Executive summary of the deployment
- Step-by-step process documentation with annotated screenshots
- Configuration details for EC2 instance, security groups, and web server
- URL of your deployed webpage and verification screenshot
- Cost breakdown using AWS Pricing Calculator
- Security analysis discussing implemented measures and potential improvements
- Reflection on challenges encountered and solutions implemented
- Appendix with key commands used

**Technical Requirements:**
- Use t2.micro instance (free tier eligible)
- Tag all resources with your student ID
- Include your student number in the HTML page content
- Terminate instance after completion and include termination screenshot

**Submission:**
Upload PDF to learning management system by [due date]. Include 'AWS-Lab-[StudentID]' in filename.
grading_notes: Use detailed rubric for consistent grading. Award partial credit within each category: Excellent (90-100%), Good (80-89%), Satisfactory (70-79%), Needs Improvement (60-69%), Unsatisfactory (<60%). Common issues include: incomplete security group configuration, missing cost analysis, poor screenshot quality, failure to terminate resources. Expect 70% of students to score 75-85 points. Deduct points for late submissions per syllabus policy. Verify webpage URLs are functional during grading. Check that instances are properly terminated to avoid unexpected charges.

title: Project Risk Management and Stakeholder Engagement Assessment
description: Students will demonstrate intermediate-level PMP competencies by analyzing a project scenario, creating a risk register, developing stakeholder engagement strategies, and justifying their approach using PMI methodologies and best practices.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply risk identification, analysis, and response planning techniques in accordance with PMBOK Guide standards
Develop appropriate stakeholder engagement strategies based on stakeholder analysis and project requirements
Demonstrate understanding of integrated project management processes and their interdependencies
Utilize PMI terminology and frameworks correctly in project management contexts
rubric_criteria: Risk Management Application (25 points): Accurately identifies 5-7 relevant risks, properly categorizes them, assigns appropriate probability/impact ratings, and develops realistic response strategies using PMI risk management processes

Stakeholder Analysis and Engagement (25 points): Conducts thorough stakeholder identification, creates accurate power/interest grid, develops specific engagement strategies appropriate for each stakeholder category, and aligns approaches with project objectives

PMI Framework Integration (25 points): Correctly applies PMBOK Guide processes, uses proper PMI terminology throughout, demonstrates understanding of process interactions, and references appropriate knowledge areas and process groups

Professional Communication and Justification (25 points): Provides clear rationale for all decisions, writes professionally using proper project management language, organizes responses logically, and supports recommendations with sound project management principles
instructions: You are the project manager for a 12-month software implementation project at a mid-size healthcare organization. The project involves replacing the current patient management system with a cloud-based solution, affecting 200+ staff members across 5 departments. Budget is $800,000 with a firm go-live deadline due to regulatory compliance requirements. Complete the following three tasks: (1) Create a comprehensive risk register identifying at least 6 risks specific to this scenario. For each risk, provide: risk description, category, probability (1-5 scale), impact (1-5 scale), risk score, and response strategy with specific actions. (2) Develop a stakeholder engagement plan by first identifying key stakeholders, plotting them on a power/interest grid, and then describing specific engagement strategies for each stakeholder group. Include frequency of communication and preferred methods. (3) Write a brief executive summary (200-250 words) explaining how your risk management and stakeholder engagement approaches integrate with overall project success, referencing specific PMBOK Guide knowledge areas and processes. Format your response using clear headings for each section. Show all work and calculations. Use professional project management terminology throughout. Submit as a single document with your name and date.
grading_notes: Grade holistically within each criterion rather than item-by-item. For Risk Management: Look for realistic healthcare/IT risks, not generic ones. Probability/impact scores should align with descriptions. Response strategies must be actionable. For Stakeholder Engagement: Should identify clinical staff, IT teams, executives, patients, vendors, and regulators. Power/interest placement should be logical. Engagement strategies must be specific, not vague. For PMI Integration: Must reference at least 3 knowledge areas correctly. Common errors include confusing process groups with knowledge areas. For Communication: Professional tone is essential. Vague statements like 'communicate regularly' should receive lower scores. Expect grade distribution of 15% A-level (90+), 60% B-level (80-89), 20% C-level (70-79), 5% below 70%. Partial credit available within each criterion based on completeness and accuracy.

title: Enterprise Network Design and BGP Implementation Assessment
description: A comprehensive practical examination where students design, configure, and troubleshoot a multi-site enterprise network using advanced Cisco technologies including BGP, OSPF, VLANs, VPNs, and security policies. Students must demonstrate expert-level knowledge of routing protocols, network security, and enterprise-grade network architecture.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design scalable enterprise network architectures using hierarchical models and redundancy principles
Configure and optimize BGP routing protocols for multi-homed environments with proper path selection
Implement advanced OSPF features including multi-area designs, route summarization, and authentication
Deploy enterprise security policies using ACLs, VPNs, and firewall configurations
Troubleshoot complex network issues using systematic methodologies and Cisco diagnostic tools
Optimize network performance through QoS implementation and bandwidth management techniques
rubric_criteria: Network Architecture Design (25 points): Demonstrates expert understanding of hierarchical network design, proper VLAN segmentation, redundancy implementation, and scalability considerations. Full points require complete documentation with justified design decisions.

Routing Protocol Configuration (25 points): Correctly configures BGP with proper neighbor relationships, route filtering, path manipulation, and OSPF multi-area design with appropriate area types and route summarization. Must include IPv4 and IPv6 implementations.

Security Implementation (25 points): Deploys comprehensive security policies including properly configured ACLs, site-to-site VPN tunnels, AAA authentication, and port security. Must demonstrate understanding of security best practices and threat mitigation.

Troubleshooting and Optimization (25 points): Uses systematic troubleshooting methodology to identify and resolve network issues, implements QoS policies for voice/video traffic, and provides performance optimization recommendations with supporting evidence from show commands.
instructions:
You are tasked with designing and implementing a complete enterprise network solution for a multi-site organization. The scenario involves three office locations requiring secure connectivity, redundant internet connections, and support for voice/video applications.

REQUIREMENTS:
1. Design a hierarchical network architecture with proper documentation including network diagrams, IP addressing schemes (both IPv4 and IPv6), and VLAN designs
2. Configure BGP on edge routers with dual ISP connections, implementing proper route filtering, path manipulation, and load balancing
3. Implement OSPF as the internal routing protocol with multi-area design, including backbone area, standard areas, and at least one stub area
4. Configure site-to-site VPN tunnels between all locations using IPSec
5. Implement comprehensive security policies including zone-based firewalls, ACLs, and AAA authentication
6. Deploy QoS policies to prioritize voice and video traffic across WAN links
7. Document all configurations with comments explaining design decisions
8. Provide troubleshooting scenarios resolution with supporting show command outputs
9. Include network optimization recommendations with performance metrics

SUBMISSION FORMAT:
- Complete network documentation package (diagrams, addressing plans, configurations)
- Running configurations for all devices with detailed comments
- Verification outputs showing protocol operation and connectivity
- Troubleshooting report with methodology and solutions
- Performance analysis and optimization recommendations

Submit all materials in a organized digital portfolio with clear labeling and professional presentation.
grading_notes: Evaluation should focus on practical implementation accuracy and professional documentation quality. Key areas to assess: 1) Network designs must demonstrate understanding of enterprise best practices - deduct points for single points of failure or poor scalability choices. 2) BGP configurations should show proper understanding of path attributes and policy implementation - watch for missing route filtering or improper neighbor relationships. 3) Security implementations must be comprehensive and properly applied - partial credit for incomplete ACLs or misconfigured VPNs. 4) Troubleshooting sections should demonstrate systematic methodology - look for logical problem-solving approaches rather than random configuration attempts. Grade distribution expectation: 20% should score 90+, 40% should score 80-89, 30% should score 70-79, 10% below 70. Common issues to watch: incomplete IPv6 implementation, missing route summarization, improper QoS classification, and inadequate documentation of design decisions.

title: Algorithm Selection and Problem-Solving Discussion
description: Students will analyze a real-world problem, select appropriate algorithms to solve it, and engage in peer discussion about their reasoning and alternative approaches. This assessment evaluates understanding of basic algorithms, problem decomposition, and technical communication skills.
estimated_time: 3-4 hours (initial post: 2 hours, peer responses: 1-2 hours)
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify and explain the characteristics of fundamental algorithms (sorting, searching, basic data structures)
Analyze problems and select appropriate algorithmic approaches based on efficiency and constraints
Communicate technical concepts clearly using proper computer science terminology
Evaluate and critique algorithmic solutions proposed by peers
rubric_criteria: Problem Analysis (25 points): Correctly identifies the core problem, breaks it into subproblems, and recognizes relevant constraints (time, space, data size). Shows clear understanding of what needs to be solved.

Algorithm Selection and Justification (25 points): Chooses appropriate algorithms for each subproblem, explains why selected algorithms are suitable, discusses time/space complexity in basic terms, considers alternative approaches.

Technical Communication (25 points): Uses correct computer science terminology, explains concepts clearly for a beginner audience, provides concrete examples, organizes thoughts logically with proper formatting.

Peer Engagement (25 points): Provides constructive feedback on at least two peer posts, asks thoughtful follow-up questions, suggests improvements or alternatives, responds professionally to feedback received.
instructions:
You will analyze the following scenario and propose an algorithmic solution:

**Scenario**: A small library wants to digitize their book management system. They need to: (1) store information about 5,000 books (title, author, ISBN, availability status), (2) allow patrons to search for books by title or author, (3) track which books are checked out and when they're due back, and (4) generate a daily report of overdue books.

**Your Task**:
1. **Initial Post** (due by Wednesday): Write 400-500 words addressing: What data structure(s) would you use to store book information and why? What algorithm(s) would you use for searching books? How would you handle the overdue book reporting? Explain your reasoning in simple terms, discuss advantages/disadvantages of your choices, and mention at least one alternative approach you considered.

2. **Peer Responses** (due by Friday): Respond thoughtfully to at least two classmates' posts (100-150 words each). Compare their approaches to yours, ask clarifying questions, or suggest improvements. Focus on the technical merits of different solutions.

**Format Requirements**: Use clear headings, code snippets if helpful, and cite any external resources. Post directly in the discussion forum with your name and date.
grading_notes: Look for evidence of genuine understanding rather than memorized definitions. Students should demonstrate they can connect abstract algorithms to practical applications. Common issues: confusing data structures with algorithms, not considering scalability, vague explanations without examples. Excellent responses (90-100) show creativity and deeper thinking beyond basic requirements. Good responses (80-89) meet all requirements competently. Satisfactory responses (70-79) show understanding but lack depth or have minor technical errors. Below 70 indicates significant gaps in understanding or incomplete submissions. Encourage students who struggle with terminology but show good problem-solving intuition.

title: End-to-End Data Science Project Presentation: Customer Churn Analysis
description: Students will present a comprehensive data science project analyzing customer churn using a provided telecommunications dataset. The presentation must demonstrate the complete data science workflow from exploratory data analysis through model deployment recommendations, showcasing technical proficiency and business acumen.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply the complete data science methodology to solve real-world business problems
Perform comprehensive exploratory data analysis and feature engineering
Build, evaluate, and compare multiple machine learning models using appropriate metrics
Communicate technical findings effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Demonstrate understanding of model deployment considerations and business impact
rubric_criteria: Data Exploration & Preprocessing (25 points): Quality of EDA visualizations, identification of data quality issues, appropriate handling of missing values and outliers, feature engineering creativity and justification

Model Development & Evaluation (25 points): Implementation of at least 3 different algorithms, proper train/validation/test splits, appropriate evaluation metrics (precision, recall, F1, AUC-ROC), hyperparameter tuning evidence, model comparison methodology

Business Insights & Recommendations (25 points): Clear articulation of business problem, actionable insights from data analysis, practical deployment recommendations, discussion of model limitations and potential risks, ROI considerations

Presentation Quality & Communication (25 points): Clear slide organization and visual design, effective use of visualizations, confident delivery within time limit, appropriate technical depth for audience, thoughtful responses to questions
instructions: You will analyze a telecommunications customer churn dataset and present your findings in a 15-minute presentation followed by 5 minutes of Q&A. Your analysis must include: (1) Exploratory Data Analysis with at least 5 meaningful visualizations identifying key patterns and relationships; (2) Data preprocessing steps including handling missing values, outliers, and feature engineering with clear justification; (3) Implementation and comparison of at least three different machine learning models (must include one tree-based and one linear model); (4) Model evaluation using multiple appropriate metrics with discussion of trade-offs; (5) Business recommendations including specific strategies to reduce churn and estimated impact. Technical requirements: Use Python with pandas, scikit-learn, and matplotlib/seaborn. Submit a Jupyter notebook with well-documented code and a PDF of your presentation slides 24 hours before presenting. Your presentation should be accessible to a mixed audience of technical team members and business stakeholders. Include at least one slide addressing ethical considerations and model limitations. Be prepared to answer questions about your methodology, alternative approaches, and implementation challenges.
grading_notes: Grade holistically within each criterion using 4-point scale: Excellent (23-25), Good (20-22), Satisfactory (17-19), Needs Improvement (0-16). Look for evidence of critical thinking beyond basic implementation. Common issues to watch: overfitting without proper validation, inappropriate metrics for imbalanced data, lack of business context, overly technical presentation for mixed audience. Deduct 5 points for time violations (under 12 or over 18 minutes). Strong projects typically show creative feature engineering, thoughtful model selection rationale, and clear connection between technical findings and business value. Grade distribution expectation: 20% A-range (90+), 50% B-range (80-89), 25% C-range (70-79), 5% below 70.

title: Electromagnetic Induction Laboratory Analysis Report
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive laboratory investigation of electromagnetic induction phenomena using Faraday's law, analyzing induced EMF in solenoids under varying conditions, and presenting findings in a formal research-style report with theoretical predictions, experimental methodology, data analysis, and error assessment.
estimated_time: 6-8 hours (3 hours lab work, 3-5 hours report writing)
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction to predict and calculate induced EMF in varying magnetic field scenarios
Design and execute controlled experiments to investigate the relationship between magnetic flux change and induced current
Analyze experimental data using statistical methods and uncertainty propagation to draw quantitative conclusions
Communicate complex physics concepts and experimental findings through professional scientific writing and data visualization
rubric_criteria: Theoretical Framework and Predictions (25 points): Demonstrates mastery of Faraday's law, Lenz's law, and magnetic flux concepts; provides accurate theoretical predictions with proper mathematical derivations; clearly explains physical principles underlying the experiment

Experimental Design and Methodology (25 points): Describes detailed, replicable experimental procedures; identifies and controls relevant variables; demonstrates proper use of instrumentation (oscilloscopes, function generators, coils); shows evidence of systematic data collection

Data Analysis and Interpretation (25 points): Presents data using appropriate graphs and tables; performs statistical analysis including uncertainty calculations; compares experimental results to theoretical predictions; discusses sources of error and their quantitative impact on results

Scientific Communication and Conclusions (25 points): Follows formal lab report structure (abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion); uses precise scientific language; draws evidence-based conclusions; suggests improvements and extensions; proper citation of sources
instructions: Conduct the electromagnetic induction experiment using the provided solenoids, magnets, and data acquisition equipment. Your investigation must include: (1) Measuring induced EMF as a function of magnet velocity through a solenoid, (2) Analyzing the relationship between coil geometry (number of turns, cross-sectional area) and induced EMF, (3) Investigating the effect of magnetic field strength on induction. Begin by deriving theoretical predictions using Faraday's law for each scenario. Record at least 50 data points across varied conditions, with minimum 5 trials per condition. Use oscilloscopes to capture EMF waveforms and measure peak voltages. Calculate uncertainties for all measurements using standard error propagation methods. Your report must include: executive summary (150 words), introduction with literature review, detailed methodology, results section with properly formatted graphs and tables, discussion comparing theory to experiment, conclusion, and references. Submit as PDF with embedded high-resolution figures. Include raw data spreadsheets as supplementary files. Reports must be 2500-3500 words, excluding figures and references. Use IEEE format for citations. Submit through course portal by 11:59 PM on due date. Late submissions penalized 10% per day.
grading_notes: Evaluate theoretical sections for correct application of electromagnetic theory - look for proper vector notation and calculus-based derivations. In methodology assessment, verify experimental controls and statistical rigor - students should demonstrate understanding of systematic vs. random errors. For data analysis, expect correlation coefficients >0.95 for well-executed experiments and uncertainty values <5% for EMF measurements. Strong reports will show creative problem-solving in experimental design and sophisticated error analysis. Common issues include: inadequate sampling rates on oscilloscopes, failure to account for coil resistance effects, and oversimplified uncertainty analysis. Grade distribution typically: 15% receive A grades (90-100), 35% receive B grades (80-89), 40% receive C grades (70-79), 10% receive below 70. Provide specific feedback on mathematical errors and suggest resources for improvement in weak areas.

title: E-commerce Customer Segmentation and Revenue Optimization Analysis
description: Students will analyze a real-world e-commerce dataset to identify customer segments, analyze purchasing patterns, and provide actionable business recommendations using statistical analysis and data visualization techniques.
