learning_objectives_assessed: Apply exploratory data analysis techniques to identify patterns and insights in business datasets
Implement customer segmentation using clustering algorithms and statistical methods
Create effective data visualizations to communicate findings to business stakeholders
Formulate data-driven business recommendations based on analytical findings
rubric_criteria: Data Exploration and Cleaning (25 points): Thorough examination of dataset structure, handling of missing values, outlier detection, and creation of meaningful derived variables with clear documentation of all preprocessing steps

Customer Segmentation Analysis (25 points): Appropriate application of clustering techniques (K-means, hierarchical), proper validation of cluster quality, clear interpretation of segment characteristics, and justification of optimal number of segments

Data Visualization and Communication (25 points): Creation of professional, well-labeled charts and graphs that effectively communicate insights, appropriate choice of visualization types, clear narrative connecting visuals to business implications

Business Recommendations and Report Quality (25 points): Actionable, specific recommendations supported by data evidence, clear executive summary, professional report formatting, and demonstration of business acumen in translating analytical findings
instructions:
You will receive an e-commerce dataset containing customer transactions, demographics, and product information spanning 12 months. Your task is to conduct a comprehensive analysis and deliver a business report with recommendations.

Deliverables:
1. Jupyter notebook (.ipynb) containing all code, analysis, and visualizations with markdown explanations
2. Executive summary presentation (8-10 slides) highlighting key findings
3. Written business report (4-6 pages) with recommendations

Required Analysis Components:
- Dataset overview with summary statistics and data quality assessment
- Customer segmentation using at least two different approaches
- Revenue analysis by segment including lifetime value calculations
- Seasonal and trend analysis of purchasing patterns
- Product performance analysis across segments
- Statistical significance testing for key findings

Technical Requirements:
- Use Python with pandas, numpy, matplotlib/seaborn, and scikit-learn
- Include at least 8 meaningful visualizations
- Implement proper statistical testing where appropriate
- Document all assumptions and limitations

Submission Format:
- Submit all files in a single ZIP folder
- Name files: LastName_FirstName_DataAnalysis_[type]
- Include a README file listing all dependencies
- Ensure code runs without errors and produces all outputs

Due date: [Insert specific date]. Late submissions will lose 5 points per day.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical competency alongside business insight. Look for: proper statistical methodology, code efficiency and readability, creative problem-solving approaches, and realistic business understanding. Common issues include: inadequate data cleaning documentation, choosing wrong number of clusters without validation, creating misleading visualizations, and providing generic rather than specific recommendations. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level work (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 40% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. Deduct points for code that doesn't run, missing deliverables, or poor professional presentation. Bonus consideration for innovative approaches or insights beyond requirements.

title: Comprehensive Project Recovery and Stakeholder Crisis Management Exam
description: Students will analyze a failing project scenario involving multiple stakeholders, budget overruns, scope creep, and team conflicts. They must develop a comprehensive recovery plan, conduct stakeholder analysis, create risk mitigation strategies, and present executive-level recommendations for project continuation or termination.
learning_objectives_assessed: Evaluate project performance using advanced metrics and develop data-driven recovery strategies
Conduct comprehensive stakeholder analysis and design targeted communication strategies for crisis situations
Apply risk management frameworks to identify, assess, and mitigate project threats and opportunities
Synthesize project management methodologies to make strategic decisions about project viability and resource allocation
rubric_criteria: Project Analysis and Recovery Strategy (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of project metrics (SPI, CPI, EAC, BAC), accurately diagnoses root causes of project failure, and develops feasible recovery timeline with realistic resource requirements and milestone adjustments

Stakeholder Management and Communication Plan (25 points): Conducts thorough stakeholder analysis using power/interest matrices, identifies key influencers and blockers, designs differentiated communication strategies for each stakeholder group, and addresses conflict resolution with specific tactics

Risk Assessment and Mitigation Framework (25 points): Identifies and quantifies project risks using probability/impact analysis, develops comprehensive mitigation strategies with contingency plans, demonstrates understanding of risk tolerance levels, and integrates risk monitoring into project governance

Executive Decision Making and Strategic Recommendations (25 points): Presents clear go/no-go recommendation with supporting financial analysis, demonstrates understanding of organizational strategy alignment, provides alternative scenarios with cost-benefit analysis, and shows advanced critical thinking in project portfolio context
instructions: You are the newly appointed Senior Project Manager for TechGlobal Corp's failing ERP implementation project. The project is 18 months into a planned 24-month timeline, 40% over budget ($2.4M spent of $1.7M approved), and 25% behind schedule. Key issues include: vendor relationship breakdown, user resistance to system changes, incomplete data migration, and executive sponsor turnover. Your task is to prepare a comprehensive assessment and recommendation report for the Executive Committee meeting in 72 hours. Your submission must include: (1) Executive Summary with clear recommendation (continue/pivot/terminate), (2) Current state analysis using earned value management calculations and critical path assessment, (3) Stakeholder analysis matrix identifying 8-10 key stakeholders with individual engagement strategies, (4) Risk register with 15-20 identified risks, probability/impact ratings, and specific mitigation plans, (5) Three alternative scenarios (aggressive recovery/conservative recovery/controlled termination) with timeline, budget, and resource implications for each, (6) Implementation roadmap for your recommended scenario including 90-day action plan with specific deliverables and success metrics. Format your response as a professional consulting report with data visualizations, financial projections, and executive-level language. Include assumptions, constraints, and success criteria. Minimum 2,500 words excluding charts and appendices.
grading_notes: Look for evidence of advanced project management concepts beyond basic PM knowledge. Students should demonstrate familiarity with PMI standards, agile/hybrid methodologies, and organizational change management. Exceptional responses will show original thinking in stakeholder psychology, creative problem-solving for resource constraints, and sophisticated understanding of business case development. Common weaknesses include oversimplified risk analysis, unrealistic recovery timelines, and failure to address organizational politics. Grade distribution should follow: 90-100% (demonstrates mastery with innovative solutions), 80-89% (solid competency with minor gaps), 70-79% (basic understanding with significant weaknesses), below 70% (inadequate grasp of advanced concepts). Pay special attention to financial calculations accuracy and stakeholder communication differentiation.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Simulation: Multi-Stakeholder Decision Analysis
description: Students analyze and debate leadership decisions during a complex organizational crisis involving ethical dilemmas, competing stakeholder interests, and resource constraints. Through facilitated discussion, students demonstrate advanced leadership competencies including strategic thinking, stakeholder management, ethical reasoning, and adaptive decision-making under pressure.
learning_objectives_assessed: Evaluate complex leadership decisions using multiple theoretical frameworks and stakeholder perspectives
Demonstrate advanced ethical reasoning and moral leadership in crisis situations
Synthesize strategic thinking with emotional intelligence to navigate organizational conflicts
Apply transformational and adaptive leadership principles to drive organizational change during uncertainty
rubric_criteria: Strategic Analysis & Decision Quality (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of strategic implications, evaluates multiple viable alternatives, integrates risk assessment with stakeholder impact analysis, and proposes well-reasoned solutions supported by leadership theory

Stakeholder Management & Communication (25 points): Identifies all relevant stakeholders and power dynamics, articulates clear communication strategies for different audiences, demonstrates cultural sensitivity and inclusive leadership approaches, and shows awareness of long-term relationship implications

Ethical Leadership & Moral Reasoning (25 points): Applies ethical frameworks consistently, recognizes moral complexity and competing values, demonstrates integrity in decision-making processes, and balances organizational needs with social responsibility and individual rights

Discussion Leadership & Professional Engagement (25 points): Facilitates meaningful dialogue, challenges assumptions constructively, builds on others' contributions effectively, demonstrates active listening and empathy, and maintains professional demeanor while managing conflict productively
instructions: You will participate in a structured case discussion analyzing the leadership challenges faced by Taylor Chen, newly appointed CEO of MedTech Solutions, a pharmaceutical company facing simultaneous crises: a potential drug safety issue, major layoffs due to market pressures, activist investor demands, and whistleblower allegations of research misconduct. Pre-discussion preparation (60 minutes): Read the comprehensive case study materials, identify key stakeholders and their competing interests, research relevant leadership theories and ethical frameworks, and prepare three strategic recommendations with supporting rationale. During the discussion session, you will engage in three phases: (1) Stakeholder Analysis Round Table - present your stakeholder mapping and discuss power dynamics (45 minutes); (2) Ethical Dilemma Deep Dive - debate the moral dimensions using structured ethical frameworks (45 minutes); (3) Strategic Decision Simulation - role-play board meeting scenarios with assigned stakeholder perspectives (30 minutes). You must actively contribute substantive insights, challenge peers' assumptions respectfully, and demonstrate integration of course concepts. Participation will be evaluated in real-time using observation rubrics. Submit a one-page reflection within 24 hours summarizing your key insights and how your thinking evolved during the discussion.
grading_notes: Use real-time observation sheets to track individual contributions across all four criteria. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-range, 60% B-range, 25% C-range for expert-level assessment. Common issues to monitor: students defaulting to simplistic solutions without considering stakeholder complexity, failing to apply theoretical frameworks rigorously, dominating discussion without building on others' ideas, or avoiding difficult ethical questions. Award full points only for sophisticated analysis that demonstrates mastery-level integration of multiple leadership competencies. Mid-session check-ins help calibrate participation levels. Post-discussion reflections should show evidence of learning and perspective shifts to earn full credit.

title: AWS Cloud Fundamentals Business Case Presentation
description: Students will create and deliver a 10-minute presentation proposing AWS cloud migration for a fictional small business, demonstrating understanding of core AWS services, benefits, and basic cost considerations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify and explain core AWS services (EC2, S3, RDS) and their business applications
Articulate the key benefits of cloud computing using AWS
Demonstrate understanding of AWS pricing models and cost optimization basics
Communicate technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders effectively
rubric_criteria: Technical Content Accuracy (25 points): Correct explanation of at least 3 core AWS services, accurate description of cloud benefits, proper use of AWS terminology
Business Application (25 points): Realistic business scenario, appropriate service selection for use case, clear connection between technical solutions and business needs
Cost Analysis (25 points): Demonstrates understanding of AWS pricing models, includes basic cost estimation using AWS Calculator, addresses cost optimization strategies
Presentation Quality (25 points): Clear delivery within time limit, professional slides with AWS architecture diagram, effective communication to business audience
instructions: You will create a 10-minute business presentation proposing AWS cloud migration for a fictional company of your choice (retail, healthcare, education, etc.). Your presentation must include: (1) Company background and current IT challenges, (2) Proposed AWS solution using at least 3 core services (choose from EC2, S3, RDS, Lambda, VPC), (3) Benefits analysis covering scalability, reliability, and security, (4) Cost breakdown using AWS Simple Monthly Calculator with at least one optimization strategy, (5) Basic architecture diagram showing service connections. Create 8-12 professional slides suitable for a business audience. Include speaker notes for each slide. Submit your presentation file 24 hours before your scheduled presentation slot. During delivery, assume your audience consists of business executives with limited technical background. You will have 2 minutes for Q&A after your presentation. Presentations exceeding 12 minutes will lose points. Use official AWS service names and avoid overly technical jargon.
grading_notes: Focus on conceptual understanding rather than deep technical implementation. Expect students to use basic AWS terminology correctly but may need clarification on advanced concepts. Common issues: oversimplifying cost analysis, choosing inappropriate services for use case, exceeding time limits, too much technical detail for business audience. Grade distribution should follow: 90-100 (exceptional business case with accurate technical content), 80-89 (solid understanding with minor technical errors), 70-79 (basic competency with some conceptual gaps), below 70 (significant technical inaccuracies or incomplete requirements). Provide immediate feedback after each presentation focusing on technical accuracy and business communication effectiveness.

title: Project Risk Management Portfolio: Comprehensive Risk Assessment and Response Planning
description: Students will develop a complete risk management portfolio for a realistic project scenario, demonstrating their ability to identify, analyze, prioritize, and develop response strategies for project risks using PMP-standard methodologies and tools.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply systematic risk identification techniques to uncover potential project threats and opportunities
Perform qualitative and quantitative risk analysis using probability-impact matrices and expected monetary value calculations
Develop appropriate risk response strategies aligned with organizational risk tolerance and project constraints
Create comprehensive risk monitoring and control processes with clear metrics and triggers
rubric_criteria: Risk Identification and Documentation (25 points): Comprehensive identification of at least 15 relevant risks using multiple techniques (brainstorming, SWOT, expert interviews), proper categorization using RBS, complete risk register with clear descriptions and potential impacts

Risk Analysis and Prioritization (25 points): Accurate qualitative analysis with justified probability/impact ratings, properly constructed probability-impact matrix, quantitative analysis including EMV calculations for top 5 risks, clear risk prioritization with supporting rationale

Risk Response Planning (25 points): Appropriate response strategies (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept) for all high and medium risks, detailed action plans with assigned owners, realistic budgets and timelines, identification of residual and secondary risks

Risk Monitoring Framework (25 points): Comprehensive monitoring plan with KPIs and trigger conditions, clear escalation procedures, regular review schedule, lessons learned documentation process, integration with overall project management processes
instructions: You are the project manager for a $2.5M software implementation project at a mid-sized healthcare organization. The project involves implementing a new electronic health records (EHR) system across three hospital locations over 18 months. Your portfolio must include: 1) Executive Summary (2 pages) outlining your risk management approach and key findings, 2) Complete Risk Register identifying minimum 15 risks across technical, organizational, external, and project management categories, 3) Risk Analysis Report showing qualitative assessment using probability-impact matrix and quantitative analysis (EMV) for top 5 risks, 4) Risk Response Plan detailing specific strategies, action items, owners, budgets, and timelines for all medium and high-priority risks, 5) Risk Monitoring and Control Plan including KPIs, review schedules, reporting templates, and escalation procedures. Use professional project management templates and tools. Assume a risk budget of $125K (5% of project budget) and organizational risk tolerance of medium-low. Submit as a single PDF with clear sections, executive-level formatting, and appendices for detailed calculations. Include at least 3 credible external sources supporting your risk assessment methodology.
grading_notes: Evaluate portfolios based on practical applicability and PMP alignment. Look for realistic risk scenarios specific to healthcare IT implementations, not generic project risks. Expect students to demonstrate understanding of risk tolerance impact on response strategies. Common issues include: insufficient risk detail, unrealistic probability/impact assessments, inappropriate response strategies, and weak monitoring frameworks. Grade distribution should target 15% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 40% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. Deduct points for late submission, formatting issues, or failure to use proper PM terminology. Provide specific feedback on risk assessment accuracy and response strategy feasibility.

title: Personal Task Manager Console Application
description: Students will design and implement a command-line task manager application using fundamental programming concepts including data structures, file I/O, user input validation, and basic algorithms. The application will allow users to add, view, edit, delete, and save tasks with priority levels.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply fundamental programming constructs (variables, loops, conditionals, functions)
Implement basic data structures (lists/arrays) to store and manipulate data
Demonstrate file input/output operations for data persistence
Design user-friendly command-line interfaces with input validation
Apply problem-solving skills to break down complex requirements into manageable components
rubric_criteria: Core Functionality (25 points): Application successfully implements all required features - add task, view tasks, edit task, delete task, and save/load from file with proper error handling
Code Quality and Structure (25 points): Code is well-organized with appropriate functions, meaningful variable names, consistent formatting, and includes comments explaining key logic sections
User Interface and Input Validation (25 points): Clear menu system, helpful prompts, appropriate error messages for invalid input, and intuitive user experience throughout the application
Data Persistence and File Operations (25 points): Tasks are properly saved to and loaded from a text file, handles file errors gracefully, and maintains data integrity across program sessions
instructions: Create a console-based task manager application in your chosen programming language (Python, Java, or C++). Your program must include: 1) A main menu with options to add, view, edit, delete tasks, and exit; 2) Task storage using a list/array where each task has a title, description, priority (High/Medium/Low), and completion status; 3) Add function that prompts for task details with input validation; 4) View function displaying all tasks in a formatted table with numbering; 5) Edit function allowing users to modify existing tasks by selecting task number; 6) Delete function to remove tasks by number with confirmation prompt; 7) Automatic save/load functionality using a text file (tasks.txt) that persists data between program runs. Include error handling for invalid menu choices, empty task lists, invalid task numbers, and file operations. Submit your source code file(s), a sample tasks.txt file with 3-5 example tasks, and a brief README explaining how to run your program. Code must include comments explaining major functions and logic. Test thoroughly with various inputs including edge cases.
grading_notes: Focus on functionality first - ensure all required features work correctly before evaluating code style. Common issues include: inadequate input validation (deduct from UI criteria), missing error handling for file operations, poor menu design, and insufficient comments. Expect most students to achieve 70-85 points, with full points reserved for polished implementations with excellent error handling and user experience. Accept any reasonable file format for data persistence. Allow minor variations in menu structure as long as all core functionality is present. Partial credit: 50% for incomplete functionality, 25% deduction for major bugs, 10% deduction for poor code organization or missing comments.

title: Customer Churn Prediction: End-to-End Data Science Analysis
description: Students will perform a comprehensive data science analysis on a customer churn dataset, including data preprocessing, exploratory data analysis, feature engineering, model building, evaluation, and business recommendations. This assessment evaluates practical application of the complete data science workflow.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply data preprocessing techniques including handling missing values, outliers, and categorical encoding
Conduct meaningful exploratory data analysis with appropriate visualizations and statistical insights
Implement feature engineering techniques to improve model performance
Build, compare, and evaluate multiple machine learning models using appropriate metrics
Interpret model results and provide actionable business recommendations
rubric_criteria: Data Preprocessing & Feature Engineering (25 points): Proper handling of missing values, outliers, data types, scaling, and creation of meaningful features. Code is clean, well-commented, and efficient.

Exploratory Data Analysis (25 points): Comprehensive analysis with appropriate visualizations, statistical summaries, correlation analysis, and clear insights about churn patterns. Visualizations are properly labeled and interpretable.

Model Development & Evaluation (25 points): Implementation of at least 2 different algorithms, proper train/validation/test splits, appropriate evaluation metrics (precision, recall, F1, AUC-ROC), hyperparameter tuning, and comparison of model performance.

Business Insights & Communication (25 points): Clear interpretation of results, identification of key churn drivers, actionable business recommendations, and professional presentation of findings with executive summary.
instructions: You are provided with a telecommunications customer dataset containing 20 features and 7,043 customer records. Your task is to build a predictive model for customer churn and provide business insights. Submit a Jupyter notebook with the following sections: 1) Data Loading & Initial Exploration (load data, examine structure, identify data quality issues), 2) Data Preprocessing (handle missing values, encode categorical variables, address outliers, feature scaling), 3) Exploratory Data Analysis (create 5-7 meaningful visualizations showing churn patterns, calculate key statistics, identify correlations), 4) Feature Engineering (create at least 2 new features that could improve prediction), 5) Model Development (implement Logistic Regression and Random Forest, use 70/15/15 train/validation/test split, perform hyperparameter tuning using validation set), 6) Model Evaluation (compare models using confusion matrices, ROC curves, and classification reports on test set), 7) Business Insights (executive summary with top 3 churn drivers and 3 specific retention strategies). grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy and business acumen equally. Deduct points for: code that doesn't run (-10 points), missing required visualizations (-5 points each), inappropriate evaluation metrics (-10 points), lack of hyperparameter tuning (-10 points). Critically evaluate mathematical solutions and reasoning presented by peers
Communicate mathematical concepts clearly using appropriate terminology and notation
Synthesize multiple mathematical approaches to justify optimal solution strategies

grading_notes: Evaluate initial posts for mathematical sophistication beyond basic algebraic manipulation - look for calculus, statistics, linear algebra, or differential equations as appropriate. title: Complex Project Crisis Management and Recovery Assessment
description: Students will analyze a multi-faceted project crisis scenario, demonstrate advanced risk assessment capabilities, develop comprehensive recovery strategies, and present actionable solutions using industry-standard project management methodologies. This assessment evaluates critical thinking, stakeholder management, resource optimization, and leadership decision-making under pressure.
estimated_time: 4-5 hours (3 hours analysis/planning + 1-2 hours presentation preparation)
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced risk management frameworks to identify, analyze, and prioritize project threats and opportunities
Develop comprehensive project recovery strategies using evidence-based decision-making and stakeholder analysis
Demonstrate mastery of project control techniques including schedule compression, resource reallocation, and scope management
Integrate multiple project management methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, Hybrid) to address complex organizational challenges
Evaluate project success metrics and recommend sustainable practices for long-term project governance
rubric_criteria: Crisis Analysis and Risk Assessment (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of root cause analysis, uses appropriate risk management tools (risk registers, probability-impact matrices), identifies interconnected risks, and provides quantitative/qualitative risk evaluation with supporting evidence

Recovery Strategy Development (25 points): Presents comprehensive, realistic recovery plan with clear timeline, resource requirements, and stakeholder considerations; incorporates multiple PM methodologies appropriately; addresses scope, schedule, budget, and quality constraints with specific techniques

Stakeholder Communication and Change Management (25 points): Develops detailed communication plan for various stakeholder groups, addresses resistance management, demonstrates understanding of organizational change dynamics, and provides specific scripts/templates for critical conversations

Implementation Feasibility and Controls (25 points): Establishes measurable success criteria, defines monitoring and control mechanisms, addresses sustainability of solutions, considers organizational constraints, and provides realistic implementation roadmap with contingency planning
instructions:
You are the Senior Project Manager for TechNova Corp's $2.8M digital transformation initiative, 18 months into a planned 24-month timeline. Your project faces multiple critical issues: 30% budget overrun, key vendor bankruptcy requiring technology platform change, two senior team members departing, regulatory compliance requirements changing mid-project, and CEO demanding accelerated delivery for competitive advantage. Additionally, user acceptance testing revealed 40% of features don't meet stakeholder expectations, and the IT infrastructure team reports capacity constraints affecting deployment.

Complete the following deliverables:

1. **Crisis Assessment Report** (40% of assessment): Conduct comprehensive root cause analysis using fishbone diagrams or similar tools. Create updated risk register with probability-impact analysis. Provide quantified assessment of current project health across all knowledge areas.

2. **Recovery Strategy Plan** (40% of assessment): Develop detailed recovery roadmap addressing all identified issues. Include specific techniques for schedule compression, resource optimization, and scope management. Justify methodology selection (Agile transition, hybrid approach, etc.) with supporting rationale.

3. **Stakeholder Communication Strategy** (20% of assessment): Create communication plan for CEO, project team, vendors, and end-users. Include sample communications for critical conversations and change management approach.

Submit as professional project document (8-12 pages) with executive summary, detailed analysis, visual aids (charts, diagrams, timelines), and appendices with supporting tools. Use industry-standard templates and terminology. Include references to PMI standards, frameworks, and best practices. All recommendations must be actionable and resource-specific.
grading_notes: Evaluate depth of analysis over surface-level recommendations. Look for integration of multiple PM knowledge areas and realistic resource considerations. Excellent responses will demonstrate understanding of organizational dynamics and change management complexity. Common issues include oversimplified solutions, ignoring stakeholder politics, unrealistic timelines, and failure to address root causes. Grade distribution expectation: 20% A-level (90-100), 40% B-level (80-89), 30% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. Deduct points for generic recommendations not tied to specific scenario details. Reward creative but feasible solutions supported by PM theory and practice.

title: Strategic Organizational Change Leadership Initiative

learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate strategic thinking and systems-level analysis in complex organizational contexts
Apply advanced change management theories and frameworks to real-world leadership challenges
Design effective stakeholder engagement and communication strategies for organizational transformation
Evaluate and mitigate resistance to change through evidence-based leadership interventions
Create measurable implementation plans with risk assessment and contingency strategies
rubric_criteria: Strategic Analysis & Vision (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of organizational context, identifies root causes vs. symptoms, articulates compelling vision for change with clear business rationale and measurable success metrics

Stakeholder Management & Communication (25 points): Conducts comprehensive stakeholder mapping with influence/impact analysis, designs targeted communication strategies for different audiences, addresses cultural considerations and potential conflicts

Change Implementation Strategy (25 points): Develops detailed phased implementation plan with realistic timelines, resource allocation, risk mitigation strategies, and contingency plans; incorporates change management best practices and theoretical frameworks

Leadership Presence & Presentation (25 points): Delivers executive-level presentation with confidence and authority, responds effectively to challenging questions, demonstrates authentic leadership style, uses data visualization and storytelling to influence decision-makers
instructions: Select a real organization (your current/former employer, case study, or publicly documented company) facing a significant change challenge. Your project must include: 1) Executive Summary (2 pages) outlining the change initiative and expected ROI; 2) Situational Analysis (4-5 pages) using frameworks like SWOT, stakeholder mapping, and cultural assessment; 3) Change Strategy & Implementation Plan (6-8 pages) detailing phases, timelines, resource requirements, communication plans, and success metrics; 4) Risk Assessment & Mitigation (2-3 pages) identifying potential obstacles and contingency strategies; 5) 20-minute executive presentation with Q&A session simulating a board-level proposal. Use minimum 12 credible sources including peer-reviewed articles, industry reports, and leadership texts. Format: APA style, 12-point font, double-spaced. Submit written report 48 hours before presentation. Include appendices with supporting materials (surveys, templates, budget details). Your presentation should persuade senior leadership to approve your change initiative - focus on business impact, not just process. Be prepared to defend your strategy against skeptical questioning and alternative approaches.
grading_notes: Evaluate based on depth of analysis rather than just completion of requirements. Look for evidence of original thinking and practical applicability. Excellent work (90-100) shows innovative solutions with sophisticated stakeholder psychology understanding. Good work (80-89) demonstrates solid frameworks application with realistic implementation. Satisfactory work (70-79) covers basics but lacks strategic depth. Common issues include: oversimplified stakeholder analysis, unrealistic timelines, generic change models without customization, weak financial justification, and poor presentation delivery. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-range, 60% B-range, 25% C-range given expert difficulty level. Pay special attention to how students handle challenging questions during presentations - this reveals true leadership readiness. Provide specific feedback on leadership presence and executive communication skills.

title: AWS Core Services Implementation and Architecture Design Exam
description: Students will demonstrate foundational knowledge of AWS core services by designing a basic three-tier web application architecture, configuring security groups, and explaining cost optimization strategies. This practical exam tests understanding of EC2, S3, RDS, VPC fundamentals, and AWS best practices.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design basic AWS architectures using core services (EC2, S3, RDS, VPC)
Configure fundamental AWS security controls and access management
Apply cost optimization principles to AWS resource selection
Demonstrate understanding of AWS global infrastructure and service availability
rubric_criteria: Architecture Design (25 points): Correctly designs a three-tier web application using appropriate AWS services, shows proper component relationships, demonstrates understanding of availability zones and regions
Security Implementation (25 points): Properly configures security groups, demonstrates understanding of IAM basics, shows knowledge of data encryption options and network security fundamentals
Cost Optimization (25 points): Selects appropriate instance types and storage classes, explains Reserved Instance concepts, demonstrates understanding of free tier limitations and billing basics
Technical Accuracy (25 points): Uses correct AWS terminology, shows accurate understanding of service capabilities and limitations, provides realistic configuration parameters and settings
instructions:
This exam consists of three sections that must be completed within 90 minutes. You may use AWS documentation and the AWS console for reference, but no collaboration is permitted.

SECTION 1 - Architecture Diagram (40 minutes): Create a detailed architecture diagram for a three-tier web application serving 1000+ users. Your design must include: web servers in multiple availability zones, application load balancer, RDS database with backup strategy, S3 bucket for static content, and VPC with public/private subnets. Label all components and include brief explanations for your choices.

SECTION 2 - Security Configuration (30 minutes): Design security groups for your architecture from Section 1. Specify inbound/outbound rules for each tier, explain the principle of least privilege application, and describe how you would implement user authentication and database access controls. Include IAM role recommendations for EC2 instances.

SECTION 3 - Cost Analysis (20 minutes): Calculate estimated monthly costs for your architecture assuming moderate usage (2 t3.medium instances, 100GB RDS storage, 500GB S3 storage, standard data transfer). Recommend three specific cost optimization strategies and explain how Reserved Instances could reduce expenses. Show your calculations and reasoning.

Submit your work as a single PDF document with clearly labeled sections. Include all diagrams, configurations, and calculations. Ensure your architecture diagram is readable and professionally presented.
grading_notes: Grade each section independently, then sum for total score. Architecture diagrams should show logical connections between components - artistic quality is less important than technical accuracy. For security configurations, look for understanding of layered security rather than memorization of specific port numbers. Cost calculations don't need to be exact to the penny, but should demonstrate understanding of AWS pricing models. Common issues to watch: students mixing up security group rules direction, overcomplicating architectures, unrealistic cost estimates. Expect score distribution: 15% scoring 90-100 points, 60% scoring 70-89 points, 25% scoring below 70 points. Partial credit should be given for partially correct answers that show understanding of concepts.

title: Risk Management Strategy Discussion: Multi-Project Portfolio Scenario
description: Students will analyze a complex multi-project portfolio scenario and develop comprehensive risk management strategies while engaging in peer discussions about risk identification, assessment, and mitigation approaches across different project types and organizational contexts.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate proficiency in identifying and categorizing project risks using PMI risk management processes
Apply qualitative and quantitative risk analysis techniques to prioritize risks effectively
Develop appropriate risk response strategies aligned with organizational risk tolerance
Evaluate the effectiveness of risk monitoring and control mechanisms in dynamic project environments
rubric_criteria: Risk Identification and Analysis (25 points): Comprehensive identification of at least 8-10 relevant risks across technical, organizational, external, and project management categories. Demonstrates clear understanding of risk probability and impact assessment with appropriate justification for risk ratings.

Risk Response Strategy Development (25 points): Proposes specific, actionable risk response strategies (avoid, transfer, mitigate, accept) that are appropriate for each identified risk. Includes contingency plans and considers cost-benefit analysis of proposed responses.

Peer Engagement and Discussion Quality (25 points): Provides substantive responses to at least 3 peer posts with constructive feedback, alternative perspectives, or additional insights. Demonstrates active listening and builds upon others' ideas while maintaining professional discourse.

Application of PMP Knowledge and Best Practices (25 points): Correctly applies PMI terminology, processes, and tools. References appropriate PMBOK Guide processes and demonstrates understanding of risk management integration with other knowledge areas.
instructions:
You are a senior project manager at TechGlobal Corp, overseeing a portfolio containing three concurrent projects: (1) ERP system implementation across 15 international offices, (2) new mobile app development for customer service, and (3) office consolidation involving 500+ employee relocations. Each project has different stakeholder groups, timelines, and success criteria, but they share some resources and have interdependencies.

Your task is to create a comprehensive risk management discussion post (800-1000 words) that addresses: 1) Identify and categorize at least 8-10 significant risks across the three projects, explaining your risk identification techniques; 2) Conduct qualitative risk analysis by rating each risk's probability and impact, providing clear justification for your assessments; 3) Develop specific risk response strategies for your top 5 highest-priority risks, including primary responses and contingency plans; 4) Propose a risk monitoring and control framework that accounts for the multi-project environment and resource sharing.

After posting your initial response, engage with at least three classmates' posts by Thursday. Provide constructive feedback on their risk assessments, suggest alternative mitigation strategies, or share insights from your professional experience. Your responses should be 150-200 words each and add meaningful value to the discussion.

Format your post with clear headings for each section. Use bullet points for risk lists and ensure all risk ratings include brief explanations. Submit your initial post by Tuesday 11:59 PM and complete peer responses by Thursday 11:59 PM.
grading_notes: Look for evidence of systematic thinking rather than generic risk lists. Students should demonstrate understanding that risks in multi-project environments can have cascading effects. Award full points for risk identification only when students show variety across risk categories and provide project-specific examples. For risk responses, evaluate feasibility and appropriateness rather than creativity alone. Peer engagement should be substantive - simple agreement or generic comments should receive partial credit. Watch for students who apply risk management processes in isolation rather than integrating with other PM knowledge areas. Expected grade distribution: 20% A-level (90-100), 50% B-level (80-89), 25% C-level (70-79), 5% below 70. Deduct points for late submissions: 5% per day for initial post, 3% per day for peer responses.

title: Basic Python Programming Lab Report: Temperature Converter Application
description: Students will develop a Python program that converts temperatures between Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin, then document their development process, code analysis, and testing results in a comprehensive lab report.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply fundamental Python programming concepts including variables, functions, and control structures
Implement user input validation and error handling in Python applications
Document code effectively using comments and technical writing
Test and debug programs systematically using various test cases
Analyze program efficiency and suggest potential improvements
rubric_criteria: Code Implementation (25 points): Program correctly converts between all three temperature scales, uses appropriate functions, includes proper variable naming, and handles basic user input

Error Handling & Validation (25 points): Implements input validation for non-numeric values, handles edge cases (e.g., below absolute zero), provides meaningful error messages, and program doesn't crash on invalid input

Documentation & Code Quality (25 points): Code includes clear comments explaining logic, follows consistent formatting/indentation, uses descriptive variable names, and lab report includes complete code listings with explanations

title: Customer Churn Prediction: Exploratory Data Analysis and Model Implementation Quiz
description: Students will analyze a customer churn dataset, perform comprehensive exploratory data analysis, implement and compare multiple machine learning models, and provide actionable business insights. This assessment evaluates practical data science skills including data preprocessing, visualization, model selection, and interpretation of results.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply appropriate data preprocessing techniques including handling missing values, encoding categorical variables, and feature scaling
Conduct comprehensive exploratory data analysis using statistical methods and visualizations to identify patterns and relationships
Implement and compare multiple supervised learning algorithms for classification problems
Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics and interpret results in business context
Communicate findings effectively through data visualizations and written analysis
rubric_criteria: Data Preprocessing and Cleaning (25 points): Correctly handles missing values, encodes categorical variables appropriately, addresses outliers, and scales features where necessary. Demonstrates understanding of data quality issues and their impact on modeling.

Exploratory Data Analysis and Visualization (25 points): Creates meaningful visualizations that reveal data patterns, calculates relevant statistical summaries, identifies correlations and relationships between variables, and provides insights about churn factors.

Model Implementation and Comparison (25 points): Successfully implements at least three different classification algorithms (e.g., logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting), properly splits data into training/validation/test sets, tunes hyperparameters appropriately, and compares models using multiple evaluation metrics.

instructions:

1. Jupyter notebook (.ipynb) with well-documented code and markdown explanations
2. Executive summary (500-750 words) presenting key findings and recommendations

title: Mathematical Modeling of Epidemic Spread: A Comprehensive Analysis Project
description: Students will develop and analyze mathematical models to predict disease transmission patterns, comparing SIR (Susceptible-Infected-Recovered) models with real-world COVID-19 data. This project integrates differential equations, statistical analysis, parameter estimation, and mathematical communication skills.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply differential equations to model real-world phenomena and solve systems of ODEs
Analyze mathematical models by determining equilibrium points, stability, and long-term behavior
Use statistical methods to estimate parameters from real data and validate model predictions
Communicate complex mathematical concepts through written reports and visual representations
Evaluate model limitations and propose improvements based on mathematical reasoning
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Model Development (25 points): Correctly formulates SIR differential equation system, clearly defines variables and parameters, demonstrates understanding of model assumptions, and shows proper mathematical notation and setup

Mathematical Analysis and Solution Methods (25 points): Accurately solves differential equations using appropriate techniques (analytical or numerical), finds and analyzes equilibrium points, determines stability conditions, and calculates key metrics like basic reproduction number R₀

Data Analysis and Parameter Estimation (25 points): Effectively uses real epidemic data to estimate model parameters, applies curve-fitting or optimization techniques, validates model against actual data, and performs sensitivity analysis on key parameters

Communication and Interpretation (25 points): Produces clear, well-structured written report with proper mathematical exposition, creates effective visualizations and graphs, interprets results in context, discusses model limitations and real-world implications with mathematical precision
instructions: You will create a comprehensive mathematical analysis of epidemic spread using the SIR model framework. Begin by researching the basic SIR model: dS/dt = -βSI/N, dI/dt = βSI/N - γI, dR/dt = γI, where S, I, R represent susceptible, infected, and recovered populations respectively. Your project must include: (1) Mathematical Development: Derive the model from first principles, explain each parameter's meaning (β = transmission rate, γ = recovery rate), and analyze the basic reproduction number R₀ = β/γ. Find equilibrium points and determine their stability. (2) Numerical Solution: Implement the model using computational tools (Python, MATLAB, or similar) to generate solution curves for various parameter values. Create phase portraits and analyze long-term behavior. (3) Real Data Analysis: Obtain COVID-19 case data from a specific region/country during a clear outbreak period. Use curve-fitting techniques to estimate β and γ from real data. Compare your model predictions with actual data progression. (4) Model Validation and Extensions: Discuss where your model succeeds and fails compared to real data. Propose and briefly analyze one extension (e.g., SEIR model adding exposed population, vaccination effects, or time-varying parameters). Submit a 8-10 page written report including all mathematical work, code appendix, data sources, graphs, and analysis. Include a 1-page executive summary highlighting key findings. All mathematical statements must be properly justified, and graphs must be clearly labeled with appropriate scales and units.
grading_notes: Look for mathematical rigor in model derivation and analysis - students should show understanding of differential equations theory, not just computational results. Parameter estimation should demonstrate statistical thinking, not just curve-fitting software use. Common issues include: incorrect stability analysis of equilibrium points, unrealistic parameter values without justification, poor scaling in numerical solutions, and failure to address model limitations. Expect grade distribution: 15% will demonstrate exceptional mathematical insight and extension ideas (A+ range), 25% will complete all requirements with solid mathematical understanding (A range), 40% will have good mathematical development but weaker data analysis or communication (B range), 15% will show basic competency but significant gaps in analysis (C range), 5% will demonstrate insufficient mathematical understanding (below C). Pay special attention to mathematical communication - advanced students should write clearly for mathematical audiences while explaining real-world significance.

title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics and Electromagnetic Theory Comprehensive Exam
description: A rigorous examination testing mastery of quantum mechanical principles, wave functions, electromagnetic field theory, and their applications to real-world systems. Students will solve complex problems involving Schrödinger equations, quantum tunneling, Maxwell's equations, and electromagnetic wave propagation.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply Schrödinger equation to solve quantum mechanical problems involving potential barriers and harmonic oscillators
Analyze electromagnetic field interactions using Maxwell's equations and boundary conditions
Evaluate quantum tunneling phenomena and calculate transmission coefficients
Synthesize electromagnetic wave theory to predict wave behavior in various media
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Problem Solving (25 points): Demonstrates correct application of quantum mechanics equations, proper mathematical derivations, accurate calculations, and appropriate use of boundary conditions
Electromagnetic Theory Application (25 points): Shows mastery of Maxwell's equations, correct application of Gauss's law, Faraday's law, and Ampère's law to complex field configurations

Conceptual Understanding (25 points): Exhibits deep comprehension of physical principles, provides clear physical interpretations of mathematical results, and demonstrates understanding of quantum-classical correspondence
Problem Analysis and Communication (25 points): Presents logical problem-solving approach, clear diagrams and explanations, proper units throughout calculations, and well-organized solutions
instructions: This comprehensive examination consists of four major problems covering quantum mechanics and electromagnetic theory. You have 4 hours to complete all sections. Show all work clearly, including setup equations, substitutions, and final numerical answers with proper units. Partial credit will be awarded for correct methodology even if final answers contain minor errors. Use the provided formula sheet and physical constants page. Problem 1 involves solving the time-independent Schrödinger equation for a particle in a finite potential well, requiring calculation of energy eigenvalues and normalization of wave functions. Problem 2 requires analysis of electromagnetic fields around a charged cylindrical conductor using Gauss's law and calculation of surface charge density. Problem 3 focuses on quantum tunneling through a rectangular barrier, demanding calculation of transmission and reflection coefficients. Problem 4 involves electromagnetic wave propagation in dispersive media, requiring determination of phase velocity and group velocity. Calculators are permitted, but all symbolic work must be shown before numerical substitution. Draw clear diagrams where appropriate, especially for potential energy plots and field configurations. Write legibly and box final answers. Begin each problem on a new page and clearly label all variables and assumptions.
grading_notes: Grade holistically within each criterion, awarding full points for excellent work, 80% for good work with minor errors, 60% for adequate work with significant gaps, and proportionally less for incomplete understanding. Common issues include: failure to properly normalize wave functions, incorrect application of boundary conditions, sign errors in electromagnetic field calculations, and dimensional analysis mistakes. Expect 15-20% of students to score 90+, 40-50% to score 70-89, and remaining students to score below 70. Award partial credit generously for correct physical reasoning even with computational errors. Look for proper use of limiting cases as reality checks. Deduct points for missing units or unrealistic final answers that aren't questioned by students.

title: Software Development Lifecycle Discussion: Planning Your First Web Application
description: Students will participate in a structured discussion analyzing the software development lifecycle by proposing and discussing a simple web application project. They will demonstrate understanding of development phases, planning considerations, and collaborative problem-solving in software projects.
estimated_time: 2 hours (including research, initial post, and peer responses)
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify and explain the phases of the software development lifecycle (SDLC)
Apply basic project planning concepts to a software development scenario
Demonstrate understanding of requirements gathering and analysis
Communicate technical concepts clearly to peers
rubric_criteria: Initial Project Proposal (30 points): Clearly describes a simple web application idea, identifies target users, lists 3-5 core features, and explains the purpose/problem it solves. Shows creativity and feasibility for a beginner project.

SDLC Phase Analysis (30 points): Accurately identifies and explains how planning, analysis, design, implementation, and testing phases would apply to their proposed project. Demonstrates understanding of each phase's purpose and activities.

Technical Considerations (20 points): Discusses at least 3 technical decisions (programming language, database needs, user interface approach, hosting, etc.) with basic reasoning. Shows awareness of technology choices in web development.

Peer Engagement (20 points): Provides thoughtful responses to 2 classmates' proposals, asks relevant questions, offers constructive suggestions, or shares similar experiences. Demonstrates active participation and professional communication.
instructions: You will propose a simple web application project and analyze how you would approach its development using the software development lifecycle. Post your initial response (300-400 words) addressing: 1) Your web application idea - describe what it does, who would use it, and what problem it solves. Keep it simple (think: personal task tracker, recipe organizer, book wishlist, etc.). 2) SDLC phases - explain how you would approach each phase: Planning (timeline, resources), Analysis (gathering requirements), Design (user interface, data structure), Implementation (coding approach), and Testing (how you'd verify it works). 3) Technical decisions - discuss your choices for programming language, database (if needed), styling approach, and where you might host it. Explain your reasoning. After posting, respond meaningfully to two classmates' proposals. Ask questions about their technical choices, suggest features, or share how you might solve similar challenges. Responses should be 75-100 words each. Submit your initial post by Wednesday 11:59 PM, and peer responses by Friday 11:59 PM. Use proper grammar and professional tone. Include specific technical terms learned in class.
grading_notes: Look for practical, achievable project ideas rather than overly complex applications. Students should demonstrate basic SDLC understanding without requiring advanced technical knowledge. Accept reasonable technology choices even if not optimal - focus on their reasoning process. Common issues: overly ambitious project scope, skipping SDLC phases, vague technical explanations, superficial peer responses. Grade distribution expectation: 70% of students should score 80+ points with adequate preparation. Deduct 5 points per day for late submissions. Encourage creativity while maintaining realism for beginner skill level.

title: Customer Behavior Analytics: Insights & Recommendations Presentation
description: Students will analyze a provided e-commerce customer dataset using statistical methods and visualization techniques, then present their findings, insights, and business recommendations in a 15-minute presentation to simulate a real-world business analytics scenario.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply descriptive and inferential statistical methods to analyze customer behavior patterns
Create effective data visualizations that clearly communicate analytical findings
Interpret analytical results to generate actionable business insights and recommendations
Present complex data analysis findings to non-technical stakeholders using clear, professional communication
rubric_criteria: Data Analysis Methodology (25 points): Appropriate use of statistical techniques, correct data cleaning procedures, valid analytical approaches, and proper handling of missing data or outliers

Visualization Quality (25 points): Clear, well-designed charts and graphs with proper labeling, appropriate chart types for data, effective use of color and formatting, and visualizations that support the narrative

Business Insights & Recommendations (25 points): Demonstrates clear understanding of business context, provides specific actionable recommendations based on data findings, addresses potential limitations, and shows critical thinking about implications

Presentation Delivery (25 points): Professional presentation style, clear verbal communication, stays within time limits, effectively uses visual aids, engages audience, and demonstrates mastery of content through Q&A responses
instructions: You will receive a dataset containing 12 months of customer transaction data from an online retailer, including customer demographics, purchase history, and website behavior metrics. Your task is to conduct a comprehensive analysis and present your findings in a 15-minute presentation followed by 5 minutes of Q&A. Your analysis must include: (1) Exploratory data analysis with at least 5 meaningful visualizations, (2) Customer segmentation analysis using appropriate clustering or statistical methods, (3) Identification of key trends and patterns in customer behavior, (4) At least three specific business recommendations with supporting evidence. Create a presentation deck (10-12 slides maximum) that tells a coherent story from data exploration to business recommendations. Include one slide with technical methodology details and another with limitations and assumptions. Submit your presentation slides (PDF format) and a supplementary technical appendix (2-3 pages) containing detailed statistical outputs, code snippets, and additional charts not included in the main presentation. All data sources and analytical methods must be properly cited. Presentations will be delivered in class during weeks 3-4 of the module, with specific time slots assigned randomly. Practice your timing carefully as presentations exceeding 15 minutes will be stopped.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical rigor without expecting advanced statistical methods - focus on appropriate application of intermediate techniques like correlation analysis, basic regression, or k-means clustering. Look for evidence of proper data exploration (checking distributions, identifying outliers, handling missing values). Common issues include: overly complex visualizations that don't communicate clearly, recommendations that don't logically follow from the analysis, and poor time management during presentation. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-range (90-100), 60% B-range (80-89), 20% C-range (70-79), 5% below 70. Deduct points for late submission (5 points per day) and failing to stay within time limits (5 points for every minute over). During Q&A, assess depth of understanding - students should be able to explain their methodology choices and acknowledge limitations of their analysis.

title: Comprehensive Project Management Portfolio: End-to-End Project Lifecycle Implementation
description: Students will create a comprehensive project management portfolio demonstrating mastery of project lifecycle management through the development and documentation of a realistic organizational project. The portfolio must include initiation documentation, detailed project plans, risk management strategies, stakeholder communication plans, and post-project evaluation with lessons learned.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply project management methodologies (traditional and agile) to complex organizational scenarios
Develop comprehensive project plans including scope, time, cost, and resource management
Create and implement risk management and stakeholder communication strategies
Demonstrate proficiency in project management tools and techniques for monitoring and control
Evaluate project outcomes and synthesize lessons learned for continuous improvement
rubric_criteria: Project Initiation & Planning (25 points): Project charter with clear scope, objectives, and constraints; detailed WBS; realistic timeline with critical path analysis; comprehensive resource allocation and budget; stakeholder analysis and communication plan

Risk Management & Quality Assurance (25 points): Thorough risk register with probability/impact analysis; mitigation and contingency strategies; quality management plan with measurable standards; change management procedures

Implementation Documentation & Monitoring (25 points): Detailed execution plan with milestones; progress tracking tools and dashboards; status reports demonstrating monitoring and control techniques; evidence of adaptive management and problem-solving

Project Closure & Reflection (25 points): Comprehensive project evaluation against original objectives; stakeholder feedback analysis; lessons learned documentation; recommendations for future projects; professional presentation of portfolio
instructions: Select a realistic organizational project (e.g., system implementation, facility renovation, product launch, process improvement) worth $50K-$500K with 6-12 month timeline. Your portfolio must include: 1) Project Charter (2-3 pages) defining scope, objectives, success criteria, and key stakeholders; 2) Detailed Project Plan including Gantt chart, WBS, resource allocation, and budget breakdown; 3) Risk Management Plan with risk register, analysis matrix, and response strategies; 4) Communication Plan with stakeholder matrix and reporting schedule; 5) Quality Management Plan with standards and control measures; 6) Three monthly status reports showing progress tracking and issue resolution; 7) Project Closure Report with performance evaluation, stakeholder feedback, and lessons learned. Use professional project management software (MS Project, Smartsheet, or equivalent) for scheduling and tracking. Include actual screenshots and exported reports. Portfolio should be professionally formatted, 25-30 pages total, with executive summary and appendices. Submit as PDF with separate Excel files for templates and tools created.
grading_notes: Evaluate realism and feasibility of chosen project - unrealistic scope or timeline should be penalized. Look for evidence of actual PM tool usage rather than generic templates. Strong portfolios will show integration between components (e.g., risks connected to specific WBS elements, communication plan aligned with stakeholder analysis). Deduct points for generic or template-based content without customization. Expect 15-20% A grades for truly comprehensive, professional-quality work; 60-70% B grades for solid, complete portfolios with minor gaps; C grades for portfolios missing key components or showing superficial analysis. Common issues: unrealistic budgets/timelines, inadequate stakeholder analysis, generic risk identification, poor integration between portfolio components.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Management Laboratory Analysis
description: Students will conduct an in-depth analysis of a real-world organizational crisis, evaluate the leadership response, and develop comprehensive improvement strategies using advanced leadership frameworks. This assessment requires critical evaluation of leadership decisions, stakeholder management, and strategic communication during high-stakes situations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Analyze complex leadership decisions using multiple theoretical frameworks and evaluate their effectiveness in crisis situations
Synthesize advanced leadership theories to develop innovative solutions for organizational challenges and stakeholder conflicts
Demonstrate mastery of strategic thinking, ethical decision-making, and transformational leadership principles in high-pressure environments
rubric_criteria: Crisis Analysis & Leadership Evaluation (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of the crisis context, accurately identifies key leadership challenges, and provides sophisticated analysis of actual leadership responses using at least three advanced leadership theories (transformational, authentic, adaptive leadership frameworks)

Strategic Recommendations & Innovation (25 points): Develops creative, evidence-based improvement strategies that address root causes, demonstrates systems thinking, and provides specific, actionable recommendations with clear implementation timelines and resource requirements

Stakeholder Impact Assessment (25 points): Conducts thorough stakeholder analysis identifying primary and secondary affected parties, evaluates communication effectiveness across different stakeholder groups, and demonstrates understanding of ethical leadership obligations and reputational management

Professional Presentation & Evidence Integration (25 points): Presents findings in executive-level format with clear executive summary, integrates minimum 12 credible sources including peer-reviewed research, demonstrates sophisticated writing and analytical skills appropriate for senior leadership audience
instructions: Select a significant organizational crisis from the past 5 years (e.g., corporate scandals, natural disasters, cybersecurity breaches, pandemic responses) involving a major corporation or public institution. Your analysis must include: (1) Executive Summary (1 page) outlining key findings and recommendations; (2) Crisis Context Analysis (2-3 pages) describing the situation, timeline, and stakeholder landscape; (3) Leadership Response Evaluation (3-4 pages) analyzing actual leadership decisions using transformational, authentic, and adaptive leadership frameworks, identifying strengths and failures; (4) Strategic Improvement Plan (2-3 pages) providing specific recommendations for prevention and response improvement, including implementation steps and success metrics; (5) Stakeholder Communication Strategy (1-2 pages) addressing how different groups should be engaged during similar future crises. Format: Professional report, 12-point Times New Roman, double-spaced, APA citations. Include appendices with stakeholder mapping, timeline visualization, and theoretical framework comparison chart. Submit via learning management system as single PDF by 11:59 PM on due date. Minimum 12 scholarly sources required, with preference for recent peer-reviewed articles on crisis leadership and organizational behavior.
grading_notes: This expert-level assessment evaluates students' ability to apply advanced leadership theory to real-world situations. Look for evidence of critical thinking beyond basic application - students should demonstrate synthesis across multiple frameworks and innovative solution development. Grade distribution expectation: 15% A grades (90-100), 35% B grades (80-89), 35% C grades (70-79), 15% below C. Common issues include: superficial crisis analysis without considering organizational culture and industry context; recommendations that lack specificity or feasibility; failure to distinguish between different stakeholder needs; inadequate integration of leadership theory with practical application. Strong submissions will show evidence of executive-level thinking, demonstrate understanding of complex organizational dynamics, and provide actionable insights. Deduct points for late submissions (10% per day), inadequate source quality, or failure to meet minimum page requirements. Consider offering revision opportunities for borderline cases to encourage deeper learning.

title: Google Analytics 4 Advanced Implementation and Strategic Analysis Exam
description: Students will demonstrate mastery of Google Analytics 4 by implementing advanced tracking configurations, analyzing complex customer journey data, creating custom reporting solutions, and developing data-driven strategic recommendations for business optimization.
learning_objectives_assessed: Configure advanced GA4 tracking including custom events, enhanced ecommerce, and cross-domain implementation
Analyze multi-channel attribution and customer lifetime value using GA4's advanced reporting features
Create custom dimensions, metrics, and audiences for sophisticated business intelligence
Develop strategic recommendations based on advanced GA4 data analysis and interpretation
Implement GA4 data integration with Google Ads, Google Tag Manager, and third-party platforms
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation (25 points): Accurate configuration of GA4 property with custom events, enhanced ecommerce tracking, cross-domain setup, and proper GTM integration. Code must be syntactically correct and follow best practices.

Data Analysis and Interpretation (25 points): Comprehensive analysis of provided dataset including funnel analysis, cohort analysis, attribution modeling, and customer segmentation. Conclusions must be supported by specific metrics and statistical significance.

Custom Reporting and Visualization (25 points): Creation of advanced custom reports, calculated metrics, and audiences that address specific business questions. Reports must demonstrate understanding of GA4's exploration tools and API capabilities.

Strategic Recommendations (25 points): Development of actionable business recommendations based on data insights, including ROI calculations, optimization strategies, and measurable KPIs. Recommendations must be realistic and tied to specific GA4 metrics.
instructions: This comprehensive exam consists of four sections that must be completed sequentially. You will receive access to a demo GA4 property and sample dataset. Section 1: Configure a GA4 property for a multi-domain ecommerce site including custom events for video engagement, file downloads, and scroll tracking. Implement enhanced ecommerce tracking and set up cross-domain measurement. Provide screenshots of your configuration and export the GTM container. Section 2: Using the provided 6-month dataset, perform funnel analysis identifying drop-off points, conduct cohort analysis for user retention, analyze attribution models comparing first-click vs. data-driven attribution, and create user segments based on behavior patterns. Document your methodology and statistical approaches. Section 3: Build three custom exploration reports addressing: customer lifetime value by acquisition channel, product performance analysis with custom calculated metrics, and audience overlap analysis. Create two custom audiences for remarketing and export configurations. Section 4: Develop a strategic presentation with five data-driven recommendations for improving conversion rates, reducing customer acquisition costs, and increasing user engagement. Include specific metrics, expected outcomes, and implementation timelines. Submit all work as a single PDF with clearly labeled sections, include all screenshots, code snippets, and data exports. Ensure all analysis includes confidence intervals and sample sizes where applicable.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy first - incorrect GA4 configurations should receive partial credit only if methodology is sound. For data analysis, look for proper statistical interpretation and avoid giving full credit for conclusions not supported by data. Custom reporting should demonstrate advanced GA4 features beyond basic reports - basic funnel reports don't meet advanced criteria. Strategic recommendations must be specific and measurable - avoid vague suggestions like 'improve user experience.' Common issues include: incorrect event parameter naming, misunderstanding GA4 vs. Universal Analytics metrics, inadequate sample sizes for statistical significance, and unrealistic ROI projections. Grade distribution should follow: 90-100 (comprehensive mastery), 80-89 (strong understanding with minor gaps), 70-79 (adequate knowledge with significant weaknesses), below 70 (insufficient understanding). Partial credit available for each criterion, but technical implementation errors should impact subsequent analysis sections.

title: Enterprise Network Design Architecture Discussion: Multi-Site MPLS VPN Implementation
description: Students will engage in a comprehensive discussion analyzing the design, implementation, and optimization of a complex enterprise multi-site MPLS VPN network infrastructure, demonstrating expert-level understanding of Cisco networking technologies, protocols, and best practices.
learning_objectives_assessed: Evaluate and design complex MPLS VPN architectures using BGP, OSPF, and LDP protocols
Analyze QoS implementation strategies for voice, video, and data traffic across WAN connections
Assess network security frameworks including IPSec, DMVPN, and access control implementations
Synthesize troubleshooting methodologies for complex enterprise network issues
rubric_criteria: Technical Accuracy and Depth (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of MPLS VPN concepts, routing protocols (BGP, OSPF, LDP), and Cisco IOS configurations. Uses correct terminology and exhibits expert-level technical knowledge.

Critical Analysis and Problem-Solving (25 points): Provides detailed analysis of network design challenges, identifies potential failure points, and proposes viable solutions with justification. Demonstrates ability to troubleshoot complex scenarios.

Professional Communication and Peer Engagement (25 points): Communicates technical concepts clearly and professionally, actively engages with peer responses through meaningful questions and constructive feedback, and maintains discussion thread continuity.

Implementation Feasibility and Best Practices (25 points): Recommendations align with Cisco best practices and industry standards, considers scalability, redundancy, and cost factors. Addresses real-world implementation challenges and constraints.
instructions:
You are the Senior Network Architect for a Fortune 500 company implementing a new MPLS VPN infrastructure connecting 15 sites across North America. The network must support 5,000+ users with mixed traffic including VoIP, video conferencing, and mission-critical applications requiring 99.9% uptime.

Initial Post (Due Day 3): Create a comprehensive network design discussion (800-1000 words) addressing: 1) MPLS VPN topology recommendations with PE/CE router placement and BGP/OSPF design considerations, 2) QoS implementation strategy including traffic classification, marking, and queuing mechanisms, 3) Redundancy and failover mechanisms including backup circuits and route optimization, 4) Security framework incorporating IPSec encryption and access controls.

Peer Responses (Due Day 5): Respond substantively to at least three classmates (300+ words each). Challenge assumptions, ask probing technical questions, or suggest alternative approaches. Include specific Cisco IOS commands or configuration examples where relevant.

Final Analysis (Due Day 7): Post a 400-word reflection incorporating insights from peer discussions, addressing how feedback influenced your original design, and identifying three critical implementation challenges with proposed solutions.

Submission Requirements: Use discussion forum with clear headings, include network diagrams (hand-drawn acceptable), reference Cisco documentation, and maintain professional tone throughout all posts.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy by checking protocol understanding, configuration syntax, and alignment with Cisco best practices. Look for evidence of practical experience through specific examples and realistic constraint considerations. Award full points for peer engagement only when responses demonstrate genuine technical discourse beyond simple agreement. Common issues include oversimplified QoS strategies, inadequate redundancy planning, and unrealistic bandwidth assumptions. Expect grade distribution: 15% A+ (exceptional depth), 35% A (solid technical competency), 40% B+ (good understanding with minor gaps), 10% B or below (significant technical deficiencies). Deduct points for late submissions: 5% per day for initial post, 3% per day for responses.

title: End-to-End Data Science Project Portfolio: Customer Churn Prediction
description: Students will complete a comprehensive data science project demonstrating the full pipeline from data exploration to model deployment.
