Using a customer churn dataset, students will perform EDA, feature engineering, model building, evaluation, and create a presentation of their findings and business recommendations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply data preprocessing and feature engineering techniques to prepare real-world datasets
Implement and compare multiple machine learning algorithms for classification problems
Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics and validation techniques
Communicate data science findings effectively to technical and non-technical audiences
Demonstrate understanding of the complete data science workflow from problem formulation to deployment
rubric_criteria: Data Exploration & Preprocessing (25 points): Thorough EDA with meaningful visualizations, proper handling of missing values and outliers, appropriate data transformations, and clear documentation of data quality issues and solutions

Feature Engineering & Model Development (25 points): Creative and justified feature creation, implementation of at least 3 different algorithms (e.g., logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost), proper cross-validation techniques, and hyperparameter tuning

Model Evaluation & Analysis (25 points): Use of appropriate metrics (precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC), confusion matrix analysis, feature importance interpretation, comparison of models with statistical significance testing, and discussion of business impact

Code Quality & Communication (25 points): Well-structured, documented code in Jupyter notebook, clear markdown explanations, professional presentation slides, actionable business recommendations, and reproducible results with requirements.txt file
instructions: Select a customer churn dataset (suggestions: Telco, Banking, or E-commerce) with at least 5,000 records and 10+ features. Your portfolio must include: 1) A Jupyter notebook containing your complete analysis with sections for data loading, EDA (minimum 5 visualizations), preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, and evaluation. 2) A 10-minute presentation (slides + brief video) explaining your methodology, key insights, and business recommendations. 3) A deployment-ready Python script that can make predictions on new data. Submit all files in a GitHub repository with a comprehensive README. Your notebook should tell a story - explain your decisions, interpret results, and discuss limitations. Include at least one advanced technique (e.g., SHAP values, ensemble methods, or automated feature selection). Address class imbalance if present and justify your choice of evaluation metrics. Provide specific, actionable recommendations for reducing customer churn based on your model insights. Code must be PEP-8 compliant and include appropriate error handling.
grading_notes: Look for depth of analysis rather than just completion of steps. Award full points for data exploration only if students go beyond basic statistics to uncover meaningful patterns. In model development, credit creative feature engineering and proper justification of algorithm choices. Common issues: inadequate cross-validation, ignoring class imbalance, poor visualization choices, and generic business recommendations. Excellent work (90-100) shows advanced techniques, statistical rigor, and clear business value. Good work (80-89) meets all requirements with solid execution. Satisfactory (70-79) covers basics but lacks depth or has minor technical errors. Expect 15% A's, 35% B's, 35% C's, 15% below C based on typical intermediate-level performance.

title: Mathematical Modeling Lab Report: Optimization of a Solar Panel Array System
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive mathematical analysis to determine the optimal configuration, placement, and efficiency of a solar panel array system. This lab report requires applying calculus optimization techniques, statistical analysis of energy output data, and linear programming to solve real-world constraints while demonstrating rigorous mathematical reasoning and clear technical communication.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply multivariable calculus and optimization techniques to solve complex real-world problems
Utilize statistical methods to analyze data sets and draw meaningful conclusions
Implement linear programming methods to handle constraint optimization problems
Communicate mathematical findings through professional technical writing with proper notation and visualization
Synthesize multiple mathematical domains to create comprehensive solutions to engineering problems
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Analysis and Methods (25 points): Correct application of calculus optimization, statistical analysis, and linear programming techniques with proper mathematical notation, clear variable definitions, and accurate calculations throughout all problem components

Problem-Solving and Reasoning (25 points): Demonstrates logical mathematical reasoning, appropriate model selection and justification, identification of constraints and assumptions, and comprehensive consideration of multiple solution approaches with validation of results

Data Analysis and Interpretation (25 points): Accurate statistical analysis of provided energy output datasets, appropriate use of regression analysis, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, and meaningful interpretation of statistical results in context of the optimization problem

Technical Communication and Presentation (25 points): Professional lab report format with clear executive summary, well-organized sections, proper mathematical notation, effective graphs and visualizations, appropriate citations, and conclusions that directly address the optimization objectives
instructions: Your task is to develop an optimal solar panel array configuration for a 10-acre industrial site. You will receive historical weather data, energy consumption patterns, and cost constraints. Your lab report must include: (1) Executive Summary (1 page) presenting your optimal solution and key findings; (2) Mathematical Model Development section deriving objective functions for energy output maximization and cost minimization using multivariable calculus, including partial derivatives and critical point analysis; (3) Statistical Analysis section analyzing 2 years of provided weather and energy data using regression analysis, hypothesis testing, and confidence interval construction to predict future performance; (4) Constraint Optimization section implementing linear programming to handle budget constraints, zoning restrictions, and maintenance requirements; (5) Results and Validation section presenting your optimal configuration with mathematical justification, sensitivity analysis, and error assessment; (6) Conclusion section discussing practical implications and model limitations. Submit as PDF with all calculations shown, including Mathematica/MATLAB code appendix. Minimum 15 pages, maximum 20 pages excluding appendices. Due date allows for one draft review session with instructor during week 3.
grading_notes: Focus evaluation on mathematical rigor rather than engineering practicality. Expect 15% of students to struggle with multivariable optimization - provide partial credit for correct setup even with calculation errors. Statistical analysis section often shows weakness in interpretation rather than computation - deduct points for correct calculations without contextual meaning. Look for common errors: incorrect constraint formulation in linear programming, confusion between correlation and causation in data analysis, and inadequate validation of optimization results. Grade distribution should target: 20% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 35% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. Provide detailed feedback on mathematical notation consistency and require resubmission if technical communication standards are not met. Allow partial credit for alternative valid approaches to optimization problems.

title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics and Electromagnetic Theory Comprehensive Quiz
description: Expert-level assessment covering quantum mechanical systems, electromagnetic field theory, and their mathematical foundations. Students will solve complex problems involving wave functions, field equations, and relativistic quantum mechanics, demonstrating mastery of advanced physics concepts and mathematical techniques.
learning_objectives_assessed: Solve the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for complex quantum systems using advanced mathematical methods
Apply Maxwell's equations to analyze electromagnetic wave propagation in various media and boundary conditions
Demonstrate understanding of relativistic quantum mechanics and Klein-Gordon/Dirac equations
Integrate quantum field theory concepts with classical electromagnetic theory
Utilize advanced mathematical techniques including Green's functions, Fourier transforms, and tensor calculus in physics problem-solving
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Rigor and Technique (25 points): Correct application of advanced mathematical methods, proper use of boundary conditions, accurate manipulation of differential equations, and appropriate choice of coordinate systems

Physical Reasoning and Conceptual Understanding (25 points): Clear demonstration of underlying physics principles, proper interpretation of quantum mechanical observables, understanding of field-particle duality, and logical problem-solving approach

Problem-Solving Strategy and Methodology (25 points): Systematic approach to multi-step problems, appropriate approximations and limiting cases, dimensional analysis verification, and integration of multiple physics concepts

Precision and Communication (25 points): Clear mathematical notation, proper units and significant figures, logical presentation of solutions, and accurate final answers with appropriate physical interpretation
instructions: This comprehensive quiz consists of 8 problems covering quantum mechanics, electromagnetic theory, and mathematical physics. You have 180 minutes to complete all problems. Show all work clearly and systematically. Each problem requires multiple steps and integration of advanced concepts. For quantum mechanics problems, explicitly state your assumptions about normalization, boundary conditions, and measurement interpretations. For electromagnetic problems, specify coordinate systems and justify field configurations. Use appropriate mathematical notation throughout, including proper vector/tensor notation where applicable. Partial credit will be awarded based on methodology and intermediate steps, even if final answers are incorrect. You may use standard physics reference sheets and mathematical tables, but no electronic devices or textbooks. Begin each problem on a new page and number all equations. For problems involving approximations, clearly state your assumptions and their validity ranges. Submit your complete solution set with your name and student ID on each page. Late submissions will incur a 10% penalty per 15-minute interval. If you encounter ambiguous problem statements, state your interpretation clearly and proceed with your solution. Focus on demonstrating your understanding of fundamental principles rather than memorized formulas.
grading_notes: Evaluate solutions holistically, giving significant weight to methodology over final numerical answers. Look for proper application of boundary conditions in differential equation solutions, appropriate use of symmetry arguments, and correct limiting behavior analysis. Common issues include: incorrect normalization of wave functions, sign errors in Maxwell equation applications, improper treatment of relativistic effects, and dimensional inconsistencies. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90-100), 25% B-level (80-89), 35% C-level (70-79), 20% D-level (60-69), 5% below 60. Award partial credit generously for correct setup and methodology. Deduct points for mathematical errors that propagate through solutions. Exceptional insight or elegant alternative solution methods should receive bonus consideration.

title: Critical Analysis of Complex Project Recovery: A Strategic Discussion Forum
description: Students will analyze a multi-phase project failure scenario, develop comprehensive recovery strategies, and engage in peer critique through structured online discussions. Assessment focuses on strategic thinking, risk assessment, stakeholder management, and evidence-based decision making in crisis project management situations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Analyze complex project failures and identify root causes using systematic methodologies
Develop comprehensive project recovery strategies incorporating risk management, resource reallocation, and stakeholder communication
Evaluate alternative project management approaches and justify strategic decisions with evidence-based reasoning
Demonstrate advanced understanding of project governance, change management, and crisis leadership principles
rubric_criteria: Initial Analysis Post (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of project failure causes, uses appropriate PM frameworks (e.g., fishbone analysis, 5-whys), identifies systemic issues beyond surface problems, references relevant PM theories and best practices

Recovery Strategy Development (25 points): Proposes comprehensive, realistic recovery plan with specific timelines, resource requirements, risk mitigation strategies, stakeholder communication plan, and success metrics aligned with organizational objectives

Peer Engagement Quality (25 points): Provides substantive, constructive feedback on 3+ peer posts, challenges assumptions professionally, offers alternative perspectives, asks probing questions, demonstrates active listening and builds upon others' ideas

Evidence-Based Reasoning (25 points): Integrates course concepts with external research, cites relevant case studies or industry examples, supports recommendations with data/metrics, acknowledges limitations and assumptions in proposed solutions
instructions: You will participate in a structured discussion analyzing the 'Phoenix Systems ERP Implementation Crisis' case study (provided in course materials). INITIAL POST (due Week 1, Thursday): Write a 500-700 word analysis addressing: (1) Root cause analysis of the project failure using at least two PM diagnostic tools, (2) Comprehensive recovery strategy including timeline, budget adjustments, team restructuring, and stakeholder communication plan, (3) Risk assessment of your proposed solution with contingency planning. PEER RESPONSES (due Week 2, Tuesday): Respond substantively to at least three classmates' posts (200-300 words each). Challenge assumptions, propose alternatives, ask clarifying questions, and build upon their ideas. Focus on constructive critique rather than simple agreement. FINAL REFLECTION (due Week 2, Sunday): Post a 300-word reflection on insights gained from peer discussions and how they influenced your thinking. All posts must be professional, cite relevant sources (minimum 3 academic/industry sources), and demonstrate graduate-level critical thinking. Use APA format for citations. Late submissions lose 10% per day.
grading_notes: Look for depth over breadth - students should demonstrate mastery of PM concepts rather than surface-level understanding. Strong responses will connect theory to practice and show awareness of organizational context. Watch for evidence of original thinking vs. regurgitation of course materials. Peer responses should show genuine engagement, not perfunctory comments. Grade distribution expectation: 15% A+, 35% A/A-, 35% B+/B, 15% B-/C+. Common issues: oversimplified solutions ignoring stakeholder complexity, failure to consider budget/resource constraints, weak peer engagement that doesn't advance discussion. Exceptional work will demonstrate innovation, consider ethical implications, and show understanding of long-term organizational impact.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Management: Organizational Transformation Presentation
description: Students will present a comprehensive analysis of a real organizational crisis, demonstrating advanced leadership principles through strategic decision-making frameworks, stakeholder management, and organizational change implementation. This expert-level assessment evaluates the ability to synthesize complex leadership theories with practical crisis resolution strategies.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate mastery of strategic leadership decision-making frameworks in high-stakes, ambiguous situations
Analyze and synthesize multiple stakeholder perspectives while maintaining ethical leadership principles
Design and articulate comprehensive organizational transformation strategies using evidence-based leadership approaches
Evaluate leadership communication effectiveness across diverse audiences during crisis situations
rubric_criteria: Strategic Analysis & Decision Framework (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of crisis assessment, applies multiple leadership theories appropriately, presents clear decision-making framework with risk analysis, shows evidence of systems thinking

Stakeholder Management & Ethical Leadership (25 points): Identifies all key stakeholders with nuanced understanding of interests/power dynamics, addresses ethical dilemmas with principled reasoning, demonstrates cultural sensitivity and inclusive leadership approaches

Transformation Strategy & Implementation (25 points): Presents comprehensive change management plan with clear milestones, addresses resistance and organizational dynamics, incorporates innovation and adaptive leadership concepts, shows measurable outcomes

Executive Presence & Communication Mastery (25 points): Delivers with confidence and authenticity, adapts communication style for executive audience, handles challenging questions strategically, uses compelling data visualization and storytelling
instructions: Select a major organizational crisis from the past 5 years involving a Fortune 500 company or equivalent. Your 20-minute presentation must address: (1) Crisis context and leadership challenges faced, (2) Critical analysis of actual leadership responses using minimum 3 advanced leadership frameworks, (3) Your alternative strategic approach with detailed implementation roadmap, (4) Stakeholder communication strategy and ethical considerations, (5) Long-term organizational transformation plan. Required materials: Professional slide deck (15-20 slides), executive summary handout (2 pages), and 3 peer-reviewed leadership research sources. Presentation format should mirror C-suite boardroom style. Submit materials 24 hours prior to presentation date. Be prepared for challenging questions from instructor and peers acting as board members. Focus on demonstrating executive-level strategic thinking rather than basic crisis response. Your analysis should reveal deep understanding of leadership complexity, ambiguity tolerance, and systems-level impact of leadership decisions.
grading_notes: Look for evidence of graduate-level synthesis rather than mere description of events. Strong presentations will demonstrate original thinking and creative problem-solving while grounding recommendations in solid theoretical frameworks. Common weaknesses include superficial stakeholder analysis, lack of implementation specifics, and inability to handle probing questions about assumptions. Expect grade distribution: 15% A+ (exceptional strategic insights), 25% A (strong mastery), 40% A-/B+ (competent with minor gaps), 20% B/B- (meets basic requirements but limited depth). Deduct points for presentation time violations, unprofessional delivery, or failure to address ethical dimensions. Bonus consideration for innovative solutions that demonstrate thought leadership potential.

title: Project Risk Management Analysis and Response Planning Lab Report
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive risk analysis on a provided project scenario, identify potential risks using multiple techniques, perform qualitative and quantitative risk analysis, and develop detailed risk response strategies with monitoring plans.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply risk identification techniques including brainstorming, SWOT analysis, and expert judgment to systematically identify project risks
Perform qualitative risk analysis using probability and impact matrices to prioritize identified risks
Develop appropriate risk response strategies (avoid, transfer, mitigate, accept) with detailed implementation plans
Create risk monitoring and control procedures with key risk indicators and response triggers
rubric_criteria: Risk Identification and Documentation (25 points): Identifies minimum 15 realistic risks across multiple categories (technical, organizational, external, project management) using at least 3 different identification techniques. Risks are clearly documented with comprehensive descriptions and potential causes.

Qualitative Risk Analysis (25 points): Correctly applies probability and impact assessment using a 5x5 matrix, provides justified ratings for each risk based on sound reasoning, and accurately prioritizes risks. Includes risk categorization and updated risk register with rankings.

Risk Response Planning (25 points): Develops specific, actionable response strategies appropriate to each high and medium priority risk. Assigns clear ownership, realistic timelines, and resource requirements. Demonstrates understanding of risk response strategy selection (avoid, transfer, mitigate, accept).

Risk Monitoring and Control Plan (25 points): Creates detailed monitoring procedures with specific key risk indicators (KRIs), establishes clear trigger conditions for response activation, defines reporting frequency and formats, and includes contingency plan activation criteria.
instructions: Using the provided construction project scenario (Downtown Office Complex - 18-month, $12M project), complete a comprehensive risk management analysis following PMI standards. Your lab report must include: (1) Executive Summary (1 page) highlighting key findings and recommendations; (2) Risk Identification section using brainstorming, SWOT analysis, and checklist review techniques - document minimum 15 risks with detailed descriptions; (3) Risk Analysis section featuring a completed 5x5 probability/impact matrix with justified ratings and risk prioritization; (4) Risk Response Planning section with detailed strategies for all high/medium risks including ownership assignments, timelines, and resource needs; (5) Risk Monitoring Plan specifying KRIs, trigger points, and reporting procedures. Format requirements: 8-12 pages, professional business format, include all risk register templates and matrices as appendices. Submit as single PDF file with clear section headers and page numbers. Use PMI terminology throughout and reference PMBOK Guide standards. Include minimum 3 credible external sources supporting your risk assessments and response strategies.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy of risk management processes against PMI standards. Look for realistic, project-appropriate risks rather than generic textbook examples. Assess quality of risk ratings - students should demonstrate understanding that high probability + high impact = high priority. Common issues include: insufficient risk detail, unrealistic response strategies, missing ownership assignments, and inadequate monitoring procedures. Grade distribution expectation: 15% A grades (90-100), 35% B grades (80-89), 40% C grades (70-79), 10% below 70. Deduct points for missing appendices, incorrect matrix calculations, or failure to use PMI terminology consistently.

title: Enterprise Network Infrastructure Design and Implementation Project
description: Students will design, configure, and document a complete enterprise network infrastructure for a multi-site organization, implementing advanced routing protocols, security measures, QoS policies, and network services while demonstrating mastery of Cisco enterprise-level networking concepts.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design and implement complex enterprise network topologies using advanced routing and switching protocols
Configure and troubleshoot OSPF, EIGRP, and BGP routing protocols in multi-area environments
Implement comprehensive network security using ACLs, VPNs, and firewall configurations
Deploy and optimize QoS policies for voice, video, and data traffic prioritization
Configure redundancy and high availability using HSRP, VRRP, and EtherChannel technologies
Implement network services including DHCP, DNS, NAT, and wireless integration
Perform advanced network troubleshooting using systematic methodologies and Cisco diagnostic tools
rubric_criteria: Network Design and Documentation (25 points): Complete network topology design with proper IP addressing scheme, VLAN segmentation, routing protocol selection justification, and comprehensive technical documentation including network diagrams, IP allocation tables, and configuration templates

Protocol Implementation and Configuration (25 points): Accurate configuration of OSPF multi-area design, EIGRP optimization, BGP peering relationships, spanning tree protocol variants, and proper implementation of routing redistribution with appropriate metric manipulation

Security and QoS Implementation (25 points): Comprehensive security policy implementation including extended ACLs, site-to-site VPN configuration, wireless security protocols, and detailed QoS policy deployment with traffic classification, marking, and bandwidth allocation for different service classes

Testing, Troubleshooting, and Optimization (25 points): Systematic network testing procedures, documented troubleshooting methodology, performance optimization evidence, redundancy validation, and detailed analysis of network performance metrics with recommendations for improvements
instructions: Design and implement a complete enterprise network for TechCorp, a growing company with headquarters and three branch offices requiring secure, reliable connectivity. Your project must include: 1) Network topology design supporting 500+ users across four sites with appropriate IP addressing using VLSM and summarization, 2) OSPF implementation with multiple areas, EIGRP for branch connectivity, and BGP for internet connectivity, 3) Comprehensive security implementation including site-to-site VPNs, ACLs restricting inter-VLAN communication, and wireless security, 4) QoS policies prioritizing voice traffic (highest), video conferencing (medium-high), business applications (medium), and general internet (low), 5) Redundancy using HSRP for gateway redundancy and EtherChannel for link aggregation. Deliverables: Complete Packet Tracer file (.pkt) with fully configured network, detailed network documentation (15-20 pages) including topology diagrams, configuration files, IP allocation tables, security policies, and testing procedures. Include a 10-minute video presentation demonstrating key configurations and troubleshooting scenarios. All configurations must use Cisco best practices with proper naming conventions, interface descriptions, and security hardening. Submit via learning management system with all files in a single ZIP archive named 'LastName_FirstName_NetworkProject.zip' by the specified deadline.
grading_notes: Evaluate projects using provided rubric with 25 points per criterion. For Network Design: Look for logical topology, proper IP addressing with no overlaps, justified technology choices, and professional documentation quality. For Protocol Implementation: Verify routing tables, test connectivity between all sites, check convergence times, and validate configuration syntax. For Security/QoS: Test ACL effectiveness, verify VPN tunnel establishment, confirm QoS marking and queuing, and validate traffic prioritization. For Testing/Troubleshooting: Review testing methodology, check for systematic approaches, evaluate optimization suggestions, and assess problem-solving documentation. Common issues include: IP addressing conflicts (deduct 5-10 points), non-functional routing protocols (major deduction), missing security implementations, inadequate documentation, and unrealistic QoS policies. Grade distribution expectation: 15% A grades (90-100), 25% B grades (80-89), 40% C grades (70-79), 15% D grades (60-69), 5% F grades (below 60). Provide detailed written feedback highlighting strengths and specific areas for improvement.

title: Ethics in Machine Learning: Bias Detection and Mitigation Strategies Discussion
description: Students will analyze real-world case studies of algorithmic bias, evaluate existing detection methods, and propose comprehensive mitigation strategies through structured discussion posts and peer responses.
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify and analyze sources of bias in machine learning models and datasets
Evaluate the effectiveness of different bias detection and mitigation techniques
Communicate complex ethical considerations in data science to diverse audiences
Synthesize multiple perspectives on ML ethics to develop comprehensive solutions
rubric_criteria: Case Study Analysis (25 points): Demonstrates thorough understanding of bias sources, impacts on stakeholders, and technical factors contributing to the problem. Uses appropriate terminology and shows deep analytical thinking.

Technical Evaluation (25 points): Accurately assesses bias detection methods and mitigation strategies, discusses trade-offs between fairness metrics, and demonstrates understanding of implementation challenges and limitations.

Solution Development (25 points): Proposes realistic, well-reasoned mitigation strategies that address technical, organizational, and ethical dimensions. Shows creativity and considers multiple stakeholder perspectives.

Discussion Engagement (25 points): Provides substantive responses to at least 3 peers, builds upon others' ideas constructively, asks thoughtful follow-up questions, and contributes meaningfully to collaborative knowledge building.
instructions: This assessment consists of an initial discussion post (due Wednesday) and peer responses (due Sunday). For your initial post (600-800 words), select one case study from the provided list (Amazon hiring algorithm, COMPAS recidivism tool, or facial recognition systems). First, analyze the bias issues: identify specific types of bias present, explain their origins in data collection/model design, and discuss impacts on affected communities. Second, evaluate at least two bias detection methods that could have identified these issues, explaining their strengths and limitations. Third, propose a comprehensive mitigation strategy addressing technical solutions (algorithmic approaches, data modifications), organizational changes (review processes, diverse teams), and ongoing monitoring systems. Support your analysis with at least 3 scholarly sources beyond course materials. For peer responses (200-300 words each), engage with classmates who chose different case studies. Compare their proposed solutions to yours, identify synergies or conflicts between approaches, and suggest additional considerations or alternative strategies. Focus on building collaborative understanding rather than critique. Use proper citation format and maintain professional, respectful tone throughout. Submit initial post as PDF attachment and responses directly in discussion forum.
grading_notes: Look for evidence of critical thinking beyond surface-level analysis. Strong responses will connect technical concepts to real-world implications and demonstrate understanding of fairness-accuracy trade-offs. Watch for oversimplified solutions that ignore implementation complexity or stakeholder concerns. Excellent work (A-level) shows original thinking and synthesis of multiple concepts. Good work (B-level) demonstrates solid understanding with minor gaps in analysis or solutions. Satisfactory work (C-level) covers requirements but lacks depth or contains misconceptions. Grade peer responses based on substantive engagement rather than agreement - students should be building on ideas, not just summarizing. Expect 20% A-level work, 50% B-level, 25% C-level, 5% below expectations. Deduct points for late submissions (5% per day) and failure to meet word count requirements.

title: Advanced Mathematical Modeling: Real-World Optimization Problem Analysis
description: Students will identify, formulate, and solve a complex real-world optimization problem using advanced mathematical techniques, then present their complete analysis including methodology, solutions, and practical implications to demonstrate mastery of mathematical modeling and communication skills.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced calculus and optimization techniques to solve complex real-world problems
Demonstrate proficiency in mathematical modeling and problem formulation
Communicate mathematical concepts and solutions effectively to diverse audiences
Critically analyze and interpret mathematical results in practical contexts
rubric_criteria: Problem Selection and Mathematical Formulation (25 points): Problem demonstrates appropriate complexity, variables are clearly defined, constraints and objective functions are mathematically sound and realistic

Mathematical Analysis and Solution Methods (25 points): Appropriate advanced techniques applied correctly (multivariable calculus, linear programming, differential equations, etc.), calculations are accurate, alternative approaches considered where relevant

Presentation Quality and Mathematical Communication (25 points): Clear logical flow, effective use of visual aids, mathematical notation used correctly, appropriate level for audience, confident delivery within time constraints

Critical Analysis and Real-World Application (25 points): Results interpreted meaningfully, limitations and assumptions acknowledged, practical implications discussed, recommendations are actionable and well-justified
instructions: Select a real-world optimization problem from fields such as economics, engineering, biology, or operations research that requires advanced mathematical techniques for solution. Your presentation must include: (1) Clear problem statement with background context and why optimization is needed, (2) Mathematical model formulation including all variables, constraints, and objective functions with justification for choices, (3) Solution methodology showing step-by-step mathematical analysis using techniques such as Lagrange multipliers, linear programming, calculus of variations, or numerical methods, (4) Complete solution with verification and sensitivity analysis, (5) Interpretation of results with discussion of practical implications and limitations. Prepare a 15-minute presentation using slides, including visual representations of your mathematical work. Submit your slides and a 2-page mathematical appendix showing detailed calculations 24 hours before presentation. Be prepared for 5 minutes of questions from instructor and peers. Examples of appropriate problems: supply chain optimization, resource allocation, portfolio optimization, population dynamics modeling, or engineering design optimization. Avoid basic single-variable problems or purely theoretical exercises.
grading_notes: Expect most students to score 70-85 points with exceptional work earning 90+. Common issues include: oversimplified problems lacking mathematical depth, computational errors in optimization techniques, poor visual presentation of mathematical content, and failure to connect results to real-world context. Award full points for mathematical formulation only when constraints and objectives are both realistic and mathematically sophisticated. Presentation scores should reflect clarity of mathematical explanation to non-expert audience. Deduct points for going significantly over time limits. Strong submissions will demonstrate creativity in problem selection while maintaining mathematical rigor.

title: Advanced Physics Research Portfolio: Investigating Complex Physical Phenomena
description: Students will compile a comprehensive portfolio demonstrating mastery of advanced physics concepts through independent research, mathematical modeling, experimental design, and critical analysis of cutting-edge physics topics. The portfolio includes original research proposals, peer review activities, and synthesis of multiple physics domains.
learning_objectives_assessed: Synthesize knowledge across multiple physics domains (mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics, quantum mechanics, relativity) to analyze complex phenomena
Design and evaluate experimental methodologies for investigating advanced physics problems with appropriate error analysis and uncertainty quantification
Apply advanced mathematical techniques (differential equations, vector calculus, statistical analysis) to model and solve physics problems
Critically analyze current physics research literature and communicate findings to both technical and general audiences
Demonstrate understanding of the historical development and philosophical implications of major physics theories
rubric_criteria: Research Quality and Depth (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of chosen physics topic through comprehensive literature review, integration of primary sources, identification of current research gaps, and original theoretical insights. Includes minimum 15 peer-reviewed sources with critical evaluation of methodologies and findings.

Mathematical Modeling and Analysis (25 points): Develops rigorous mathematical models using appropriate advanced techniques, shows complete derivations with clear assumptions, performs dimensional analysis, conducts uncertainty propagation, and validates results through multiple approaches. All calculations must be clearly documented and reproducible.

Experimental Design and Methodology (25 points): Proposes feasible experimental procedures with detailed protocols, identifies and quantifies sources of systematic and random errors, designs appropriate controls, selects suitable instrumentation, and demonstrates understanding of measurement limitations and statistical significance requirements.

Communication and Professional Presentation (25 points): Produces clear, well-organized written reports following professional physics journal format, creates effective visual representations of data and concepts, demonstrates ability to explain complex topics to different audiences, and provides constructive peer reviews showing deep understanding of physics principles.
instructions: Your portfolio must contain five components submitted progressively throughout the assessment period: (1) Research Proposal (2 pages): Select a cutting-edge physics topic (e.g., quantum computing, dark matter detection, metamaterials, plasma physics applications). Provide background, identify research questions, and outline methodology. (2) Literature Review (4-5 pages): Analyze minimum 15 peer-reviewed articles, synthesize current understanding, identify controversies or gaps, and demonstrate how your topic connects to fundamental physics principles. (3) Mathematical Analysis (3-4 pages): Develop detailed mathematical treatment of key aspects, including derivations from first principles, numerical modeling or simulations, and error analysis. Show all work and clearly state assumptions. (4) Experimental Design Proposal (3 pages): Design realistic experiment to test hypothesis or measure key parameters. Include equipment specifications, procedural steps, data collection methods, expected results with uncertainty estimates, and discussion of limitations. (5) Synthesis Report (2-3 pages): Connect your topic to broader physics themes, discuss implications for technology or society, and reflect on learning process. Additionally, complete peer reviews of two classmates' proposals using provided rubric. Submit all components in professional format with proper citations (AIP style), figures/graphs where appropriate, and appendices for lengthy calculations. Final portfolio due Week 8 with intermediate deadlines for components.
grading_notes: Evaluate portfolios holistically while using rubric for consistency. Expect expert-level work demonstrating graduate-school readiness. Look for evidence of independent thinking beyond textbook applications. Common issues include insufficient mathematical rigor, unrealistic experimental proposals, and superficial literature analysis. Strong portfolios will show creative connections between topics and demonstrate genuine physics intuition. Grade distribution should reflect high standards: A-level work (90-100) shows exceptional insight and could contribute to actual research; B-level work (80-89) demonstrates solid competency with minor gaps; C-level work (70-79) meets basic requirements but lacks depth or contains significant errors. Provide detailed feedback on mathematical derivations and experimental feasibility. Consider organizing peer review sessions to enhance learning and maintain assessment authenticity.

title: Comprehensive Project Recovery and Optimization Plan
description: Students will analyze a failing real-world project scenario, develop a comprehensive recovery strategy, and create an implementation plan that addresses scope, schedule, budget, quality, and stakeholder management challenges while demonstrating advanced project management methodologies.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced project management techniques to diagnose and resolve complex project issues
Integrate risk management, stakeholder engagement, and change management strategies
Demonstrate proficiency in project planning tools and methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, Hybrid)
Evaluate and optimize project performance using quantitative metrics and qualitative analysis
Communicate project strategies effectively to diverse stakeholder audiences
rubric_criteria: Problem Analysis & Diagnosis (25 points): Thorough identification of root causes using appropriate analytical frameworks (fishbone, 5-whys, SWOT), accurate assessment of current project health metrics, clear prioritization of issues based on impact and urgency

Recovery Strategy Development (25 points): Comprehensive action plan addressing scope, schedule, budget, and quality issues; appropriate selection and application of PM methodologies; realistic timeline and resource allocation; integration of risk mitigation strategies

Stakeholder Management & Communication Plan (25 points): Detailed stakeholder analysis with engagement strategies; clear communication protocols and escalation procedures; change management approach; conflict resolution mechanisms; executive presentation quality

Implementation Planning & Controls (25 points): Detailed work breakdown structure; realistic project schedule with critical path analysis; budget revision with cost control measures; quality assurance plan; performance monitoring framework with KPIs and dashboards
instructions: You are the newly appointed project manager for TechFlow Solutions' Digital Transformation Initiative, a $2.3M project that is 8 months into its 12-month timeline. The project is 45% over budget, 3 months behind schedule, and facing significant scope creep. Key stakeholders have lost confidence, the development team is demoralized, and the original project manager has resigned. Your deliverables must include: (1) Executive Summary (2 pages) presenting your diagnosis and high-level recovery strategy, (2) Detailed Recovery Plan (8-10 pages) including revised project charter, scope statement, schedule, budget, and risk register, (3) Stakeholder Communication Strategy (3-4 pages) with engagement matrix and communication protocols, (4) Implementation Roadmap (2-3 pages) with 90-day action plan and success metrics, and (5) Executive Presentation (10-12 slides) suitable for the steering committee. Use real project management tools (MS Project, Jira, or equivalent) for scheduling components. Include at least 5 academic or industry sources. Format: Professional business document with proper citations, charts, and appendices. Submit as PDF with separate presentation file.
grading_notes: Evaluate realism and feasibility of proposed solutions - avoid overly optimistic timelines or unrealistic budget cuts. Look for evidence-based decision making with proper PM methodologies applied correctly. Strong submissions will demonstrate understanding of organizational change management and stakeholder psychology. Common weaknesses include insufficient root cause analysis, generic solutions not tailored to the scenario, and poor integration between different project elements. Grade distribution typically: 90-100 (exceptional integration and innovation), 80-89 (solid application of PM principles), 70-79 (adequate but missing key elements), below 70 (fundamental misunderstanding of PM concepts). Partial credit available within each criterion based on depth and accuracy of analysis.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Management Examination
description: A comprehensive exam assessing advanced leadership competencies through crisis scenario analysis, strategic decision-making frameworks, and organizational transformation leadership. Students demonstrate expertise in crisis leadership, stakeholder management, change implementation, and ethical decision-making under pressure.
learning_objectives_assessed: Analyze complex organizational crises and develop comprehensive leadership response strategies
Apply advanced leadership theories and frameworks to real-world strategic challenges
Evaluate ethical implications of leadership decisions and stakeholder impact
Design and justify organizational change management initiatives during crisis periods
Demonstrate mastery of communication strategies for diverse stakeholder groups during uncertainty
rubric_criteria: Crisis Analysis & Strategic Thinking (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of crisis dynamics, identifies root causes, assesses organizational vulnerabilities, and develops comprehensive situational analysis with multiple scenario considerations

Leadership Framework Application (25 points): Expertly applies multiple leadership theories and models, integrates frameworks appropriately, demonstrates deep understanding of leadership principles, and shows innovative adaptation of theoretical concepts to practical situations

Stakeholder Management & Communication Strategy (25 points): Develops nuanced stakeholder mapping, creates targeted communication plans for diverse audiences, demonstrates cultural sensitivity, addresses resistance management, and shows mastery of crisis communication principles

Implementation Planning & Ethical Reasoning (25 points): Creates detailed, realistic implementation timelines with resource allocation, addresses ethical dilemmas with sophisticated moral reasoning, demonstrates accountability frameworks, and shows consideration for long-term organizational sustainability
instructions: This exam consists of a comprehensive crisis leadership scenario requiring strategic analysis and solution development. You will receive a detailed organizational crisis case study involving multiple stakeholders, ethical dilemmas, and time-sensitive decisions. Your response must include: (1) A thorough crisis analysis identifying key issues, stakeholders, and organizational vulnerabilities; (2) Application of minimum three leadership theories/frameworks with justification for their relevance; (3) A detailed stakeholder communication strategy with specific messaging for different audiences; (4) An implementation plan with timeline, resource requirements, and risk mitigation strategies; (5) Ethical analysis addressing moral implications of proposed decisions. Format your response as a professional executive briefing document, maximum 3,500 words, with clear section headers, executive summary, and appendices for supporting frameworks. Include minimum 10 scholarly leadership sources published within last 5 years. Cite all sources using APA format. Submit as PDF with professional formatting. Graphs, charts, and visual aids are encouraged to support your analysis. Assume you are presenting to the board of directors who need clear, actionable recommendations with strong theoretical foundation.
grading_notes: Evaluate responses using expert-level expectations for strategic thinking and leadership sophistication. Look for evidence of systems thinking, not just surface-level analysis. Strong responses will demonstrate integration of multiple perspectives, acknowledge complexity and ambiguity, and show innovative problem-solving. Deduct points for generic solutions lacking specificity to the case context. Expect graduate-level writing quality and professional presentation. Grade distribution typically: 90-100 (exceptional strategic insight with innovative solutions), 80-89 (solid analysis with good framework application), 70-79 (adequate response meeting basic requirements), below 70 (insufficient depth or major gaps in leadership understanding). Watch for ethical blindness, oversimplified solutions, poor stakeholder analysis, and failure to consider implementation challenges. Reward creative but realistic approaches supported by solid theoretical foundation.

title: AWS Cloud Migration Planning Discussion
description: Students will analyze a small business scenario and develop a comprehensive plan for migrating their IT infrastructure to AWS Cloud, demonstrating understanding of core AWS services, cost considerations, and migration best practices.
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify appropriate AWS services for common business requirements
Analyze cost implications and benefits of cloud migration
Explain AWS security and compliance fundamentals
Design basic AWS architecture solutions for small business needs
rubric_criteria: AWS Service Selection (25 points): Correctly identifies and justifies appropriate AWS services (EC2, S3, RDS, etc.) for the business scenario with clear reasoning for each choice
Cost Analysis (25 points): Provides realistic cost estimates, compares on-premises vs. cloud costs, and demonstrates understanding of AWS pricing models and cost optimization strategies
Security and Compliance (25 points): Addresses data security, access management, backup strategies, and relevant compliance requirements using AWS security services
Migration Strategy (25 points): Outlines a logical migration timeline, identifies potential challenges, proposes solutions, and includes testing and rollback considerations
instructions:
You are an IT consultant advising 'GreenLeaf Accounting,' a 25-employee firm currently running on-premises servers for email, file storage, accounting software, and client data management. They spend $8,000 annually on server maintenance and want to explore AWS migration.

Create a comprehensive migration plan (800-1200 words) addressing:

1. **Service Recommendations**: Identify specific AWS services for their needs (email, file storage, application hosting, database). Explain why each service fits their requirements.

2. **Cost Analysis**: Estimate monthly AWS costs using AWS Pricing Calculator or publicly available pricing. Compare with current expenses and justify the investment.

3. **Security Plan**: Detail how you'll protect sensitive financial data using AWS security services. Address encryption, access controls, and backup strategies.

4. **Migration Timeline**: Create a 6-month implementation plan with phases, milestones, and risk mitigation strategies.

Format your response as a business proposal with clear headings. Support recommendations with specific AWS service names and features. Include at least one architecture diagram (hand-drawn sketches acceptable). Submit as PDF through the course portal by 11:59 PM on the due date. Late submissions lose 10 points per day.
grading_notes: Award full points when students demonstrate clear understanding rather than perfect technical accuracy. Look for logical reasoning and practical considerations. Common issues include: unrealistic cost estimates (guide toward AWS Pricing Calculator), overlooking data migration complexity, insufficient security planning, and overly ambitious timelines. Expect most students to score 70-85 points. Award 90+ for exceptional detail and creativity. Partial credit available for each criterion - minimum 10 points if basic understanding shown, even with errors.

title: Comprehensive E-commerce Analytics Strategy Portfolio
description: Students will create a complete Google Analytics implementation and optimization strategy for a fictional e-commerce business, demonstrating advanced analytics setup, data analysis, and actionable business recommendations through a multi-component portfolio submission.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design and implement advanced Google Analytics 4 configurations including custom events, conversions, and audience segments
Analyze complex e-commerce data to identify trends, opportunities, and performance issues using advanced GA4 features
Create comprehensive measurement frameworks and KPI dashboards aligned with business objectives
Develop data-driven recommendations for website optimization and marketing strategy improvements
Demonstrate proficiency in advanced GA4 reporting, custom dimensions, and cross-platform tracking
rubric_criteria: Analytics Implementation & Configuration (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive GA4 setup including proper event tracking, e-commerce implementation, custom dimensions/metrics, audience creation, and conversion tracking with technically accurate configurations

Data Analysis & Insights (25 points): Provides thorough analysis of user behavior, conversion funnels, traffic sources, and e-commerce performance with clear identification of trends, anomalies, and business-critical insights using advanced GA4 features

Strategic Recommendations & Action Plans (25 points): Delivers specific, data-driven recommendations for website optimization, marketing improvements, and business growth with clear implementation timelines, expected outcomes, and ROI projections

Professional Presentation & Documentation (25 points): Submits well-organized portfolio with clear visualizations, professional reporting format, executive summary, and comprehensive documentation that effectively communicates findings to stakeholders
instructions: Create a comprehensive analytics portfolio for 'TechGear Pro,' a fictional online electronics retailer. Your submission must include: (1) A detailed GA4 implementation plan document outlining property setup, event tracking schema, custom dimensions, audience definitions, and conversion goals; (2) Three months of simulated data analysis using GA4 demo account or sandbox environment, including user acquisition analysis, behavior flow examination, e-commerce performance review, and mobile vs desktop comparison; (3) A strategic recommendations report with specific optimization suggestions for improving conversion rates, reducing cart abandonment, and enhancing user experience; (4) An executive dashboard mockup showing key KPIs and automated reporting setup. Submit all components as a single PDF portfolio (15-25 pages) with clear sections, professional formatting, and supporting screenshots from GA4 interface. Include an appendix with your measurement framework documentation and any custom Google Tag Manager configurations. Demonstrate use of advanced features like custom segments, cohort analysis, attribution modeling, and cross-device tracking. Your analysis should reveal at least 5 specific business insights and provide 8-10 actionable recommendations with implementation priorities.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy of GA4 configurations by checking against current platform capabilities and best practices. Look for depth of analysis beyond surface-level metrics - students should demonstrate understanding of statistical significance, data sampling, and attribution complexities. Strong submissions will show creative use of advanced features like custom audiences, predictive metrics, and cross-platform measurement. Common issues include: incomplete event tracking schemas, superficial data analysis without context, recommendations lacking specificity or feasibility, and poor visual presentation. Expect grade distribution: 20% A-level (90-100), 40% B-level (80-89), 30% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. Deduct points for missing GA4 interface screenshots, unrealistic recommendations, or failure to address mobile analytics requirements. Bonus consideration for integration with other Google Marketing Platform tools or advanced statistical analysis techniques.

title: Predictive Analytics Project: Customer Churn Analysis
description: Students will conduct an end-to-end data science project analyzing customer churn patterns using provided telecommunications dataset. This assessment evaluates data preprocessing, exploratory analysis, feature engineering, model development, and business insights communication.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply data preprocessing and cleaning techniques to handle real-world dataset inconsistencies
Conduct comprehensive exploratory data analysis to identify patterns and generate hypotheses
Implement feature engineering strategies to improve model performance
Build, evaluate, and compare multiple machine learning models using appropriate metrics
Communicate data-driven insights and recommendations effectively to business stakeholders
rubric_criteria: Data Preprocessing & Cleaning (25 points): Proper handling of missing values, outliers, data type conversions, and documentation of preprocessing decisions with clear justification
Exploratory Data Analysis (25 points): Thorough statistical analysis, meaningful visualizations, identification of key patterns, correlations, and actionable insights about churn drivers

Model Development & Evaluation (25 points): Implementation of at least 3 different algorithms, proper train/validation/test splits, appropriate evaluation metrics, hyperparameter tuning, and model comparison
Communication & Business Impact (25 points): Clear executive summary, well-structured technical report, actionable recommendations, and professional presentation of findings with business context
instructions: You will analyze a telecommunications customer dataset (provided via course portal) to predict customer churn and provide actionable business recommendations. Your deliverables include: (1) Jupyter notebook with complete analysis workflow, (2) Executive summary presentation (8-10 slides), and (3) Technical report (6-8 pages). Start by exploring the dataset structure and quality - document all preprocessing steps including handling of missing values, categorical encoding, and feature scaling. Conduct thorough EDA using statistical summaries and visualizations to understand churn patterns across different customer segments. Develop at least three different predictive models (e.g., logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting) and evaluate using precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC. Include feature importance analysis and model interpretation. Your executive presentation should focus on business insights - which customer segments are at highest risk, what factors drive churn, and specific retention strategies. The technical report should detail methodology, model performance comparison, limitations, and future improvements. Submit all files via course portal by 11:59 PM on the due date. Ensure your notebook runs completely from top to bottom and includes clear markdown explanations throughout. Code should be well-commented and follow PEP 8 style guidelines.
grading_notes: Evaluate code quality and reproducibility - notebooks should run without errors. Look for proper statistical thinking in EDA, not just basic descriptive statistics. Model evaluation should demonstrate understanding of classification metrics and business trade-offs (precision vs recall for churn prediction). Common issues include: inadequate handling of class imbalance, data leakage in preprocessing, overfitting without proper validation. Exceptional work (90-100) shows creative feature engineering, ensemble methods, or business metric optimization. Satisfactory work (70-89) meets all requirements with minor issues. Below expectations (<70) has significant methodological flaws or incomplete deliverables. Allocate roughly 30% A grades, 50% B grades, 20% C or below based on demonstrated mastery of data science workflow.

title: Quantum Mechanics Interpretations: Copenhagen vs Many-Worlds Analysis
description: Students will engage in a structured discussion analyzing the fundamental differences between the Copenhagen and Many-Worlds interpretations of quantum mechanics, evaluating their explanatory power for quantum phenomena and implications for our understanding of reality.
estimated_time: 120-150 minutes (including research, writing, and peer responses)
learning_objectives_assessed: Analyze and compare different interpretations of quantum mechanical phenomena
Evaluate the philosophical and scientific implications of quantum measurement theory
Synthesize complex theoretical concepts to form evidence-based arguments
Critically assess the strengths and limitations of competing theoretical frameworks
rubric_criteria: Theoretical Understanding (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive grasp of both interpretations, accurately explains key concepts (wave function collapse, superposition, measurement problem), and shows understanding of mathematical formalism implications

Critical Analysis (25 points): Provides sophisticated comparison of interpretations, identifies key philosophical differences, evaluates experimental evidence, and addresses the measurement problem from multiple perspectives

Evidence and Examples (25 points): Uses specific quantum phenomena (double-slit, Schrödinger's cat, EPR paradox, delayed-choice experiments) to support arguments, references relevant research or thought experiments, and connects theory to observable consequences

Scientific Communication (25 points): Presents clear, logical arguments with proper physics terminology, engages constructively with peers' posts, maintains scientific rigor while discussing philosophical implications, and demonstrates ability to explain complex concepts clearly
instructions: This discussion requires you to take a position on which interpretation of quantum mechanics—Copenhagen or Many-Worlds—provides a more satisfactory framework for understanding quantum phenomena. Your initial post (400-500 words) must: (1) Clearly state your chosen interpretation and rationale, (2) Explain how your chosen interpretation handles the measurement problem and wave function collapse, (3) Address at least two specific quantum phenomena (e.g., double-slit experiment, quantum entanglement, delayed-choice experiments) from your interpretation's perspective, (4) Acknowledge and respond to the strongest objection to your position. Use peer-reviewed sources and cite appropriately. After posting, you must respond substantively to at least two classmates who chose the opposite interpretation (150-200 words each). Your responses should challenge their reasoning constructively, propose alternative explanations for their examples, or identify assumptions in their arguments. Focus on the physics and philosophy, not personal opinions. All posts must use proper scientific terminology and demonstrate understanding of the mathematical formalism underlying quantum mechanics. Submit your initial post by Wednesday 11:59 PM and responses by Sunday 11:59 PM.
grading_notes: Look for students who can distinguish between the physics (mathematical formalism) and interpretation (meaning). Excellent responses will address the hard problem of consciousness, locality vs. non-locality, and the role of the observer. Watch for common misconceptions: confusing decoherence with collapse, misunderstanding the role of consciousness, or oversimplifying many-worlds as 'splitting universes.' Grade distribution should reflect: 90-100 points for sophisticated understanding with nuanced arguments; 80-89 for solid grasp with minor gaps; 70-79 for basic understanding but lacking depth; below 70 for fundamental misunderstandings. Credit creative thinking about experimental tests or novel philosophical insights. Deduct points for failure to engage meaningfully with opposing views or for responses that don't demonstrate expert-level physics knowledge.

title: Personal Software Development Portfolio Presentation
description: Students will create and present a portfolio showcasing their software development journey, including 2-3 beginner projects with code demonstrations, technical explanations, and reflection on their learning process.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate understanding of basic programming concepts and syntax
Explain the software development process from planning to implementation
Identify and articulate problem-solving approaches in coding
Communicate technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
rubric_criteria: Technical Content (25 points): Projects demonstrate correct use of basic programming concepts (variables, loops, conditionals, functions). Code is functional and shows understanding of syntax and logic flow.

Project Documentation (25 points): Each project includes clear problem statement, approach explanation, and code walkthrough. Documentation is well-organized and demonstrates understanding of development process.
Presentation Skills (25 points): Clear verbal communication, appropriate pacing, effective use of visual aids, maintains audience engagement. Technical concepts explained in accessible language.
Learning Reflection (25 points): Thoughtful analysis of challenges faced, problem-solving strategies used, lessons learned, and future development goals. Shows growth mindset and self-awareness.
instructions: Create a 10-minute presentation showcasing your software development portfolio. Include 2-3 beginner-level projects you've completed (examples: calculator app, simple game, basic website, data analysis script). For each project: (1) Explain the problem you were solving, (2) Walk through your code highlighting key programming concepts used, (3) Demonstrate the working application, (4) Discuss one challenge you overcame. Conclude with a 2-minute reflection on your learning journey, including what concepts clicked for you, what you found most challenging, and your next learning goals. Use slides or screen sharing to show your code and running applications. Submit your presentation slides and project files 24 hours before your presentation slot. Dress professionally and be prepared for 2-3 follow-up questions about your projects. Focus on explaining your thinking process rather than just showing what the code does.
grading_notes: Look for understanding over complexity - beginner projects with clear explanations score better than advanced projects poorly explained. Common issues include rushing through code explanations, not demonstrating actual functionality, and weak reflection components. Expect grade distribution: 20% excellent (90-100), 60% proficient (75-89), 20% developing (60-74). Deduct points for non-functional code, unclear explanations, going significantly over/under time limit. Provide specific feedback on technical accuracy and communication clarity.

title: E-commerce Customer Analytics Portfolio Project
description: Students will analyze a real e-commerce dataset to identify customer segments, purchasing patterns, and business insights. They will create a comprehensive portfolio demonstrating data cleaning, exploratory analysis, statistical modeling, and business recommendations using tools like Python/R, SQL, and visualization software.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply data cleaning and preprocessing techniques to handle missing values, outliers, and inconsistent data formats
Conduct exploratory data analysis using appropriate statistical methods and visualizations
Implement customer segmentation using clustering algorithms and interpret results
Communicate data-driven insights effectively through written reports and visual presentations
Evaluate model performance and validate analytical conclusions using appropriate metrics
rubric_criteria: Data Preparation & Quality (25 points): Demonstrates thorough data cleaning, handles missing values appropriately, documents data quality issues, creates clean dataset ready for analysis

Analysis & Methodology (25 points): Uses appropriate statistical methods, implements customer segmentation correctly, shows proper use of analytical tools, demonstrates understanding of chosen techniques
Visualization & Interpretation (25 points): Creates clear, informative visualizations, interprets results accurately, identifies meaningful patterns and trends, uses appropriate chart types for data

Business Recommendations & Communication (25 points): Provides actionable business insights, writes clear executive summary, demonstrates understanding of business context, presents findings professionally
instructions: Using the provided e-commerce dataset (contains 12 months of customer transactions, demographics, and product data), create a comprehensive analytics portfolio with four components: 1) Data Quality Report: Document data issues found, cleaning steps taken, and final dataset structure. Include code and explanations. 2) Exploratory Analysis: Perform statistical analysis of customer behavior, purchasing patterns, and product performance. Create at least 6 meaningful visualizations with interpretations. 3) Customer Segmentation: Implement K-means or hierarchical clustering to identify distinct customer segments. Validate your segmentation and profile each segment. 4) Business Recommendations: Write a 2-page executive summary with actionable recommendations for marketing, inventory, and customer retention strategies. Submit as a GitHub repository or portfolio website containing Jupyter notebooks/R Markdown files, visualizations, cleaned datasets, and executive summary. Include a README file explaining your approach and how to reproduce your analysis. All code must be well-commented and reproducible.
grading_notes: Look for evidence of systematic thinking in data cleaning approach - students should document what they found and why they made specific decisions. In analysis section, assess whether statistical methods match the research questions and data types. Visualization quality should be evaluated on clarity, appropriateness, and insight generation, not just technical execution. Business recommendations must connect directly to analytical findings - watch for generic advice not supported by the data. Common issues: insufficient data exploration before modeling, choosing clustering parameters without justification, creating visualizations without clear purpose, making recommendations that ignore analytical constraints. Expect grade distribution: 20% A-level work (90-100), 50% B-level work (80-89), 25% C-level work (70-79), 5% below 70. Provide specific feedback on technical accuracy and business insight quality.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Management and Organizational Transformation Case Analysis
description: A comprehensive assessment evaluating advanced leadership competencies through analysis of a complex organizational crisis scenario, requiring strategic decision-making, stakeholder management, and change leadership implementation across multiple business units and cultural contexts.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate advanced crisis leadership and strategic decision-making under uncertainty
Apply systems thinking to complex organizational challenges across multiple stakeholders
Design and justify comprehensive change management strategies for organizational transformation
Evaluate ethical leadership considerations in high-stakes business environments
Synthesize leadership theories with practical implementation in multicultural organizational contexts
rubric_criteria: Strategic Analysis and Decision-Making (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of crisis dynamics, identifies root causes, evaluates multiple strategic options with risk assessment, and justifies decisions using relevant frameworks and data analysis

Stakeholder Management and Communication Strategy (25 points): Develops comprehensive stakeholder mapping, creates tailored communication plans for diverse audiences, addresses conflicting interests with diplomatic solutions, and demonstrates cultural sensitivity in global contexts

Change Leadership and Implementation Planning (25 points): Designs detailed transformation roadmap with clear phases, anticipates resistance and mitigation strategies, establishes measurable success metrics, and demonstrates understanding of organizational psychology and change dynamics

Ethical Reasoning and Professional Judgment (25 points): Identifies complex ethical dilemmas, applies multiple ethical frameworks, balances competing moral claims, demonstrates integrity in decision-making, and considers long-term consequences on all stakeholders
instructions: You will analyze the provided case study of MegaCorp International's simultaneous product recall crisis, regulatory investigation, and market expansion challenges. Your analysis must include: (1) Executive Summary (500 words): Synthesize key issues and your strategic recommendations. (2) Crisis Leadership Plan (1000 words): Detail immediate actions for the first 90 days, including decision-making processes, resource allocation, and risk mitigation. Address the product recall, regulatory compliance, and reputation management simultaneously. (3) Stakeholder Engagement Strategy (800 words): Create specific communication plans for employees, customers, regulators, media, and international partners. Include messaging frameworks and engagement timelines. (4) Organizational Transformation Design (1200 words): Propose comprehensive changes to prevent future crises, including structural, cultural, and process improvements. Justify your approach using change management theories and provide implementation timeline with success metrics. (5) Ethical Framework and Reflection (500 words): Analyze ethical dilemmas present in the case, apply relevant ethical theories, and reflect on how your personal leadership philosophy influences your recommendations. Use APA format, minimum 15 scholarly sources including current leadership research. Submit as PDF with appendices for supporting frameworks or tools referenced.
grading_notes: Evaluate depth of analysis rather than length - look for evidence of systems thinking and integration across leadership domains. Excellent responses (90-100) will demonstrate original insights, sophisticated use of multiple theoretical frameworks, and innovative solutions. Good responses (80-89) show solid application of concepts with some original thinking. Satisfactory responses (70-79) demonstrate basic competency but lack depth or integration. Watch for superficial analysis, generic recommendations without justification, failure to address cultural/global dimensions, or inadequate consideration of implementation challenges. Expect grade distribution: 20% A, 40% B, 30% C, 10% below C. Provide specific feedback on each rubric criterion and suggest 2-3 areas for leadership development based on their analysis approach.

title: PMP Practice Exam: Project Execution and Monitoring & Controlling
description: A comprehensive 50-question multiple choice examination covering Project Management Professional (PMP) concepts focused on executing project work and monitoring & controlling project performance. Students will demonstrate knowledge of project management tools, techniques, and processes across various knowledge areas including scope, schedule, cost, quality, and risk management.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply project execution processes including directing and managing project work, quality assurance, and team development
Demonstrate understanding of monitoring and controlling processes including performance measurement, change control, and risk monitoring
Analyze project scenarios to select appropriate project management tools and techniques
Evaluate project situations to determine correct responses according to PMI standards and best practices
rubric_criteria: Process Knowledge (25 points): Demonstrates understanding of PMBOK process groups, inputs, outputs, and tools & techniques across knowledge areas
Situational Analysis (25 points): Correctly interprets project scenarios and identifies appropriate management responses and decision-making approaches
Tool Application (25 points): Shows knowledge of when and how to apply specific project management tools, formulas, and methodologies
PMI Standards Alignment (25 points): Responses align with PMI Code of Ethics, professional responsibility, and established project management standards
instructions: This exam consists of 50 multiple-choice questions worth 2 points each, covering PMP domains with emphasis on executing and monitoring & controlling processes. You have 90 minutes to complete the assessment. Each question has four options (A, B, C, D) with only one correct answer. Read each question carefully and select the BEST answer based on PMI standards and PMBOK Guide principles. Questions may include scenario-based problems requiring you to analyze project situations, calculate earned value metrics, determine critical path, or recommend appropriate project management responses. Some questions will test your knowledge of formulas - no calculators are permitted, but basic calculations should be manageable mentally. Mark your answers clearly on the provided answer sheet. If unsure about a question, make your best educated guess as there is no penalty for incorrect answers. Budget your time effectively - approximately 1.8 minutes per question. Review your answers if time permits, paying special attention to any questions you marked for review. Ensure you have answered all questions before submitting. This assessment simulates the actual PMP exam environment, so maintain academic integrity and work independently. Submit your completed answer sheet when finished or when time expires.
grading_notes: Use answer key provided separately. Award 2 points for each correct answer, 0 points for incorrect answers. Passing score is 70% (70 points). Track performance by domain: Initiating (10%), Planning (24%), Executing (31%), Monitoring & Controlling (25%), Closing (10%). Common student weaknesses include earned value calculations, critical path method, and distinguishing between similar processes. Watch for patterns in incorrect answers to identify knowledge gaps. Provide detailed feedback report showing domain-specific performance. Students scoring below 70% should review missed concepts before attempting certification. Grade distribution typically ranges: 90-100 (excellent), 80-89 (proficient), 70-79 (acceptable), below 70 (needs improvement). Consider partial remediation for scores 65-69.

title: Advanced Google Analytics Implementation Strategy: Multi-Channel Attribution Analysis
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive discussion-based analysis of advanced Google Analytics 4 (GA4) implementation strategies, focusing on multi-channel attribution modeling, custom event tracking, and data-driven decision making for complex e-commerce scenarios. This assessment evaluates students' ability to critically analyze attribution models, recommend implementation strategies, and defend their analytical approach through peer discussion.
