estimated_time: 4-5 hours (including research, analysis, and discussion participation)
learning_objectives_assessed: Evaluate and compare different attribution models in GA4 for multi-channel marketing campaigns
Design custom event tracking strategies for complex user journeys and business objectives
Analyze cross-platform data integration challenges and propose solutions using GA4's measurement protocol
Synthesize advanced GA4 features to create actionable insights for strategic business decisions
rubric_criteria: Attribution Model Analysis (25 points): Demonstrates deep understanding of first-click, last-click, linear, time-decay, position-based, and data-driven attribution models. Provides specific use cases, advantages/disadvantages, and clear recommendations with supporting rationale.

Custom Implementation Strategy (25 points): Develops comprehensive custom event tracking plan including Enhanced Ecommerce parameters, custom dimensions/metrics, and audience segmentation. Shows technical accuracy and business alignment with detailed implementation steps.

Cross-Platform Integration Solutions (25 points): Identifies and addresses data integration challenges across web, mobile, and offline touchpoints. Proposes specific solutions using Measurement Protocol, Google Tag Manager, and data import features with consideration for privacy regulations.

Discussion Quality and Peer Engagement (25 points): Provides substantive responses to peers with evidence-based arguments, asks insightful questions that advance discussion, synthesizes multiple viewpoints, and demonstrates collaborative problem-solving skills.
instructions:
You will participate in a structured online discussion analyzing a complex e-commerce scenario requiring advanced GA4 implementation. 

SCENARIO: A multi-brand retail company operates across web, mobile app, physical stores, and third-party marketplaces. They need to track customer journeys spanning 6-month consideration periods, measure the impact of influencer partnerships, and attribute revenue across 12+ marketing channels.

REQUIREMENTS:
1. INITIAL POST (48 hours): Submit a 500-700 word analysis addressing: (a) Recommended attribution model with detailed justification, (b) Custom event tracking strategy including specific parameters and triggers, (c) Cross-platform data integration approach addressing technical and privacy constraints.

2. PEER RESPONSES (next 72 hours): Respond substantively to at least 3 classmates' posts (200-300 words each). Challenge assumptions, offer alternative approaches, or build upon their strategies with specific examples.

3. SYNTHESIS POST (final 24 hours): Write a 300-400 word reflection synthesizing key insights from the discussion, identifying areas of consensus/disagreement, and presenting your refined recommendations.

FORMAT: Use clear headings, cite specific GA4 features, include relevant screenshots or diagrams when helpful. Reference at least 3 authoritative sources (Google documentation, industry reports, case studies). Submit all posts within the designated discussion forum with proper threading.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy against current GA4 capabilities - watch for outdated Universal Analytics references. Strong responses will demonstrate practical implementation knowledge, not just theoretical understanding. Look for evidence of original thinking vs. regurgitation of course materials. Peer engagement should show active listening and build meaningful dialogue. Common issues include: oversimplified attribution model selection, ignoring privacy/GDPR implications, unrealistic implementation timelines, and superficial peer responses. Grade distribution expectation: 15% exemplary (90-100), 60% proficient (80-89), 20% developing (70-79), 5% inadequate (below 70). Provide specific feedback on technical misconceptions and highlight innovative approaches for class sharing.

title: Enterprise Network Infrastructure Design and Security Implementation Presentation
description: Students will design and present a comprehensive enterprise network infrastructure solution for a multi-site organization, incorporating advanced routing protocols, network security, QoS implementation, and disaster recovery strategies. The presentation must demonstrate mastery of Cisco enterprise technologies and industry best practices.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design scalable enterprise network architectures using advanced Cisco routing and switching protocols
Implement comprehensive network security solutions including firewalls, VPNs, and access control
Configure Quality of Service (QoS) policies for voice, video, and data traffic prioritization
Develop network monitoring, troubleshooting, and disaster recovery strategies
Evaluate and justify technology choices based on business requirements and industry standards
rubric_criteria: Network Architecture Design (25 points): Demonstrates advanced understanding of hierarchical network design, OSPF/EIGRP implementation, VLAN segmentation, inter-VLAN routing, and scalability considerations with proper Cisco device selection and configuration examples

Security Implementation (25 points): Presents comprehensive security strategy including ASA firewall configuration, site-to-site and remote access VPN setup, 802.1X authentication, network access control, and threat mitigation strategies with specific Cisco security technologies

Technical Accuracy and Implementation Details (25 points): Shows expert-level knowledge of Cisco IOS commands, configuration syntax, protocol operations, QoS marking and queuing strategies, and provides realistic implementation timelines with potential challenges identified

Professional Presentation and Business Justification (25 points): Delivers clear, well-organized presentation with appropriate technical diagrams, cost-benefit analysis, ROI calculations, compliance considerations, and effectively answers technical questions demonstrating deep understanding
instructions: You are tasked with designing a complete network infrastructure for GlobalTech Solutions, a financial services company with headquarters (500 users), two branch offices (150 users each), and 200 remote workers. Your 20-minute presentation must include: (1) Network topology diagram showing physical and logical connections, (2) Detailed routing protocol configuration (OSPF or EIGRP) with area/AS design, (3) VLAN strategy with inter-VLAN routing implementation, (4) Comprehensive security architecture including firewall rules, VPN configurations, and access control policies, (5) QoS implementation for voice (VoIP), video conferencing, and critical business applications, (6) Network monitoring solution with SNMP, NetFlow, and alerting strategies, (7) Disaster recovery and business continuity plan, (8) Implementation timeline with budget estimates and risk assessment. Include specific Cisco device models, IOS commands, and configuration snippets. Address regulatory compliance requirements for financial services. Prepare for technical questions about protocol selection, scalability, troubleshooting scenarios, and alternative solutions. Submit presentation slides (15-20 slides) and a technical appendix with detailed configurations 48 hours before presentation date. Use professional network diagramming tools and include vendor documentation references.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical depth over presentation polish - students should demonstrate hands-on Cisco experience through specific command syntax and realistic configuration examples. Look for industry-standard practices, proper subnet design, appropriate protocol selection for network size, and security-first mindset. Common weaknesses include oversimplified security implementations, unrealistic timelines, missing QoS considerations, and inability to justify design decisions. Grade distribution expectation: 90-100 points (demonstrates professional-level competency), 80-89 points (solid technical understanding with minor gaps), 70-79 points (adequate knowledge but missing critical components), below 70 points (insufficient technical depth for expert level). During Q&A, probe troubleshooting scenarios, protocol convergence issues, scalability limitations, and alternative technology choices. Award full points only for responses showing genuine understanding rather than memorized answers.

title: Beginning Programmer's Portfolio: Basic Programming Concepts Showcase
description: Students will create a comprehensive portfolio demonstrating fundamental programming concepts through Python code examples, explanations, and reflections. The portfolio showcases understanding of variables, control structures, functions, and basic problem-solving skills through original programs and documented learning experiences.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate understanding of basic programming concepts including variables, data types, and operators
Apply control structures (if/else, loops) to solve simple problems
Create and use functions with parameters and return values
Write clear, readable code with appropriate comments and documentation
Reflect on learning process and problem-solving approaches
rubric_criteria: Code Functionality (25 points): Programs run correctly without errors, produce expected outputs, and demonstrate proper use of Python syntax. All code examples work as intended and show mastery of basic programming concepts.

Problem-Solving Application (25 points): Clear demonstration of using variables, control structures, and functions to solve practical problems. Code shows logical thinking and appropriate algorithm design for beginner-level challenges.

Code Quality and Documentation (25 points): Code is well-organized, properly indented, uses meaningful variable names, and includes helpful comments. Each program includes clear explanations of what it does and how it works.

Reflection and Learning Documentation (25 points): Thoughtful reflection on learning process, challenges faced, and solutions discovered. Portfolio includes evidence of iterative improvement and understanding of programming concepts beyond just syntax.
instructions: Create a digital portfolio containing five Python programs that demonstrate your understanding of fundamental programming concepts. Your portfolio must include: (1) A simple calculator program using variables and arithmetic operators, (2) A number guessing game implementing if/else statements and loops, (3) A program that processes a list of data using loops and conditional logic, (4) Two custom functions that solve specific problems and demonstrate parameter passing, and (5) One creative program of your choice that combines multiple concepts. Each program must be accompanied by: a brief description of what the program does, commented code explaining key sections, sample input/output, and a reflection paragraph discussing what you learned and any challenges you overcame. Format your portfolio as a single document (Word/PDF) or website with clear sections for each program. Include an introduction explaining your programming journey and a conclusion reflecting on your overall learning experience. All code must be original work, properly tested, and executable. Submit your portfolio along with all .py files in a compressed folder. Portfolio should be 8-12 pages if written format, or equivalent content if web-based.
grading_notes: Focus on conceptual understanding rather than advanced features. Expect some minor syntax errors but programs should demonstrate clear grasp of fundamental concepts. Look for evidence of iterative development and learning from mistakes in reflections. Common issues include: insufficient commenting, programs that don't demonstrate required concepts clearly, missing reflection components, or code that appears copied rather than original work. Grade distribution should reflect beginner level - students showing solid understanding of basics with clear documentation should earn B-range grades, while those demonstrating mastery plus creativity/depth should earn A-range. Partial credit available for non-functional code if logic and understanding are evident.

title: Advanced Multivariable Calculus Applications Quiz
description: Comprehensive assessment covering optimization problems, vector fields, line integrals, and surface integrals with real-world applications in physics and engineering contexts
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply Lagrange multipliers to solve constrained optimization problems in three dimensions
Evaluate line integrals and surface integrals using appropriate parameterizations
Analyze vector fields and apply Green's theorem, Stokes' theorem, and the divergence theorem
Model and solve real-world problems using multivariable calculus techniques
rubric_criteria: Problem Setup and Mathematical Modeling (25 points): Correctly identifies given information, establishes coordinate systems, sets up equations with proper notation, and translates word problems into mathematical expressions

Computational Accuracy and Technique (25 points): Demonstrates mastery of calculus techniques including partial derivatives, multiple integrals, parameterizations, and applies theorems correctly with accurate arithmetic

Reasoning and Justification (25 points): Shows logical progression of steps, explains choice of methods, provides mathematical reasoning for decisions, and demonstrates understanding of underlying concepts

Communication and Interpretation (25 points): Uses clear mathematical notation, provides complete solutions with appropriate units, interprets results in context, and presents work in organized, readable format
instructions:
This quiz consists of 4 multi-part problems requiring comprehensive solutions. You have 120 minutes to complete all problems. Show all work clearly and justify your methods. Partial credit will be awarded based on correct setup, appropriate techniques, and logical reasoning even if final answers are incorrect.

Problem 1: Constrained Optimization - Find the maximum and minimum values of a function subject to two constraints using Lagrange multipliers. Verify your results and interpret geometrically.

Problem 2: Vector Field Analysis - Given a vector field, determine if it's conservative, find potential functions if applicable, and evaluate line integrals along specified curves using the most efficient method.

Problem 3: Surface Integrals - Calculate the flux of a vector field through a closed surface using both direct integration and the divergence theorem. Compare results and explain any discrepancies.

Problem 4: Real-world Application - Model and solve an engineering optimization problem involving heat distribution or fluid flow, requiring integration of multiple multivariable calculus concepts.

Submission Requirements: Write solutions legibly in blue or black ink, number all pages, include your name and student ID on each page. Calculator use is permitted but show all setup work. Submit all scratch work attached. Late submissions will incur a 10% penalty per day.
grading_notes: Award partial credit generously for correct approach and setup even with computational errors. Look for conceptual understanding over perfect arithmetic. Common issues: students often forget to check boundary conditions in optimization, confuse orientation in surface integrals, and struggle with parameterization choices. Grade distribution should approximate: 15% A-level (90-100), 25% B-level (80-89), 40% C-level (70-79), 20% below 70. Deduct points for unclear notation or skipped justification steps. Bonus consideration for elegant alternative solution methods or exceptional insight into geometric interpretations.

title: Data-Driven Business Decision Analysis Discussion
description: Students will analyze a real-world business scenario using provided datasets, identify key insights through statistical analysis, and engage in peer discussions about methodology choices and business implications. This assessment evaluates both technical analytical skills and the ability to communicate findings effectively to business stakeholders.
estimated_time: 4-5 hours (2 hours initial analysis + 2-3 hours discussion participation)
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply appropriate statistical methods to analyze business data and identify meaningful patterns
Interpret data visualization outputs and draw actionable business conclusions
Communicate analytical findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
Evaluate and critique different analytical approaches used by peers
rubric_criteria: Data Analysis Quality (25 points): Demonstrates proper data cleaning, appropriate statistical methods selection, accurate calculations, and comprehensive exploration of the dataset
Business Insights & Recommendations (25 points): Identifies relevant business implications, provides actionable recommendations supported by data, and addresses potential limitations or risks

Communication & Visualization (25 points): Uses clear, professional language appropriate for business audience, creates effective visualizations that support arguments, and structures findings logically

Discussion Participation (25 points): Provides substantive responses to peers, asks thoughtful questions about methodology, offers constructive feedback, and defends own analytical choices with evidence
instructions: You will receive a business case study with accompanying datasets (customer sales, marketing campaigns, and demographic data). Complete the following steps: 1) Conduct exploratory data analysis to understand data quality and key variables. 2) Perform statistical analysis to answer the provided business questions (correlation analysis, trend identification, customer segmentation). 3) Create 3-4 visualizations that clearly communicate your key findings. 4) Write a 500-word executive summary with data-driven recommendations. 5) Post your summary and one key visualization to the discussion forum by Wednesday. 6) Respond to at least three classmates' posts by Sunday, focusing on: alternative analytical approaches they could have used, questions about their methodology or assumptions, and how their findings compare to yours. Each response should be 150-200 words and demonstrate critical thinking about data analysis choices. Include specific references to their data or visualizations. Submit your complete analysis (including code/spreadsheet work, all visualizations, and executive summary) as a single PDF. Ensure all charts are properly labeled with titles, axis labels, and data sources.
grading_notes: Look for evidence of systematic analytical thinking rather than just correct answers. Award full points for data analysis quality when students demonstrate proper data exploration, handle missing values appropriately, and justify their statistical method choices. For business insights, prioritize practical, implementable recommendations over theoretical discussions. Communication scores should reflect clarity for business audiences - deduct points for excessive technical jargon without explanation. Discussion participation quality matters more than quantity - substantive critiques and methodology questions earn higher scores than simple agreement. Common issues to watch: inadequate data cleaning documentation, visualizations without clear business context, recommendations not supported by the analysis, and superficial peer responses. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90-100), 50% B-level (80-89), 30% C-level (70-79), 5% below 70. Students scoring below 70 typically show incomplete analysis or fail to connect data findings to business implications.

title: Complex Project Recovery and Turnaround Strategy Presentation
description: Students will analyze a real-world failed or troubled project, develop a comprehensive recovery strategy, and present their turnaround plan to stakeholders. This assessment evaluates advanced project management skills including risk mitigation, stakeholder management, resource reallocation, and crisis leadership.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced risk management and crisis resolution techniques to salvage troubled projects
Demonstrate strategic thinking in resource reallocation and scope management under constraints
Execute effective stakeholder communication and change management during project turnaround
Synthesize multiple project management methodologies to develop innovative recovery solutions
rubric_criteria: Problem Analysis & Root Cause Assessment (25 points): Demonstrates thorough analysis of project failure factors, identifies underlying causes beyond surface symptoms, uses appropriate analytical frameworks (fishbone, 5-whys, etc.), and provides evidence-based conclusions about what went wrong

Recovery Strategy Development (25 points): Presents a comprehensive, realistic turnaround plan with specific timelines, resource requirements, and success metrics. Strategy shows integration of multiple PM methodologies and addresses scope, schedule, budget, and quality constraints effectively

Stakeholder Management & Communication Plan (25 points): Identifies all affected stakeholders, develops targeted communication strategies for each group, addresses resistance management, and demonstrates understanding of organizational politics and change management principles

Presentation Quality & Professional Delivery (25 points): Delivers clear, engaging presentation appropriate for executive audience, handles Q&A professionally, uses visual aids effectively, stays within time limits, and demonstrates confidence in recommendations
instructions: Select a documented failed or troubled project from any industry (examples: Berlin Brandenburg Airport, Healthcare.gov launch, Boeing 787 delays). Your presentation must include: (1) Executive Summary: 2-minute overview of the situation and your recommended approach; (2) Situation Analysis: Detailed breakdown of what went wrong, including timeline, budget impacts, and stakeholder effects; (3) Recovery Strategy: Your comprehensive turnaround plan including immediate actions (0-30 days), short-term recovery (1-6 months), and long-term stabilization (6-12 months); (4) Implementation Plan: Resource requirements, revised timeline, budget implications, and success metrics; (5) Risk Management: Identification of recovery risks and mitigation strategies; (6) Stakeholder Communication: Specific messaging for different stakeholder groups. Format: 20-minute presentation using professional slides, followed by 10-minute stakeholder Q&A session. Submit presentation slides and a 2-page executive summary 24 hours before presentation date. Dress professionally and assume your audience consists of senior executives, project sponsors, and key stakeholders. Be prepared to defend your recommendations and discuss alternative approaches.
grading_notes: Focus on depth of analysis rather than presentation polish - students should demonstrate genuine understanding of complex project dynamics. Look for evidence of research beyond basic case study facts. Strong responses will show creative problem-solving while remaining realistic about constraints. Common weaknesses include: oversimplifying root causes, proposing unrealistic timelines, ignoring political/organizational factors, and poor stakeholder analysis. Grade distribution expectation: 10% exceptional (A+), 25% strong (A/A-), 40% proficient (B range), 20% developing (C range), 5% inadequate (D/F). During Q&A, assess ability to think on feet and defend decisions under pressure. Partial credit available for each criterion - use 4-point scale within each 25-point section (Exemplary=23-25, Proficient=20-22, Developing=15-19, Inadequate=0-14).

title: Executive Leadership Portfolio: Strategic Transformation Case Study
description: Students develop a comprehensive leadership portfolio documenting their strategic approach to leading organizational transformation, including stakeholder analysis, change management framework, crisis response protocols, and measurable outcomes assessment across a 12-month simulated executive scenario.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate advanced strategic thinking and decision-making under uncertainty and competing priorities
Design and implement comprehensive stakeholder engagement and communication strategies for complex organizational change
Evaluate and apply sophisticated change management frameworks to real-world transformation scenarios
Analyze leadership effectiveness through quantitative metrics and qualitative feedback integration
rubric_criteria: Strategic Vision & Planning (25 points): Develops comprehensive 12-month transformation strategy with clear milestones, risk assessment, resource allocation, and contingency planning. Demonstrates systems thinking and anticipates second/third-order effects.

Stakeholder Management & Communication (25 points): Creates detailed stakeholder mapping with influence/interest analysis, tailored communication strategies, conflict resolution protocols, and measurable engagement metrics. Shows cultural sensitivity and emotional intelligence.

Change Leadership & Implementation (25 points): Applies evidence-based change management framework with specific tactics for resistance management, team motivation, capability building, and momentum maintenance. Includes leadership presence and authenticity strategies.

Performance Measurement & Reflection (25 points): Establishes quantitative KPIs and qualitative success measures, creates feedback loops, demonstrates adaptive leadership based on results, and provides sophisticated self-reflection on leadership growth and blind spots.
instructions: Create a comprehensive leadership portfolio addressing a complex organizational transformation scenario (provided separately). Your portfolio must include: 1) Executive Summary (2 pages) outlining your leadership philosophy and transformation approach; 2) Strategic Plan (8-10 pages) with detailed timeline, resource requirements, and risk mitigation strategies; 3) Stakeholder Analysis & Communication Framework (6-8 pages) including stakeholder maps, communication matrices, and conflict resolution protocols; 4) Change Management Implementation Guide (8-10 pages) with specific tactics, team development strategies, and cultural integration approaches; 5) Performance Dashboard (4-6 pages) showing KPIs, measurement tools, and feedback mechanisms; 6) Leadership Reflection Essay (4-5 pages) analyzing your decision-making process, lessons learned, and personal development areas. Use professional formatting with executive-level presentation quality. Include minimum 15 scholarly sources and 5 real-world case study references. Submit as PDF portfolio with interactive table of contents. All work must demonstrate expert-level critical thinking and practical applicability.
grading_notes: Evaluate portfolios holistically for executive-level thinking and presentation. Look for evidence of sophisticated strategic reasoning, not just theoretical knowledge application. Strong portfolios will show innovative solutions while demonstrating awareness of implementation challenges. Common issues include: oversimplified stakeholder analysis, generic change management approaches, unrealistic timelines, and superficial self-reflection. Expect 10% A grades (90-100), 25% B+ grades (87-89), 40% B grades (83-86), 20% B- grades (80-82), 5% below 80. Provide detailed feedback on leadership presence, decision-making rationale, and practical viability of proposed approaches.

title: AWS EC2 Instance Setup and Web Server Deployment Lab Report
description: Students will launch an AWS EC2 instance, configure security groups, install a web server, and document the complete process including troubleshooting steps and best practices observed during implementation.
learning_objectives_assessed: Deploy and configure AWS EC2 instances using the AWS Management Console
Implement basic security configurations including security groups and key pairs
Install and configure web services on cloud infrastructure
Document cloud deployment processes and apply troubleshooting methodologies
rubric_criteria: EC2 Instance Configuration (25 points): Correctly launches t2.micro instance, selects appropriate AMI, configures storage, and creates/uses key pairs with proper naming conventions
Security Group Setup (25 points): Creates security group with appropriate inbound rules (SSH port 22, HTTP port 80), applies principle of least privilege, and documents security decisions
Web Server Installation and Testing (25 points): Successfully installs Apache/Nginx, creates custom index.html page, demonstrates functionality through screenshots, and shows proper service status

Documentation and Reflection (25 points): Provides clear step-by-step process documentation, includes relevant screenshots, identifies challenges encountered, and demonstrates understanding of AWS concepts
instructions:
Complete the following AWS lab exercise and submit a comprehensive report documenting your process:

**Lab Tasks:**
1. Launch an Amazon EC2 t2.micro instance using Amazon Linux 2 AMI
2. Create and configure a security group allowing SSH (port 22) and HTTP (port 80) access
3. Generate a new key pair for secure access
4. Connect to your instance using SSH
5. Install and start Apache web server
6. Create a custom HTML page displaying your name and the current date
7. Test web server accessibility through the public IP address
8. Document all steps with screenshots

**Report Requirements:**
Submit a PDF document (8-12 pages) containing:
- Executive summary of the lab objectives and outcomes
- Detailed step-by-step process with numbered instructions
- Screenshots of key AWS console configurations and terminal commands
- Your custom web page displayed in a browser
- Reflection section discussing challenges faced and solutions implemented
- Cost analysis showing charges incurred (if any)
- Cleanup verification showing instance termination

**Technical Specifications:**
- Use only AWS Free Tier eligible resources
- Include AWS region information in documentation
- Show both AWS console and command-line interactions
- Demonstrate proper resource cleanup to avoid charges

**Submission Guidelines:**
Upload your PDF report through the course portal by the specified deadline. Ensure all screenshots are clearly visible and properly labeled. Late submissions will incur point deductions as per course policy.
grading_notes:
**Instructor Evaluation Guidelines:**

**Grade Distribution Expectations:** 85% of students should achieve 70+ points with proper lab completion. Award full points only when all technical requirements are met with clear documentation.

**Common Issues to Monitor:** Students often struggle with security group configurations (check for overly permissive rules like 0.0.0.0/0 for SSH), SSH connection problems (verify key pair usage and permissions), and incomplete cleanup documentation. Ensure students demonstrate actual web server functionality, not just installation commands.

**Technical Verification:** Look for evidence of hands-on completion rather than copied instructions. Valid indicators include: unique custom HTML content, consistent timestamps across screenshots, proper AWS resource naming conventions, and authentic troubleshooting documentation.

**Documentation Quality:** Reward clear, professional presentation with logical flow. Deduct points for missing screenshots, unclear explanations, or failure to address the reflection component. Strong submissions will show learning progression and genuine problem-solving approaches.

**Partial Credit Guidelines:** Award partial credit for incomplete technical implementation if documentation demonstrates understanding. Security group errors warrant significant deductions due to real-world implications.

title: PMP Risk Management and Stakeholder Engagement Scenario Analysis Quiz
description: Students will analyze a complex project scenario involving risk identification, assessment, response planning, and stakeholder management challenges. This assessment evaluates understanding of risk management processes, stakeholder analysis techniques, and integration of these knowledge areas in realistic project situations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply risk identification and qualitative risk analysis techniques to project scenarios
Develop appropriate risk response strategies and contingency plans
Conduct stakeholder analysis and create engagement strategies
Integrate risk management and stakeholder management processes effectively
rubric_criteria: Risk Identification and Analysis (25 points): Correctly identifies at least 8 project risks, categorizes them appropriately (technical, external, organizational, project management), and applies qualitative analysis techniques including probability and impact assessment with proper risk scoring

Risk Response Planning (25 points): Develops appropriate response strategies (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept) for identified risks, provides specific actionable responses, estimates resource requirements, and establishes clear triggers and ownership assignments

Stakeholder Analysis and Engagement (25 points): Creates comprehensive stakeholder register identifying all relevant parties, correctly plots stakeholders on power/interest grid, develops tailored engagement strategies, and addresses communication needs and frequency requirements

Integration and Professional Application (25 points): Demonstrates understanding of how risk and stakeholder management integrate with other knowledge areas, shows consideration of project constraints and organizational factors, uses proper PMP terminology, and provides realistic implementation timelines
instructions: You are the project manager for GreenTech Solutions' new smart building automation system implementation at a 40-story corporate headquarters. The 18-month, $2.8M project involves integrating IoT sensors, HVAC controls, lighting systems, and security features. The client has aggressive energy savings targets and a fixed go-live date coinciding with their lease renewal. Your team includes internal developers, three vendor partners, and client stakeholders from facilities, IT, security, and executive leadership. Recent challenges include: vendor delays on sensor delivery, client IT department resistance to cloud integration, budget concerns from finance, and new environmental regulations that may affect system specifications. Complete the following analysis: 1) Risk Register: Identify and analyze at least 8 specific project risks. For each risk, provide: category classification, probability (1-5 scale), impact (1-5 scale), risk score calculation, and brief description. 2) Risk Response Plan: Select 4 highest-priority risks and develop detailed response strategies. Include: response type (avoid/mitigate/transfer/accept), specific actions, resource requirements, timeline, responsible party, and trigger conditions. 3) Stakeholder Analysis: Create stakeholder register with at least 8 key stakeholders. Include: name/role, influence level (high/medium/low), interest level (high/medium/low), current attitude (supporter/neutral/resistor), and engagement approach. 4) Integration Summary: Explain how your risk and stakeholder management approaches support overall project success, including connections to scope, schedule, cost, and quality management. Format responses clearly with headers and bullet points. Show all calculations. Provide specific, actionable recommendations rather than generic statements.
grading_notes: Award full points only for comprehensive, specific responses that demonstrate practical PMP knowledge application. Common issues to watch for: generic risk descriptions without project context, inappropriate risk response strategies, incomplete stakeholder identification missing key parties like end users or regulatory bodies, and failure to show integration between knowledge areas. Partial credit guidelines: 20-25 points (comprehensive and accurate), 15-19 points (mostly complete with minor gaps), 10-14 points (adequate but lacks depth or contains errors), 5-9 points (incomplete or significant inaccuracies), 0-4 points (minimal effort or major misunderstanding). Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 35% C-level (70-79), 15% below 70%. Look for evidence of real-world thinking beyond textbook knowledge, such as considering organizational culture impacts or regulatory compliance requirements.

title: Enterprise Network Design and Troubleshooting Comprehensive Assessment
description: Students will design, configure, and troubleshoot a complex enterprise network infrastructure including OSPF routing, VLANs, inter-VLAN routing, access control lists, and network address translation. This assessment evaluates advanced Cisco networking concepts through practical implementation and systematic troubleshooting scenarios.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design and implement hierarchical network topologies using advanced routing protocols
Configure and optimize OSPF routing with multiple areas and route summarization
Implement VLAN segmentation and inter-VLAN routing using Layer 3 switches
Design and deploy comprehensive security policies using extended ACLs
Configure NAT/PAT for enterprise internet connectivity
Systematically diagnose and resolve complex network connectivity issues
Analyze network performance and implement optimization strategies
rubric_criteria: Network Design and OSPF Implementation (25 points): Correctly designs multi-area OSPF topology with proper area types, implements route summarization, configures authentication, and demonstrates understanding of LSA types and SPF algorithm

VLAN and Inter-VLAN Configuration (25 points): Creates logical network segmentation with appropriate VLAN design, configures trunk ports with proper encapsulation, implements SVI-based or router-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routing, and ensures proper VLAN database consistency

Security Implementation and NAT Configuration (25 points): Designs and implements extended ACLs with specific permit/deny rules, applies ACLs to appropriate interfaces and directions, configures dynamic NAT with overload (PAT), and ensures security policies align with business requirements

Troubleshooting and Network Optimization (25 points): Systematically identifies network issues using appropriate show and debug commands, provides detailed root cause analysis, implements effective solutions, and demonstrates advanced troubleshooting methodology
instructions: This comprehensive assessment consists of four integrated tasks that must be completed sequentially. You will work with a provided network topology diagram showing a multi-site enterprise network with headquarters and two branch offices. Begin by analyzing the requirements document detailing IP addressing schemes, routing policies, VLAN assignments, and security requirements. Task 1 requires you to configure OSPF routing across all sites with Area 0 as the backbone, Area 1 as a standard area for Branch A, and Area 2 as a totally stubby area for Branch B. Implement proper route summarization and MD5 authentication. Task 2 involves creating VLANs for different departments (Management, Sales, Engineering, Guest) with appropriate IP subnets, configuring trunk links between switches, and enabling inter-VLAN routing. Task 3 requires implementing security policies through extended ACLs that restrict inter-departmental access according to the provided security matrix, and configuring NAT/PAT for internet access with a pool of public IP addresses. Task 4 presents three network failure scenarios where you must diagnose issues using show commands, provide detailed analysis of problems found, and implement corrective actions. Document all configurations using proper CLI syntax, provide verification commands with expected outputs, and include network diagrams showing your final implementation. Submit your work as a detailed technical report with configuration files, troubleshooting logs, and verification screenshots. All configurations must be production-ready with appropriate descriptions and security considerations.
grading_notes: Evaluate students using the four equal-weight criteria, awarding partial credit for partially correct implementations. For OSPF configuration, verify proper area assignments, neighbor relationships, route advertisements, and authentication implementation. Check routing tables and OSPF database for accuracy. For VLAN assessment, confirm proper port assignments, trunk configuration, and successful inter-VLAN communication through ping tests. Security evaluation should verify ACL logic correctness, proper application to interfaces, and NAT functionality through translation table verification. Troubleshooting assessment requires systematic approach demonstration, accurate problem identification, and effective solution implementation. Deduct points for configuration syntax errors, incomplete documentation, missing verification steps, or security vulnerabilities. Expect grade distribution of 15% A-level (90-100), 25% B-level (80-89), 35% C-level (70-79), 20% D-level (60-69), and 5% below passing. Common issues include incorrect OSPF area types, VLAN mismatch problems, ACL ordering errors, and insufficient troubleshooting documentation.

title: Programming Language Comparison Discussion
description: Students will engage in structured discussions comparing two popular programming languages (Python vs Java), analyzing their strengths, weaknesses, and appropriate use cases while demonstrating understanding of fundamental programming concepts.
learning_objectives_assessed: Compare and contrast fundamental characteristics of different programming languages
Identify appropriate programming language choices for specific problem domains
Demonstrate understanding of basic programming concepts such as syntax, data types, and execution models
Communicate technical concepts clearly in written form
rubric_criteria: Technical Accuracy (25 points): Demonstrates correct understanding of language features, syntax differences, and technical concepts with minimal factual errors
Analysis and Comparison (25 points): Provides thoughtful analysis of strengths/weaknesses, includes specific examples, and makes meaningful comparisons between languages
Use Case Identification (25 points): Correctly identifies appropriate scenarios for each language use, justifies recommendations with logical reasoning
Communication and Engagement (25 points): Writes clearly and professionally, responds meaningfully to at least 2 peer posts, contributes constructively to discussion
instructions:
You will participate in a week-long discussion forum comparing Python and Java programming languages. Your participation consists of two parts:

**Initial Post (due by Wednesday, 11:59 PM):**
Create a 300-400 word post addressing the following:
1. Compare Python and Java syntax using a simple example (like declaring variables or writing a basic loop)
2. Identify two strengths and two weaknesses of each language
3. Recommend which language a beginner should learn first and justify your choice
4. Suggest one real-world application where each language would be the better choice

**Response Posts (due by Sunday, 11:59 PM):**
Respond to at least two classmates' posts with substantive comments (100-150 words each). Your responses should:
- Add new information or alternative perspectives
- Ask thoughtful questions that advance the discussion
- Respectfully challenge or support their recommendations with evidence
- Share relevant personal experiences if applicable

**Formatting Requirements:**
- Use proper grammar and spelling
- Include code examples in code blocks when discussing syntax
- Cite any external sources using simple web links
- Keep responses professional and constructive

**Submission:** Post directly to the discussion forum. No separate document submission required.
grading_notes: Grade initial posts first, focusing on technical accuracy and depth of analysis. Common issues include: oversimplified comparisons, incorrect technical information about compilation vs interpretation, and vague use case recommendations. For response posts, look for meaningful engagement rather than simple agreement. Expect most students to score 20-25 points per criterion. Deduct points for late submissions (5 points per day) and posts that don't meet minimum word requirements. Watch for copied content from online sources without attribution.

title: End-to-End Data Science Project Presentation
description: Students will present a complete data science project including problem formulation, data analysis, model development, and business recommendations. This presentation demonstrates their ability to communicate technical findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders through a structured 15-minute presentation followed by Q&A.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply the complete data science pipeline from problem definition to solution deployment
Communicate complex analytical findings effectively to diverse audiences
Demonstrate proficiency in data preprocessing, exploratory analysis, and predictive modeling
Evaluate model performance and provide actionable business recommendations
rubric_criteria: Problem Definition & Data Understanding (25 points): Clearly articulates business problem, demonstrates thorough understanding of dataset characteristics, identifies relevant variables and potential challenges, shows appropriate data quality assessment

Technical Analysis & Methodology (25 points): Implements appropriate preprocessing techniques, conducts meaningful exploratory data analysis, selects and justifies suitable modeling approaches, demonstrates proper model validation and performance evaluation

Results Interpretation & Business Impact (25 points): Accurately interprets model outputs and statistical significance, translates technical findings into business insights, provides specific actionable recommendations, addresses limitations and potential risks

Presentation Quality & Communication (25 points): Maintains clear logical flow and timing, uses effective visualizations and storytelling, adapts technical content for audience level, handles Q&A confidently and demonstrates deep project understanding
instructions: Select a real-world dataset from provided sources (Kaggle, UCI Repository, or instructor-approved alternative) containing at least 1,000 observations and 8+ variables. Your presentation must follow this structure: (1) Problem Statement & Business Context (3 minutes) - Define the business problem, explain dataset relevance, and state your analytical objectives. (2) Data Exploration & Preprocessing (4 minutes) - Present key dataset characteristics, data quality issues discovered, and preprocessing steps taken. Include 2-3 compelling visualizations that reveal important patterns. (3) Modeling Approach & Results (5 minutes) - Justify your chosen methodology, explain model development process, and present performance metrics with appropriate validation techniques. (4) Business Recommendations & Next Steps (3 minutes) - Translate findings into specific business actions, discuss implementation considerations, and acknowledge limitations. Submit your presentation slides (PDF format) and a technical appendix containing code, detailed results, and supplementary analysis 48 hours before your presentation date. Presentations will be recorded for assessment purposes. Come prepared to answer technical questions about your methodology, alternative approaches you considered, and deeper implications of your findings.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical rigor while emphasizing communication effectiveness. Look for evidence of iterative analysis rather than just final results. Deduct points for: overfitting without acknowledgment, inappropriate statistical methods, unsupported business claims, or poor time management. Award bonus consideration for: creative problem-solving, sophisticated feature engineering, thoughtful handling of ethical considerations, or exceptional visualization design. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 35% C-level (70-79), 15% below 70. During Q&A, assess depth of understanding by probing methodology choices and asking about alternative approaches. Students should demonstrate they can defend their decisions and acknowledge uncertainties.

title: Advanced Electromagnetic Induction Laboratory Report: Faraday's Law and Lenz's Law Investigation
description: Students conduct a comprehensive experimental investigation of electromagnetic induction phenomena, analyzing the relationship between changing magnetic flux and induced EMF while demonstrating understanding of Faraday's and Lenz's laws through quantitative measurements and theoretical calculations.
estimated_time: 6-8 hours (3 hours lab work, 3-5 hours analysis and report writing)
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply Faraday's law quantitatively to calculate induced EMF from changing magnetic flux
Demonstrate understanding of Lenz's law through experimental observation and theoretical prediction
Analyze experimental uncertainties and sources of error in electromagnetic measurements
Synthesize experimental data with theoretical models to draw valid scientific conclusions
rubric_criteria: Experimental Design and Data Collection (25 points): Systematic variation of parameters (coil turns, magnet speed, distance), proper use of oscilloscope/multimeter, complete data tables with appropriate precision, evidence of multiple trials for reliability

Mathematical Analysis and Calculations (25 points): Correct application of Faraday's law (EMF = -dΦ/dt), accurate calculation of magnetic flux changes, proper error propagation analysis, appropriate use of calculus for time-varying quantities

Scientific Reasoning and Interpretation (25 points): Clear explanation of Lenz's law observations, comparison between experimental and theoretical EMF values, discussion of factors affecting induced current direction, integration of multiple physics concepts

Professional Communication and Report Quality (25 points): Well-structured lab report with clear methodology, professional graphs with error bars and trend lines, appropriate use of scientific terminology, comprehensive conclusion linking results to electromagnetic theory
instructions: Conduct a multi-part investigation of electromagnetic induction using solenoid coils, permanent magnets, and digital measurement equipment. Your report must include: (1) Introduction explaining Faraday's and Lenz's laws with relevant equations, (2) Detailed experimental procedure for at least three different setups (varying coil parameters, magnet motion, and geometric arrangements), (3) Comprehensive data analysis section with calculations of theoretical vs. experimental EMF values, including uncertainty analysis, (4) Results section with properly formatted graphs showing EMF vs. time relationships and flux change rates, (5) Discussion addressing discrepancies between theory and experiment, sources of systematic and random errors, and real-world applications of electromagnetic induction, (6) Conclusion summarizing key findings and their significance. Use standard scientific report format with numbered equations, properly cited figures, and SI units throughout. Submit both electronic copy with embedded graphs and raw data spreadsheet. Minimum 2000 words excluding figures and references.
grading_notes: Expect expert-level students to demonstrate calculus-based understanding of electromagnetic concepts. Look for sophisticated error analysis including discussion of equipment limitations, environmental factors, and measurement precision. Grade distribution should reflect: 90-100 points for exceptional work showing deep conceptual understanding and minimal experimental errors; 80-89 points for solid work with minor calculation mistakes or incomplete analysis; 70-79 points for adequate work missing key theoretical connections; below 70 points for significant conceptual errors or inadequate experimental procedure. Common issues include: incorrect sign conventions in Lenz's law applications, failure to account for coil geometry in flux calculations, inadequate discussion of systematic errors, and poor integration of multiple experimental setups in conclusions.

title: Comprehensive Project Recovery and Risk Mitigation Examination
description: Students will analyze a complex, failing project scenario and develop a comprehensive recovery strategy, demonstrating mastery of advanced project management principles including risk assessment, stakeholder management, resource reallocation, and change management techniques.
learning_objectives_assessed: Evaluate and diagnose critical project failures using advanced analytical frameworks
Design and justify comprehensive project recovery strategies incorporating risk mitigation
Apply stakeholder management principles to address competing interests and resistance
Integrate change management methodologies with project control techniques
Synthesize multiple project management frameworks (Agile, Waterfall, PRINCE2) for optimal solutions
rubric_criteria: Problem Analysis & Root Cause Identification (25 points): Demonstrates systematic analysis using appropriate PM frameworks (fishbone, 5-whys, risk registers). Identifies multiple interconnected failure points including scope creep, resource constraints, communication breakdowns, and stakeholder misalignment. Shows deep understanding of project complexity.

Recovery Strategy Development (25 points): Presents comprehensive, realistic recovery plan with specific timelines, resource requirements, and success metrics. Strategy addresses all identified problems with appropriate PM methodologies. Includes contingency planning and alternative approaches with clear justification for chosen approach.

Stakeholder Management & Communication Plan (25 points): Develops detailed stakeholder analysis matrix identifying power/influence relationships. Creates targeted communication strategies for different stakeholder groups. Addresses resistance management and conflict resolution. Plans include frequency, methods, and key messages for each stakeholder group.

Implementation & Control Mechanisms (25 points): Designs robust project control systems including updated WBS, revised schedules, budget reallocations, and quality assurance measures. Establishes clear KPIs, monitoring processes, and decision gates. Demonstrates understanding of change control processes and governance structures.
instructions: You are presented with TechGlobal Corp's failed ERP implementation project, currently 18 months behind schedule and 200% over budget. The scenario includes detailed project background, stakeholder profiles, current status reports, and organizational constraints. Your examination consists of four sections: (1) Conduct a comprehensive failure analysis identifying root causes and contributing factors using at least three project management analytical tools. (2) Develop a detailed recovery strategy including revised project charter, scope definition, timeline, budget, and resource allocation. Justify your approach using established PM methodologies. (3) Create a stakeholder management and communication plan addressing resistance, competing interests, and alignment issues. Include specific strategies for executive sponsors, end-users, IT department, and external vendors. (4) Design implementation and control mechanisms including governance structure, progress monitoring systems, risk management processes, and success metrics. All responses must be supported with specific project management principles, tools, and best practices. Use charts, matrices, and diagrams where appropriate. Assume you have been appointed as the new Project Manager with full authority to restructure the project. Your solutions must be realistic given organizational constraints provided in the scenario.
grading_notes: Award full points only when students demonstrate synthesis-level thinking, connecting multiple PM concepts coherently. Look for evidence of practical application rather than theoretical regurgitation. Common weaknesses include: superficial root cause analysis missing systemic issues, unrealistic timelines in recovery plans, generic stakeholder strategies without customization, and weak control mechanisms. Exceptional responses will show innovation in problem-solving while maintaining PM best practices. Expect grade distribution: 10-15% A grades (90+), 25-30% B grades (80-89), 40-45% C grades (70-79), remainder below 70%. Partial credit available within each criterion based on depth of analysis and practical applicability.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Response: Multi-Stakeholder Analysis and Decision Framework
description: Students will analyze a complex organizational crisis scenario, develop a comprehensive leadership response strategy, and facilitate a structured discussion on stakeholder management, ethical decision-making, and change implementation while defending their approach against peer critiques.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate advanced strategic thinking and systems analysis in crisis leadership situations
Synthesize multiple leadership theories to develop comprehensive stakeholder engagement strategies
Evaluate ethical implications and trade-offs in high-stakes organizational decisions
Facilitate productive dialogue and navigate conflicting perspectives in leadership contexts
rubric_criteria: Strategic Analysis & Systems Thinking (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of interconnected organizational systems, identifies root causes beyond surface symptoms, anticipates second and third-order consequences of leadership decisions, and integrates multiple analytical frameworks

Stakeholder Engagement & Communication Strategy (25 points): Develops nuanced stakeholder mapping with power-interest analysis, creates tailored communication strategies for diverse audiences, demonstrates cultural competency and emotional intelligence, and addresses resistance management proactively

Ethical Framework & Decision Quality (25 points): Applies multiple ethical frameworks to evaluate decision alternatives, acknowledges moral complexity and competing values, demonstrates transparency in reasoning process, and balances short-term pressures with long-term organizational integrity

Discussion Facilitation & Leadership Presence (25 points): Maintains productive dialogue under pressure, synthesizes diverse viewpoints effectively, demonstrates active listening and adaptive communication, and exhibits executive presence while managing conflict constructively
instructions: You will receive a complex organizational crisis scenario 48 hours before the assessment. Prepare a 15-minute presentation of your leadership response strategy, followed by 60 minutes of facilitated peer discussion. Your presentation must include: (1) Situational analysis using at least two leadership frameworks, (2) Stakeholder impact assessment with specific engagement strategies for 5+ key groups, (3) Ethical decision matrix weighing competing values and trade-offs, (4) Implementation timeline with risk mitigation strategies, and (5) Success metrics and contingency planning. During the discussion phase, you will face challenging questions from peers representing different stakeholder perspectives. You must defend your decisions while remaining open to alternative viewpoints and adapting your approach based on new information presented. Prepare 3-5 provocative questions to drive discussion about leadership dilemmas in your scenario. Submit your presentation slides and a 2-page executive summary 24 hours before the session. Come prepared to think on your feet, as the instructor may introduce scenario complications during the discussion. Professional business attire required. Assessment focuses on depth of analysis, quality of reasoning, stakeholder sensitivity, ethical sophistication, and leadership presence under pressure.
grading_notes: Evaluate students on expert-level integration of leadership theory with practical application. Look for evidence of systems thinking beyond linear cause-effect relationships. Strong responses will demonstrate awareness of organizational politics, cultural dynamics, and unintended consequences. In stakeholder analysis, expect sophisticated understanding of competing interests and power dynamics. Ethical reasoning should go beyond simple frameworks to grapple with genuine moral complexity. During facilitation, observe ability to maintain composure under pressure, synthesize conflicting viewpoints, and demonstrate authentic leadership presence. Grade distribution should reflect expert-level expectations: 90-100 (exceptional strategic insight and executive presence), 80-89 (solid analysis with minor gaps), 70-79 (adequate but lacks sophistication), below 70 (insufficient for expert level). Watch for students who rely too heavily on theoretical knowledge without practical application, or conversely, those who lack theoretical grounding. Deduct points for failure to engage constructively with peer challenges or inability to adapt position when presented with compelling counter-arguments.

title: AWS Core Services Architecture Presentation
description: Students will create and deliver a 10-minute presentation explaining how three core AWS services work together to support a real-world application scenario, demonstrating their understanding of AWS fundamentals and service integration.
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify and explain the purpose of core AWS services (EC2, S3, RDS)
Describe how AWS services integrate to create basic cloud architectures
Articulate the benefits of cloud computing using AWS examples
Communicate technical concepts clearly to various audiences
rubric_criteria: Service Knowledge (25 points): Accurately explains the function, key features, and use cases of three core AWS services with correct terminology
Architecture Integration (25 points): Clearly demonstrates how the three services work together in a realistic scenario with logical connections and data flow
Real-World Application (25 points): Presents a relevant, practical use case that effectively showcases the business value and problem-solving capabilities of the AWS solution
Presentation Quality (25 points): Delivers clear, well-organized content within time limit using appropriate visual aids and demonstrates confidence in explaining technical concepts
instructions: Create a 10-minute presentation explaining how three core AWS services (choose from EC2, S3, RDS, Lambda, or VPC) work together to support a specific real-world application. Your presentation must include: (1) A brief explanation of each service's primary function and key benefits, (2) A realistic scenario or use case (e.g., e-commerce website, mobile app backend, data analytics platform), (3) An architecture diagram showing how the services connect and interact, (4) Specific examples of how data flows between services, and (5) At least three benefits this AWS solution provides over traditional on-premises infrastructure. Use 6-8 slides with clear visuals and minimal text. Include one diagram created using draw.io, Lucidchart, or similar tool. Practice your timing to stay within the 10-minute limit. Submit your slide deck as PDF 24 hours before presentation day. Be prepared to answer 2-3 questions about your scenario after presenting. Focus on clarity over complexity - your audience includes both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy using AWS documentation as reference. Look for logical service connections rather than complex architectures. Award full points for Service Knowledge if students correctly identify core functions even with minor terminology issues. Architecture Integration should show clear data flow - students often struggle with explaining how services actually communicate. Real-World Application should be practical and relatable, not overly ambitious. Common issues include: unrealistic scenarios, confusing EC2 with containers, unclear S3 integration, and poor time management. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90-100), 60% B-level (80-89), 20% C-level (70-79), 5% below 70. Provide immediate feedback on technical misconceptions during Q&A portion.

title: Project Risk Management Portfolio: End-to-End Risk Analysis and Response Planning
description: Students will demonstrate comprehensive project risk management competencies by developing a complete risk management plan for a realistic project scenario, including risk identification, qualitative and quantitative analysis, response strategies, and monitoring approaches aligned with PMI standards.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply systematic risk identification techniques using multiple methodologies (brainstorming, expert judgment, SWOT analysis, checklist analysis)
Conduct qualitative risk analysis using probability and impact matrices with proper risk categorization
Perform quantitative risk analysis including expected monetary value calculations and sensitivity analysis
Develop comprehensive risk response strategies (avoid, transfer, mitigate, accept) with specific action plans
Create risk monitoring and control procedures with defined triggers and escalation protocols
rubric_criteria: Risk Identification and Documentation (25 points): Identifies minimum 15 diverse risks across technical, organizational, external, and project management categories using at least 3 different identification techniques. Risk register includes complete risk statements with clear cause-effect relationships and proper PMI formatting.

Qualitative and Quantitative Analysis (25 points): Demonstrates accurate probability and impact assessments with justified ratings, creates properly structured P&I matrix, calculates EMV for top 5 risks with supporting data, and provides meaningful risk prioritization with clear ranking rationale.

Risk Response Planning (25 points): Develops specific, actionable response strategies for top 10 risks with assigned owners, realistic timelines, and budget considerations. Includes contingency plans for high-priority risks and demonstrates understanding of when to apply each response strategy type.

Risk Monitoring and Communication Plan (25 points): Creates comprehensive monitoring framework with defined KPIs, reporting templates, review schedules, and escalation procedures. Includes risk communication matrix identifying stakeholders, frequency, and communication methods with realistic implementation timeline.
instructions: Select a project scenario from the provided list (construction, IT implementation, product launch, or organizational change) or propose your own with instructor approval. Your portfolio must include: 1) Executive Summary (1 page) outlining project context and risk management approach, 2) Comprehensive Risk Register with minimum 15 identified risks using proper PMI format, 3) Risk Analysis section showing qualitative assessment matrix and quantitative analysis (EMV calculations) for top 5 risks, 4) Risk Response Plan detailing strategies for top 10 risks with specific actions, owners, and timelines, 5) Risk Monitoring and Control Plan including KPIs, reporting templates, and communication procedures. Use professional formatting with proper PMI terminology throughout. Submit as a single PDF document (15-20 pages) with appendices for templates and supporting calculations. Include a references section citing PMI standards and at least 3 additional scholarly sources. All monetary calculations must show work and assumptions. Risk register must be presented in both narrative and tabular formats. Portfolio should demonstrate real-world applicability and professional quality suitable for actual project implementation.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy of PMI methodologies and terminology usage. Look for realistic risk scenarios that demonstrate practical understanding rather than textbook examples. Common weaknesses include: vague risk statements, unrealistic probability/impact ratings, generic response strategies, and missing implementation details. Exceptional work (90-100) shows creative risk identification, sophisticated analysis techniques, and innovative monitoring approaches. Adequate work (70-79) meets minimum requirements but lacks depth or contains minor technical errors. Below 70 indicates fundamental misunderstanding of risk management processes. Deduct points for late submission (5% per day) and failure to follow formatting requirements. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level, 60% B-level, 20% C-level, 5% below C-level.

title: Advanced E-commerce Analytics Implementation and Optimization Lab Report
description: Students will implement Google Analytics 4 (GA4) enhanced e-commerce tracking for a simulated online store, analyze 6 months of provided data, identify conversion bottlenecks, and create actionable optimization recommendations with projected ROI calculations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Configure and implement advanced GA4 e-commerce tracking with custom events and parameters
Analyze complex customer journey data to identify conversion optimization opportunities
Create data-driven recommendations using advanced GA4 reporting and analysis techniques
Calculate and project ROI for proposed analytics-driven optimizations
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation (25 points): Correct GA4 property setup, enhanced e-commerce configuration, custom event tracking implementation, and proper parameter mapping. Must include screenshots of configuration and working tracking code.

Data Analysis Quality (25 points): Comprehensive analysis of user behavior, conversion funnels, attribution models, and audience segmentation. Must identify at least 3 specific bottlenecks with supporting data visualizations and statistical significance testing.

Strategic Recommendations (25 points): Actionable optimization strategies based on data findings, including A/B test proposals, UX improvements, and marketing channel adjustments. Each recommendation must include implementation timeline and success metrics.

ROI Calculations and Business Impact (25 points): Detailed financial projections for proposed optimizations, including cost estimates, revenue impact calculations, and risk assessment. Must demonstrate understanding of business metrics beyond basic analytics KPIs.
instructions: Using the provided e-commerce dataset and test environment, implement GA4 enhanced e-commerce tracking for 'TechGear Online Store.' Your submission must include: 1) Technical documentation showing complete GA4 setup including custom events for 'add_to_wishlist,' 'begin_checkout,' and 'purchase' with proper e-commerce parameters, 2) Data analysis report examining user acquisition channels, product performance, checkout abandonment patterns, and customer lifetime value segments using GA4's built-in and custom reports, 3) Three optimization recommendations addressing identified conversion bottlenecks, each with A/B testing methodology and 90-day implementation roadmap, 4) Financial impact assessment calculating potential revenue increase, implementation costs, and 12-month ROI projections. Submit as a comprehensive lab report (15-20 pages) with executive summary, methodology, findings, recommendations, and appendices containing screenshots, code snippets, and raw data exports. Include a 10-minute video walkthrough demonstrating your GA4 implementation and explaining key findings. All analysis must use proper statistical methods and acknowledge data limitations. Reference at least 5 current industry sources on e-commerce analytics best practices.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy by testing provided GA4 configuration against requirements checklist. Look for proper use of measurement protocol, correct parameter naming conventions, and valid tracking implementation. In analysis section, assess data interpretation skills, chart selection appropriateness, and statistical rigor. Common issues include: incorrect event parameter mapping, superficial funnel analysis without cohort consideration, unrealistic ROI projections, and recommendations lacking specificity. Expect grade distribution: 20% A-level (90-100), 40% B-level (80-89), 30% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. Deduct points for missing statistical significance testing, generic recommendations not tied to specific data insights, or technical implementations that don't properly track e-commerce events. Award bonus consideration for creative use of GA4's machine learning insights or integration with other Google Marketing Platform tools.

title: Comprehensive Data Science Pipeline Analysis and Implementation
description: Students will demonstrate their understanding of the complete data science workflow by analyzing a real-world dataset, implementing appropriate statistical methods, creating predictive models, and presenting actionable insights through both technical documentation and business-oriented recommendations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply data preprocessing techniques including cleaning, transformation, and feature engineering
Implement and compare multiple machine learning algorithms for prediction tasks
Conduct proper statistical analysis and hypothesis testing
Create effective data visualizations to communicate findings
Translate technical results into business-actionable recommendations
rubric_criteria: Data Preprocessing and Exploration (25 points): Thorough data cleaning, handling of missing values, outlier detection, appropriate feature engineering, comprehensive exploratory data analysis with meaningful insights

Statistical Analysis and Modeling (25 points): Correct implementation of at least two different ML algorithms, proper train-test split, appropriate evaluation metrics, model comparison with justified selection, validation of assumptions

Visualization and Communication (25 points): Clear, professional visualizations that support findings, proper labeling and formatting, effective use of different chart types, visualizations directly support narrative

Business Insights and Code Quality (25 points): Actionable recommendations based on analysis, clear understanding of business implications, well-documented code with comments, reproducible workflow, professional presentation
instructions: You will receive a dataset containing customer transaction data from an e-commerce platform. Your task is to complete a full data science pipeline analysis. Submit a Jupyter notebook containing: 1) Data preprocessing section with cleaning steps, missing value treatment, and feature engineering documented with markdown explanations. 2) Exploratory data analysis with at least 5 different visualizations showing key patterns and relationships. 3) Implementation of two different machine learning models (one tree-based, one linear) to predict customer lifetime value, including proper cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning. 4) Statistical analysis section testing at least two business hypotheses using appropriate statistical tests. 5) Results section with model comparison, performance metrics (RMSE, MAE, R²), and feature importance analysis. 6) Business recommendations section (500 words) translating technical findings into actionable strategies for marketing, customer retention, and revenue optimization. Format requirements: Use clear section headers, include all code with explanations, ensure all plots have proper titles and axis labels, cite any external resources used. Submit both .ipynb file and exported PDF. Code must be executable and reproduce all results. Include brief methodology justification for each analytical choice made.
grading_notes: Grade holistically while ensuring each rubric criterion is met. Common issues to watch: insufficient data exploration leading to poor model performance, using inappropriate algorithms for the problem type, visualizations without clear purpose or poor formatting, technical analysis without business context, and non-reproducible code. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 35% C-level (70-79), 15% below C-level. Deduct points for: missing statistical assumptions validation (-5), inadequate model comparison (-5), poor code documentation (-5), unrealistic business recommendations (-5). Award bonus points for: innovative feature engineering (+3), advanced visualization techniques (+3), additional relevant analysis beyond requirements (+4).

title: Mathematical Proof Techniques and Problem-Solving Strategies Forum Discussion
description: Students will engage in advanced mathematical discourse by presenting original proofs, analyzing complex problem-solving approaches, and critically evaluating peer solutions across multiple mathematical domains including real analysis, abstract algebra, and discrete mathematics.
learning_objectives_assessed: Construct rigorous mathematical proofs using various proof techniques (direct, contradiction, induction, contrapositive)
Analyze and critique mathematical arguments for logical validity and completeness
Communicate complex mathematical concepts clearly using proper mathematical notation and terminology
Apply advanced problem-solving strategies to novel mathematical problems
Synthesize connections between different areas of mathematics
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Rigor and Proof Quality (25 points): Original proof demonstrates correct logic, complete reasoning, proper mathematical notation, and addresses all necessary cases with clear justification for each step

Critical Analysis and Peer Engagement (25 points): Provides substantive, constructive feedback on peer solutions, identifies mathematical errors or gaps, suggests improvements, and engages meaningfully with at least 3 peer posts using mathematical evidence

Problem-Solving Approach and Strategy (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated problem-solving techniques, explains reasoning behind chosen methods, considers alternative approaches, and shows deep understanding of underlying mathematical concepts

Mathematical Communication and Presentation (25 points): Uses precise mathematical language, proper notation and formatting, clear logical structure, and effectively explains complex ideas in an accessible manner while maintaining mathematical accuracy
instructions: This week-long discussion forum requires you to complete three main components: (1) Initial Post: Select one of the provided advanced problems from real analysis, abstract algebra, or number theory. Present a complete, rigorous proof or solution using proper mathematical notation. Your post should include your reasoning process, alternative approaches considered, and connections to broader mathematical concepts. Minimum 400 words with proper LaTeX formatting for mathematical expressions. (2) Peer Analysis: Respond to at least three classmates' solutions with detailed mathematical critique. Verify their logic, check for completeness, identify any errors or gaps, and suggest improvements or alternative approaches. Each response should be 200-300 words and demonstrate deep engagement with their mathematical reasoning. (3) Reflection Post: After receiving feedback, post a reflection discussing what you learned from peer critiques, how you might revise your approach, and insights gained about proof techniques. Include one new problem you've formulated related to your original solution. Submit all components by Friday 11:59 PM, with peer responses due by Sunday 11:59 PM.
