Use the discussion board's equation editor or LaTeX formatting for all mathematical notation. Cite any external sources using proper mathematical bibliography format.
grading_notes: Evaluate proofs for mathematical correctness first, then assess presentation quality. Common issues include: incomplete justifications, logical gaps, improper notation, and failure to consider edge cases. Expect 15-20% of students to struggle with proof rigor - provide specific feedback on logical structure. Grade peer responses based on mathematical insight, not just participation - look for evidence students actually worked through the mathematics. Strong responses (A-level) should show original thinking and deep mathematical understanding. Average responses (B-level) demonstrate competency but may lack sophistication. Below-average responses (C-level or lower) show fundamental misunderstandings or insufficient mathematical reasoning. Allocate partial credit generously for good mathematical intuition even with minor technical errors.

title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics Research Presentation: Contemporary Applications and Theoretical Implications
description: Students will deliver a comprehensive 20-minute presentation on a cutting-edge topic in quantum mechanics, demonstrating mastery of advanced theoretical concepts, mathematical formulations, and their applications in modern technology or research. The presentation must include original analysis, mathematical derivations, and critical evaluation of current research literature.
estimated_time: 3-4 weeks preparation + 20 minutes presentation + 10 minutes Q&A
learning_objectives_assessed: Synthesize advanced quantum mechanical principles with contemporary research applications
Demonstrate proficiency in mathematical formulations of quantum systems and phenomena
Critically analyze and evaluate current scientific literature in quantum physics
Communicate complex theoretical concepts effectively to expert audiences
Apply quantum mechanical models to predict and explain experimental observations
rubric_criteria: Theoretical Mastery & Mathematical Rigor (25 points): Demonstrates deep understanding of quantum mechanical principles, includes accurate mathematical derivations, properly applies formalism (operators, wavefunctions, eigenvalue equations), and shows mastery of advanced concepts like entanglement, decoherence, or many-body systems

Research Quality & Literature Integration (25 points): Incorporates at least 8 peer-reviewed sources from last 5 years, critically evaluates conflicting theories or experimental results, identifies knowledge gaps or controversies, and demonstrates original synthesis of multiple research perspectives

Technical Communication & Visual Design (25 points): Uses appropriate scientific terminology, creates clear and informative figures/diagrams, presents mathematical content accessibly, maintains logical flow from fundamentals to applications, and designs professional-quality slides with proper citations

Depth of Analysis & Critical Thinking (25 points): Provides original insights beyond literature summary, discusses limitations of current models, proposes future research directions, connects theory to experimental observations, and demonstrates ability to answer complex follow-up questions during Q&A session
instructions: Select a contemporary quantum mechanics topic such as quantum computing algorithms, topological quantum states, quantum error correction, many-body localization, or quantum field theory applications. Your presentation must include: (1) Introduction establishing theoretical foundation with key mathematical relationships, (2) Literature review of at least 8 recent peer-reviewed sources, critically comparing different approaches or findings, (3) Detailed mathematical analysis including derivations relevant to your topic (minimum 3 equations with full explanations), (4) Discussion of experimental validation or technological applications, (5) Critical evaluation identifying current limitations and future research directions. Format requirements: 18-22 slides, 20-minute presentation plus 10-minute Q&A, professional scientific presentation style with proper citations. Submit your slide deck and a 2-page bibliography with source summaries 24 hours before presentation. Be prepared to derive key equations on the board and answer technical questions about mathematical details, experimental implications, and connections to other areas of physics. Your audience consists of advanced physics students and faculty, so maintain appropriate technical depth throughout.
grading_notes: Evaluate mathematical accuracy carefully - deduct significantly for incorrect formalism or conceptual errors. Look for evidence of genuine understanding rather than memorization by observing student responses during Q&A. Expect expert-level presentations to go beyond textbook material and demonstrate engagement with current research. Common weaknesses include insufficient mathematical detail, superficial literature review, or inability to explain concepts when questioned. Grade distribution should reflect expert-level expectations: 90-100 points for exceptional presentations showing original insights, 80-89 for solid presentations meeting all requirements, 70-79 for presentations with significant gaps in understanding or preparation, below 70 for presentations failing to meet expert-level standards.

title: Personal Website Portfolio - HTML, CSS, and JavaScript Fundamentals
description: Students will create a complete personal portfolio website demonstrating fundamental web development skills including HTML structure, CSS styling, responsive design, and basic JavaScript interactivity. learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate proficiency in HTML5 semantic markup and document structure
Apply CSS styling principles including layout, typography, and responsive design
Implement basic JavaScript for user interaction and DOM manipulation
Create well-organized, maintainable code with proper commenting and file structure
Design user-friendly interfaces following basic UX principles
rubric_criteria: HTML Structure and Semantics (25 points): Proper use of HTML5 semantic elements, valid markup, logical document structure, appropriate use of headings, lists, forms, and links
CSS Styling and Responsive Design (25 points): Effective visual design, proper CSS organization, mobile-responsive layout using flexbox or grid, consistent styling, and cross-browser compatibility
JavaScript Functionality (25 points): Working interactive elements, proper event handling, clean code structure, error-free execution, and meaningful user interactions
Code Quality and Organization (25 points): Clean, well-commented code, logical file organization, proper naming conventions, version control usage, and professional presentation
instructions:

- Include a navigation menu that works across all pages

Your portfolio should reflect your personality while maintaining a professional appearance suitable for showing potential employers or collaborators.
grading_notes: Evaluate based on both technical execution and creative implementation. Look for students who go beyond minimum requirements while maintaining code quality. title: Customer Segmentation Analysis Lab Report
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive data analysis project using Python/R to segment customers based on purchasing behavior, create visualizations, and provide business recommendations. This lab report assesses practical data analysis skills including data cleaning, exploratory analysis, statistical modeling, and professional reporting.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply data cleaning and preprocessing techniques to real-world datasets
Perform exploratory data analysis using statistical methods and visualizations
Implement clustering algorithms for customer segmentation
Interpret statistical results and translate findings into business insights
Create professional data analysis reports with clear visualizations
rubric_criteria: Data Preprocessing & Cleaning (25 points): Handles missing values appropriately, identifies and addresses outliers, performs necessary data transformations, documents all preprocessing decisions with clear justification

Exploratory Data Analysis (25 points): Creates meaningful descriptive statistics, generates appropriate visualizations (histograms, scatter plots, correlation matrices), identifies key patterns and relationships in data, uses proper statistical measures

Clustering Analysis & Implementation (25 points): Correctly implements K-means or hierarchical clustering, determines optimal number of clusters using appropriate methods (elbow method, silhouette analysis), validates clustering results, interprets cluster characteristics accurately

Business Insights & Report Quality (25 points): Provides actionable business recommendations based on findings, writes clear executive summary, maintains professional formatting, includes well-labeled figures and tables, demonstrates critical thinking in conclusions
instructions:

**Dataset**: Contains 5,000 customer records with variables including: CustomerID, Age, Gender, Annual Income, Spending Score, Purchase History, and Product Categories.

**Technical Requirements**: Use Python (pandas, scikit-learn, matplotlib/seaborn) or R (dplyr, cluster, ggplot2). Submit both code file (.py or .R) and compiled report (PDF).

**Analysis Steps**:
1. **Data Exploration**: Load dataset, examine structure, identify data quality issues
2. **Data Cleaning**: Handle missing values, remove duplicates, address outliers with documented rationale
3. **Exploratory Analysis**: Generate summary statistics, create 5-7 meaningful visualizations, analyze correlations
4. **Customer Segmentation**: Apply clustering algorithm, determine optimal clusters (k=3-6), profile each segment
5. **Business Recommendations**: Develop 3-5 specific marketing strategies based on segments

**Report Structure** (6-8 pages):
- Executive Summary (1 page)
- Data Overview & Cleaning (1-2 pages)
- Exploratory Analysis with Visualizations (2-3 pages)
- Clustering Results & Segment Profiles (2 pages)
- Business Recommendations & Conclusions (1 page)
- Code Appendix

**Submission**: Upload PDF report and code file to LMS by [due date] 11:59 PM. Late submissions lose 10% per day.
grading_notes: Grade distribution should target: 15% A's, 35% B's, 35% C's, 15% D/F. Common issues to deduct points: inadequate documentation of preprocessing decisions (-5 pts), generic visualizations without insights (-3-5 pts), incorrect clustering validation (-8-10 pts), vague business recommendations (-5-8 pts). Partial credit available for each criterion - students showing good process but minor errors should receive 70-80% of points. title: Complex Project Recovery and Risk Management Simulation
description: Students analyze a failing multi-phase software development project, diagnose root causes, develop a comprehensive recovery plan, and create advanced risk mitigation strategies. learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced project recovery methodologies to diagnose and resolve complex project failures
Develop comprehensive risk management frameworks for high-stakes projects
Design stakeholder communication strategies for crisis situations
Evaluate resource reallocation and schedule compression techniques
Integrate change management principles with project recovery processes
rubric_criteria: Problem Diagnosis & Root Cause Analysis (25 points): Demonstrates systematic analysis using appropriate PM frameworks (fishbone, 5-whys, failure mode analysis), identifies multiple contributing factors, distinguishes symptoms from causes, provides evidence-based conclusions

Recovery Strategy & Implementation Plan (25 points): Develops realistic, phased recovery approach with clear milestones, addresses scope/schedule/budget constraints, incorporates lessons learned, includes contingency planning and success metrics

Risk Management Framework (25 points): Creates comprehensive risk register with probability/impact analysis, develops proactive mitigation strategies, establishes monitoring triggers, demonstrates understanding of risk response strategies (avoid, transfer, mitigate, accept)

Stakeholder Management & Communication Plan (25 points): Identifies all key stakeholders with influence/interest matrix, develops tailored communication strategies, addresses conflict resolution, includes escalation procedures and feedback mechanisms
instructions: You are the newly appointed project manager for TechFlow Solutions' critical ERP implementation project. Your analysis package must include: (1) Executive Summary (1 page) presenting key findings and recommended actions, (2) Root Cause Analysis (2-3 pages) using minimum two PM diagnostic tools with supporting evidence, (3) Recovery Plan (3-4 pages) detailing phases, resources, timeline, and success metrics, (4) Risk Management Framework (2-3 pages) including risk register with 15+ identified risks and mitigation strategies, (5) Stakeholder Communication Matrix (1 page) showing communication frequency, methods, and key messages for each stakeholder group. Use professional formatting with charts, graphs, and tables where appropriate. Support recommendations with project management best practices and cite relevant frameworks (PMI, PRINCE2, Agile). Submit as single PDF with appendices for supporting calculations and templates. Total document should be 10-12 pages excluding appendices.
grading_notes: Look for evidence of systematic thinking rather than intuitive responses. Strong submissions will reference multiple PM methodologies and demonstrate integration of theoretical knowledge with practical application. Watch for unrealistic timelines or budgets in recovery plans - deduct points for solutions that don't acknowledge constraints. Award full points for comprehensive stakeholder analysis that goes beyond obvious stakeholders to include influencers and affected parties. Common issues: oversimplified root cause analysis, generic risk responses not tailored to specific scenario, communication plans lacking detail on message content and timing. Grade distribution expectation: 20% A-level (90-100), 40% B-level (80-89), 30% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. Provide specific feedback on practical feasibility of recommendations and suggest industry resources for improvement.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Simulation: Leading Through Complex Organizational Change
description: Students will lead a simulated organization through a multi-faceted crisis scenario, developing and implementing a comprehensive leadership strategy while managing stakeholder relationships, team dynamics, and strategic decision-making under pressure. This capstone assessment evaluates advanced leadership competencies in real-world contexts.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate advanced strategic thinking and decision-making under uncertainty and time pressure
Apply transformational leadership principles to guide organizational change and crisis management
Effectively manage diverse stakeholder relationships and navigate competing organizational interests
Design and implement sustainable leadership strategies that balance short-term crisis response with long-term organizational vision
rubric_criteria: Strategic Decision-Making & Problem-Solving (25 points): Quality of crisis analysis, strategic options evaluation, decision rationale, risk assessment, and adaptive leadership responses to evolving scenarios

Stakeholder Management & Communication (25 points): Effectiveness of stakeholder mapping, communication strategies, conflict resolution approaches, coalition building, and maintaining trust during crisis
Team Leadership & Change Management (25 points): Ability to motivate and guide team members, manage resistance to change, delegate effectively, develop others, and maintain team cohesion under stress

Implementation & Results (25 points): Feasibility and innovation of proposed solutions, measurement systems, timeline management, resource allocation, and demonstration of sustainable organizational outcomes
instructions: You are the newly appointed CEO of MidTech Solutions, a 500-employee technology consulting firm facing simultaneous crises: a major client lawsuit, 30% revenue decline, key talent departure, and regulatory compliance issues. Using the provided organizational data, stakeholder profiles, and financial reports, you must: (1) Conduct comprehensive situational analysis and develop a 90-day crisis response plan, (2) Create stakeholder communication strategy with specific messaging for employees, clients, investors, and media, (3) Design team restructuring plan including retention strategies for critical personnel, (4) Develop long-term organizational transformation roadmap addressing culture, operations, and market positioning. Deliverables include: executive summary (2 pages), detailed strategic plan (15-20 pages), stakeholder communication templates, implementation timeline with milestones, and 20-minute recorded presentation to the board of directors. Throughout the project, you'll receive weekly scenario updates requiring adaptive leadership responses. All decisions must be justified with leadership theory application and supported by data analysis. Submit all components via learning management system by specified deadline, with interim check-ins scheduled at weeks 2 and 4.
grading_notes: Evaluate depth of strategic thinking over superficial solutions - look for evidence of systems thinking and consideration of unintended consequences. Strong submissions will demonstrate integration of multiple leadership theories rather than relying on single approaches. Pay attention to realistic resource constraints and timeline feasibility. Communication deliverables should show audience awareness and persuasive clarity. Deduct points for generic solutions that don't address specific organizational context. Exceptional work (90-100) shows innovative approaches and sophisticated understanding of leadership complexity. Proficient work (80-89) demonstrates solid competency with minor gaps. Developing work (70-79) shows basic understanding but lacks depth or has significant implementation issues. Inadequate work (below 70) fails to meet professional standards or shows fundamental misunderstanding of leadership principles.

title: AWS Cloud Foundations Practical Exam
description: A comprehensive hands-on examination testing fundamental AWS cloud concepts through practical implementation tasks including EC2 instance deployment, S3 bucket configuration, IAM user management, and basic security implementation. Students will demonstrate their understanding of core AWS services and best practices.
learning_objectives_assessed: Deploy and configure EC2 instances with appropriate security groups
Create and manage S3 buckets with proper access controls and versioning
Implement IAM users, groups, and policies following least privilege principles
Apply fundamental AWS security best practices across multiple services
rubric_criteria: EC2 Implementation (25 points): Successfully launches EC2 instance with correct AMI, instance type, security group configuration allowing SSH/HTTP access, proper key pair assignment, and appropriate tags

S3 Configuration (25 points): Creates S3 bucket with versioning enabled, uploads sample files, configures appropriate bucket policies, demonstrates understanding of storage classes and lifecycle management
IAM Management (25 points): Creates IAM user with programmatic access, assigns user to appropriate group, implements least privilege policy, demonstrates MFA setup and access key management

Security Best Practices (25 points): Implements security group rules following principle of least privilege, uses appropriate encryption settings, demonstrates understanding of AWS security shared responsibility model, documents security considerations
instructions:
This practical exam requires you to complete four AWS implementation tasks within the AWS Free Tier. You must document each step with screenshots and brief explanations in a single PDF document.

Task 1 - EC2 Deployment: Launch a t2.micro EC2 instance running Amazon Linux 2. Configure a security group allowing SSH (port 22) from your IP and HTTP (port 80) from anywhere. Create and download a key pair. Tag your instance with 'Environment: Test' and 'Owner: [YourName]'.

Task 2 - S3 Configuration: Create an S3 bucket with a globally unique name. Enable versioning and upload three different file types (text, image, document). Create a folder structure and demonstrate file organization. Configure a basic bucket policy restricting public access.

Task 3 - IAM Setup: Create an IAM user named 'test-user' with programmatic access. Create a group called 'S3-ReadOnly' and attach the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess policy. Add your user to this group. Generate and securely store access keys.

Task 4 - Security Implementation: Review and document the security configurations from tasks 1-3. Identify potential security improvements and explain the AWS shared responsibility model as it applies to your implementations.

Submission Requirements: Submit a single PDF containing screenshots of each completed task, AWS console confirmation pages, brief explanations of your configuration choices, and responses to security questions. Ensure all screenshots clearly show your AWS account identifier and timestamps. Name your file: 'AWS_Exam_[LastName]_[FirstName].pdf'
grading_notes: Grade based on technical accuracy and completion rather than perfection. Deduct 5 points per criterion for missing screenshots or documentation. Award partial credit for partially completed tasks - 60% for attempting but not fully completing requirements. Watch for common issues: incorrect security group configurations, missing tags, overly permissive IAM policies, and failure to use Free Tier eligible resources. Expect grade distribution: 85-100 (A), 70-84 (B), 55-69 (C), below 55 (F). Students should demonstrate understanding of concepts even if minor configuration errors occur. Provide feedback on security improvements and cost optimization opportunities.

title: Risk Management Strategy Discussion: Analyzing Critical Project Scenarios
description: Students will analyze complex project risk scenarios, propose comprehensive risk management strategies, and engage in peer discussion to evaluate different approaches using PMP risk management principles and methodologies.
estimated_time: 3-4 hours (2 hours initial analysis and response, 1-2 hours peer interaction)
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply risk identification, analysis, and response planning techniques to complex project scenarios
Evaluate and critique risk management strategies using PMP methodology and best practices
Demonstrate understanding of risk monitoring and control processes throughout project lifecycle
rubric_criteria: Risk Identification and Analysis (25 points): Thoroughly identifies potential risks using appropriate techniques (SWOT, brainstorming, expert judgment), categorizes risks by type and impact, demonstrates clear understanding of qualitative and quantitative risk analysis methods

Risk Response Strategy Development (25 points): Develops comprehensive risk response plans using appropriate strategies (avoid, transfer, mitigate, accept), provides specific actionable steps, considers resource implications and timeline impacts, aligns responses with project objectives

Critical Thinking and Application (25 points): Demonstrates deep understanding of PMP risk management processes, provides well-reasoned justifications for decisions, connects theoretical knowledge to practical application, shows awareness of interconnected project impacts

Peer Engagement and Professional Communication (25 points): Provides thoughtful, constructive feedback on peer responses, asks relevant follow-up questions, contributes meaningfully to discussion threads, maintains professional tone and demonstrates collaborative problem-solving approach
instructions: You will be presented with a detailed project scenario containing multiple risk factors. Your task is to conduct a comprehensive risk management analysis and engage in meaningful discussion with peers. INITIAL RESPONSE (750-1000 words): Begin by thoroughly reading the provided scenario. Identify at least 6-8 significant risks across different categories (technical, organizational, external, project management). For each identified risk, provide: risk description and potential triggers, probability and impact assessment (use High/Medium/Low scale with justification), risk category and ownership assignment, and detailed response strategy with specific actions and timelines. Conclude with your overall risk monitoring and control approach for this project. PEER ENGAGEMENT: Respond substantively to at least 3 peer posts (200-300 words each). Focus on: comparing your risk identification with theirs, evaluating the feasibility and effectiveness of their proposed strategies, offering alternative approaches or additional considerations, and asking thoughtful questions that promote deeper analysis. FORMATTING REQUIREMENTS: Use clear headings and bullet points for organization, reference specific PMP processes and knowledge areas where applicable, cite relevant tools and techniques from PMBOK Guide, and maintain professional project management terminology. Submit your initial response by the midweek deadline, complete peer responses by the final deadline, and ensure all posts demonstrate original thinking and analysis.
grading_notes: Evaluate initial responses for depth of risk analysis rather than just quantity of risks identified. Look for evidence of structured risk management thinking and appropriate use of PMP terminology. Strong responses will demonstrate understanding of risk interdependencies and secondary risks. For peer engagement, assess quality over quantity - meaningful critique and alternative suggestions should score higher than simple agreement. Watch for students who may identify obvious risks but miss subtle organizational or stakeholder-related risks. Excellent work (90-100 points) will show sophisticated understanding of risk management integration with other project processes. Average work (70-79 points) typically shows basic risk identification but lacks depth in response strategies or peer engagement. Expect most students to score in the 75-85 range with proper effort and preparation.

title: Advanced Google Analytics Implementation Strategy Presentation

learning_objectives_assessed: Design comprehensive GA4 measurement strategies for complex business scenarios with multiple touchpoints and conversion paths
Configure advanced tracking implementations including custom events, enhanced ecommerce, and cross-domain tracking
Develop sophisticated reporting frameworks using custom dimensions, metrics, and audience segmentation
Create data-driven attribution models and ROI measurement systems for multi-channel marketing campaigns
Communicate technical GA4 concepts effectively to stakeholder audiences with varying technical expertise
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation Design (25 points): Demonstrates mastery of GA4 setup including property configuration, enhanced ecommerce tracking, custom event architecture, audience definitions, and cross-platform measurement. Advanced Analytics Strategy (25 points): Presents sophisticated measurement framework with custom dimensions/metrics, conversion path analysis, attribution modeling, and advanced segmentation. Business Intelligence & ROI Framework (25 points): Develops comprehensive reporting strategy with automated dashboards, custom reports, and KPI tracking aligned to business objectives. Presentation Quality & Stakeholder Communication (25 points): Delivers clear, professional presentation with appropriate technical depth for audience. instructions: You are a digital analytics consultant tasked with proposing a comprehensive Google Analytics 4 implementation for TechFlow Solutions, a B2B SaaS company with a mobile app, web platform, customer portal, and offline sales team. Create a 20-minute presentation covering: (1) Complete GA4 property setup including enhanced ecommerce configuration, custom event tracking for SaaS metrics (trial signups, feature usage, subscription upgrades), and cross-domain tracking between their main site and customer portal; (2) Advanced measurement strategy incorporating customer lifetime value tracking, multi-touch attribution modeling, and predictive audience creation for churn prevention; (3) Custom reporting framework with automated dashboards for different stakeholder groups (marketing, product, sales, executives), including funnel analysis for the trial-to-paid conversion process and cohort analysis for subscription retention; (4) Data integration strategy connecting GA4 with their CRM, marketing automation platform, and customer success tools. grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy of GA4 configurations - look for proper event parameter naming conventions, appropriate use of custom dimensions vs metrics, and realistic implementation approaches. Award full points for implementations that demonstrate understanding of GA4's event-based model vs Universal Analytics' session-based model. Strong responses will show understanding of GA4 limitations and propose supplementary tools where necessary. Common issues: unrealistic implementation timelines, over-reliance on deprecated Universal Analytics concepts, insufficient consideration of data sampling at scale, and failure to address cross-device measurement challenges. title: Introduction to Python Programming Lab Report
description: Students will complete a series of basic Python programming exercises and document their problem-solving process, code implementation, and testing results in a comprehensive lab report format.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate understanding of basic Python syntax including variables, data types, and operators
Implement simple control structures (if-else statements and loops) to solve programming problems
Apply problem-solving methodology to break down programming tasks into logical steps
Document code effectively with comments and explain programming logic in written form
rubric_criteria: Code Implementation (25 points): All four programming exercises are completed with correct syntax, proper variable usage, and functional logic that produces expected outputs
Problem-Solving Process (25 points): Clear documentation of approach for each problem including pseudocode or flowcharts, identification of required inputs/outputs, and logical step-by-step breakdown
Code Documentation and Comments (25 points): All code includes meaningful comments explaining logic, variables are named descriptively, and code structure is clean and readable

Testing and Analysis (25 points): Each program is tested with multiple input cases, results are documented with screenshots or output examples, and any errors or limitations are identified and discussed
instructions:
Complete the following four Python programming exercises and document your work in a lab report format. For each exercise: (1) Read the problem statement carefully, (2) Write pseudocode or draw a simple flowchart showing your approach, (3) Implement the solution in Python with appropriate comments, (4) Test your program with at least 3 different input cases, (5) Take screenshots of your code and output. 

Exercises: 1) Create a program that calculates the area and perimeter of a rectangle given length and width inputs. 2) Write a program that determines if a number entered by the user is even or odd. 3) Develop a program that calculates the sum of all numbers from 1 to N (where N is user input). 4) Create a simple grade calculator that converts numerical scores (0-100) to letter grades (A, B, C, D, F). 

Your lab report should include: an introduction explaining the purpose of each exercise, your problem-solving approach for each task, complete Python code with comments, test results with screenshots, and a conclusion reflecting on challenges encountered and lessons learned. Format your report with clear headings, proper grammar, and professional presentation. Submit as a PDF file including all code and screenshots.
grading_notes: Evaluate code functionality first - programs should run without syntax errors and produce correct outputs. Look for evidence of logical thinking in problem-solving sections; students should show clear understanding of the problem before jumping to code. Comments should explain 'why' not just 'what' the code does. Partial credit available for each exercise (6-7 points each). Common issues include: missing input validation, unclear variable names, insufficient testing cases, and poorly formatted reports. Expect 70% of students to score 75-85 points, with full points reserved for exceptional documentation and thorough testing.

title: Customer Churn Prediction Analysis Quiz
description: Students will analyze a customer churn dataset using Python/R, implement and compare multiple machine learning algorithms, and provide business insights. This assessment evaluates practical data science skills including data preprocessing, model selection, evaluation, and interpretation.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply appropriate data preprocessing techniques including handling missing values, feature scaling, and categorical encoding
Implement and compare multiple supervised learning algorithms (logistic regression, decision trees, random forest)
Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics and interpret results in business context
Communicate findings effectively through data visualization and written analysis
rubric_criteria: Data Preprocessing and EDA (25 points): Correctly handles missing values, identifies outliers, performs appropriate feature engineering, creates meaningful visualizations to understand data patterns

Model Implementation (25 points): Successfully implements at least 3 different algorithms with proper parameter tuning, demonstrates understanding of train/validation/test splits, applies cross-validation techniques

Model Evaluation and Comparison (25 points): Uses appropriate evaluation metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, AUC-ROC), compares models effectively, identifies best performing model with statistical justification
Business Interpretation and Communication (25 points): Provides actionable business insights, explains feature importance in business terms, communicates limitations and recommendations clearly
instructions:
You are provided with a telecommunications customer churn dataset (telecom_churn.csv) containing 7,043 customer records with 21 features including demographics, account information, and service usage patterns. Your task is to build predictive models to identify customers likely to churn and provide actionable business recommendations.

Deliverables:
1. Jupyter notebook (.ipynb) or R Markdown (.Rmd) file with complete analysis
2. Executive summary (1-2 pages) highlighting key findings and recommendations

Technical Requirements:
- Perform comprehensive exploratory data analysis with at least 5 visualizations
- Handle missing values and categorical variables appropriately
- Implement minimum 3 algorithms: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest
- Use 70/15/15 train/validation/test split
- Apply k-fold cross-validation (k=5) on training data
- Evaluate models using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC
- Include feature importance analysis
- Code must be well-commented and reproducible

Business Requirements:
- Identify top 5 factors contributing to churn
- Recommend 3 specific retention strategies
- Quantify potential business impact of your model
- Discuss model limitations and deployment considerations

Submission: Upload both files to the course portal by 11:59 PM on the due date. Ensure your notebook runs completely without errors.
grading_notes: Instructors should focus on both technical execution and business acumen. Common issues include: improper handling of categorical variables, data leakage through incorrect splitting, overfitting without proper validation, and lack of business context in interpretations. Grade distribution typically: 90-100 (exceptional analysis with novel insights), 80-89 (solid technical work with good interpretation), 70-79 (meets requirements but limited depth), below 70 (incomplete or significant errors). Deduct points for: non-reproducible code (-5), late submission (-10 per day), missing visualizations (-3 each), inadequate business interpretation (-10). Bonus points (+5) for creative feature engineering or advanced techniques like ensemble methods.

title: Mathematical Modeling and Optimization: Real-World Business Case Study
description: Students will develop a comprehensive mathematical model to solve a real-world business optimization problem, applying calculus, linear algebra, and statistical analysis to provide data-driven recommendations with complete mathematical justification.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply multivariable calculus and optimization techniques to solve complex real-world problems
Construct and analyze mathematical models using linear algebra and systems of equations
Interpret statistical data and incorporate uncertainty into mathematical decision-making
Communicate mathematical reasoning clearly through written reports and visual presentations
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Model Development (25 points): Correctly formulates constraints, objective functions, and variables; demonstrates appropriate use of calculus, linear algebra, or statistical methods; shows mathematical rigor in model construction

Problem-Solving and Analysis (25 points): Applies optimization techniques correctly; solves systems accurately; performs sensitivity analysis; identifies and addresses mathematical limitations or assumptions

Data Integration and Interpretation (25 points): Effectively incorporates real data sources; applies statistical analysis appropriately; quantifies uncertainty; validates model results against actual data when possible

Communication and Presentation (25 points): Provides clear mathematical explanations; uses appropriate notation and terminology; creates effective visualizations; presents actionable recommendations with mathematical justification
instructions: Select one business optimization scenario from the provided list (inventory management, resource allocation, profit maximization, or supply chain optimization) or propose your own with instructor approval. Your project must include: (1) Problem Definition: Clearly state the business problem, identify key variables, constraints, and objectives. Define your mathematical approach and justify your methodology choice. (2) Mathematical Model: Develop a comprehensive model using appropriate mathematical techniques. This must include at least two of the following: multivariable calculus with optimization, linear algebra with systems of equations, or statistical analysis with uncertainty quantification. Show all mathematical work with proper notation. (3) Data Analysis: Incorporate real or realistic data from credible sources. Apply your model to this data, showing detailed calculations. Perform sensitivity analysis to test how changes in key parameters affect outcomes. (4) Results and Recommendations: Present your mathematical findings clearly with graphs, tables, and visualizations. Provide specific, quantified business recommendations supported by your mathematical analysis. (5) Deliverables: Submit a 15-20 page written report (including appendices with detailed calculations), a 10-minute presentation with slides, and all mathematical work/code files. Reports must follow academic formatting with proper citations for data sources. Mathematical notation should be clear and consistent throughout. All graphs and tables must be properly labeled and referenced in the text.
grading_notes: Evaluate mathematical accuracy first - incorrect fundamental calculations should receive significant deductions even if other elements are strong. Look for appropriate complexity in mathematical techniques; simple algebra-only solutions are insufficient for advanced level. Deduct points for late submissions: 5% per day up to one week, then 50% reduction.

title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics and Statistical Physics Comprehensive Examination
description: A comprehensive expert-level examination covering advanced quantum mechanical systems, statistical thermodynamics, and solid-state physics applications. Students will demonstrate mastery of mathematical formalism, physical interpretation, and problem-solving techniques in quantum many-body systems, phase transitions, and condensed matter phenomena.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced quantum mechanical operators and formalism to solve many-body problems involving fermions and bosons
Analyze statistical mechanical systems using ensemble theory and derive thermodynamic properties from partition functions
Evaluate electronic band structures in crystalline solids and predict transport properties
Synthesize quantum field theory concepts to explain superconductivity and magnetic phase transitions
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Rigor and Formalism (25 points): Correct application of quantum operators, statistical ensembles, and differential equations; proper use of boundary conditions and approximation methods; accurate mathematical derivations with clear step-by-step progression

Physical Interpretation and Conceptual Understanding (25 points): Demonstration of deep understanding of quantum states, thermodynamic processes, and solid-state phenomena; ability to explain physical meaning of mathematical results; correct identification of relevant physical principles

Problem-Solving Strategy and Analysis (25 points): Systematic approach to complex multi-part problems; appropriate choice of theoretical frameworks; effective use of approximation techniques; logical progression from given information to final answers

Communication and Presentation (25 points): Clear exposition of solutions with proper scientific notation; well-organized responses with logical flow; appropriate use of diagrams and graphs; professional presentation of results with correct units and significant figures
instructions: This examination consists of four comprehensive problems covering quantum many-body systems, statistical mechanics, condensed matter physics, and quantum field applications. Each problem is worth 25 points and should be completed in approximately one hour. You must show all work, including intermediate steps, assumptions, and approximations used. Clearly state your approach to each problem before beginning calculations. For theoretical derivations, explain the physical significance of each major step. When making approximations, justify their validity and discuss their limitations. Include properly labeled diagrams where appropriate, especially for energy level schemes, crystal structures, or phase diagrams. Express all final numerical answers with appropriate units and significant figures. For conceptual questions, provide thorough explanations demonstrating your understanding of underlying physics principles. You may use standard reference materials including fundamental constants, but all problem-solving techniques must be your own work. Partial credit will be awarded for correct methodology even if final answers are incorrect, so clearly document your reasoning throughout. Submit all work on the provided answer sheets, using additional pages as needed. Ensure your name and student ID appear on every page submitted.
grading_notes: Evaluate mathematical competency by checking operator algebra, integration techniques, and series expansions. Award partial credit generously for correct methodology even with computational errors. Look for proper treatment of quantum mechanical commutation relations and statistical mechanical partition function manipulations. Assess conceptual understanding through students' physical interpretations of results and their ability to connect mathematical formalism to observable phenomena. Common issues include incorrect normalization of wave functions, misapplication of statistical ensembles, and confusion between classical and quantum statistical treatments. Expect grade distribution: 15% A grades (90-100), 25% B grades (80-89), 35% C grades (70-79), 20% D grades (60-69), 5% F grades (<60). Deduct points for dimensional analysis errors and unrealistic numerical results. Credit innovative solution approaches that demonstrate deep understanding even if different from standard methods.

title: Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) Discussion Forum
description: Students will engage in a structured discussion analyzing different SDLC methodologies, sharing experiences with development phases, and collaboratively exploring best practices for software project management in beginner-level development scenarios.
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify and explain the key phases of software development life cycle
Compare and contrast different SDLC methodologies (Waterfall, Agile, Iterative)
Recognize the importance of planning, testing, and documentation in software projects
Communicate technical concepts clearly using appropriate terminology
rubric_criteria: Initial Post Quality (25 points): Demonstrates clear understanding of SDLC phases, provides specific examples, uses correct terminology, and shows evidence of research or personal experience
Methodology Analysis (25 points): Accurately compares at least two SDLC methodologies, identifies strengths/weaknesses, and explains appropriate use cases for each approach
Peer Engagement (25 points): Responds meaningfully to at least 3 classmates with substantive comments that extend discussion, ask thoughtful questions, or provide additional insights
Communication & Professionalism (25 points): Uses clear, professional language, proper grammar/spelling, appropriate technical vocabulary, and maintains respectful tone throughout all interactions
instructions:
This week-long discussion focuses on Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) methodologies and their real-world applications. 

INITIAL POST (due by Wednesday): Write a 300-400 word post addressing: (1) Describe the key phases of SDLC using a simple software project example (like a basic calculator app or to-do list). (2) Compare two SDLC methodologies - choose from Waterfall, Agile Scrum, or Iterative development. Explain when you might use each approach. (3) Share any personal experience with software development phases (from class projects, internships, or personal coding). If you have no experience, research and discuss one phase that interests you most.

RESPONSE POSTS (due by Sunday): Reply to at least 3 classmates with substantial responses (100+ words each). Consider: asking follow-up questions about their examples, sharing alternative perspectives on methodology choices, relating their experiences to your own, or suggesting improvements to their project approaches.

FORMATTING: Use clear paragraphs, proper headings, and cite any external sources using simple web links. Include specific examples and avoid generic statements.

SUBMISSION: Post directly in the designated discussion forum. Late posts lose 10 points per day.
grading_notes: Look for evidence of genuine understanding rather than copied definitions. Strong posts will include personal reflection or specific examples. For methodology comparison, students should demonstrate understanding of practical differences, not just list features. Peer responses should add value to discussion - simple agreement or generic praise receives lower scores. Watch for students who post all responses on the same day (suggests minimal engagement). Expect most students to score 80-90 points if they follow instructions completely. Reserve 95+ points for exceptional insight or creativity. Common issues: overly technical language, superficial methodology comparison, late participation affecting peer interaction quality.

title: Customer Segmentation Analysis Presentation
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive data analysis of customer transaction data to identify distinct customer segments, present their methodology and findings through visualizations, and provide actionable business recommendations in a 15-minute presentation format.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply exploratory data analysis techniques to understand customer behavior patterns
Implement clustering algorithms and evaluate their effectiveness for segmentation
Create compelling data visualizations that communicate insights clearly

Present technical analysis results to non-technical stakeholders effectively
rubric_criteria: Data Exploration & Preprocessing (25 points): Demonstrates thorough data cleaning, handles missing values appropriately, identifies outliers, and provides comprehensive descriptive statistics with meaningful insights about data quality and distribution

Analysis Methodology & Implementation (25 points): Correctly applies clustering techniques (K-means, hierarchical, or DBSCAN), justifies algorithm selection, determines optimal number of clusters using appropriate metrics (silhouette score, elbow method), and validates results

instructions: You will analyze a provided customer transaction dataset containing purchase history, demographics, and behavioral metrics to identify distinct customer segments. Submit your presentation slides (PDF), analysis code (Python/R script with comments), and a 2-page executive summary highlighting key insights and recommendations. Executive summary should be written for a non-technical business audience.
grading_notes: Evaluate code quality and reproducibility - scripts should run without errors and include sufficient comments. Look for appropriate statistical techniques and proper interpretation of clustering metrics. Strong submissions will show creativity in feature engineering and segment characterization. Common issues include: inadequate data preprocessing, poor cluster validation, visualizations that don't support the narrative, and recommendations that lack specificity. title: Comprehensive Project Management Portfolio: End-to-End Project Execution

Stakeholder Management and Communication (25 points): Stakeholder analysis matrix, tailored communication plan, meeting minutes/reports, conflict resolution documentation, and evidence of stakeholder engagement throughout project lifecycle

instructions: Develop a comprehensive project management portfolio based on a real or simulated project of significant scope (minimum 6-month timeline, $50K+ budget, 5+ team members). grading_notes: Evaluate portfolios holistically for professional presentation and integration across components. Look for evidence of iterative planning and realistic constraints rather than theoretical perfection. Deduct points for: incomplete WBS (less than 3 levels), unrealistic timelines, generic risk assessments, missing stakeholder engagement evidence, or lack of critical analysis in closure documents. Reward innovative approaches, sophisticated risk thinking, and demonstrated learning from execution challenges. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90+), 35% B-level (80-89), 40% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Management Simulation and Analysis Report
description: Students will participate in a multi-phase leadership crisis simulation, demonstrate real-time decision-making under pressure, and produce a comprehensive analytical report examining their leadership approach, stakeholder management, and strategic outcomes.
estimated_time: 8-10 hours (2 hours simulation + 6-8 hours report preparation)
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate advanced crisis leadership skills including rapid decision-making, stakeholder communication, and team coordination under high-pressure conditions
Analyze and evaluate leadership effectiveness using established frameworks and demonstrate reflective leadership practices
Apply strategic thinking to complex organizational challenges while balancing competing priorities and ethical considerations
Synthesize leadership theory with practical application and articulate lessons learned for future leadership development
rubric_criteria: Crisis Leadership Performance (25 points): Evaluation of real-time decision-making quality, stakeholder communication effectiveness, team coordination skills, and adaptability during the simulation phases

Strategic Analysis and Framework Application (25 points): Depth of analysis using relevant leadership theories, quality of strategic recommendations, integration of multiple leadership models, and demonstration of systems thinking

Stakeholder Management and Communication (25 points): Assessment of stakeholder identification and prioritization, communication strategy effectiveness, conflict resolution approaches, and ethical decision-making processes

Reflection and Professional Development (25 points): Quality of self-assessment, identification of leadership strengths and growth areas, actionable development plan creation, and integration of feedback from simulation observers
instructions: Complete a three-phase crisis leadership simulation followed by a comprehensive 3,000-word analytical report. Phase 2: Address emerging complications including stakeholder conflicts and ethical dilemmas in a 45-minute continuation. Phase 3: Participate in a 45-minute stakeholder meeting to present your crisis response strategy. Throughout the simulation, you will be observed and evaluated on leadership behaviors, decision-making processes, and communication effectiveness. Your report must include: (1) Executive summary of crisis events and your leadership approach, (2) Strategic analysis using minimum three leadership frameworks (transformational, situational, authentic leadership theories), (3) Stakeholder analysis with communication strategy evaluation, (4) Ethical considerations and decision-making rationale, (5) Critical self-reflection on leadership effectiveness with specific behavioral examples, (6) Professional development plan with actionable goals and timelines. Submit your report as a professionally formatted document with APA citations, including appendices with stakeholder communication examples and decision-making matrices. Simulation recordings will be reviewed alongside written submissions for comprehensive evaluation.
grading_notes: Evaluate both live simulation performance and written analysis equally. For simulation performance, focus on observable leadership behaviors rather than simulation outcomes - effective leadership can occur even with challenging results. Look for evidence of emotional intelligence, clear communication under pressure, and ethical decision-making. In written reports, prioritize depth of analysis over description of events. Strong reports will demonstrate sophisticated understanding of leadership complexity and provide specific, actionable insights. Common issues include: surface-level analysis without theoretical grounding, failure to address ethical dimensions, insufficient self-reflection, and generic development plans. Expect grade distribution of 15% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 35% C-level (70-79), 15% below C-level. title: End-to-End Data Science Project Portfolio: Predicting Customer Churn
description: Students will complete a comprehensive data science project demonstrating the full analytical pipeline from data acquisition and exploration through model development, evaluation, and business recommendations. The portfolio must include a Jupyter notebook with code, visualizations, and analysis, plus a executive summary presentation.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply data preprocessing and exploratory data analysis techniques to real-world datasets
Implement and compare multiple machine learning algorithms for classification problems
Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics and validation techniques
Communicate data science findings effectively to both technical and business audiences
Demonstrate proficiency with Python data science libraries (pandas, scikit-learn, matplotlib/seaborn)
rubric_criteria: Data Exploration and Preprocessing (25 points): Thorough EDA with meaningful visualizations, proper handling of missing data, feature engineering, data quality assessment, and clear documentation of preprocessing steps

Model Development and Implementation (25 points): Implementation of at least 3 different classification algorithms, proper train/validation/test splits, hyperparameter tuning, and clean, well-commented code following best practices

Model Evaluation and Validation (25 points): Use of appropriate evaluation metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC), cross-validation, interpretation of results, comparison of model performance, and discussion of model limitations

Communication and Business Impact (25 points): Clear executive summary with actionable business recommendations, professional visualizations, logical narrative flow, and appropriate technical depth for intended audience
instructions: Using the provided customer churn dataset (or a similar publicly available dataset), complete a full data science project following these requirements: 1) Submit a Jupyter notebook containing your complete analysis, including data loading, exploration (minimum 5 visualizations), preprocessing steps, model development (minimum 3 algorithms: logistic regression, random forest, and one additional method), and evaluation. 2) Include a 2-page executive summary (PDF format) presenting your findings and recommendations to business stakeholders. 3) Your notebook must be well-documented with markdown cells explaining your approach, findings, and decisions. 4) Provide a requirements.txt file listing all dependencies. 5) Include a brief reflection (300 words) on challenges encountered and lessons learned. All code must be reproducible and run without errors. Submit all files in a single ZIP folder named 'LastName_FirstName_DataScience_Portfolio.zip'. Ensure your analysis addresses the business question: 'Which customers are most likely to churn and what factors drive churn behavior?'
grading_notes: Evaluate code quality, reproducibility, and adherence to data science best practices. Look for evidence of critical thinking in feature selection and model choice justification. Common issues include: inadequate EDA, data leakage in preprocessing, improper validation techniques, and overly technical executive summaries. Expect grade distribution: A (90-100): Exceptional work with innovative approaches; B (80-89): Solid analysis meeting all requirements; C (70-79): Adequate work with minor issues; D (60-69): Incomplete or flawed analysis; F (<60): Major technical errors or missing components. Partial credit available for each criterion - students can excel in some areas while being weaker in others.

title: Statistical Analysis Laboratory Report: Real-World Data Investigation
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive statistical analysis of a real-world dataset, applying advanced statistical methods including hypothesis testing, regression analysis, and confidence intervals. The report must demonstrate mathematical rigor, proper use of statistical software, and clear interpretation of results.
estimated_time: 4-6 weeks (including data collection, analysis, and report writing)
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced statistical methods to analyze real-world data and draw meaningful conclusions
Demonstrate proficiency in hypothesis testing, regression analysis, and confidence interval construction
Communicate mathematical findings effectively through written reports with appropriate visualizations
Critically evaluate statistical assumptions and limitations in data analysis
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Methodology (25 points): Correct application of statistical methods, appropriate test selection, accurate calculations, proper verification of assumptions, and sound mathematical reasoning throughout the analysis

Data Analysis and Computation (25 points): Effective use of statistical software, appropriate data visualization, accurate interpretation of output, proper handling of outliers or missing data, and evidence of exploratory data analysis

Scientific Communication (25 points): Clear problem statement, well-structured report following scientific format, appropriate use of mathematical notation, effective tables and figures with proper captions, and professional presentation

Critical Thinking and Conclusions (25 points): Thoughtful interpretation of results, acknowledgment of limitations, discussion of practical significance versus statistical significance, appropriate scope of conclusions, and suggestions for further investigation
instructions: Select a dataset from an approved source (government databases, research repositories, or collect original data with instructor approval) containing at least 100 observations and 5 variables. Your dataset must allow for both descriptive and inferential statistical analysis. Structure your report as follows: (1) Introduction and Research Questions - clearly state your research objectives and formulate specific hypotheses to test; (2) Data Description - provide dataset overview, variable definitions, summary statistics, and initial exploratory analysis including appropriate graphs; (3) Methodology - justify your choice of statistical methods, verify necessary assumptions, and describe your analytical approach; (4) Results - present findings using appropriate statistical tests, construct relevant confidence intervals, perform regression analysis if applicable, and include well-designed visualizations; (5) Discussion and Conclusions - interpret results in context, discuss limitations, and address practical implications. Your report must be 8-12 pages (excluding appendices), include all statistical output as appendices, use proper mathematical notation, and cite sources in APA format. Submit both the written report and your data file with analysis code. All calculations must be reproducible.
grading_notes: Evaluate mathematical accuracy first - incorrect statistical methods or computational errors should significantly impact the grade regardless of presentation quality. Look for evidence that students understand when and why to use specific statistical tests rather than just applying them mechanically. Common issues include: failing to check assumptions, over-interpreting correlation as causation, ignoring practical significance, and inadequate discussion of limitations. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level work (demonstrates mastery with original insights), 35% B-level work (solid understanding with minor errors), 40% C-level work (basic competency with some conceptual gaps), 10% below C-level (significant methodological or computational errors). Deduct points for late submission, failure to include required components, or academic integrity violations. Provide specific feedback on mathematical reasoning and suggestions for improvement in statistical thinking.

title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics and Relativistic Physics Comprehensive Quiz
description: A comprehensive expert-level assessment covering quantum field theory fundamentals, relativistic mechanics, particle physics interactions, and advanced electromagnetic theory. Students will solve complex multi-step problems requiring deep conceptual understanding and mathematical proficiency in graduate-level physics.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply quantum field theory principles to calculate scattering amplitudes and cross-sections for fundamental particle interactions
Solve relativistic mechanics problems involving four-momentum conservation and Lorentz transformations in high-energy scenarios
Analyze electromagnetic field configurations using Maxwell's equations in curved spacetime and gauge theory frameworks
Demonstrate mastery of statistical mechanics in quantum systems including Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac distributions
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Rigor and Technique (25 points): Correct application of advanced mathematical methods including tensor calculus, complex analysis, and differential geometry. Proper use of units, significant figures, and mathematical notation throughout all calculations.

Conceptual Understanding and Physics Principles (25 points): Demonstrates deep comprehension of underlying physical principles, correctly identifies applicable theories and models, shows understanding of physical meaning behind mathematical results, and recognizes limits of applicability.

Problem-Solving Strategy and Methodology (25 points): Systematic approach to complex problems, logical progression from given information to solution, appropriate use of approximations and limiting cases, clear identification of assumptions and constraints.

Communication and Presentation (25 points): Clear explanation of reasoning and methodology, well-organized solutions with logical flow, appropriate use of diagrams and visual aids, professional presentation of final answers with proper interpretation of physical significance.
instructions: This assessment consists of four comprehensive problems requiring advanced knowledge of quantum mechanics, relativity, and electromagnetic theory. You have 3 hours to complete all questions. Show all work including intermediate steps, assumptions, and reasoning. Use appropriate mathematical notation and maintain dimensional consistency throughout. For each problem, begin by clearly stating the physical principles involved and your solution strategy. Include relevant diagrams where applicable. Partial credit will be awarded based on methodology and understanding even if final answers are incorrect. You may use standard reference materials including fundamental constants, but all problem-solving must be your own work. Calculator and computer algebra systems are permitted for numerical computations only. Present solutions in a clear, logical sequence that another physicist could follow. For problems involving approximations, state your assumptions explicitly and justify their validity. Final answers should include appropriate units, uncertainty estimates where relevant, and brief physical interpretation of results. Submit all work in a single PDF document with pages numbered and your name clearly indicated. Ensure mathematical expressions are legible and properly formatted. Late submissions will incur a 10% penalty per hour.
grading_notes: Use holistic rubric assessment rather than strict point deduction. Award full credit for alternative valid solution methods. Common issues include: inadequate justification of approximations, dimensional errors, confusion between classical and quantum limits, improper gauge choices in electromagnetic problems. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-range (90-100), 35% B-range (80-89), 35% C-range (70-79), 15% below 70. Focus on understanding over computational accuracy. Provide specific feedback on mathematical technique and conceptual gaps. Watch for memorization without understanding - require students to explain physical reasoning.

title: Customer Behavior Analysis: E-commerce Sales Data Exam
description: Students will analyze a real-world e-commerce dataset to identify customer purchasing patterns, perform statistical analysis, and present actionable business insights using appropriate data analysis techniques and visualizations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply descriptive and inferential statistical methods to interpret business data
Create effective data visualizations to communicate analytical findings
Identify patterns, trends, and outliers in complex datasets
Formulate data-driven recommendations for business decision-making
rubric_criteria: Data Exploration & Cleaning (25 points): Demonstrates thorough examination of dataset structure, identifies missing values/outliers, applies appropriate cleaning techniques, documents data quality issues

Statistical Analysis (25 points): Correctly applies descriptive statistics, performs appropriate hypothesis tests or correlation analysis, interprets statistical significance, shows proper use of analytical methods

Data Visualization (25 points): Creates clear, accurate, and purposeful charts/graphs, uses appropriate visualization types for data, includes proper labels and legends, visualizations enhance understanding of findings

Business Insights & Recommendations (25 points): Draws logical conclusions from analysis, provides specific actionable recommendations, connects findings to business context, demonstrates critical thinking about implications
instructions: You will receive a dataset containing 6 months of e-commerce transaction data including customer demographics, product categories, purchase amounts, and timestamps. Complete the following tasks using any statistical software (R, Python, Excel, SPSS): 1) Perform exploratory data analysis including summary statistics and data quality assessment. Document any data cleaning steps taken. 2) Conduct statistical analysis to answer: Which customer segments generate highest revenue? Are there seasonal purchasing patterns? What factors correlate with purchase amount? 3) Create 4-6 visualizations that effectively communicate your key findings. Include at least one each of: distribution plot, relationship plot, and time series plot. 4) Write a 2-page executive summary presenting your insights and 3-5 specific business recommendations. Submit: cleaned dataset file, analysis code/calculations, visualization files, and executive summary as PDF. Show all work and explain your analytical choices. Ensure visualizations are publication-ready with clear titles, labels, and professional formatting.
grading_notes: Instructors should evaluate technical accuracy of statistical methods and appropriateness for the data type. Look for evidence of proper data exploration before analysis. Common issues include: inadequate data cleaning documentation, incorrect statistical test selection, unclear or misleading visualizations, and recommendations not supported by analysis. Grade distribution expectation: 15% excellent (90-100), 60% proficient (75-89), 20% developing (60-74), 5% inadequate (below 60). Partial credit available for each criterion - students showing correct process with minor errors should receive 70-80% of points for that section.

title: Complex Project Scenario Analysis: Multi-Stakeholder Crisis Management Discussion
description: Students will analyze a complex project crisis scenario involving budget overruns, scope creep, stakeholder conflicts, and timeline pressures. Through structured discussion, they will demonstrate advanced project management competencies including stakeholder management, risk mitigation, change control, and strategic decision-making under uncertainty.
estimated_time: 3-4 hours (2 hours preparation + 1-2 hours discussion participation)
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced stakeholder management strategies in crisis situations involving conflicting interests and power dynamics
Evaluate and implement change control processes when facing scope creep and budget constraints
Synthesize risk management techniques with crisis communication strategies to maintain project viability
Demonstrate strategic thinking in project recovery scenarios while balancing competing organizational priorities
rubric_criteria: Stakeholder Analysis & Management Strategy (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of stakeholder mapping, power-interest analysis, and develops specific, actionable strategies for managing conflicting stakeholder demands. Addresses communication plans and conflict resolution approaches.

Change Control & Scope Management (25 points): Provides detailed analysis of scope creep causes, evaluates change control processes, and proposes specific mechanisms for managing scope while maintaining project objectives. Includes cost-benefit analysis of proposed changes.

Risk Assessment & Mitigation Planning (25 points): Identifies primary and secondary risks, evaluates probability and impact, develops comprehensive mitigation strategies, and creates contingency plans. Demonstrates understanding of risk interdependencies.

Discussion Quality & Professional Communication (25 points): Engages meaningfully with peers' analyses, provides constructive feedback, asks probing questions, and demonstrates professional project management communication. Shows evidence of reflective thinking and adaptation of initial positions based on discussion.
instructions:
You are the senior project manager for a $2.5M enterprise software implementation project that is 8 months into a planned 12-month timeline. Your project faces multiple critical issues: 30% budget overrun due to unexpected technical complexities, scope creep from three different business units, a key vendor threatening contract termination, and executive pressure to accelerate delivery by 2 months. The steering committee includes the CIO (your sponsor), CFO (budget concerns), and three business unit directors with conflicting priorities. 

Prepare a comprehensive analysis addressing: (1) Stakeholder management strategy including specific tactics for each stakeholder group, communication plans, and conflict resolution approaches; (2) Change control recommendations with detailed process improvements and scope management strategies; (3) Risk assessment matrix with mitigation plans for top 5 risks and contingency strategies; (4) Project recovery plan with timeline, budget, and scope recommendations.

Your initial post (800-1000 words) should present your analysis with specific examples and justifications. Subsequently, engage in substantive discussion by responding to at least three peers' analyses (200-300 words each), providing constructive feedback, alternative perspectives, or additional considerations. Cite relevant project management frameworks (PMI, PRINCE2, Agile) and best practices. Submit your initial analysis by Wednesday 11:59 PM; complete peer responses by Sunday 11:59 PM.
grading_notes: Look for application of advanced PM concepts rather than basic definitions. Excellent responses (90-100) should demonstrate synthesis of multiple PM methodologies and show strategic thinking beyond textbook solutions. Good responses (80-89) show solid understanding with practical applications but may lack depth in stakeholder psychology or risk interdependencies. Satisfactory responses (70-79) address requirements but with limited critical analysis or generic solutions. Below 70 indicates failure to demonstrate advanced PM competency. Pay special attention to how students balance competing priorities and justify trade-off decisions. Discussion quality should show evolution of thinking - students who merely defend initial positions without considering peer feedback should lose points in the communication criterion. Expect 15% A grades, 35% B grades, 40% C grades, 10% below C.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Management Presentation
description: Students will deliver a 20-minute executive-level presentation analyzing a real organizational crisis, evaluating the leadership response, and presenting their own comprehensive crisis management strategy with implementation framework.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate advanced strategic thinking and decision-making under pressure
Apply crisis leadership frameworks to complex, real-world scenarios
Communicate executive-level recommendations with confidence and clarity
Synthesize multiple leadership theories into actionable crisis management strategies
rubric_criteria: Crisis Analysis & Leadership Evaluation (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of crisis dynamics, stakeholder impact assessment, and critical evaluation of actual leadership decisions with evidence-based analysis

Strategic Framework Development (25 points): Presents original, well-structured crisis management strategy incorporating multiple leadership models, clear decision-making protocols, and measurable implementation milestones

Executive Communication & Presence (25 points): Exhibits executive-level presentation skills, confident delivery, professional visual aids, effective use of data visualization, and compelling storytelling that engages C-suite audience

Critical Thinking & Q&A Response (25 points): Shows ability to defend recommendations under scrutiny, adapt thinking based on challenging questions, acknowledge limitations, and demonstrate deep understanding through spontaneous responses
instructions: Select a significant organizational crisis from the past 5 years (minimum $50M impact or 1000+ employee affected). Your presentation must include: (1) Crisis timeline and stakeholder mapping, (2) Critical analysis of actual leadership decisions using minimum 3 leadership frameworks, (3) Your alternative crisis management strategy with specific tactics, communication plan, and success metrics, (4) Implementation roadmap with 30-60-90 day milestones. Format requirements: 15-20 slides, executive summary handout, minimum 8 credible sources including academic journals and primary sources. Visual aids must include data charts, process flows, or infographics. Dress professionally as you're presenting to a board of directors. Submit slides and sources 24 hours prior to presentation. Time limit strictly enforced: 20-minute presentation + 10-minute Q&A. Be prepared to defend your strategy against challenging scenarios and alternative viewpoints.
grading_notes: Evaluate as if students are competing for senior leadership positions. Look for sophisticated analysis beyond surface-level observations. Excellent presentations will challenge conventional wisdom and demonstrate original thinking. Watch for: over-reliance on hindsight bias, insufficient stakeholder consideration, unrealistic implementation timelines, poor visual design, and inability to handle pressure during Q&A. Grade distribution should reflect expert-level expectations: 90-100 (exceptional executive potential), 80-89 (strong leadership capability), 70-79 (developing skills), below 70 (significant gaps). Deduct points for time violations and unprofessional presentation elements.

title: Risk Management Laboratory: Creating a Complete Risk Management Plan
description: Students will develop a comprehensive risk management plan for a provided project scenario, including risk identification, analysis, response planning, and monitoring strategies. This hands-on assessment evaluates practical application of risk management processes using PMP framework methodologies.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply systematic risk identification techniques to identify potential project risks across all knowledge areas
Perform qualitative and quantitative risk analysis using probability-impact matrices and expected monetary value calculations
Develop appropriate risk response strategies (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept) with detailed implementation plans
Create risk monitoring and control procedures with defined triggers and escalation paths
rubric_criteria: Risk Identification and Documentation (25 points): Identifies minimum 15 relevant risks across multiple categories (technical, organizational, external, project management) using proper risk register format with clear risk statements following 'condition-cause-effect' structure
