Risk Analysis and Prioritization (25 points): Completes qualitative analysis with justified probability/impact ratings, creates accurate probability-impact matrix, performs quantitative analysis for top 5 risks including EMV calculations and sensitivity analysis

Risk Response Planning (25 points): Develops specific, actionable response strategies for each high and medium-priority risk, assigns clear ownership, establishes realistic timelines, includes contingency plans with defined trigger conditions

Risk Monitoring Plan and Professional Presentation (25 points): Creates comprehensive monitoring framework with KPIs, reporting schedules, and escalation procedures; presents work professionally with proper PMP terminology, clear formatting, and error-free documentation
instructions:
You are the project manager for a 12-month software implementation project with a $2.5M budget for a healthcare organization. Your team includes 15 members across development, testing, and implementation functions. Using the provided project charter and stakeholder analysis, create a complete Risk Management Plan following PMI standards.

Your deliverable must include: (1) Executive Summary (1 page) highlighting key risk themes and overall strategy, (2) Risk Register documenting minimum 15 identified risks using condition-cause-effect format with probability/impact ratings, (3) Probability-Impact Matrix with clear scoring criteria and risk categorization, (4) Quantitative Analysis performing EMV calculations for your top 5 risks, (5) Risk Response Plan detailing specific strategies, owners, timelines, and success criteria for each medium/high risk, (6) Risk Monitoring and Control Plan establishing review schedules, KPIs, reporting formats, and escalation procedures.

Format requirements: Use provided templates, maintain consistent professional formatting, include page numbers and headers, cite any external sources. Submit as single PDF file named 'LastName_RiskPlan.pdf' via course portal by 11:59 PM on due date. Late submissions receive 10-point daily penalty. Ensure all risk statements follow PMI format and use appropriate project management terminology throughout.
grading_notes: Evaluate completeness and quality over quantity - well-developed analysis of 15 risks scores higher than superficial treatment of 20+ risks. Look for realistic probability/impact assessments rather than all risks rated as 'high.' Response strategies should be specific and actionable, not generic statements. Common issues include: vague risk statements, unrealistic probability assessments, generic response strategies, missing quantitative calculations. Grade distribution typically: 90-100 (comprehensive work with minor gaps), 80-89 (solid work missing some elements), 70-79 (adequate but significant omissions), below 70 (major deficiencies). Provide specific feedback on PMI methodology application and professional presentation quality.

title: Advanced Google Analytics Implementation and Strategic Analysis
description: Students will demonstrate mastery of advanced Google Analytics features by implementing complex tracking solutions, creating custom reports and dashboards, and providing strategic recommendations based on comprehensive data analysis for a multi-channel business scenario.
learning_objectives_assessed: Configure advanced tracking implementations including custom events, e-commerce tracking, and cross-domain measurement
Create and interpret custom segments, calculated metrics, and advanced reporting solutions
Analyze multi-channel attribution models and user journey mapping
Develop data-driven strategic recommendations based on advanced analytics insights
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation (25 points): Correctly configures GTM tags, custom events, enhanced e-commerce tracking, and cross-domain setup with proper parameter syntax and testing validation
Advanced Reporting & Analysis (25 points): Creates meaningful custom segments, calculated metrics, and cohort analyses with accurate interpretations of statistical significance and data quality

Multi-Channel Attribution Assessment (25 points): Demonstrates understanding of attribution models, analyzes customer journey paths, and evaluates channel performance using advanced attribution reporting
Strategic Recommendations (25 points): Provides actionable, data-driven recommendations with clear ROI projections, proper goal alignment, and implementation timelines based on comprehensive analysis
instructions: You are the digital marketing analyst for TechFlow Solutions, an e-commerce company selling software and digital services across multiple channels (website, mobile app, social media, email). Using the provided sample dataset and business context, complete the following deliverables: 1) Configure a complete Google Analytics 4 and Google Tag Manager setup including enhanced e-commerce tracking, custom events for software trial downloads, cross-domain tracking for their support subdomain, and audience segmentation for B2B vs B2C customers. Document your implementation with screenshots and GTM export files. 2) Create five custom reports addressing: user acquisition cost by channel, customer lifetime value analysis, conversion funnel analysis with drop-off identification, mobile vs desktop user behavior comparison, and seasonal trend analysis. Include calculated metrics and custom segments where appropriate. 3) Analyze the multi-channel customer journey using attribution modeling, identifying the most effective channel combinations and recommending budget reallocation strategies. Use both first-click and data-driven attribution models for comparison. 4) Prepare an executive summary (800-1000 words) presenting three strategic recommendations with supporting data visualizations, expected impact metrics, and implementation priorities. Submit as a comprehensive report with: technical documentation, exported GTM container, custom report screenshots with analysis, attribution analysis spreadsheet, and executive summary presentation. All work must demonstrate advanced feature usage and strategic thinking beyond basic reporting.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy by checking GTM configuration logic, parameter syntax, and tracking validation. Look for proper use of advanced features like custom dimensions, calculated metrics, and complex segments rather than basic reporting. Attribution analysis should show understanding of model differences and business impact. Common issues include: incomplete e-commerce tracking setup, basic segments instead of advanced behavioral segmentation, attribution analysis without actionable insights, and recommendations lacking specific metrics or timelines. Grade distribution expectation: 15% of students should score 90-100 (exceptional technical depth and strategic insight), 60% should score 75-89 (solid implementation with good analysis), 20% should score 60-74 (basic requirements met with minor technical issues), 5% below 60 (significant implementation problems or superficial analysis). Deduct points for generic recommendations not tied to specific data insights.

title: Enterprise Network Design and Implementation: Multi-Site OSPF Network with Advanced Services
description: Students will design, configure, and document a complete enterprise network infrastructure connecting three sites using OSPF routing, implementing VLANs, inter-VLAN routing, HSRP redundancy, DHCP services, access control lists, and network monitoring. This comprehensive project demonstrates mastery of advanced Cisco networking concepts in a realistic enterprise scenario.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design and implement hierarchical network topologies using OSPF multi-area routing
Configure advanced switching features including VLANs, STP, and EtherChannel
Implement high availability solutions using HSRP and redundant links
Deploy network services including DHCP, NAT, and access control policies
Troubleshoot complex network issues using systematic methodologies
Create comprehensive network documentation and perform security analysis
rubric_criteria: Network Design and OSPF Implementation (25 points): Correct multi-area OSPF configuration with appropriate area types, proper summarization, and optimal path selection. All routers must form proper adjacencies with convergence under 30 seconds.

Switching and VLAN Configuration (25 points): Proper VLAN segmentation with functional inter-VLAN routing, spanning-tree optimization, EtherChannel implementation, and port security. All VLANs must communicate through designated Layer 3 device.

High Availability and Network Services (25 points): Functional HSRP configuration with proper preemption, DHCP pools serving all VLANs, NAT/PAT for internet connectivity, and appropriate ACLs restricting traffic between network segments.

Documentation and Troubleshooting (25 points): Complete network documentation including topology diagrams, IP addressing scheme, configuration backups, and detailed troubleshooting procedures. Must include performance baseline and security assessment.
instructions: You will design and implement a three-site enterprise network using Cisco equipment (physical or Packet Tracer). The network must connect a main headquarters (100 users), branch office (50 users), and data center (20 servers) using OSPF routing across WAN links. Requirements: Configure OSPF with Area 0 as backbone, Area 1 for headquarters, Area 2 for branch office, and Area 3 as NSSA for data center. Implement at least 4 VLANs per site (Management, Users, Voice, Guest) with appropriate subnetting from 172.16.0.0/16. Deploy HSRP on all distribution switches for gateway redundancy. Configure DHCP services, implement NAT for internet access, and create ACLs restricting inter-VLAN communication. All links between distribution switches must use EtherChannel. Deliverables include: complete running configurations for all devices, logical and physical topology diagrams, IP addressing spreadsheet, OSPF database analysis, traffic flow documentation, and a troubleshooting guide with at least 5 common scenarios and solutions. Test connectivity between all sites and demonstrate failover scenarios. Submit all files in organized folder structure with README file explaining setup procedures. Include performance metrics showing convergence times and throughput measurements.
grading_notes: Evaluate configurations by importing into network simulator to verify functionality. Key evaluation points: OSPF neighbor relationships and LSA propagation (check with 'show ip ospf neighbor' and 'show ip ospf database'), VLAN connectivity across trunk links, HSRP active/standby status and failover timing, DHCP lease assignments, NAT translation tables, and ACL hit counters. Common issues include incorrect OSPF area assignments, VLAN mismatches on trunks, HSRP priority conflicts, DHCP scope conflicts, and overly restrictive ACLs. Expect 15% of students to achieve 90-100 points with flawless implementation, 50% to score 75-89 with minor configuration errors, 30% to score 60-74 with functional but suboptimal designs, and 5% below 60 requiring remediation. Deduct points for missing documentation, non-functional services, or security vulnerabilities. Bonus points available for advanced features like QoS implementation or IPv6 dual-stack configuration.

title: Feature Engineering Ethics and Impact Discussion
description: Students will analyze and discuss the ethical implications and societal impact of feature engineering decisions in real-world data science scenarios, demonstrating understanding of bias, fairness, and responsible AI practices.
estimated_time: 3-4 hours (including research, analysis, and peer responses)
learning_objectives_assessed: Evaluate ethical considerations in feature selection and engineering processes
Analyze potential sources of bias in data preprocessing and feature creation
Apply fairness principles to real-world data science scenarios
Communicate complex ethical concepts clearly to technical and non-technical audiences
rubric_criteria: Ethical Analysis Depth (25 points): Demonstrates thorough understanding of ethical implications, identifies multiple stakeholders affected, and considers both immediate and long-term consequences of feature engineering decisions

Bias Identification and Mitigation (25 points): Accurately identifies potential sources of bias in the scenario, explains how biases can be introduced through feature engineering, and proposes specific, implementable mitigation strategies

Real-world Application (25 points): Provides relevant examples from industry or research, connects theoretical concepts to practical implementation challenges, and demonstrates understanding of regulatory and compliance considerations

Communication and Peer Engagement (25 points): Presents ideas clearly with appropriate technical depth, responds thoughtfully to at least two peers with substantive feedback, and facilitates meaningful discussion through questions or alternative perspectives
instructions: You will participate in a structured discussion analyzing the ethical implications of feature engineering in data science projects. Choose one of three provided scenarios: (1) Healthcare prediction model using demographic features, (2) Hiring algorithm incorporating educational and experience features, or (3) Credit scoring system with alternative data sources. Your initial post (800-1000 words) must include: a detailed analysis of potential ethical concerns in your chosen scenario, identification of at least three sources of bias that could emerge during feature engineering, specific recommendations for bias mitigation with technical implementation details, discussion of stakeholder impact including affected communities, and consideration of regulatory requirements (GDPR, Fair Credit Reporting Act, etc.). Support your analysis with at least three peer-reviewed sources or industry case studies. After posting your initial analysis, respond to two classmates' posts (200-300 words each) with constructive feedback, alternative perspectives, or additional considerations they may have missed. Focus on the technical feasibility of their proposed solutions and potential unintended consequences. All posts must demonstrate professional communication suitable for both technical teams and business stakeholders. Submit your initial post by Wednesday 11:59 PM and peer responses by Sunday 11:59 PM. Include proper citations in APA format and ensure all claims are supported by evidence.
grading_notes: Evaluate initial posts for depth of ethical reasoning beyond surface-level concerns. Look for specific technical knowledge of feature engineering processes and realistic mitigation strategies. Award full points for bias identification only when students demonstrate understanding of how bias enters through data collection, feature selection, and transformation processes. For real-world application, expect concrete examples with specific company names, regulations, or documented cases rather than hypothetical situations. Peer responses should be substantive and demonstrate critical thinking - simple agreement or generic feedback warrants point deduction. Grade distribution expectation: 15-20% should receive 90+ points, 60-70% should receive 75-89 points, remaining students 60-74 points. Common issues to watch: oversimplified ethical analysis, proposed solutions that are technically unfeasible, lack of consideration for multiple stakeholders, and peer responses that don't add value to the discussion. Provide specific feedback on technical accuracy of bias mitigation strategies and clarity of communication for mixed audiences.

title: Advanced Physics Research Portfolio: Independent Investigation of Complex Physical Systems
description: Students conduct an in-depth investigation of a complex physical system or phenomenon, demonstrating mastery of theoretical principles, experimental design, mathematical modeling, and scientific communication through a comprehensive portfolio of research artifacts.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced theoretical physics principles to analyze complex multi-variable systems
Design and execute sophisticated experimental methodologies with appropriate controls and error analysis
Develop and validate mathematical models using differential equations, statistical analysis, and computational methods
Synthesize research findings and communicate complex physics concepts to diverse audiences through multiple formats
Critically evaluate scientific literature and integrate current research into original investigations
Demonstrate proficiency with advanced laboratory equipment and computational physics tools
rubric_criteria: Theoretical Foundation & Literature Review (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of underlying physics principles, cites and critically analyzes minimum 8 peer-reviewed sources, connects theory to investigation with mathematical rigor, shows mastery of relevant equations and derivations

Experimental Design & Implementation (25 points): Develops sophisticated experimental methodology with clear hypothesis, identifies and controls variables, uses appropriate instrumentation, implements proper safety protocols, documents procedures with sufficient detail for replication, addresses limitations and sources of error

Data Analysis & Mathematical Modeling (25 points): Performs rigorous statistical analysis with appropriate uncertainty calculations, develops mathematical models using relevant differential equations or computational methods, validates models against experimental data, demonstrates proficiency with analysis software (Python/MATLAB/Mathematica)

Scientific Communication & Portfolio Organization (25 points): Presents findings through multiple formats (formal report, visual presentation, peer discussion), uses appropriate scientific writing conventions, creates clear figures and graphs with proper captions, organizes portfolio logically with executive summary, demonstrates ability to explain complex concepts to different audiences
instructions: Select a complex physical system or phenomenon for independent investigation (examples: nonlinear oscillators, fluid dynamics, electromagnetic field interactions, quantum mechanical systems, thermodynamic processes, or astrophysical phenomena). Your portfolio must include: (1) Executive Summary (2 pages) outlining your research question, methodology, and key findings; (2) Comprehensive Literature Review (4-5 pages) analyzing relevant research and theoretical foundations; (3) Detailed Experimental Section documenting your methodology, setup, and procedures with photographs and diagrams; (4) Results and Analysis Section presenting data, calculations, statistical analysis, and mathematical modeling with proper error analysis; (5) Discussion and Conclusions connecting findings to broader physics principles and suggesting future research directions; (6) Professional presentation (15-20 slides) suitable for a physics colloquium; (7) All raw data, calculations, and code in organized appendices. Submit portfolio components in phases: topic proposal and initial literature review (Week 2), experimental design and methodology (Week 4), preliminary data and analysis (Week 6), complete portfolio (Week 8). All written work must follow APA format with proper citation of sources. Mathematical derivations should be clearly shown, and all figures must be original with appropriate captions and uncertainty bars where applicable.
grading_notes: Evaluate portfolios holistically, looking for integration across components rather than treating each section independently. Excellence indicators include: original insights beyond basic application of formulas, sophisticated error analysis, creative experimental approaches, and ability to connect findings to broader physics principles. Common issues to address: insufficient error analysis, lack of connection between theory and experiment, poor organization of data, inadequate literature review depth. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 35% C-level (70-79), 15% below C-level. Provide detailed feedback on mathematical rigor, experimental technique, and scientific writing. Consider offering revision opportunities for portfolios scoring below 75 points.

title: Basic Web Calculator Lab Report
description: Students will develop a simple web-based calculator application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, then document their development process, challenges encountered, and testing procedures in a comprehensive lab report.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate understanding of basic HTML structure and form elements
Apply CSS styling principles for user interface design
Implement JavaScript functions for mathematical operations and DOM manipulation
Document software development processes and reflect on problem-solving approaches
Conduct basic testing and debugging procedures
rubric_criteria: Code Implementation (25 points): Calculator performs all four basic operations (+, -, ×, ÷), handles user input correctly, includes proper HTML structure, CSS styling, and functional JavaScript with appropriate variable names and comments

User Interface Design (25 points): Clean, intuitive layout with clearly labeled buttons, appropriate color scheme, responsive design elements, proper alignment, and user-friendly input/output display areas

Documentation Quality (25 points): Lab report includes complete development process description, code explanations, challenges faced and solutions implemented, clear screenshots of working application, and proper formatting with correct grammar

Testing and Error Handling (25 points): Demonstrates thorough testing of all operations, documents test cases and results, implements basic error handling (division by zero, invalid input), and shows debugging process used to resolve issues
instructions:
Create a functional web calculator that performs addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division operations. Your submission must include: (1) Three separate files: index.html, styles.css, and script.js; (2) A complete lab report document (PDF format, 3-4 pages). 

Technical Requirements: HTML file must contain a calculator interface with number buttons (0-9), operation buttons (+, -, ×, ÷), equals button, clear button, and display area. CSS file should include styling for layout, colors, fonts, and hover effects. JavaScript file must contain functions for each mathematical operation, event listeners for button clicks, display update functions, and basic error handling.

Lab Report Requirements: Include an introduction explaining the project purpose, a development methodology section describing your approach, a detailed code explanation section with screenshots, a testing section documenting all test cases performed, a challenges and solutions section describing problems encountered and how you solved them, and a conclusion reflecting on lessons learned. Use 12-point font, double spacing, and include your name, date, and course information.

Submission: Upload all files in a single ZIP folder named 'LastName_Calculator_Lab' containing the three code files and your lab report PDF. Ensure your calculator works in modern web browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) before submission. Late submissions will be penalized 10 points per day.
grading_notes: Instructors should test the calculator functionality in multiple browsers before grading. Common issues to watch for include: missing error handling for division by zero (deduct 5-10 points), poor variable naming or lack of comments (deduct 5 points), broken CSS links or JavaScript references (deduct 10-15 points), and incomplete lab report sections (deduct points proportionally). Grade distribution expectation: 85-100 points for excellent work with all requirements met, 70-84 points for good work with minor issues, 55-69 points for acceptable work with several problems, below 55 points for incomplete or non-functional submissions. Provide specific feedback on code structure, documentation clarity, and areas for improvement. Consider offering partial credit for non-functional code that shows understanding of concepts.

title: Customer Segmentation Analysis Quiz
description: Students will analyze an e-commerce customer dataset to identify distinct customer segments, evaluate purchasing patterns, and provide data-driven business recommendations through descriptive statistics, visualization, and clustering techniques.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply exploratory data analysis techniques to identify patterns and outliers in customer behavior data
Create appropriate statistical visualizations to communicate key findings about customer segments
Interpret clustering results and translate analytical insights into actionable business recommendations
Demonstrate proficiency in calculating and interpreting descriptive statistics for business decision-making
rubric_criteria: Data Exploration and Cleaning (25 points): Correctly identifies data quality issues, handles missing values appropriately, detects outliers, and provides summary statistics with proper interpretation

Visualization Quality (25 points): Creates clear, well-labeled charts that effectively communicate customer patterns, uses appropriate chart types for data relationships, and includes meaningful titles and legends

Statistical Analysis (25 points): Accurately calculates customer lifetime value, purchase frequency metrics, and seasonal trends; correctly applies and interprets clustering algorithms with appropriate number of segments

Business Insights and Recommendations (25 points): Provides specific, actionable recommendations based on data findings, clearly explains the business impact of identified customer segments, and justifies proposed strategies with quantitative evidence
instructions: You will analyze a dataset containing 12 months of customer transaction data from an online retailer. The dataset includes customer demographics, purchase history, product categories, and spending amounts. Complete all four sections of this assessment: 1) DATA EXPLORATION: Calculate summary statistics for key variables (customer age, total spent, purchase frequency). Identify and document any data quality issues, missing values, or outliers. Create a data cleaning plan and execute it. 2) VISUALIZATION: Produce four charts: customer age distribution histogram, monthly sales trend line graph, spending by product category bar chart, and customer lifetime value scatter plot. Each chart must include proper labels, titles, and legends. 3) STATISTICAL ANALYSIS: Segment customers using appropriate clustering techniques. Calculate average customer lifetime value, identify seasonal purchasing patterns, and determine the top 20% of customers by revenue contribution. Show all calculations and methodology. 4) BUSINESS RECOMMENDATIONS: Based on your analysis, provide three specific marketing strategies targeting different customer segments. Include expected outcomes and success metrics for each recommendation. Submit your work as a single document containing your analysis, charts, calculations, and recommendations. Include all code/formulas used and cite any external sources. File format: PDF or Word document, maximum 10 pages.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy first, then assess business application. Look for evidence of systematic analytical thinking rather than just correct answers. Common issues include: inadequate data cleaning documentation, charts without proper scaling or labels, clustering without validation metrics, and generic recommendations not tied to specific findings. Grade distribution should target: 90-100 points for comprehensive analysis with clear business connection, 80-89 for solid technical work with minor gaps in interpretation, 70-79 for correct calculations but weak business insights, below 70 for significant technical errors or missing components. Pay special attention to whether students validate their clustering results and provide quantitative support for recommendations.

title: Comprehensive Project Management Simulation: Software Development Initiative
description: Students will develop and execute a complete project management plan for a simulated 6-month software development project, demonstrating mastery of project lifecycle management, risk assessment, resource allocation, and stakeholder communication through realistic scenarios and deliverables.
learning_objectives_assessed: Develop comprehensive project plans using industry-standard methodologies and tools
Analyze and mitigate project risks through systematic risk management processes
Optimize resource allocation and schedule management under realistic constraints
Design effective stakeholder communication and change management strategies
Evaluate project performance using quantitative metrics and KPIs
Apply crisis management and problem-solving techniques to project disruptions
rubric_criteria: Project Planning & Methodology (25 points): Comprehensive WBS with 50+ tasks, realistic timeline using critical path method, appropriate methodology selection (Agile/Waterfall/Hybrid) with clear justification, detailed resource requirements and budget allocation

Risk Management & Quality Assurance (25 points): Identification of 15+ risks with probability/impact assessment, detailed mitigation strategies, contingency planning, quality metrics definition, testing and validation protocols, compliance considerations

Stakeholder Management & Communication (25 points): Stakeholder analysis matrix with influence/interest mapping, communication plan with frequency and methods, meeting structures and governance framework, conflict resolution procedures, change request process

Crisis Response & Adaptability (25 points): Effective response to 3 provided crisis scenarios (budget cut, key personnel loss, scope creep), revised project plans with impact analysis, recovery strategies, lessons learned documentation, performance metrics adjustment
instructions: You are the Project Manager for TechCorp's new customer portal development project with a $500K budget, 15-person cross-functional team, and 6-month deadline. Create a complete project management portfolio including: (1) Project Charter with scope, objectives, and success criteria; (2) Detailed project plan using MS Project or equivalent, including WBS, Gantt chart, and resource allocation; (3) Risk register with qualitative and quantitative analysis; (4) Stakeholder communication matrix and meeting schedules; (5) Quality assurance plan with testing protocols. Midway through the project, you'll receive three crisis scenarios via email requiring immediate response with revised plans and impact assessments. Submit all documents in a professional project folder with executive summary. Use PMI standards and include at least 5 industry-specific templates. Address regulatory compliance for financial data handling and international user base. All deliverables must be client-ready with professional formatting, clear documentation, and actionable recommendations. Include monthly status report templates and project closure checklist.
grading_notes: Evaluate realism and feasibility of timelines - many students underestimate complexity. Look for integration between documents rather than isolated deliverables. Crisis scenario responses should demonstrate true understanding of project interdependencies, not just surface-level solutions. Expect 15-20% of students to struggle with resource leveling and critical path identification. Strong submissions will show evidence of iterative planning and consideration of multiple alternatives. Deduct points for generic templates without customization to the specific project context. Grade distribution typically: 15% A-level (90+), 35% B-level (80-89), 40% C-level (70-79), 10% below C. Common weaknesses include unrealistic risk probability assessments, inadequate stakeholder analysis, and poor integration between planning documents. Award bonus consideration for innovative solutions to resource conflicts and creative stakeholder engagement strategies.

title: Executive Leadership Crisis Management and Strategic Decision-Making Assessment
description: A comprehensive examination evaluating advanced leadership competencies through real-world crisis scenarios, strategic decision-making under pressure, stakeholder management, and organizational transformation leadership. Students demonstrate mastery of executive-level leadership principles through case analysis, strategic planning, and leadership philosophy articulation.
learning_objectives_assessed: Analyze complex organizational crises and develop comprehensive leadership response strategies
Demonstrate advanced stakeholder management and communication skills during high-pressure situations
Design and justify strategic organizational transformation initiatives with measurable outcomes
Articulate and defend a personal executive leadership philosophy grounded in ethical decision-making frameworks
rubric_criteria: Crisis Analysis and Response Strategy (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of crisis dynamics, identifies all key stakeholders, develops comprehensive multi-phase response strategy with clear timelines, contingency plans, and risk mitigation approaches. Shows evidence of systems thinking and anticipates second and third-order effects.

Strategic Decision-Making and Justification (25 points): Makes well-reasoned strategic decisions supported by relevant frameworks and data analysis, clearly articulates decision rationale with consideration of multiple alternatives, demonstrates understanding of resource allocation and implementation challenges, shows awareness of competitive and market implications.

Stakeholder Communication and Change Leadership (25 points): Develops targeted communication strategies for diverse stakeholder groups, demonstrates emotional intelligence and cultural sensitivity, creates compelling change narratives, shows understanding of resistance management and buy-in strategies, includes feedback mechanisms and adaptation processes.

Leadership Philosophy and Ethical Framework (25 points): Articulates coherent personal leadership philosophy with clear ethical foundation, demonstrates integration of multiple leadership theories and approaches, shows evidence of self-awareness and continuous learning mindset, addresses moral courage and values-based decision making in complex situations.
instructions: This assessment consists of three integrated components completed in sequence. First, analyze the provided multi-stakeholder organizational crisis scenario (TechGlobal Inc. data breach and regulatory investigation case study) and develop a comprehensive 90-day crisis response and recovery plan including immediate actions, stakeholder communications, and long-term strategic adjustments. Your response must include executive summary, situation analysis, stakeholder mapping, communication timeline, resource requirements, success metrics, and contingency options. Second, design a strategic organizational transformation initiative that addresses the systemic issues revealed by the crisis. Include vision statement, change strategy, implementation roadmap, resistance management plan, and measurement framework. Third, write a reflective leadership philosophy statement that integrates lessons from the case analysis with your personal leadership approach, addressing how you would maintain ethical standards and stakeholder trust during similar challenges. All responses must be typed, professionally formatted with clear headings and subheadings. Include relevant leadership frameworks and cite at least 8 academic sources. Submit as single PDF document with components clearly labeled. Executive summary should not exceed 2 pages; crisis response plan 8-10 pages; transformation initiative 6-8 pages; leadership philosophy 4-5 pages including references.
grading_notes: Evaluate depth of analysis over breadth - look for sophisticated understanding rather than surface-level coverage of many topics. Strong responses will show integration across all three components rather than treating them as separate exercises. Watch for evidence of practical implementation thinking, not just theoretical knowledge. Common weaknesses include: inadequate stakeholder analysis, unrealistic timelines, lack of contingency planning, weak integration of leadership theory with practice, and insufficient attention to ethical considerations. Grade distribution expectation: 15% A-level (90-100), 25% B-level (80-89), 40% C-level (70-79), 20% below proficient. Partial credit available for each criterion - award points based on demonstrated competency level within each 25-point category. Provide specific feedback on areas for improvement and highlight exceptional insights or innovative approaches.

title: AWS Core Services Business Case Discussion
description: Students will analyze a real-world business scenario and recommend appropriate AWS core services to address specific business needs, demonstrating understanding of service functions, benefits, and cost considerations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify and explain the purpose of AWS core services (EC2, S3, RDS, Lambda, CloudFront)
Match appropriate AWS services to specific business requirements and use cases
Demonstrate understanding of basic AWS pricing models and cost optimization principles
Articulate the business benefits of cloud migration using AWS services
rubric_criteria: Service Selection and Justification (25 points): Correctly identifies 3-4 appropriate AWS services for the scenario with clear reasoning for each choice
Technical Understanding (25 points): Demonstrates accurate understanding of how selected services work and their key features
Business Value Analysis (25 points): Explains specific business benefits, cost implications, and competitive advantages of the proposed solution
Communication and Presentation (25 points): Uses proper AWS terminology, presents ideas clearly, and provides well-structured responses
instructions: You are an AWS solutions consultant advising TechStart Inc., a growing e-commerce company with 50 employees. They currently run their online store on a single physical server that's becoming unreliable and expensive to maintain. The company experiences seasonal traffic spikes (3x normal traffic during holidays), stores customer data and product images, and wants to expand internationally. Their current challenges include: server downtime during peak traffic, slow website loading times for international customers, manual backup processes, and high IT maintenance costs. Your task is to recommend 3-4 AWS core services that would address these challenges. For each service, explain: (1) Which specific business problem it solves, (2) How the service works in simple terms, (3) Why it's better than their current approach, and (4) One cost consideration or benefit. Format your response as a business proposal with clear sections for each recommended service. Use professional language appropriate for business stakeholders who may not be technical experts. Your complete response should be 800-1000 words. Submit your proposal as a typed document (PDF or Word) through the course management system. Include your name and date on the document.
grading_notes: Look for practical service recommendations like EC2 for scalable computing, S3 for storage, CloudFront for global content delivery, and RDS for database management. Students should avoid overly technical explanations and focus on business benefits. Expect 85-90% of students to score 70+ points if they follow instructions. Deduct points for unrealistic service selections, inaccurate technical descriptions, or failure to address the specific business scenario. Common issues include recommending too many advanced services, not connecting services to specific problems, or focusing only on technical features without business context.

title: E-commerce Analytics Strategy & Implementation Portfolio
description: Students will create a comprehensive Google Analytics implementation and optimization strategy for a multi-channel e-commerce business, demonstrating advanced analytics configuration, custom reporting, attribution modeling, and actionable insights generation.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design and implement advanced Google Analytics configurations including Enhanced E-commerce, custom dimensions, and goal funnels
Create sophisticated custom reports, dashboards, and segments for multi-channel attribution analysis
Analyze complex user behavior patterns and conversion paths to identify optimization opportunities
Develop data-driven recommendations using advanced analytics features like cohort analysis and audience insights
Integrate Google Analytics with other marketing tools and demonstrate ROI measurement capabilities
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation (25 points): Proper GA4 configuration with Enhanced E-commerce tracking, custom events, conversions, audiences, and UTM parameter strategy. Must include GTM container export and measurement plan documentation.

Advanced Analysis & Reporting (25 points): Creation of 5+ custom reports/dashboards covering attribution modeling, cohort analysis, funnel visualization, and cross-device tracking. Must demonstrate proficiency with Looker Studio integration.

Strategic Insights & Recommendations (25 points): Data-driven business recommendations with supporting evidence, identified optimization opportunities, A/B testing proposals, and ROI calculations. Must include executive summary with key findings.

Documentation & Presentation (25 points): Professional portfolio presentation including implementation guide, methodology explanation, visual data storytelling, and actionable next steps. Must be client-ready quality.
instructions: Select a real or fictional e-commerce business (minimum 3 product categories, 2 traffic sources). Your portfolio must include: 1) Complete GA4 implementation plan with Enhanced E-commerce setup, custom events (video engagement, scroll tracking, file downloads), and audience configuration exported from Google Tag Manager; 2) Measurement plan documenting all tracked events, custom dimensions, and conversion definitions; 3) Five advanced custom reports in Looker Studio covering attribution analysis, customer lifetime value, product performance, and user journey mapping; 4) Written analysis (1,500-2,000 words) presenting key insights, identifying 3 major optimization opportunities with supporting data, and ROI projections for proposed improvements; 5) Executive dashboard summarizing monthly performance with automated alerts and annotations. Include screenshots, exported reports, and GTM container file. Submit as a professional PDF portfolio with appendices containing raw data exports and configuration files. Ensure all sensitive data is anonymized or use demo account data.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy by reviewing GTM configurations and GA4 setup completeness. Look for proper event tracking implementation, meaningful custom dimensions, and logical conversion setup. Assess analytical depth by examining insight quality, statistical significance understanding, and business context application. Common issues include incomplete Enhanced E-commerce setup, lack of cross-domain tracking consideration, superficial analysis without actionable recommendations, and poor data visualization choices. Expect 20% A grades for exceptional strategic thinking and flawless technical implementation, 40% B grades for solid work with minor gaps, 30% C grades for basic requirements met with limited depth, 10% below C for significant technical errors or missing components. Bonus points (up to 5) for creative advanced features like custom attribution models, BigQuery integration, or predictive analytics applications.

title: Multi-Site Enterprise Network Implementation with Advanced Routing and Security Lab Report
description: Students will design, implement, and document a complete multi-site enterprise network infrastructure incorporating OSPF routing, inter-VLAN routing, site-to-site VPN connectivity, and comprehensive security policies. This assessment evaluates advanced Cisco networking skills through hands-on implementation and detailed technical documentation.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design and implement hierarchical network topologies using advanced routing protocols (OSPF multi-area)
Configure inter-VLAN routing and Layer 3 switching with redundancy protocols (HSRP/VRRP)
Establish secure site-to-site VPN tunnels using IPSec and evaluate tunnel performance
Implement comprehensive network security policies including ACLs, port security, and AAA authentication
Troubleshoot complex network issues using systematic methodology and Cisco diagnostic tools
Document network architecture with professional-grade network diagrams and configuration management
rubric_criteria: Network Implementation and Functionality (25 points): All devices properly configured with OSPF multi-area, inter-VLAN routing operational, VPN tunnels established with full connectivity between sites, all routing tables and adjacencies correct

Security Configuration and Policy Implementation (25 points): Comprehensive ACL implementation restricting appropriate traffic, port security configured on all access ports, AAA authentication functional, VPN encryption parameters properly configured with perfect forward secrecy

Technical Documentation and Network Diagrams (25 points): Professional-quality logical and physical topology diagrams using proper symbols, complete configuration files with meaningful comments, comprehensive IP addressing scheme documentation, detailed change log with timestamps

Troubleshooting Methodology and Problem Resolution (25 points): Systematic approach to identifying and resolving network issues, proper use of diagnostic commands (show, debug, ping, traceroute), documented troubleshooting steps with root cause analysis, verification of solutions with appropriate testing
instructions: You must design and implement a three-site enterprise network using Cisco equipment (physical or Packet Tracer/GNS3). Site A (headquarters) requires 4 VLANs (Management-10, Sales-20, Engineering-30, Guest-40) with 200+ hosts capacity each. Sites B and C (branch offices) require 2 VLANs each with 50+ hosts capacity. Implement OSPF multi-area routing with Area 0 as backbone, Area 1 for Site A, Area 2 for Site B, and Area 3 for Site C. Configure inter-VLAN routing using Layer 3 switches with HSRP for redundancy. Establish IPSec site-to-site VPN tunnels between all sites with AES-256 encryption. Implement security policies including: standard and extended ACLs controlling inter-VLAN traffic, port security on all access ports, SSH access only with AAA authentication using local user database. Your submission must include: complete network topology diagrams (logical and physical), full device configurations with comments explaining each section, IP addressing scheme spreadsheet, OSPF database and routing table captures, VPN tunnel status verification, security policy documentation, and a troubleshooting log documenting at least three network issues encountered and resolved. All configurations must follow Cisco best practices including proper naming conventions, description fields, and security hardening. Submit as a comprehensive PDF report with embedded screenshots and configuration files, plus separate packet capture files demonstrating network functionality.
grading_notes: Evaluate network functionality through systematic testing: verify full connectivity between all VLANs across sites, confirm OSPF adjacencies and proper area assignments, test VPN tunnel establishment and traffic encryption, validate ACL functionality with permitted and denied traffic flows. Common issues to watch for: incorrect OSPF network statements causing adjacency failures, misconfigured interesting traffic for VPN resulting in tunnel flapping, overly restrictive ACLs breaking legitimate network services, improper HSRP configuration causing suboptimal routing. Grade distribution expectations: 90-100 points for fully functional networks with comprehensive documentation, 80-89 points for mostly functional with minor issues or incomplete documentation, 70-79 points for partial functionality with significant configuration errors, below 70 for non-functional networks or major security vulnerabilities. Pay special attention to troubleshooting methodology - students should demonstrate systematic problem-solving approaches rather than random configuration changes. Professional documentation quality is critical at expert level - deduct points for poor diagram quality, missing configuration comments, or inadequate change management practices.

title: Introduction to Programming Concepts and Basic Algorithms Quiz
description: A comprehensive beginner-level quiz assessing fundamental programming concepts including variables, data types, control structures, basic algorithms, and problem-solving approaches using pseudocode and simple code analysis.
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify and explain fundamental programming concepts including variables, data types, and operators
Analyze simple control structures (loops, conditionals) and predict program output
Trace through basic algorithms and understand their step-by-step execution
Apply problem-solving strategies to design simple algorithmic solutions using pseudocode
rubric_criteria: Programming Fundamentals (25 points): Correctly identifies variables, data types, operators, and basic syntax elements. Demonstrates understanding of programming terminology and concepts.
Control Structure Analysis (25 points): Accurately traces through conditional statements and loops. Correctly predicts program output and identifies logical flow patterns.
Algorithm Comprehension (25 points): Successfully traces algorithm execution step-by-step. Shows understanding of algorithm logic and can identify inputs, processes, and outputs.
Problem-solving and Pseudocode (25 points): Creates clear, logical pseudocode solutions. Demonstrates systematic approach to breaking down problems into manageable steps.
instructions:
This quiz contains 20 questions covering fundamental computer science concepts. You have 45 minutes to complete all sections. Read each question carefully and select the best answer or provide the requested solution.

Section A (Questions 1-8): Multiple choice questions on programming fundamentals including variable declaration, data types, and basic operators. Each question is worth 3-4 points.

Section B (Questions 9-14): Code analysis problems where you'll trace through simple programs and predict their output. Show your work by writing intermediate values. Each question is worth 4-5 points.

Section C (Questions 15-18): Algorithm tracing exercises. You'll be given a simple algorithm and asked to trace through its execution with specific inputs. Write each step clearly. Each question is worth 5-6 points.

Section D (Questions 19-20): Problem-solving scenarios requiring pseudocode solutions. Write clear, step-by-step pseudocode for given problems. Focus on logical flow rather than specific programming language syntax. Each question is worth 8-10 points.

Submission Requirements: Submit your completed quiz with all work shown for partial credit consideration. For code tracing problems, include intermediate steps. For pseudocode problems, use clear indentation and logical structure. Ensure your name and student ID are clearly written on all pages.
grading_notes: Grade each section independently using the point distributions specified. Award partial credit for code tracing problems when students show correct intermediate steps even if final answer is wrong. For pseudocode problems, focus on logical correctness rather than syntax perfection - clear thinking process should receive full credit even with minor notation issues. Common issues to watch: students confusing assignment vs. equality operators, off-by-one errors in loop tracing, and incomplete pseudocode logic. Expected grade distribution: 85-100 (A level - 25%), 75-84 (B level - 40%), 65-74 (C level - 25%), below 65 (needs improvement - 10%). Provide specific feedback on incorrect answers to help students understand mistakes.

title: Personal Software Project Showcase Presentation
description: Students will create and present a 10-minute presentation showcasing a simple software project they built, explaining their development process, challenges faced, and lessons learned. This assessment evaluates their ability to communicate technical concepts clearly and reflect on their coding experience.
estimated_time: 3-4 hours (2-3 hours preparation, 10 minutes presentation, 5 minutes Q&A)
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate understanding of basic software development lifecycle concepts
Communicate technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
Reflect critically on problem-solving approaches and learning experiences
Present a functional software solution with proper documentation
rubric_criteria: Project Demonstration (25 points): Successfully demonstrates a working software application with clear functionality, shows understanding of basic programming concepts, and explains how the code works
Development Process Explanation (25 points): Clearly describes the planning, coding, testing, and debugging phases; explains tools and technologies used; discusses project timeline and milestones

Problem-Solving and Reflection (25 points): Identifies specific challenges encountered during development, explains solutions implemented, reflects on what was learned and what would be done differently

Presentation Skills and Communication (25 points): Speaks clearly and confidently, uses appropriate technical vocabulary, engages audience effectively, manages time well, and responds thoughtfully to questions
instructions: Create a 10-minute presentation about a software project you have built (can be from class assignments, personal projects, or tutorial follow-alongs). Your presentation must include: 1) A live demonstration of your working software (2-3 minutes), 2) Explanation of your development process including planning, coding, and testing phases (3-4 minutes), 3) Discussion of at least two specific challenges you faced and how you solved them (2-3 minutes), 4) Reflection on key lessons learned and future improvements (1-2 minutes). Required materials: Laptop with your project ready to run, any necessary slides or visual aids, and a backup plan if technology fails. Your project should be simple but functional - examples include a basic calculator, to-do list app, simple game, or data visualization tool. Focus on explaining your thought process and learning experience rather than complex features. Prepare for 2-3 questions from classmates about your code, design choices, or development experience. Submit your project files and any presentation materials 24 hours before your scheduled presentation date.
grading_notes: Evaluate based on effort and learning demonstration rather than code complexity. Look for genuine understanding vs. copied code by asking follow-up questions about specific implementation choices. Common issues: students rushing through demos, not explaining code clearly, focusing too much on features vs. learning process. Expect grade distribution: 85-100 points for well-prepared presentations with clear explanations, 70-84 for adequate presentations with minor issues, 60-69 for presentations lacking key components or showing limited understanding, below 60 for incomplete or poorly prepared presentations. Encourage peer questions but step in if questions become too advanced for beginner level.

title: E-commerce Customer Behavior Analysis Portfolio
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive analysis of an e-commerce dataset to identify customer purchasing patterns, segment customers, and provide actionable business recommendations. This portfolio demonstrates proficiency in data cleaning, exploratory data analysis, statistical analysis, and data visualization using real-world business data.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply data cleaning and preprocessing techniques to prepare messy datasets for analysis
Conduct exploratory data analysis using appropriate statistical methods and visualizations
Perform customer segmentation using clustering techniques or RFM analysis
Create clear, professional data visualizations that effectively communicate insights
Translate analytical findings into actionable business recommendations
rubric_criteria: Data Preparation & Quality (25 points): Demonstrates thorough data cleaning including handling missing values, outliers, and data type conversions. Documents all preprocessing steps with clear rationale. Creates reproducible code with proper commenting.

Exploratory Data Analysis (25 points): Conducts comprehensive EDA with appropriate descriptive statistics, identifies key patterns and trends, uses multiple visualization types effectively, and formulates relevant hypotheses about customer behavior.

Advanced Analysis & Modeling (25 points): Implements customer segmentation using appropriate techniques (K-means clustering, RFM analysis, or similar). Validates model results, interprets segment characteristics, and demonstrates understanding of analytical methods used.

Communication & Business Impact (25 points): Presents findings in a professional format with clear executive summary, creates compelling visualizations with proper labels and context, provides specific and actionable business recommendations, and demonstrates understanding of business implications.
instructions: Using the provided e-commerce dataset (orders, customers, and products tables), create a comprehensive analysis portfolio consisting of: (1) A Jupyter notebook containing your complete analysis with clear markdown documentation, well-commented code, and inline explanations of your methodology and findings. (2) A 2-page executive summary report targeting business stakeholders, highlighting key insights and recommendations. Your analysis must include: data quality assessment and cleaning procedures; exploratory analysis of sales trends, customer demographics, and product performance; customer segmentation analysis using quantitative methods; at least 5 professional-quality visualizations using libraries like matplotlib, seaborn, or plotly; and 3-5 specific, data-driven business recommendations. Technical requirements: Use Python with pandas, numpy, and scikit-learn; include statistical tests where appropriate; ensure all code is reproducible with clear documentation. Submit both your .ipynb file and PDF executive summary via the course portal. Include a brief reflection (200 words) on challenges encountered and lessons learned. Your analysis should demonstrate understanding of the complete data science workflow from raw data to business insights.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical proficiency alongside business acumen. Look for evidence of critical thinking in data interpretation, not just technical execution. Common issues include: insufficient data cleaning documentation, generic visualizations without business context, clustering without proper validation or interpretation, and recommendations not supported by analysis. Expect grade distribution: 90-100% for exceptional work showing advanced insights and professional presentation; 80-89% for solid analysis meeting all requirements; 70-79% for adequate work with some missing elements or weak business connection; below 70% for incomplete analysis or significant technical errors. Pay particular attention to reproducibility of code and clarity of business communication. Bonus consideration for creative approaches to segmentation or additional external data integration.

title: Comprehensive Project Post-Implementation Analysis Lab Report
description: Students will conduct a detailed analysis of a completed real-world project (successful or failed) by applying advanced project management frameworks, identifying critical success factors, analyzing stakeholder management effectiveness, and developing actionable recommendations for future similar projects.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced project management methodologies and frameworks to analyze complex project scenarios
Evaluate stakeholder management strategies and their impact on project outcomes
Assess risk management effectiveness and identify mitigation strategies
Synthesize project performance data to develop evidence-based recommendations
Demonstrate critical thinking in analyzing project success factors and failure points
rubric_criteria: Project Analysis Framework (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of PM methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, PRINCE2, etc.), correctly applies relevant frameworks to the chosen project, shows deep analysis of project lifecycle phases, and provides comprehensive scope, timeline, and resource analysis

Stakeholder Management Evaluation (25 points): Identifies all key stakeholders and their influence/interest levels, analyzes communication strategies and their effectiveness, evaluates stakeholder engagement throughout project phases, and assesses impact of stakeholder decisions on project outcomes

Risk Assessment and Critical Analysis (25 points): Identifies and categorizes project risks using appropriate tools (risk matrices, SWOT analysis), evaluates risk mitigation strategies implemented, analyzes unexpected issues and their resolution, and demonstrates understanding of risk-reward relationships

Recommendations and Professional Presentation (25 points): Provides actionable, evidence-based recommendations for future projects, demonstrates integration of lessons learned, presents findings in professional report format with proper citations, uses appropriate PM terminology and industry standards
instructions: Select a real-world project from the past 5 years (minimum $1M budget or 50+ team members) from any industry. Your analysis must include: (1) Executive Summary (1 page) highlighting key findings and recommendations; (2) Project Overview (2-3 pages) detailing scope, objectives, timeline, budget, and methodology used; (3) Stakeholder Analysis (2-3 pages) mapping all stakeholders, analyzing their management throughout the project lifecycle; (4) Risk and Issue Analysis (2-3 pages) identifying risks, evaluating mitigation strategies, analyzing critical decision points; (5) Performance Evaluation (2 pages) using KPIs, budget variance, schedule adherence, and quality metrics; (6) Lessons Learned and Recommendations (2-3 pages) providing specific, actionable recommendations for similar future projects. Use minimum 10 credible sources including project documentation, industry reports, and academic literature. Submit as PDF with APA formatting, 12-point font, double-spaced. Include appendices with supporting charts, graphs, or project artifacts. Due dates: Project selection approval (Week 1), Draft outline (Week 2), Final submission (Week 3). Late submissions penalized 10% per day.
grading_notes: Evaluate depth of analysis over breadth - students should demonstrate mastery of PM concepts rather than surface-level coverage. Look for original insights and critical thinking, not just description of events. Common issues include: choosing projects with insufficient public information, failing to connect theory to practice, weak recommendations lacking specificity, and poor integration between sections. Grade distribution expectation: 20% A-level (90-100), 40% B-level (80-89), 30% C-level (70-79), 10% below C-level. Exceptional work shows innovation in approach, uses advanced PM tools/software for analysis, or provides industry-relevant insights. Deduct points for generic recommendations, unsupported claims, or failure to follow formatting requirements. Provide specific feedback on PM terminology usage and professional presentation standards.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Management Assessment
description: Students will analyze a complex organizational crisis scenario, develop a comprehensive leadership response strategy, and demonstrate advanced decision-making skills under pressure. This assessment evaluates strategic thinking, stakeholder management, ethical leadership, and crisis communication capabilities.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate advanced strategic decision-making in high-stakes organizational contexts
Apply ethical leadership principles when managing competing stakeholder interests
Design comprehensive crisis communication strategies for multiple stakeholder groups
Evaluate long-term organizational implications of crisis management decisions
rubric_criteria: Strategic Analysis and Decision-Making (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of crisis dynamics, identifies root causes, evaluates multiple solution pathways, and makes well-reasoned strategic decisions with clear rationale

Stakeholder Management and Communication (25 points): Develops targeted communication strategies for distinct stakeholder groups, anticipates stakeholder reactions, addresses competing interests, and maintains transparency while protecting organizational interests

Ethical Leadership and Values Integration (25 points): Consistently applies ethical frameworks to decision-making, balances short-term pressures with long-term values, demonstrates moral courage, and addresses ethical dilemmas with nuanced understanding

Implementation Planning and Risk Assessment (25 points): Creates detailed, actionable implementation timeline, identifies potential obstacles and mitigation strategies, establishes measurable success metrics, and demonstrates realistic resource allocation
instructions: You are the newly appointed CEO of MediTech Solutions, a mid-sized medical device company. Three simultaneous crises have emerged: (1) A critical product defect affecting 50,000+ patients has been discovered, (2) A data breach has compromised patient information, and (3) Your predecessor's financial misconduct investigation has gone public. Develop a comprehensive leadership response addressing all three crises. Your submission must include: A 3-page executive briefing document outlining your immediate 72-hour action plan, stakeholder impact analysis, and ethical considerations. Create specific communication templates for five key audiences: patients/families, healthcare providers, employees, board of directors, and media/public. Develop a 6-month strategic recovery plan with measurable milestones, resource requirements, and risk mitigation strategies. Include a 2-page reflection analyzing your leadership decision-making process, ethical frameworks applied, and lessons learned. Format: Professional business documents with clear headers, bullet points where appropriate, and executive summary. Submit as single PDF with all components clearly labeled. Assume unlimited budget for crisis response but must justify all major expenditures. Base decisions on realistic regulatory, legal, and market constraints.
grading_notes: Look for evidence of systems thinking - students should recognize interconnections between all three crises rather than treating them separately. Exceptional responses will demonstrate understanding of regulatory requirements (FDA, HIPAA), legal implications, and industry-specific challenges. Common weaknesses include oversimplified solutions, inadequate attention to employee morale during crisis, and unrealistic timelines. Grade distribution should reflect: 90-100 points for responses showing exceptional strategic insight and practical implementation details; 80-89 for solid responses with minor gaps in stakeholder consideration or implementation planning; 70-79 for adequate responses lacking depth in ethical analysis or strategic thinking; Below 70 for responses showing fundamental misunderstanding of leadership responsibilities or crisis management principles. Pay special attention to authenticity of voice - responses should reflect CEO-level thinking, not entry-level perspectives.

title: AWS Three-Tier Web Application Deployment Project
description: Students will design and deploy a basic three-tier web application on AWS using EC2, RDS, and S3 services. This project assesses fundamental AWS service knowledge, basic architecture design, security implementation, and cost optimization principles.
learning_objectives_assessed: Deploy and configure core AWS services (EC2, RDS, S3)
Implement basic AWS security groups and IAM policies
Design a simple multi-tier architecture on AWS
Apply AWS cost optimization best practices
Document AWS infrastructure and justify architectural decisions
rubric_criteria: AWS Service Implementation (25 points): Correctly deploys EC2 instance with web server, creates RDS database with proper configuration, sets up S3 bucket for static assets. All services are functional and properly connected.

Security Configuration (25 points): Implements appropriate security groups with minimal required access, creates IAM user with least-privilege permissions, enables basic RDS encryption, follows AWS security best practices.

Architecture Documentation (25 points): Creates clear architecture diagram showing all components and connections, provides detailed deployment steps that others can follow, explains service choices and configurations with proper justification.

Cost Optimization & Management (25 points): Uses appropriate instance types for workload, implements proper resource tagging strategy, demonstrates understanding of AWS Free Tier limitations, includes cost estimation and cleanup procedures.
instructions: Deploy a three-tier web application on AWS consisting of: 1) Web tier: EC2 instance running a simple web server (Apache/Nginx) serving a basic HTML page, 2) Application tier: Simple backend script (PHP/Python/Node.js) that connects to the database, 3) Data tier: RDS MySQL instance storing basic user data. Use S3 to host static assets (images, CSS files). Create comprehensive documentation including: architecture diagram, step-by-step deployment guide, security configuration details, and cost analysis. Submit a ZIP file containing: deployment scripts/commands, application code, architecture diagram (PDF), written report (2-3 pages) explaining your design decisions, security measures implemented, and cost optimization strategies. Include screenshots of your running application and AWS console showing deployed services. Ensure all resources are properly tagged with your name and project identifier. Provide cleanup instructions to avoid ongoing charges. All work must use AWS Free Tier eligible resources where possible.
grading_notes: Award full points only when all three tiers are demonstrably working together. For security, check that security groups aren't overly permissive (no 0.0.0.0/0 for SSH). Documentation quality significantly impacts grades - look for clear explanations of why specific services were chosen. Cost optimization should show understanding of instance sizing and include actual AWS pricing calculator estimates. Common issues: students often forget to tag resources, leave security groups too open, or don't properly connect application to database. Expect 60% of students to score 75-85 points, with points typically lost on documentation clarity and security configuration. Deduct 10 points if cleanup instructions are missing, as this teaches important cost management.

title: PMP Project Scenario Analysis: Risk Management and Stakeholder Engagement
description: Students will analyze a complex project scenario involving multiple risks and stakeholder conflicts, demonstrating their ability to apply PMP methodologies for risk assessment, stakeholder management, and corrective action planning. This assessment evaluates practical application of PMI frameworks in realistic project situations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply risk identification, analysis, and response planning techniques according to PMI standards
Demonstrate stakeholder identification, analysis, and engagement planning strategies
Evaluate project issues using appropriate PMI tools and techniques
Develop actionable project management solutions aligned with PMI best practices
rubric_criteria: Risk Analysis and Response Planning (25 points): Accurately identifies and categorizes risks using PMI risk taxonomy, applies qualitative/quantitative analysis methods, and develops appropriate response strategies (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept) with clear justifications

Stakeholder Management Strategy (25 points): Correctly identifies all stakeholders, completes stakeholder analysis using power/interest grid or similar PMI tools, and creates comprehensive engagement strategies addressing communication needs and expectations

PMI Framework Application (25 points): Demonstrates proper use of PMI tools, templates, and processes including risk register, stakeholder register, communication management plan elements, and references appropriate PMBOK Guide knowledge areas

Solution Quality and Implementation Planning (25 points): Provides practical, implementable solutions with clear timelines, resource considerations, success metrics, and addresses potential implementation challenges with contingency planning
instructions: You are the project manager for a $2.5M software implementation project at a healthcare organization. The project is 60% complete but facing multiple challenges: key stakeholders are divided on requirements changes, a critical vendor has delivery delays, budget overruns are projected at 15%, and new regulatory compliance requirements have emerged. Using the provided scenario details, complete the following deliverables: 1) Risk Register: Identify minimum 8 risks, categorize by type, assess probability/impact, and define response strategies. 2) Stakeholder Analysis Matrix: Map all stakeholders by power/influence, identify their interests/expectations, and specify engagement approaches. 3) Action Plan: Develop a comprehensive corrective action plan addressing immediate priorities, resource reallocation, timeline adjustments, and communication strategy. 4) PMI Alignment: Reference specific PMBOK Guide processes and knowledge areas used in your analysis. Format your response as a professional project management report with clear sections, executive summary, and appendices for registers/matrices. Use PMI terminology throughout and cite specific tools/techniques. Submit as PDF with all sections clearly labeled and supporting documentation included.
grading_notes: Focus evaluation on practical application rather than theoretical knowledge. Deduct points for generic responses not tied to the specific scenario. Award full points when students demonstrate understanding of PMI frameworks through correct tool usage and terminology. Common issues include: incomplete risk identification (missing positive risks/opportunities), stakeholder analysis lacking depth in engagement strategies, solutions without implementation considerations, and failure to reference appropriate PMBOK processes. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 40% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. Provide specific feedback on PMI framework application and suggest additional study areas for improvement.

title: Google Analytics Implementation Strategy and Data Privacy Compliance Discussion
description: Students will analyze a complex e-commerce business scenario and develop a comprehensive Google Analytics implementation strategy while addressing data privacy regulations, cross-platform tracking challenges, and advanced measurement techniques through structured discussion and peer evaluation.
estimated_time: 3-4 hours (2 hours preparation, 1-2 hours discussion participation)
learning_objectives_assessed: Design advanced Google Analytics implementations including GA4 configuration, custom events, and conversion tracking for complex business scenarios
Evaluate data privacy compliance strategies including GDPR, CCPA, and consent management in analytics implementations
Analyze cross-platform attribution models and recommend measurement frameworks for multi-touchpoint customer journeys
Synthesize analytics insights to propose data-driven business optimization strategies and KPI frameworks
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation Strategy (25 points): Demonstrates mastery of GA4 setup, custom dimensions/metrics, enhanced ecommerce tracking, and advanced configuration options with specific, actionable recommendations

Data Privacy and Compliance Analysis (25 points): Provides comprehensive evaluation of privacy regulations impact, consent management solutions, data retention policies, and anonymization techniques with concrete implementation steps

Cross-Platform Measurement Design (25 points): Develops sophisticated attribution modeling approach, addresses tracking limitations, proposes solutions for app-to-web journeys, and recommends appropriate measurement tools integration

Discussion Quality and Business Application (25 points): Engages meaningfully with peers' proposals, provides constructive feedback with specific examples, and connects technical solutions to measurable business outcomes
instructions: You will receive a detailed case study of 'TechStyle Fashion' - a multi-channel retailer with web, mobile app, and physical stores. Your task is to develop and discuss a comprehensive Google Analytics strategy. PREPARATION (Individual): Analyze the provided business scenario and create a 800-1000 word strategy document addressing: (1) Complete GA4 implementation roadmap including account structure, custom events for key business actions, enhanced ecommerce setup, and audience definitions; (2) Data privacy compliance framework addressing GDPR consent management, data processing agreements, retention policies, and user data rights; (3) Cross-platform measurement strategy covering mobile app integration, offline conversion import, customer lifetime value tracking, and attribution model selection; (4) Success metrics framework with specific KPIs, reporting dashboards, and optimization recommendations. DISCUSSION PHASE: Participate in structured online discussion forum over 48-hour period. Post your initial strategy, then engage with minimum 3 peer responses providing specific feedback on their technical approaches, privacy considerations, and business applications. Respond to feedback on your proposal with refinements or justifications. SUBMISSION: Submit final strategy document incorporating insights from peer discussion, clearly marking revisions made based on feedback. Include reflection paragraph on how peer input influenced your recommendations.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy using current GA4 features and limitations - watch for outdated Universal Analytics references. Strong responses will demonstrate understanding of server-side tracking, Measurement Protocol, and BigQuery integration. For privacy compliance, look for specific mention of consent modes, data processing locations, and user deletion processes rather than generic GDPR statements. Cross-platform measurement should address attribution complexity realistically, not claim perfect tracking solutions. Discussion participation quality matters more than quantity - prioritize depth of analysis over number of posts. Expect 20% of students to score 90-100 (exceptional technical depth), 60% to score 75-89 (solid understanding with minor gaps), 15% to score 60-74 (basic competency with significant omissions), and 5% below 60.
