Common issues include: confusing GA4 with Universal Analytics features, oversimplifying privacy compliance requirements, unrealistic cross-platform tracking expectations, and superficial business recommendations without supporting data rationale.

title: Enterprise Network Infrastructure Design and Implementation Presentation
description: Students will design, implement, and present a comprehensive enterprise network solution for a multi-site organization, demonstrating advanced Cisco networking concepts including EIGRP/OSPF routing, VLANs, QoS, security policies, and network optimization strategies.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design and implement complex routing protocols (EIGRP, OSPF, BGP) for multi-site enterprise networks
Configure advanced switching features including VTP, STP optimization, and inter-VLAN routing
Implement comprehensive network security using ACLs, VPNs, and Cisco security appliances
Design and configure QoS policies for voice, video, and data traffic prioritization
Troubleshoot complex network issues using advanced diagnostic tools and methodologies
Present technical solutions effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
rubric_criteria: Network Design Architecture (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of enterprise network topology, proper protocol selection (EIGRP vs OSPF), redundancy planning, scalability considerations, and adherence to Cisco best practices. Includes detailed network diagrams with proper IP addressing schemes and VLAN design.

Technical Implementation and Configuration (25 points): Shows mastery of advanced Cisco CLI commands, proper configuration of routing protocols, switching features, security policies, and QoS implementations. Includes actual configuration snippets, verification commands, and troubleshooting scenarios with solutions.

Security and Optimization Strategy (25 points): Presents robust security framework including ACL design, VPN implementation, threat mitigation strategies, and network optimization techniques. Demonstrates understanding of Cisco security appliances, network monitoring, and performance tuning methodologies.

Presentation Quality and Professional Communication (25 points): Delivers clear, organized presentation with appropriate technical depth for audience, effective use of visual aids, confident handling of Q&A session, and demonstrates ability to explain complex networking concepts to various stakeholder levels.
instructions: You will assume the role of a senior network engineer presenting a comprehensive network infrastructure solution to company executives and IT leadership. Your scenario: Design a network for a growing company with headquarters (500+ users), two branch offices (100+ users each), and remote workers requiring secure access. Your 20-minute presentation must include: (1) Executive Summary with business justification and ROI analysis, (2) Detailed network architecture diagram showing physical and logical topology, (3) Routing protocol justification and implementation strategy (EIGRP, OSPF, or hybrid approach), (4) VLAN design with security segmentation for different departments, (5) QoS implementation for voice/video traffic, (6) Comprehensive security framework including site-to-site VPNs and remote access solutions, (7) Disaster recovery and redundancy planning, (8) Implementation timeline with phases and milestones, (9) Ongoing maintenance and monitoring strategy. Submit your presentation slides (PDF format) and a technical appendix containing actual Cisco configurations, IP addressing tables, and equipment specifications 48 hours before your presentation date. Be prepared for a 10-minute Q&A session covering technical details, alternative solutions, troubleshooting scenarios, and budget considerations. Your presentation should demonstrate expert-level knowledge while remaining accessible to non-technical executives.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy using current Cisco documentation and best practices. Look for proper subnet calculations, appropriate protocol selections, and realistic implementation timelines. Deduct points for: incorrect CLI syntax, improper VLAN assignments, unrealistic QoS policies, or inadequate security measures. Award bonus consideration for: innovative solutions, cost-effective alternatives, or addressing emerging technologies (SD-WAN, cloud integration). Expect 15% A grades (90-100), 25% B grades (80-89), 40% C grades (70-79), with remaining grades below 70 indicating insufficient mastery of expert-level concepts. During Q&A, assess depth of understanding through follow-up questions about troubleshooting, scalability, and alternative approaches. Common issues include: oversimplified security policies, inadequate redundancy planning, unrealistic bandwidth calculations, and poor justification for protocol choices.

title: Beginning Programmer's Portfolio: Fundamentals Showcase
description: Students will create a comprehensive portfolio demonstrating mastery of fundamental programming concepts through a collection of documented Python programs, reflection essays, and problem-solving demonstrations.
learning_objectives_assessed: Write and execute basic Python programs using variables, data types, and operators
Implement control structures including conditional statements and loops
Create and use functions with parameters and return values
Apply problem-solving strategies to decompose programming challenges
Debug programs and explain error resolution processes
Document code effectively and reflect on learning progress
rubric_criteria: Code Quality and Functionality (25 points): Programs run without errors, demonstrate correct use of syntax, variables, control structures, and functions. Code is clean, well-organized, and follows Python conventions.

Problem-Solving Demonstration (25 points): Portfolio includes clear evidence of problem analysis, algorithm planning, and systematic approach to coding challenges. Shows progression from simple to more complex problems.

Documentation and Comments (25 points): All code includes meaningful comments explaining logic and purpose. Variable names are descriptive. Each program includes a brief description of its function and any assumptions made.

Reflection and Learning Analysis (25 points): Written reflections demonstrate understanding of programming concepts, identify challenges faced and overcome, and show evidence of learning growth throughout the portfolio period.
instructions: Create a digital portfolio containing 8-10 Python programs that showcase your understanding of fundamental programming concepts. Your portfolio must include: (1) Basic Programs (3-4 programs): Simple calculations, user input/output, string manipulation, and basic data type operations. (2) Control Structure Programs (2-3 programs): Programs demonstrating if/else statements, loops (for and while), and nested control structures. (3) Function-Based Programs (2-3 programs): Programs that define and use functions, including functions with parameters and return values. (4) Integrated Challenge Program (1 program): A more comprehensive program combining multiple concepts (e.g., a simple calculator, grade analyzer, or basic game). Each program must include: detailed comments explaining your logic, descriptive variable names, a brief program description at the top, and sample input/output examples. Additionally, submit a 2-3 page reflection paper discussing: your problem-solving approach for each program type, the most challenging concepts and how you overcame difficulties, examples of debugging situations and your solutions, and your overall learning progression. Submit all files in a single ZIP folder with clear file naming (e.g., 'lastname_program1_calculator.py'). Include a README file listing all programs with brief descriptions.
grading_notes: Evaluate portfolios holistically, looking for progression in complexity and understanding. Programs should demonstrate increasing sophistication over time. Accept creative interpretations of requirements as long as learning objectives are met. Common issues to watch: insufficient commenting (deduct from documentation score), programs that don't run (significant deduction from code quality), superficial reflection (impacts reflection score). Grade distribution expectation: 20% A-level work (90-100), 50% B-level work (80-89), 25% C-level work (70-79), 5% below C-level. Provide specific feedback on coding improvements and acknowledge growth demonstrated in reflections. Consider partial credit for non-functional programs that show good problem-solving approach and documentation.

title: Advanced Calculus Applications Quiz: Optimization and Related Rates
description: A comprehensive assessment evaluating students' ability to solve complex optimization problems, related rates problems, and apply calculus concepts to real-world scenarios involving multiple variables, constraints, and dynamic systems.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply derivative concepts to solve multi-step optimization problems with constraints
Analyze and solve related rates problems involving multiple changing variables
Interpret calculus results in real-world contexts and communicate mathematical reasoning
Demonstrate proficiency in advanced differentiation techniques including implicit differentiation and chain rule
rubric_criteria: Problem Setup and Mathematical Modeling (25 points): Correctly identifies variables, establishes relationships, writes appropriate equations, and clearly defines what needs to be optimized or found
Mathematical Execution and Techniques (25 points): Demonstrates accurate use of differentiation rules, algebraic manipulation, equation solving, and applies calculus theorems correctly

Solution Process and Critical Analysis (25 points): Shows logical progression through multi-step solutions, identifies critical points, verifies solutions using second derivative test or other appropriate methods, checks reasonableness of answers

Communication and Interpretation (25 points): Provides clear explanations of mathematical reasoning, interprets results in context of original problem, uses proper mathematical notation and terminology, presents work in organized manner
instructions:
This quiz consists of 4 comprehensive problems worth 25 points each. You have 90 minutes to complete all problems. Show all work clearly and justify your reasoning for full credit. Partial credit will be awarded based on correct mathematical processes even if final answers are incorrect. Use proper mathematical notation throughout your solutions.

Problem 1: Optimization - A company needs to design a cylindrical container with a fixed volume of 1000 cubic centimeters that minimizes the amount of material used. Find the dimensions that minimize surface area and explain why your solution is optimal.

Problem 2: Related Rates - A spherical balloon is being inflated at a rate of 20 cubic inches per minute. At what rate is the radius increasing when the balloon has a diameter of 12 inches? Additionally, find the rate at which the surface area is increasing at this moment.

Problem 3: Applied Optimization - A farmer has 800 feet of fencing and wants to create a rectangular enclosure against an existing barn wall (which requires no fencing). The enclosure will be divided into 3 equal sections by two additional parallel fences. Determine the dimensions that maximize the total enclosed area.

Problem 4: Complex Related Rates - A ladder 15 feet long is leaning against a vertical wall. The bottom of the ladder is sliding away from the wall at a rate of 2 feet per second. Find the rate at which the angle between the ladder and the ground is changing when the bottom of the ladder is 9 feet from the wall.

Calculators are permitted. Box your final numerical answers and include appropriate units. If you make an error early in a problem, continue with your work as you may still receive substantial partial credit for correct methods.
grading_notes: Award points progressively through each problem rather than all-or-nothing scoring. Common issues to watch for: incorrect setup of constraint equations (deduct 5-8 points), sign errors in derivatives (deduct 3-5 points), failure to verify optimization results (deduct 5-7 points), missing units (deduct 2-3 points), unclear or missing explanations (deduct 5-10 points). Expected grade distribution: 15% A grades (90-100), 25% B grades (80-89), 35% C grades (70-79), 20% D grades (60-69), 5% F grades (below 60). Be generous with partial credit for correct mathematical reasoning even with computational errors. Look for evidence of understanding calculus concepts rather than just correct final answers. Students should demonstrate clear problem-solving strategies and mathematical communication skills.

title: Personal Task Manager Application - Programming Fundamentals Exam
description: Students will design and implement a simple command-line task manager application demonstrating core programming concepts including variables, control structures, functions, and basic data handling. The assessment evaluates practical application of fundamental programming skills through a real-world project.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply fundamental programming constructs (variables, loops, conditionals) to solve practical problems
Design and implement functions with appropriate parameters and return values
Demonstrate proper code organization, commenting, and basic debugging skills
Handle user input validation and implement basic error handling strategies
rubric_criteria: Core Functionality (25 points): Application successfully adds, displays, marks complete, and deletes tasks with proper data persistence between menu selections
Code Structure & Functions (25 points): Well-organized code with at least 4 properly implemented functions, clear separation of concerns, and appropriate use of parameters/return values
User Interface & Input Validation (25 points): Clear menu system, helpful prompts, proper handling of invalid inputs, and appropriate user feedback messages
Code Quality & Documentation (25 points): Consistent naming conventions, meaningful variable names, adequate comments explaining logic, proper indentation and formatting
instructions: Create a command-line Personal Task Manager application in your chosen programming language (Python, Java, or C++). Your program must include: 1) A main menu with options to Add Task, View All Tasks, Mark Task Complete, Delete Task, and Exit; 2) Task storage using arrays/lists with at least task description and completion status; 3) Input validation for menu choices and task operations; 4) Clear user prompts and feedback messages. Technical requirements: Implement at least 4 functions (add_task, display_tasks, mark_complete, delete_task), use appropriate loops for menu system, include conditional logic for task management, and add comments explaining your code logic. Submit a single source code file with your name and student ID in header comments. Include a brief comment block describing how to run your program. Test your application thoroughly before submission - it should handle invalid menu choices gracefully and maintain task data throughout the session. File naming convention: lastname_firstname_taskmanager.py/java/cpp. Upload to the course portal by the specified deadline.
grading_notes: Test each submission by running the program and verifying all menu options work correctly. Common issues to deduct points for: programs that crash on invalid input (-5 points), missing required functions (-10 points per function), poor or missing comments (-5-10 points), non-functional core features (-15-25 points depending on severity). Award partial credit for incomplete but well-structured code. Grade distribution expectation: 20% A-level (90-100), 40% B-level (80-89), 30% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. Focus on functionality over advanced features - this is a beginner assessment emphasizing fundamentals over optimization.

title: Complex Project Recovery Case Study Presentation
description: Students will analyze a real-world failed or troubled project, develop a comprehensive recovery strategy, and present their findings to demonstrate mastery of advanced project management principles including risk management, stakeholder engagement, resource optimization, and change management.
learning_objectives_assessed: Analyze complex project failures using advanced project management frameworks and methodologies
Develop comprehensive project recovery strategies incorporating risk management, resource reallocation, and stakeholder management
Apply critical thinking to evaluate trade-offs between scope, time, cost, and quality in crisis situations
Demonstrate professional communication skills in presenting complex project management solutions to executive stakeholders
rubric_criteria: Project Analysis & Problem Identification (25 points): Demonstrates thorough analysis of project failure using multiple PM frameworks (PMBOK, PRINCE2, Agile), identifies root causes beyond surface symptoms, applies appropriate analytical tools (fishbone diagram, 5-whys, failure mode analysis)

Recovery Strategy Development (25 points): Presents comprehensive, realistic recovery plan with detailed timeline, resource requirements, risk mitigation strategies, stakeholder communication plan, and measurable success criteria aligned with business objectives

Application of PM Methodologies (25 points): Correctly applies advanced project management concepts including earned value management, critical path analysis, stakeholder matrix, change management principles, and demonstrates understanding of methodology selection rationale

Presentation Quality & Executive Communication (25 points): Delivers professional presentation suitable for C-level audience, uses appropriate visual aids and data visualization, responds effectively to questions, maintains time limits, demonstrates confidence and subject matter expertise
instructions: Select a well-documented failed or troubled project from the past 10 years (examples: Berlin Airport, Healthcare.gov, London Olympics initial planning, major ERP implementations). Your presentation must include: (1) Executive Summary (2 minutes): Project overview and key recommendations; (2) Situation Analysis (5-7 minutes): Original project scope, timeline, budget, stakeholder analysis, and detailed failure analysis using PM frameworks; (3) Recovery Strategy (8-10 minutes): Comprehensive recovery plan including revised scope, timeline, budget, risk management, stakeholder engagement, and change management approach; (4) Implementation Roadmap (3-5 minutes): Detailed 90-day action plan with milestones, resource allocation, and success metrics. Use professional presentation software with clear visual aids, charts, and diagrams. Include a one-page executive summary handout for the audience. Presentations will be delivered to a panel simulating executive stakeholders who will ask challenging questions about feasibility, costs, and risks. Cite minimum 8 credible sources including PM literature, case studies, and industry reports. Submit presentation slides and executive summary 24 hours before presentation date.
grading_notes: Evaluate presentations against executive-level expectations - focus on strategic thinking over tactical details. Look for evidence of deep PM knowledge application, not just theoretical understanding. Common weaknesses include: oversimplified root cause analysis, unrealistic recovery timelines, insufficient stakeholder consideration, poor risk assessment. Grade distribution should reflect advanced level: 90-100 (exceptional strategic insight and flawless execution), 80-89 (strong analysis with minor gaps), 70-79 (adequate understanding with significant improvement areas), below 70 (fundamental PM concept misunderstandings). Pay special attention to Q&A responses as they reveal true understanding versus memorized content.

title: Strategic Leadership Portfolio: Crisis Management and Organizational Transformation
description: Students develop a comprehensive portfolio documenting their leadership philosophy, crisis management strategy, and organizational transformation plan through real-world case analysis, reflective practice, and strategic planning exercises.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate advanced strategic thinking and decision-making under uncertainty
Apply transformational leadership principles to drive organizational change
Evaluate and synthesize multiple leadership theories in complex scenarios
Design evidence-based solutions for crisis management and stakeholder engagement
rubric_criteria: Strategic Analysis & Crisis Response Plan (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of crisis leadership, provides comprehensive stakeholder analysis, develops actionable response strategies with clear timelines and contingencies

Leadership Philosophy Integration (25 points): Articulates well-developed personal leadership philosophy supported by multiple theoretical frameworks, shows clear evolution of thinking, connects theory to practice through specific examples

Organizational Transformation Strategy (25 points): Designs realistic change management plan with measurable outcomes, addresses resistance strategies, incorporates cultural considerations and ethical implications

Reflection & Professional Growth (25 points): Provides deep self-assessment of leadership capabilities, identifies specific development areas with concrete action plans, demonstrates metacognitive awareness of leadership impact
instructions: Create a professional portfolio containing four interconnected components: (1) Crisis Leadership Case Study - Select a real organizational crisis from the past 5 years and develop a 10-page alternative response strategy, including stakeholder mapping, communication plan, and recovery timeline. (2) Personal Leadership Philosophy - Write a 5-page manifesto integrating at least five leadership theories with your personal experiences and values. Include specific examples of how this philosophy would guide decision-making. (3) Transformation Blueprint - Design a comprehensive change initiative for a struggling organization, including 15-page implementation plan with metrics, timeline, and risk mitigation strategies. (4) Reflective Leadership Journal - Document your leadership growth through 8-10 entries (2-3 pages each) analyzing real leadership situations you've observed or participated in. Portfolio must be professionally formatted, include executive summary, table of contents, and bibliography with minimum 15 scholarly sources. Submit as PDF with appendices containing supporting documents, templates, or tools you've developed. All work must be original with proper citations.
grading_notes: Evaluate portfolios holistically, looking for integration across components rather than treating sections independently. Excellence (90-100) shows original thinking, sophisticated analysis, and practical applicability. Proficient (80-89) meets all requirements with good analysis but limited innovation. Developing (70-79) shows understanding but lacks depth or has significant gaps. Inadequate (below 70) fails to demonstrate expert-level leadership thinking. Common issues include: superficial crisis analysis without considering long-term implications, leadership philosophy that merely summarizes theories without personal integration, transformation plans lacking realistic implementation details, and reflection that focuses on description rather than analysis. Expect 15% A grades, 35% B grades, 40% C grades, 10% below C for typical graduate cohorts.

title: AWS EC2 Web Application Deployment Lab Report
description: Students will deploy a simple web application on AWS EC2, configure security groups, and document their implementation process, challenges encountered, and lessons learned in a comprehensive lab report.
estimated_time: 3-4 hours (2 hours lab work + 1-2 hours report writing)
learning_objectives_assessed: Deploy and configure EC2 instances using AWS Management Console
Implement basic AWS security best practices including security groups and key pairs
Demonstrate understanding of AWS core services and their interconnections
Document technical processes and troubleshoot common cloud deployment issues
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation (25 points): Successful EC2 instance launch, web application deployment, proper security group configuration, and functional public access to the application
Documentation Quality (25 points): Clear step-by-step process documentation with screenshots, accurate technical details, and proper formatting following lab report structure
Problem-Solving Analysis (25 points): Identification and explanation of challenges encountered, troubleshooting steps taken, solutions implemented, and alternative approaches considered
AWS Knowledge Demonstration (25 points): Accurate use of AWS terminology, explanation of services used, understanding of security implications, and discussion of cost considerations
instructions:
Complete the following AWS EC2 deployment lab and submit a comprehensive report documenting your experience. 

**Lab Requirements:**
1. Launch an Amazon EC2 t2.micro instance running Amazon Linux 2
2. Configure security groups to allow HTTP (port 80) and SSH (port 22) access
3. Create and download a new key pair for secure access
4. Connect to your instance via SSH
5. Install and configure Apache web server
6. Create a simple HTML page displaying your name and the current date
7. Verify public access to your web application
8. Terminate the instance after completion

**Report Structure (4-6 pages):**
- **Introduction:** Objective and AWS services overview
- **Methodology:** Step-by-step implementation process with screenshots
- **Results:** Evidence of successful deployment (URLs, screenshots of running application)
- **Challenges & Solutions:** Problems encountered and how you resolved them
- **Analysis:** Security considerations, cost implications, and lessons learned
- **Conclusion:** Summary of key takeaways and potential improvements

**Submission Requirements:**
- PDF format report with embedded screenshots
- Include AWS service screenshots showing your resources
- All instances must be terminated before submission
- Submit via learning management system by specified deadline
- File naming: LastName_FirstName_AWS_Lab_Report.pdf
grading_notes: Evaluate based on both practical AWS skills and documentation quality. Look for evidence of actual hands-on work through screenshots and specific details that couldn't be copied from tutorials. Common deduction areas: missing screenshots (5-10 points), failure to terminate resources (10 points), generic troubleshooting without specific examples (5-15 points), and poor documentation structure (10-15 points). Expect 70% of students to score 75-90 points, with full points requiring exceptional documentation and clear demonstration of deeper AWS understanding. Verify screenshot authenticity by checking for consistent AWS account details and realistic timestamps.

title: Project Risk Management and Change Control Assessment
description: Students will demonstrate their understanding of PMP risk management processes and change control procedures through scenario-based questions, risk analysis calculations, and change request evaluations. This assessment covers risk identification, qualitative/quantitative analysis, response strategies, and integrated change control processes.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply risk management planning and identification techniques to project scenarios
Calculate and interpret qualitative and quantitative risk analysis metrics
Evaluate appropriate risk response strategies for given situations
Analyze change requests and determine proper change control procedures
Integrate risk management with project schedule and cost baselines
rubric_criteria: Risk Identification and Analysis (25 points): Accurately identifies project risks, correctly applies probability/impact assessments, and demonstrates understanding of risk register components and Expected Monetary Value (EMV) calculations

Risk Response Strategy Selection (25 points): Selects appropriate risk response strategies (avoid, transfer, mitigate, accept) with clear justification, and develops realistic contingency and fallback plans for high-priority risks

Change Control Process Application (25 points): Correctly evaluates change requests against project baselines, demonstrates understanding of Change Control Board (CCB) processes, and assesses impact on scope, schedule, and budget

Integration and Communication (25 points): Shows how risk management integrates with other knowledge areas, demonstrates proper stakeholder communication protocols, and maintains consistency with project management plan updates
instructions: This assessment consists of three sections that must be completed within 90 minutes. Section A contains 15 multiple-choice questions covering risk management terminology, processes, and change control procedures (30 points). Section B requires you to analyze a project scenario, identify at least 5 risks, complete a probability/impact matrix, and calculate EMV for three quantitative risks (40 points). Show all calculations and provide brief justifications for probability and impact ratings. Section C presents three change request scenarios where you must evaluate each request, recommend approval/rejection with rationale, and describe the change control process steps (30 points). Use official PMP terminology throughout your responses. Submit your answers in the provided answer sheet format, clearly labeling each section and numbering your responses. For calculations, round to the nearest dollar. Written responses should be concise but comprehensive, typically 2-3 sentences per justification. No external resources are permitted during this assessment. Ensure your work is legible and organized, as partial credit depends on clear demonstration of your reasoning process.
grading_notes: Use the 4-point scale for each criterion: Exemplary (90-100%), Proficient (80-89%), Developing (70-79%), Inadequate (below 70%). Common issues include: confusing risk categories with risk events, incorrect EMV calculations (watch for sign errors), selecting inappropriate response strategies, and not following proper change control sequence. Partial credit available for showing work on calculations even if final answer is incorrect. Look for proper use of PMP terminology and evidence of understanding process integration. Grade distribution should typically follow: 20% A-level, 50% B-level, 25% C-level, 5% below C-level for intermediate students.

title: E-commerce Website Analytics Implementation and Optimization Project
description: Students will implement Google Analytics 4 (GA4) for a simulated e-commerce website, configure advanced tracking, analyze 30 days of provided data, and present actionable insights with optimization recommendations to improve conversion rates and user experience.
learning_objectives_assessed: Configure and implement GA4 with enhanced e-commerce tracking including custom events and conversions
Create and interpret custom reports, segments, and audiences for business decision-making
Analyze user behavior patterns, conversion funnels, and attribution models to identify optimization opportunities
Develop data-driven recommendations using GA4 insights to improve website performance and ROI
rubric_criteria: GA4 Implementation and Configuration (25 points): Correct setup of GA4 property, enhanced e-commerce tracking, custom events (purchase, add_to_cart, begin_checkout), goal/conversion configuration, and proper GTM integration with documented implementation steps

Data Analysis and Interpretation (25 points): Accurate analysis of user acquisition channels, behavior flow, conversion funnel performance, audience segmentation, and attribution model comparison with proper use of GA4 metrics and dimensions

Custom Reporting and Visualization (25 points): Creation of meaningful custom reports, effective use of segments and comparisons, proper dashboard setup with relevant KPIs, and clear data visualization that supports business objectives

Strategic Recommendations and Presentation (25 points): Well-supported optimization recommendations based on data insights, clear presentation of findings with professional visualizations, actionable next steps with expected impact, and demonstration of advanced GA4 features
instructions: You will work with a provided demo e-commerce website (or create a test site) to implement comprehensive Google Analytics 4 tracking and analysis. DELIVERABLES: (1) GA4 Implementation Documentation - Provide screenshots and step-by-step documentation of your GA4 setup including property configuration, enhanced e-commerce implementation, custom event tracking for key user actions, and Google Tag Manager integration. Include your measurement ID and explain your tagging strategy. (2) Analytics Dashboard - Create a custom dashboard with 8-10 key performance indicators relevant to e-commerce success. Include segments for different user types and traffic sources. Export and submit dashboard screenshots with explanations. (3) Data Analysis Report - Using the provided 30-day dataset, analyze user acquisition, behavior, and conversion patterns. Include funnel analysis, audience insights, channel performance comparison, and attribution analysis. Minimum 1,500 words with supporting charts/tables. (4) Optimization Recommendations Presentation - Deliver a 10-slide presentation with specific, data-driven recommendations for improving site performance. Include projected impact estimates and implementation priorities. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS: Use GA4 (not Universal Analytics), implement at least 5 custom events, create minimum 3 audience segments, utilize at least 2 attribution models for comparison, and demonstrate exploration reports usage. Submit all work in a shared Google Drive folder with proper file naming conventions. Include a brief video walkthrough (5-7 minutes) of your GA4 setup and key findings.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy of GA4 implementation by checking if students correctly configured enhanced e-commerce events and conversions - common errors include improper event parameter naming and missing required e-commerce fields. For data analysis, look for proper interpretation of metrics (sessions vs. users, conversion rates, attribution windows) and meaningful insights rather than just data description. Quality presentations should connect data findings directly to specific business recommendations with realistic implementation timelines. Expect 15-20% of students to struggle with GTM integration - provide additional support resources. Grade distribution typically: 20% A-level (90-100), 40% B-level (80-89), 30% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70. Bonus points (up to 5) can be awarded for advanced features like custom dimensions, calculated metrics, or API usage demonstrations.

title: Enterprise Network Design and Implementation Expert Assessment
description: Students will design, configure, and troubleshoot a complex multi-site enterprise network using advanced Cisco technologies including OSPF, BGP, MPLS VPN, network security, and Quality of Service. This comprehensive assessment evaluates mastery of enterprise-level networking concepts through practical implementation and analysis.
learning_objectives_assessed: Design and implement scalable enterprise network architectures using hierarchical models
Configure and optimize advanced routing protocols (OSPF, BGP) for multi-area and multi-AS environments
Implement MPLS Layer 3 VPN solutions for secure site-to-site connectivity
Deploy comprehensive network security measures including firewalls, VPNs, and access control
Configure and manage Quality of Service (QoS) policies for traffic prioritization
Perform advanced network troubleshooting using systematic methodologies and diagnostic tools
Analyze network performance metrics and recommend optimization strategies
rubric_criteria: Network Design and Architecture (25 points): Demonstrates expert-level understanding of hierarchical network design principles, appropriate technology selection for requirements, scalability considerations, and comprehensive documentation of design decisions with proper justifications

Routing Protocol Implementation (25 points): Correctly configures multi-area OSPF with appropriate area types, implements BGP with proper route filtering and path manipulation, demonstrates advanced routing concepts including redistribution and route summarization

MPLS VPN and Advanced Services Configuration (25 points): Successfully implements MPLS Layer 3 VPN with proper PE-CE routing, configures QoS policies with classification and queuing mechanisms, implements network security measures including firewalls and access control lists

Troubleshooting and Optimization (25 points): Identifies and resolves complex network issues using systematic approaches, provides detailed analysis of network performance problems, recommends and justifies optimization strategies with supporting evidence and metrics
instructions: You are tasked with designing and implementing a complete enterprise network solution for a multi-national corporation with headquarters and three branch offices. Using GNS3 or Packet Tracer, create a network topology that includes: 1) Core-distribution-access hierarchy with redundancy, 2) Multi-area OSPF configuration with at least 3 areas including backbone area, 3) BGP implementation for internet connectivity and inter-AS communication, 4) MPLS Layer 3 VPN connecting all sites with appropriate VRF configuration, 5) Comprehensive security implementation including zone-based firewalls and IPSec VPNs, 6) QoS policies supporting voice, video, and data traffic with appropriate classification and queuing. Submit your complete configuration files, network topology diagram with IP addressing scheme, and a detailed technical report (2000-2500 words) explaining your design decisions, configuration rationale, and testing methodology. Include screenshots of verification commands demonstrating proper operation of all implemented technologies. Additionally, provide a troubleshooting scenario analysis where you identify and resolve three complex network issues, documenting your systematic approach and resolution steps. All submissions must be original work with proper citation of any reference materials used.
grading_notes: Evaluate configurations for technical accuracy and best practices - deduct points for security vulnerabilities or inefficient implementations. Assess design documentation for clarity and professional presentation - look for logical flow and proper technical terminology. Common issues include: inadequate route summarization, missing redundancy considerations, improper QoS classification, and insufficient security hardening. Grade distribution should follow: 90-100 (demonstrates mastery with innovative solutions), 80-89 (solid implementation with minor gaps), 70-79 (basic requirements met with some technical errors), below 70 (significant gaps in understanding or implementation). Pay special attention to troubleshooting methodology - students should demonstrate systematic approaches rather than random configuration changes. Partial credit available for each criterion, but require minimum functionality thresholds to receive passing grades on major components.

title: Predictive Analytics Project Presentation: Customer Churn Analysis
description: Students will conduct a complete data science project analyzing customer churn patterns using a provided telecommunications dataset. They must present their methodology, findings, and business recommendations in a 15-minute presentation followed by a 5-minute Q&A session.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply end-to-end data science methodology from data exploration to model deployment recommendations
Evaluate and compare multiple machine learning algorithms for classification problems
Communicate technical findings effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Interpret model performance metrics and provide actionable business insights
rubric_criteria: Data Exploration & Preprocessing (25 points): Demonstrates thorough exploratory data analysis with appropriate visualizations, identifies and handles missing values/outliers, performs feature engineering, and explains preprocessing decisions clearly

Model Development & Evaluation (25 points): Implements and compares at least 3 different classification algorithms, uses appropriate train/validation/test splits, applies proper cross-validation techniques, and correctly interprets performance metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, AUC-ROC)

Business Insights & Recommendations (25 points): Translates technical findings into clear business value propositions, identifies key churn indicators and their business implications, provides specific actionable recommendations for customer retention, and estimates potential ROI of proposed solutions

Presentation Quality & Technical Communication (25 points): Delivers clear, well-structured presentation within time limits, uses effective visualizations and slides, demonstrates deep understanding through Q&A responses, and appropriately balances technical depth with accessibility for business audience
instructions: You will analyze the provided telecommunications customer dataset to build predictive models for customer churn. Your presentation must include: (1) Executive Summary highlighting key findings and recommendations, (2) Data exploration section showing dataset characteristics, feature distributions, and churn patterns, (3) Methodology section explaining your modeling approach, algorithms tested, and evaluation strategy, (4) Results section comparing model performances with visualizations of key metrics, (5) Business Impact section translating findings into retention strategies with estimated cost/benefit analysis, and (6) Implementation Roadmap outlining next steps for deployment. Technical requirements: Use Python/R with appropriate libraries, create at least 5 meaningful visualizations, test minimum 3 algorithms (logistic regression, random forest, and one advanced method), and include feature importance analysis. Submit your presentation slides (PDF), complete code notebook, and a 2-page executive summary 24 hours before presentation. Presentations will be 15 minutes plus 5 minutes Q&A. Dress professionally and prepare for questions about methodology choices, business implications, and technical implementation details.
grading_notes: Grade holistically across technical competency and communication skills. Look for students who go beyond basic analysis to provide genuine business insights. Common issues include: oversimplified EDA, inappropriate metric selection for imbalanced datasets, failure to address overfitting, unrealistic business recommendations, and poor time management during presentation. Expect grade distribution: A-level (90-100): comprehensive analysis with novel insights; B-level (80-89): solid technical work with adequate business application; C-level (70-79): meets minimum requirements but lacks depth; Below 70: significant technical or communication deficiencies. Deduct 5 points for late submission, 10 points for exceeding time limits. Encourage questions during Q&A that test understanding of assumptions, limitations, and alternative approaches.

title: Advanced Mathematical Modeling Portfolio: Real-World Problem Solutions
description: Students create a comprehensive portfolio demonstrating mastery of advanced mathematical concepts through three original problem-solving projects spanning calculus, statistics, and discrete mathematics, with complete solutions, analysis, and reflection.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced calculus concepts (derivatives, integrals, differential equations) to solve real-world optimization and modeling problems
Demonstrate statistical analysis skills including hypothesis testing, regression analysis, and interpretation of data
Utilize discrete mathematics concepts (graph theory, combinatorics, logic) in practical applications
Communicate mathematical reasoning clearly through written explanations and visual representations
Reflect critically on problem-solving approaches and mathematical thinking processes
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Accuracy and Rigor (25 points): Correct application of formulas, theorems, and procedures; accurate calculations; proper mathematical notation; logical progression of steps

Problem Selection and Real-World Application (25 points): Appropriate complexity level; genuine real-world relevance; clear connection between mathematical concepts and practical applications; originality in problem choice

Communication and Presentation (25 points): Clear written explanations; effective use of graphs, charts, and visual aids; proper mathematical language; organized structure; professional presentation quality

Critical Analysis and Reflection (25 points): Thorough analysis of results; discussion of limitations and assumptions; alternative approaches considered; meaningful reflection on learning process and mathematical insights
instructions: Create a portfolio containing three distinct mathematical projects, each focusing on a different advanced area: (1) Calculus-based optimization or modeling problem, (2) Statistical analysis project using real data, and (3) Discrete mathematics application. For each project, include: problem statement and rationale for selection, complete mathematical solution with all work shown, visual representations (graphs, charts, diagrams), analysis of results including real-world implications, and discussion of alternative approaches. Additionally, write a 2-page reflective essay discussing your problem-solving strategies, challenges encountered, and insights gained about mathematical thinking. Format requirements: typed solutions with hand-written mathematical work clearly scanned/photographed, minimum 15 pages total excluding appendices, APA citation format for any sources used. Submit as a single PDF file with clear section dividers and a table of contents. Include a cover page with your name, date, and brief abstract summarizing your three projects. All work must be original, though you may build upon existing real-world scenarios. Data sources must be cited and datasets included in appendices.
grading_notes: Evaluate mathematical accuracy first - projects with fundamental errors cannot exceed 70% total score. Look for evidence of advanced thinking beyond basic application of formulas. Strong portfolios will show connections between different mathematical areas and demonstrate creativity in problem selection. Common issues include: insufficient complexity in chosen problems, lack of real-world context, poor explanation of reasoning steps, and superficial reflection. Excellent portfolios (90-100) should demonstrate original insight and sophisticated mathematical reasoning. Good portfolios (80-89) show solid understanding with minor gaps. Acceptable portfolios (70-79) meet basic requirements but lack depth or contain some errors. Below 70 indicates significant deficiencies in mathematical understanding or incomplete work. Provide specific feedback on each rubric criterion and suggest areas for mathematical growth.

title: Advanced Electromagnetic Induction Laboratory Investigation
description: Students design and conduct a comprehensive investigation of electromagnetic induction phenomena using Faraday's and Lenz's laws, analyze complex magnetic field interactions, and present findings in a formal research-style laboratory report with quantitative error analysis and theoretical modeling.
estimated_time: 6-8 hours (3 hours lab work, 3-5 hours analysis and writing)
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply Faraday's law and Lenz's law to predict and calculate induced EMF in complex electromagnetic systems
Design controlled experiments with appropriate variables, controls, and measurement techniques for electromagnetic phenomena
Perform advanced error analysis including propagation of uncertainties and statistical analysis of experimental data
Evaluate theoretical models against experimental results and propose explanations for discrepancies
Communicate complex physics findings through professional scientific writing with proper citations and visual representations
rubric_criteria: Experimental Design and Methodology (25 points): Clear hypothesis formulation, appropriate variable identification and control, detailed procedure with safety considerations, proper equipment selection, and innovative experimental approach demonstrating deep understanding of electromagnetic principles

Data Collection and Analysis (25 points): Systematic data recording with appropriate precision, comprehensive error analysis including uncertainty propagation, statistical treatment of multiple trials, effective use of graphical analysis, and comparison of multiple experimental scenarios

Theoretical Application and Modeling (25 points): Accurate application of Faraday's and Lenz's laws with mathematical derivations, quantitative predictions compared to experimental results, identification and explanation of limiting factors, and integration of electromagnetic theory with observed phenomena

Scientific Communication and Conclusions (25 points): Professional report structure following physics journal format, clear and precise scientific writing, effective data visualization with proper figures and tables, evidence-based conclusions with discussion of broader implications, and appropriate citation of relevant physics literature
instructions: Design and execute an original investigation exploring electromagnetic induction using available laboratory equipment (solenoids, magnets, oscilloscopes, function generators, etc.). Your study must examine at least three different variables affecting induced EMF (e.g., magnetic field strength, coil geometry, relative motion parameters). Begin with a clear research question and testable hypothesis. Develop a detailed experimental protocol ensuring proper controls and multiple trials for statistical validity. Collect quantitative data with appropriate precision, documenting all measurements and observations. Perform comprehensive error analysis including instrumental uncertainties and random errors. Compare experimental results with theoretical predictions using Faraday's law calculations. Submit a complete laboratory report (8-12 pages) including: abstract, introduction with relevant physics background, detailed methodology, results section with data tables and graphs, discussion analyzing theoretical vs. experimental findings, conclusion addressing your research question, and references. Include raw data sheets and calculation examples in appendices. Reports must demonstrate graduate-level scientific writing and critical analysis. Due one week after laboratory session. Submit both hard copy and digital version with all supporting data files.
grading_notes: Evaluate experimental sophistication and originality - look for creative approaches beyond basic demonstrations. Strong reports will show evidence of preliminary research and connection to current applications. In methodology assessment, verify that safety protocols are addressed and that experimental design actually tests the stated hypothesis. For data analysis, expect proper significant figures, error bars on graphs, and discussion of systematic vs. random errors. Common weaknesses include insufficient trials, lack of control variables, and failure to address discrepancies between theory and experiment. Theoretical application should go beyond simple formula substitution to demonstrate conceptual understanding. Grade distribution typically: 15% earn A grades with exceptional insight and methodology, 35% earn B grades with solid execution, 40% earn C grades meeting basic requirements, 10% earn D/F grades with significant deficiencies. Provide specific feedback on scientific writing quality and suggest improvements for future reports.

title: Complex Multi-Phase Project Recovery and Optimization Exam
description: Students will analyze a failing multi-million dollar IT infrastructure project, develop a comprehensive recovery plan, and demonstrate advanced project management competencies including risk mitigation, stakeholder management, resource reallocation, and change control processes.
learning_objectives_assessed: Analyze complex project failures and identify root causes using advanced diagnostic frameworks
Develop comprehensive project recovery strategies incorporating risk management, stakeholder alignment, and resource optimization
Apply advanced change management principles to restructure project scope, timeline, and deliverables
Demonstrate mastery of project governance, communication protocols, and performance measurement systems
rubric_criteria: Problem Analysis & Root Cause Identification (25 points): Demonstrates systematic analysis using multiple PM frameworks (5W analysis, fishbone diagrams, etc.), identifies 5-7 critical failure points, provides evidence-based reasoning, and prioritizes issues by impact and urgency

Recovery Strategy Development (25 points): Creates comprehensive recovery plan with realistic timeline adjustments, resource reallocation strategies, revised scope statements, updated risk registers, and stakeholder communication plan with specific deliverables and milestones

Risk Management & Mitigation Planning (25 points): Identifies 8-10 project risks with probability/impact assessments, develops specific mitigation strategies, creates contingency plans for high-priority risks, and establishes monitoring triggers and escalation procedures

Implementation Framework & Success Metrics (25 points): Designs detailed implementation roadmap with phase gates, defines measurable KPIs and success criteria, establishes governance structure with clear roles/responsibilities, and creates communication protocols for progress reporting
instructions: You are the newly appointed Senior Project Manager for TechCorp's failed ERP implementation project. The $15M project is 18 months behind schedule, 300% over budget, with only 25% functionality delivered. Key stakeholders have lost confidence, the development team is demoralized, and the CEO has threatened project cancellation unless immediate recovery action is taken. Your task is to conduct a comprehensive project assessment and develop a detailed recovery plan. Your response must include: (1) Executive Summary (1 page) outlining current status and recommended actions, (2) Root Cause Analysis using at least two PM diagnostic frameworks, identifying specific failure points with supporting evidence, (3) Comprehensive Recovery Plan including revised project charter, updated work breakdown structure, resource reallocation strategy, and revised timeline with critical path analysis, (4) Risk Management Plan with updated risk register, mitigation strategies, and contingency plans, (5) Stakeholder Communication Strategy detailing how you will rebuild confidence and maintain alignment, (6) Success Metrics and monitoring framework with specific KPIs and reporting schedules. Format your response as a professional project management document with clear sections, supporting charts/diagrams where appropriate, and executive-level recommendations. Assume access to industry-standard PM tools and methodologies. Submit as a single PDF document with appendices for detailed charts and calculations.
grading_notes: Evaluate responses for practical applicability and professional sophistication. Excellent responses (90-100%) will demonstrate creative problem-solving, industry best practices, and realistic implementation approaches. Good responses (80-89%) will show solid PM fundamentals with minor gaps in strategic thinking. Average responses (70-79%) will display basic competency but lack depth in analysis or implementation planning. Watch for unrealistic timelines, generic solutions without project-specific customization, inadequate risk assessment, or failure to address stakeholder dynamics. Expect 15% A grades, 35% B grades, 35% C grades, 15% D/F grades. Deduct points for missing required sections, unprofessional presentation, or failure to use appropriate PM terminology and frameworks.

title: Strategic Leadership Crisis Simulation: Multi-Stakeholder Decision Making
description: Students engage in a structured discussion analyzing a complex organizational crisis scenario, demonstrating advanced leadership decision-making, stakeholder management, and change leadership capabilities through real-time problem-solving and peer interaction.
learning_objectives_assessed: Demonstrate advanced strategic decision-making under uncertainty and time pressure
Apply stakeholder analysis and management techniques in crisis situations
Exhibit transformational leadership behaviors during organizational change
Synthesize multiple leadership theories to address complex organizational challenges
rubric_criteria: Strategic Analysis & Decision Quality (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of systemic issues, evaluates multiple solutions using data and theory, makes defendable decisions considering long-term implications and unintended consequences

Stakeholder Management & Communication (25 points): Identifies all key stakeholders and their interests, develops tailored communication strategies, demonstrates emotional intelligence in managing conflicting demands, shows cultural sensitivity

Leadership Presence & Influence (25 points): Exhibits confidence and authenticity, builds consensus while maintaining decisiveness, adapts leadership style to situation and audience, demonstrates ethical reasoning and moral courage

Discussion Facilitation & Collaboration (25 points): Actively listens and builds on others' ideas, asks probing questions that advance the discussion, manages conflict constructively, synthesizes diverse viewpoints into actionable plans
instructions: You will participate in a 60-minute crisis simulation discussion based on the provided scenario packet (distributed 30 minutes before discussion begins). During preparation time, analyze the scenario using stakeholder mapping, SWOT analysis, and at least two leadership frameworks from course materials. Come prepared with: (1) Your initial assessment of the crisis and root causes, (2) A prioritized stakeholder map with engagement strategies, (3) Three potential solution pathways with risk assessments, (4) Your personal leadership approach for this situation. During the discussion, you will work with 4-5 peers to develop a comprehensive crisis response plan. The discussion will be divided into three phases: Problem Definition (15 min), Solution Development (30 min), and Implementation Planning (15 min). You must actively contribute to each phase while demonstrating leadership behaviors. Document your contributions and evolution of thinking on the provided reflection sheet. Be prepared to defend your recommendations with evidence from leadership theory and real-world examples. Professional communication standards apply - this simulates an actual executive team meeting.
grading_notes: Evaluate students on both content quality and process skills. Look for evidence of preparation through specific references to frameworks and data from the scenario. Award higher marks for students who advance the discussion beyond surface-level solutions to address systemic issues. Deduct points for dominating conversation or failing to engage meaningfully. Expect grade distribution: 20% A-level (90-100), 60% B-level (80-89), 20% C-level or below. Common issues include: over-reliance on single leadership style, ignoring stakeholder complexity, proposing unrealistic timelines, and avoiding difficult trade-offs. Strong responses will show integration of multiple theoretical perspectives, acknowledgment of implementation challenges, and adaptive leadership behaviors during the discussion itself.

title: AWS Cloud Fundamentals: Small Business Migration Strategy Presentation
description: Students will create and deliver a 10-minute presentation proposing an AWS cloud migration strategy for a small business, demonstrating understanding of core AWS services, pricing models, security basics, and migration planning.
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify and explain the purpose of core AWS services (EC2, S3, RDS, VPC)
Describe AWS pricing models and cost optimization strategies
Explain fundamental AWS security concepts and best practices
Analyze business requirements and recommend appropriate AWS solutions
rubric_criteria: AWS Services Knowledge (25 points): Correctly identifies and explains at least 4 core AWS services relevant to the business scenario, demonstrates understanding of service purposes and basic functionality

Cost Analysis and Pricing (25 points): Provides realistic cost estimates using AWS pricing calculator, explains chosen pricing models (On-Demand vs Reserved vs Spot), includes at least 2 cost optimization recommendations

Security and Compliance (25 points): Addresses basic security considerations (IAM, encryption, backups), mentions relevant compliance requirements, demonstrates understanding of shared responsibility model

Presentation Quality and Business Case (25 points): Clear 10-minute presentation with logical flow, addresses business benefits and risks, includes timeline for migration, uses appropriate visual aids
instructions: You will create a presentation proposing an AWS cloud migration for FreshBites Café, a small restaurant chain with 3 locations. Current setup: 2 on-premise servers (web application + database), basic website, customer loyalty program, and accounting software. Requirements: Present your migration strategy in exactly 10 minutes using 8-12 slides. Include: (1) Brief analysis of current infrastructure limitations, (2) Recommended AWS services with justification (minimum 4 services), (3) Architecture diagram showing service relationships, (4) Cost breakdown using AWS pricing calculator for first year, (5) Security measures and compliance considerations, (6) 6-month migration timeline with key milestones, (7) Business benefits and potential challenges. Submit presentation slides as PDF 24 hours before presentation date. During presentation, you may use notes but must demonstrate understanding through Q&A session. Assume monthly traffic of 10,000 website visitors, 500GB data storage needs, and moderate compute requirements. Your audience is the business owner with limited technical background.
grading_notes: Grade presentations immediately after each session for best feedback. Award full points for AWS Services Knowledge if student correctly explains service purposes even with minor technical inaccuracies. For Cost Analysis, accept estimates within 20% of actual AWS calculator results - focus on methodology over precision. Security criterion should demonstrate awareness of basic concepts rather than expert-level knowledge. Presentation Quality heavily weighs clarity and business focus over technical depth. Common issues: students overcomplicating architecture, unrealistic timelines (too aggressive), forgetting to address business impact. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-range (90-100), 60% B-range (80-89), 25% C-range or below. Deduct 5 points for exceeding time limit, 10 points for late slide submission.

title: Project Charter and Initial Risk Assessment Portfolio
description: Students will develop a comprehensive project charter and conduct an initial risk assessment for a realistic business scenario, demonstrating mastery of project initiation processes, stakeholder identification, and risk management fundamentals according to PMI standards.
learning_objectives_assessed: Develop project charters that align with organizational strategy and stakeholder needs
Identify and analyze key project stakeholders using appropriate tools and techniques
Conduct initial risk identification and qualitative risk analysis
Apply PMI terminology and processes accurately in project documentation
rubric_criteria: Project Charter Quality (25 points): Charter includes all required elements (project purpose, objectives, success criteria, high-level requirements, assumptions, constraints, key stakeholders, project manager authority), demonstrates clear business case alignment, and uses proper PMI terminology throughout

Stakeholder Analysis (25 points): Comprehensive stakeholder register with minimum 12 stakeholders, accurate power/interest grid mapping, appropriate engagement strategies for each stakeholder category, and clear rationale for classification decisions

Risk Management (25 points): Identifies minimum 15 realistic risks across multiple categories, provides detailed risk statements using proper format (cause-risk-effect), completes qualitative analysis with probability/impact ratings, and prioritizes risks using risk score methodology

Professional Presentation and PMI Integration (25 points): Documents are professionally formatted and error-free, consistently applies PMI processes and terminology, includes proper citations to PMBOK Guide, and demonstrates integration between charter, stakeholder, and risk components
instructions: Select a realistic project scenario from the provided list or propose your own (requires instructor approval). Your portfolio must include: 1) A complete project charter (2-3 pages) following PMI standards with all required sections clearly labeled and thoroughly completed. 2) A stakeholder register identifying at least 12 diverse stakeholders with complete contact information, roles, requirements, and expectations. Include a power/interest grid with stakeholders properly plotted and engagement strategies defined for each quadrant. 3) A risk register containing minimum 15 risks with detailed risk statements, probability/impact assessments, risk scores, and initial response strategies. Organize risks by category (technical, external, organizational, project management). 4) A 1-page executive summary explaining how these three components integrate and support project success. All documents must reference relevant PMBOK Guide processes and knowledge areas. Use professional business formatting with headers, page numbers, and consistent styling. Submit as a single PDF with clearly labeled sections. Include a bibliography citing the PMBOK Guide and minimum two additional project management sources. Total submission should be 8-12 pages excluding appendices.
grading_notes: Evaluate completeness and accuracy of PMI process application first, then assess content quality. Common issues include: incomplete stakeholder analysis (often missing negative stakeholders), generic risk statements lacking specificity, project charters without measurable success criteria, and inconsistent terminology usage. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level work (90-100), 60% B-level work (80-89), 20% C-level work (70-79), 5% below 70. Deduct 5 points for late submission per day. Look for evidence of critical thinking in stakeholder engagement strategies and risk response planning. Strong submissions will show clear connections between identified stakeholders and potential risks, with charter elements reflecting complexity of stakeholder landscape.

title: E-commerce Website Analytics Implementation and Performance Analysis Lab Report
description: Students will implement Google Analytics 4 (GA4) tracking on a simulated e-commerce website, configure advanced tracking features, analyze 30 days of provided sample data, and deliver comprehensive insights through custom reports and recommendations for optimization strategies.
learning_objectives_assessed: Configure and implement GA4 tracking with enhanced e-commerce events and custom parameters
Create and interpret advanced audience segments and conversion funnels for business insights
Build custom reports and dashboards using GA4's reporting interface and Google Analytics Intelligence
Analyze attribution models and customer journey data to make data-driven marketing recommendations
Demonstrate proficiency in GA4's measurement protocol and debug implementation issues
rubric_criteria: Technical Implementation (25 points): Correct GA4 setup including enhanced e-commerce tracking, custom events, conversion goals, and audience configuration. All tracking codes properly implemented with no console errors.

Data Analysis & Interpretation (25 points): Accurate analysis of user behavior, conversion paths, traffic sources, and demographic insights. Proper use of segments, filters, and comparison features to extract meaningful patterns.

Custom Reporting & Visualization (25 points): Creation of comprehensive custom reports and dashboards that effectively communicate key metrics. Proper use of dimensions, metrics, and visualization types appropriate for different stakeholder audiences.

Strategic Recommendations & Documentation (25 points): Well-researched, data-backed recommendations for website optimization, marketing strategy improvements, and user experience enhancements. Clear documentation of methodology and professional presentation of findings.
instructions: Using the provided e-commerce website template and sample dataset, complete the following deliverables: 1) Implement GA4 tracking with enhanced e-commerce events (purchase, add_to_cart, view_item) and configure at least 3 custom parameters relevant to the business. Set up conversion goals and create 2 audience segments based on user behavior. Document your implementation process and include screenshots of your GA4 configuration. 2) Analyze the provided 30-day dataset focusing on user acquisition, behavior flow, and conversion performance. Create detailed analysis of traffic sources, top-performing product categories, cart abandonment rates, and user demographics. Use GA4's Analysis Hub to build at least one funnel analysis and one cohort analysis. 3) Design and build a custom dashboard containing 8-10 key performance indicators relevant to e-commerce management. Create two additional detailed reports: one focusing on marketing channel performance and another on user experience metrics. Export visualizations and provide commentary on insights. 4) Compile findings into a professional lab report (2000-2500 words) including executive summary, methodology, key findings, strategic recommendations for improving conversion rates and user engagement, and appendices with technical documentation. Submit all GA4 screenshots, exported reports, and the final report as a single PDF, plus sharing access to your GA4 property for verification.
grading_notes: Evaluate technical accuracy by checking GA4 property setup - verify that events fire correctly using GA4 DebugView and that custom parameters appear in reports. For data analysis, look for proper use of statistical concepts and ability to identify actionable insights rather than just stating numbers. Custom reports should demonstrate understanding of appropriate metrics for different business questions. Strategic recommendations must be supported by specific data points from their analysis. Common issues include: incomplete e-commerce tracking setup, misunderstanding of GA4 event model vs Universal Analytics, superficial analysis without connecting metrics to business impact, and poor documentation. Grade distribution expectation: 15% should receive 90-100 points, 60% should receive 75-89 points, 20% should receive 65-74 points, 5% below 65 points. Partial credit available for each criterion - technical implementation can receive partial credit if setup is attempted but contains errors, analysis section should receive credit for correct methodology even if conclusions are weak.

title: E-commerce Customer Segmentation Analysis Exam
description: Students will perform comprehensive customer segmentation analysis on an e-commerce dataset using unsupervised learning techniques, evaluate model performance, and provide actionable business insights through data visualization and statistical interpretation.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply unsupervised learning algorithms (K-means, hierarchical clustering) to real-world business data
Perform exploratory data analysis and feature engineering for customer behavior datasets
Evaluate clustering model performance using appropriate metrics and validation techniques
Create compelling data visualizations that communicate insights to business stakeholders
Translate statistical findings into actionable business recommendations
rubric_criteria: Data Preprocessing and EDA (25 points): Thorough data cleaning, handling missing values, outlier detection, feature scaling, and comprehensive exploratory analysis with appropriate statistical summaries and visualizations

Clustering Implementation and Optimization (25 points): Correct implementation of at least two clustering algorithms, proper hyperparameter tuning using elbow method or silhouette analysis, and justification of optimal cluster number selection

Model Evaluation and Validation (25 points): Application of multiple clustering evaluation metrics (silhouette score, inertia, Davies-Bouldin index), interpretation of cluster stability, and comparison of different clustering approaches with statistical reasoning

Business Insights and Visualization (25 points): Creation of clear, professional visualizations that effectively communicate cluster characteristics, development of detailed customer personas for each segment, and specific, actionable business recommendations with ROI considerations
instructions:
You are provided with an e-commerce customer dataset containing purchase history, demographics, and behavioral metrics for 10,000 customers. Your task is to segment customers into meaningful groups and provide strategic recommendations.

Deliverables:
1. Jupyter notebook with complete analysis including data preprocessing, EDA, clustering implementation, and evaluation
2. Executive summary document (2-3 pages) with key findings and business recommendations
3. Professional dashboard or infographic visualizing customer segments

Technical Requirements:
- Use Python with pandas, scikit-learn, matplotlib/seaborn
- Implement K-means and one additional clustering algorithm
- Apply appropriate data preprocessing techniques
- Include statistical validation of clustering results
- Code must be well-commented and reproducible

Dataset includes: CustomerID, Age, Gender, Annual_Income, Spending_Score, Purchase_Frequency, Average_Order_Value, Days_Since_Last_Purchase, Product_Categories_Purchased, Marketing_Channel_Response

Submission Format:
- Submit .ipynb file, PDF executive summary, and visualization files
- Name files: StudentID_CustomerSegmentation_Notebook.ipynb, StudentID_ExecutiveSummary.pdf
- Include brief reflection on methodology choices and limitations
- All visualizations must have proper titles, labels, and legends
- Executive summary should target non-technical business audience
grading_notes: Grade distribution expectation: 15% A grades, 25% B grades, 40% C grades, 20% D/F grades. Focus on practical application over theoretical knowledge. Deduct points for: uncommented code (-5 points), missing statistical justification (-10 points), poor visualization quality (-5 points). Award bonus points (up to +5) for innovative approaches or exceptional insights. Common issues to watch: inappropriate feature scaling, ignoring categorical variables, over-interpretation of clusters, lack of business context. Students should demonstrate understanding that clustering is exploratory - perfect separation is not expected. Evaluate executive summary separately from technical implementation to ensure business communication skills are assessed.

title: Mathematical Modeling and Proof Strategies: Analyzing Non-Linear Dynamic Systems
description: Students will engage in advanced mathematical discourse by analyzing a complex real-world scenario involving population dynamics, constructing mathematical models, developing formal proofs, and critically evaluating multiple solution approaches through structured peer discussion and mathematical argumentation.
learning_objectives_assessed: Construct and analyze non-linear mathematical models for real-world phenomena
Develop formal mathematical proofs using multiple proof techniques
Critically evaluate and compare different mathematical approaches to complex problems
Communicate mathematical reasoning clearly through written discourse and peer interaction
rubric_criteria: Mathematical Modeling (25 points): Accurately constructs differential equation model, identifies key parameters, validates model assumptions, and demonstrates understanding of non-linear dynamics including equilibrium points and stability analysis

Proof Construction (25 points): Develops rigorous formal proof using appropriate techniques (direct proof, contradiction, or induction), shows logical progression, uses correct mathematical notation, and addresses all necessary cases or conditions

Critical Analysis (25 points): Compares at least two different solution methods, identifies strengths and limitations of each approach, discusses convergence properties, and evaluates computational efficiency and practical applicability

Mathematical Communication (25 points): Uses precise mathematical language, provides clear explanations of reasoning, responds substantively to peer posts with mathematical evidence, and demonstrates ability to clarify complex concepts for others
instructions: You will analyze a predator-prey population model where two species interact in a closed ecosystem. The scenario involves wolves and deer populations with seasonal migration patterns and limited resources. Your task consists of three phases: (1) Initial Analysis - Construct a system of non-linear differential equations modeling the population dynamics, identify equilibrium points, and analyze stability using linearization techniques. Provide a formal proof that the system has at least one stable equilibrium point. (2) Solution Comparison - Solve your system using both analytical methods (where possible) and numerical approximation techniques. Compare the accuracy, computational requirements, and practical limitations of each approach. Include phase portrait analysis and discuss long-term behavior predictions. (3) Peer Discussion - Post your initial analysis in the discussion forum within 72 hours. Then, review and respond to at least three classmates' models, focusing on mathematical accuracy, alternative approaches, and real-world validity. Your responses should include specific mathematical feedback, suggest improvements, or propose alternative modeling assumptions. All mathematical work must show complete steps, use proper notation, and include justification for major modeling decisions. Submit your initial post (1000-1200 words) and peer responses (200-300 words each) through the course discussion platform. Include all calculations, graphs, and code (if applicable) as attachments or embedded content.
grading_notes: Instructors should evaluate mathematical rigor over creativity - prioritize correct application of calculus and differential equations concepts. Look for proper use of stability analysis techniques and phase portrait interpretation. In proof sections, partial credit should be awarded for correct methodology even if minor computational errors occur.
