For peer discussions, assess quality over quantity - substantive mathematical dialogue is more valuable than multiple superficial responses. Common issues include: incorrect linearization around equilibrium points, confusion between local and global stability, and inadequate justification of modeling assumptions. Expect grade distribution: 15-20% A-level work (90-100), 30-35% B-level work (80-89), 35-40% C-level work (70-79). Students scoring below 70 typically struggle with differential equations fundamentals or proof techniques and may need additional support.

title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics Phenomenon Analysis and Research Presentation
description: Students will conduct in-depth research on a cutting-edge quantum mechanics phenomenon, analyze current experimental data and theoretical frameworks, and present their findings to demonstrate mastery of advanced quantum concepts and their real-world applications.
learning_objectives_assessed: Analyze complex quantum mechanical systems using advanced mathematical frameworks and interpret experimental quantum phenomena
Evaluate current research in quantum physics and critically assess theoretical models against experimental evidence
Synthesize quantum mechanical principles to explain emerging technologies and their potential applications
Communicate advanced physics concepts effectively to expert audiences using appropriate scientific terminology and visual representations
rubric_criteria: Scientific Content and Accuracy (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of quantum phenomenon, correctly applies relevant equations and principles, accurately interprets experimental data, and shows mastery of underlying physics concepts

Research Quality and Analysis (25 points): Uses current, peer-reviewed sources, critically evaluates competing theories, identifies limitations in current understanding, and connects phenomenon to broader quantum mechanical framework

Technical Communication and Visuals (25 points): Uses precise scientific terminology, creates clear and informative diagrams/graphs, effectively explains complex mathematical relationships, and maintains appropriate level of technical detail for expert audience

Presentation Skills and Q&A Response (25 points): Delivers confident, well-organized presentation within time limits, demonstrates deep understanding through thoughtful responses to questions, and engages audience effectively
instructions: Select a quantum mechanics phenomenon from the approved list (quantum tunneling in novel materials, quantum entanglement applications, quantum computing algorithms, topological quantum states, or quantum field theory applications). Your presentation must include: (1) Historical context and discovery background, (2) Detailed mathematical treatment using appropriate quantum mechanical formalism, (3) Analysis of at least three recent experimental studies or theoretical papers from the last five years, (4) Discussion of current technological applications or potential future applications, (5) Identification of unresolved questions or ongoing research challenges. Prepare a 20-minute presentation using professional slides, including original diagrams explaining the quantum mechanical processes involved. You must demonstrate mathematical derivations for key relationships and show how experimental data supports or challenges theoretical predictions. Include a comprehensive reference list with minimum 8 peer-reviewed sources. Submit presentation slides 24 hours before your scheduled presentation time. Be prepared for a 10-minute Q&A session where you may be asked to elaborate on mathematical concepts, defend your analysis, or discuss alternative interpretations. Your presentation should assume an audience with advanced undergraduate quantum mechanics knowledge.
grading_notes: Look for evidence of genuine understanding beyond memorization - students should be able to explain concepts in their own words and make connections between different quantum phenomena. Pay attention to mathematical rigor: equations should be properly derived or clearly explained, not just presented. Common issues include insufficient depth in mathematical treatment, over-reliance on popular science sources rather than primary literature, and inability to connect theoretical concepts to experimental reality. Excellent presentations (A range) will demonstrate original thinking, such as proposing new experimental tests or identifying novel applications. During Q&A, probe understanding by asking 'what if' scenarios or requesting clarification of assumptions. Grade distribution should reflect expert-level expectations: C-level work shows basic competency but lacks depth, B-level demonstrates solid understanding with minor gaps, A-level shows mastery with ability to synthesize and extend concepts.

title: E-commerce Customer Behavior Analysis Lab Report
description: Students will perform a comprehensive analysis of an e-commerce dataset to identify customer purchasing patterns, create visualizations, and provide data-driven business recommendations. learning_objectives_assessed: Apply descriptive and inferential statistical methods to analyze real-world datasets
Create effective data visualizations that communicate insights clearly
Interpret statistical results and translate findings into actionable business recommendations
Demonstrate proficiency in data cleaning and preprocessing techniques
rubric_criteria: Data Exploration and Cleaning (25 points): Thorough examination of data quality, appropriate handling of missing values, outlier detection and treatment, clear documentation of preprocessing steps

Statistical Analysis (25 points): Correct application of descriptive statistics, appropriate use of hypothesis testing or correlation analysis, accurate interpretation of statistical measures and significance levels
Data Visualization (25 points): Creation of 3-5 professional, well-labeled charts that effectively communicate key findings, appropriate chart selection for data types, clear legends and annotations

Business Insights and Recommendations (25 points): Clear articulation of key findings, logical connection between data analysis and business implications, specific and actionable recommendations supported by evidence
instructions: You will analyze a provided e-commerce dataset containing customer transactions, demographics, and product information. Submit as a PDF report (8-12 pages) with embedded visualizations and a separate file containing your analysis code (Python/R). Include code comments explaining your methodology. Use professional formatting with clear headings, numbered figures, and proper citations for any external sources. Data dictionary and sample questions are provided in the course materials. Late submissions lose 10% per day.
grading_notes: Look for evidence of systematic thinking in data exploration - students should identify and address data quality issues before analysis. Statistical analysis should demonstrate understanding of when to use specific tests and how to interpret results in context. Visualizations should follow best practices (appropriate scales, clear labels, consistent formatting). Common issues include: inadequate data cleaning documentation, misinterpretation of correlation vs causation, poorly designed charts, and vague recommendations. Expect grade distribution: 15% A-level (90-100), 35% B-level (80-89), 40% C-level (70-79), 10% below 70%. Provide specific feedback on technical accuracy and professional presentation quality.

title: Complex Project Risk Management and Recovery Strategy Assessment
description: Students will analyze a multi-phase software development project facing critical challenges including scope creep, resource constraints, stakeholder conflicts, and technical dependencies. They must demonstrate advanced project management competencies by developing comprehensive risk mitigation strategies, recovery plans, and stakeholder communication approaches while justifying decisions using established PM frameworks.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply advanced risk identification, analysis, and mitigation techniques in complex project scenarios
Develop and justify project recovery strategies using quantitative and qualitative analysis methods
Integrate stakeholder management principles with change control processes in crisis situations
Synthesize multiple project management frameworks (PMI, Agile, Lean) to address multifaceted project challenges
rubric_criteria: Risk Analysis and Prioritization (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive risk identification using systematic methods (SWOT, fishbone, risk registers), applies quantitative risk analysis (probability/impact matrices, Monte Carlo concepts), and prioritizes risks based on project objectives with clear justification

Recovery Strategy Development (25 points): Develops realistic, actionable recovery plans addressing schedule compression, resource reallocation, and scope management; incorporates cost-benefit analysis of alternative approaches; demonstrates understanding of change management processes and their implementation

Stakeholder Communication and Management (25 points): Creates targeted communication strategies for different stakeholder groups, addresses conflict resolution techniques, develops escalation procedures, and demonstrates cultural sensitivity and influence management in crisis situations

Framework Integration and Professional Judgment (25 points): Appropriately applies and synthesizes PM methodologies (traditional vs. agile approaches), demonstrates critical thinking in decision-making processes, provides evidence-based recommendations, and shows understanding of organizational and industry context factors
instructions: You are the project manager for Phoenix Software Solutions' largest client implementation project. The project involves migrating a Fortune 500 company's legacy customer management system to a cloud-based platform across 15 international offices. The project is currently 8 months into a planned 18-month timeline and faces multiple critical issues: 30% budget overrun, key technical architect departure, newly discovered data compliance requirements in three countries, stakeholder disagreement on feature priorities, and vendor delays affecting infrastructure readiness. Your deliverable must include: (1) A comprehensive risk assessment matrix identifying and analyzing at least 12 project risks using probability/impact scoring and categorization, (2) A detailed project recovery plan with specific timeline, resource, and budget recommendations including rationale for chosen strategies, (3) A stakeholder communication plan addressing immediate crisis communication, ongoing status reporting, and change approval processes tailored to different audience needs, (4) An executive summary (500 words maximum) recommending the project's future direction with supporting analysis. Use professional project management terminology, reference appropriate PM frameworks, and provide realistic timelines and cost estimates. Your response should total 2,500-3,000 words and demonstrate graduate-level analysis and writing quality. Submit as a single document with clear section headers and supporting exhibits (charts, matrices, timelines) as needed.
grading_notes: Evaluate responses for depth of analysis rather than just completion. Look for evidence of systematic thinking in risk identification - students should go beyond obvious risks to identify interdependencies and secondary impacts. Recovery strategies should show understanding of project constraints and realistic trade-offs rather than generic solutions. Strong responses will demonstrate stakeholder analysis skills by differentiating communication approaches for technical teams, executives, and end-users. Grade harshly on frameworks - students should show genuine understanding of when to apply different methodologies, not just name-dropping. Expect 15% of students to score in 90-100 range (exceptional strategic thinking), 60% in 75-89 range (solid professional competency), and 25% below 75 (needs improvement). Deduct points for unrealistic timelines, inadequate cost considerations, or failure to address cultural/international aspects of the scenario.

title: Organizational Transformation Leadership Simulation
description: Students will design and execute a comprehensive organizational transformation strategy for a failing company scenario, demonstrating advanced leadership competencies through strategic planning, stakeholder management, change implementation, and crisis leadership over a 6-week simulation period.
learning_objectives_assessed: Develop and implement complex organizational change strategies using advanced leadership frameworks
Demonstrate crisis leadership skills through data-driven decision making under uncertainty
Execute stakeholder engagement and communication strategies for multi-level organizational transformation
Apply systems thinking to diagnose organizational problems and design sustainable solutions
Evaluate leadership effectiveness through measurable outcomes and reflective analysis
rubric_criteria: Strategic Leadership Framework (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of transformation models, conducts thorough organizational diagnosis using multiple frameworks (Kotter, ADKAR, etc.), develops comprehensive 18-month transformation roadmap with clear milestones, risk mitigation strategies, and resource allocation plans

Crisis Leadership & Decision Making (25 points): Shows decisive leadership during simulated crisis events, makes data-informed decisions under time pressure, adapts strategy based on emerging challenges, demonstrates emotional intelligence in managing team stress, and maintains organizational morale during uncertainty

Stakeholder Management & Communication (25 points): Creates differentiated communication strategies for various stakeholder groups (board, employees, customers, investors), facilitates difficult conversations with resistant stakeholders, builds coalition support for change initiatives, and demonstrates cultural sensitivity in messaging

Implementation Excellence & Results (25 points): Executes transformation plan with measurable outcomes, tracks KPIs and adjusts tactics accordingly, manages competing priorities effectively, delivers on promised milestones, and demonstrates sustainable change integration with post-implementation monitoring systems
instructions: You are the newly appointed CEO of TechFlow Industries, a 500-employee software company experiencing 30% revenue decline, 40% employee turnover, and major client defections. grading_notes: Evaluate based on depth of strategic thinking rather than 'correct' answers - multiple viable approaches exist. Grade distribution expectation: 15% A grades (exceptional strategic insight and execution), 30% B+ grades (solid competency with minor gaps), 40% B grades (meets requirements with some weaknesses), 15% below B (significant deficiencies in strategic thinking or implementation). Bonus consideration for innovative solutions backed by research and creative stakeholder engagement strategies.

title: AWS Core Services Implementation and Architecture Exam
description: A comprehensive hands-on exam assessing students' ability to implement basic AWS infrastructure, configure core services, and apply fundamental security and cost optimization practices. Students will demonstrate practical skills through a combination of multiple-choice questions, scenario-based problems, and guided AWS console tasks.
learning_objectives_assessed: Identify and describe the core AWS services including EC2, S3, VPC, and IAM
Configure basic AWS infrastructure components following best practices
Implement fundamental security measures using IAM roles and policies
Apply cost optimization strategies for basic AWS deployments
Navigate the AWS Management Console effectively to perform common tasks
rubric_criteria: AWS Core Services Knowledge (25 points): Correctly identifies service use cases, understands service limitations, accurately describes service features and pricing models
Infrastructure Configuration (25 points): Successfully creates and configures EC2 instances, S3 buckets, and VPC components following AWS best practices and naming conventions

Security Implementation (25 points): Properly configures IAM users, roles, and policies with principle of least privilege, implements basic security group rules, demonstrates understanding of AWS security fundamentals

Cost Management and Optimization (25 points): Accurately estimates costs using AWS pricing calculator, identifies cost optimization opportunities, understands billing concepts and free tier limitations
instructions: This exam consists of three sections to be completed within 2 hours. Section A contains 20 multiple-choice questions about AWS core services, pricing, and best practices (40 minutes). Section B presents 5 scenario-based problems requiring you to select appropriate AWS services and justify your choices in 2-3 sentences each (30 minutes). Section C is a guided hands-on exercise where you'll use the provided AWS sandbox account to create a basic web application infrastructure including an EC2 instance, S3 bucket, security groups, and IAM role following the provided specifications (50 minutes). For the hands-on section, take screenshots of your completed configurations and upload them to the designated folder. All work must be completed individually using only approved AWS documentation and course materials. Submit your multiple-choice answers through the online quiz system, written responses as a PDF document, and screenshots in a zip file labeled with your student ID. Partial credit will be awarded for Section C if configurations are attempted but incomplete. Ensure your AWS resources are properly tagged with your student ID for identification during grading.
grading_notes: Grade multiple-choice questions automatically through quiz system (1.25 points each). For scenario questions, award full points for correct service selection with reasonable justification, partial credit for correct services with weak justification or suboptimal services with strong justification. Hands-on section should be graded by checking actual AWS resources in student accounts - verify EC2 instance is running with correct configuration, S3 bucket exists with proper permissions, security groups have appropriate rules, and IAM role follows least privilege principle. Common issues include overly permissive security groups, incorrect instance types, missing tags, and IAM policies with excessive permissions. Target grade distribution: 15% A grades (90-100), 35% B grades (80-89), 40% C grades (70-79), 10% below 70. Deduct 5 points for late submission, 10 points for failure to clean up AWS resources after grading period.

title: Risk Management Strategy Discussion: Analyzing Stakeholder Impact and Mitigation Approaches
description: Students will analyze a complex project scenario involving multiple risk categories and engage in structured discussions about risk identification, assessment, and response strategies while considering stakeholder perspectives and project constraints.
learning_objectives_assessed: Apply risk management processes including identification, qualitative and quantitative analysis, and response planning
Evaluate stakeholder impact and influence on risk management decisions
Demonstrate understanding of risk response strategies and their trade-offs
Analyze the relationship between project constraints and risk tolerance
rubric_criteria: Risk Identification and Analysis (25 points): Accurately identifies 5-7 relevant risks, categorizes them appropriately, and demonstrates understanding of probability and impact assessment techniques
Stakeholder Impact Assessment (25 points): Clearly articulates how identified risks affect different stakeholders, considers stakeholder risk tolerance, and addresses communication requirements

Response Strategy Development (25 points): Proposes appropriate risk response strategies (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept), justifies choices with sound reasoning, and considers implementation feasibility

Discussion Participation and Professional Communication (25 points): Actively engages with peers' analyses, provides constructive feedback, asks clarifying questions, and demonstrates professional project management communication
instructions: You are the project manager for a 14-month software implementation project for a healthcare organization. The project has a $2.8M budget and involves integrating electronic health records across three hospital locations. Key stakeholders include hospital administrators, IT staff, medical personnel, and regulatory compliance officers. Your team includes 12 members across different locations and time zones. Review the detailed scenario packet (provided separately) and prepare a comprehensive risk analysis addressing: 1) Identify and categorize 5-7 significant risks using a risk breakdown structure approach, 2) Assess each risk using probability/impact matrix methodology, 3) Analyze how each risk specifically affects different stakeholder groups, 4) Propose detailed response strategies for your top 3 highest-priority risks, and 5) Explain how project constraints (time, budget, scope, quality) influence your risk management approach. During the discussion session, you will present your analysis in 5 minutes, then participate in peer review and collaborative problem-solving. Come prepared with specific examples, quantitative assessments where possible, and be ready to defend your risk prioritization decisions. Submit your preparation notes and post-discussion reflection within 24 hours of the session.
grading_notes: Evaluate depth of risk thinking rather than just quantity of risks identified. Look for evidence of PMI risk management process understanding. Strong responses will connect risks to specific project characteristics and stakeholder needs. Watch for generic risks vs. scenario-specific risks. Discussion participation should demonstrate active listening and building on others' ideas, not just presenting own work. Common issues include: confusing issues with risks, inadequate stakeholder analysis, proposing unrealistic response strategies, and poor risk prioritization. Expect grade distribution: 15% excellent (90-100), 60% proficient (75-89), 20% developing (60-74), 5% inadequate (below 60). Provide specific feedback on risk assessment techniques and stakeholder consideration quality.
